title: A Survey on the Use of AI/ML for Storage System Design and Optimization
abstract: Storage systems are critical subsystems in modern computing architectures whether Storage systems are aimed for high performance computing ( HPC ) or for distributed cloud computing data centers . Optimizing storage systems has been a decades-old research area to use storage systems efficiently as well as to improve the performance of workloads using storage systems . Advances in Artificial Intelligence ( AI ) and Machine Learning ( ML ) have sped up the optimizations in various aspects of storage systems . In this study , we investigate numerous efforts on using AI / ML for designing and optimizing storage systems . A comprehensive survey at this scale and completeness is n't previously available . we aim to provide a comprehensive overview of the state of the art in using AI / ML in the design , management , and optimization of storage systems in HPC and cloud systems . we have surveyed ≈200 publications from premier conferences and journals that covered storage systems , operating systems , distributed computing , HPC , and embedded systems . we organize this study to describe the designs and optimizations at device , HPC and distributed system , and workload levels . we pose four research questions for each of device , HPC and distributed system , and workload levels , focusing on AI / ML usage , deployment , generalizability of the AI / ML methods , and data management . we also summarize the open research challenges faced in applying AI / ML in the final question . we strongly believe this study will serve the storage systems community as a guide for designing and optimizing storage systems by distilling influential research efforts during the past decade .

title: On stress-testing the target cycle time in aerospace manufacturing systems
abstract: Aircraft assembly lines are characterized by low-volume production , extensive manual work , limited buffer space , specialized resources , long cycle times , and a large network of external suppliers . Unlike in the automotive industry , where a cycle takes only a few minutes , a single cycle in aerospace assembly can last several days or even weeks . For technical reasons , many tasks require skilled manual labor . Assembling large , complex aircraft components requires fine human dexterity , and specialized skills that are difficult to automate or teach to robots . In a growing aerospace market , meeting planned delivery dates becomes increasingly difficult because of numerous known and unknown performance detractors ( worker absence , equipment breakdowns , missing parts , etc . ) . A first step in this direction is to assess how , and to what extent , a nominal scheduling decision can withstand uncertainty . In this work , we focus on stress-testing a given Target Cycle Time ( TCT ) in aerospace manufacturing systems .
keywords: constrained scheduling problem with multiple modes

title: Planning robust routes and charging schedules under energy consumption uncertainty
abstract: Electric vehicle ( EV ) routing faces significant operational challenges due to limited driving range , charging constraints , and uncertainty in energy consumption . This project addresses the Electric Vehicle Routing and Overnight Charging Scheduling Problem under energy consumption uncertainty , assuming exclusive depot-based overnight charging . Energy consumption on each arc is modeled as a bounded random variable and incorporated through a budgeted robust optimization framework . The resulting problem is solved using a Branch-and-Price-and-Cut algorithm based on a route-based set partitioning formulation . Robust feasibility is ensured directly within the pricing problem through an adapted labeling algorithm , while subset-row cuts and an enhanced hierarchical branching scheme accelerate convergence . Computational experiments highlight the trade-off between routing cost and protection against uncertainty , and demonstrate how robustness impacts charging schedules and route departure times .

title: From shelf signalling to delisting: CSR commitment and consumer response to nationally sourced organic private-label products
abstract: Purpose Amid growing consumer scepticism toward symbolic corporate social responsibility ( CSR ) initiatives , this study aims to investigate how the strength of retailers ' CSR commitment – operationalised as either weak ( reflected in the signalling of nationally sourced organic private-label products ( PLPs ) on shelves ) or strong ( reflected in the delisting of non-nationally sourced organic PLPs ) – influences consumer perceptions and behaviours . Specifically , this study examines how the level of CSR commitment moderates the relationship between consumer perceptions of retailers ' CSR and retailers ' actual purchases of organic PLPs . Design / methodology / approach this study combines a qualitative exploratory study with a laboratory experiment involving 315 participants . a qualitative exploratory study examines how consumers perceive CSR actions as reflecting either weak or strong commitment . a laboratory experiment involving 315 participants uses a between-subjects design to compare two conditions : shelf signage ( weak commitment ) and product delisting ( strong commitment ) . 315 participants perceptions of CSR , trust in organic private labels ( PLs ) , behavioural intentions and actual purchases of organic PLPs are measured and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling and multigroup analysis . Findings Results show that strong CSR commitment – manifested through the voluntary delisting of non-nationally sourced organic PLPs – leads to higher perceived respect for consumers and suppliers , greater trust in the organic PL and increased purchases of organic PLPs . Trust and behavioural intentions fully mediate the relationship between perceived CSR and actual purchases . Originality / value this study conceptualises CSR as a continuum of commitment and demonstrates that the strength of CSR actions significantly shapes consumer responses . this study contributes to CSR and retail literature by highlighting the importance of signal credibility and the strategic value of substantial CSR initiatives .

title: Tight MDD Integration for Global Constraints: the Multi-Cumulatives Case
abstract: In problems with objects that have multiple feasible configurations , also known as multi-mode problems , a lack of communication often arises between global constraints and side constraints . To address arises , we propose a novel approach where object configurations are represented using multi-valued decision diagrams ( MDDs ) . Within a novel approach where object configurations are represented using multi-valued decision diagrams ( MDDs ) , global constraint filtering algorithms can directly query multi-valued decision diagrams ( MDDs ) to obtain a more accurate estimate of the bounds of a variable . we formally introduced this new method and a direct application is proposed through the Cumulative constraint . we propose two new constraints , named MDD-Cumulative and MDD-Multi-Cumulatives . MDD-Cumulative is based on the state-of-the-art timetabling algorithm , while the latter takes advantage of the method for filtering mode assignments . we provide numerical evidence that demonstrates the effectiveness of two new constraints , named MDD-Cumulative and MDD-Multi-Cumulatives over the state-of-the-art multi-mode resource-constrained project scheduling problem ( MM-RCPSP ) benchmarks .

title: MicrobioRel : A Set of Datasets for Microbiome Relation Extraction
abstract: Abstract Biomedical knowledge curation relies on a variety of Natural Language Processing tasks , including biomedical entity recognition and document-level relation extraction . With the growing size and capabilities of Language Models , effectively deploying Language Models in specific and specialised domains remains a persistent challenge , highlighting the need for high-quality , domain-adapted datasets . In this work , we present MicrobioRel , a corpus of two datasets to study the relations between biological entities in the gut microbiome . The first dataset , MicrobioRel-cur , is a document-level labelled corpus , corresponding to paragraphs from journal articles that were manually annotated with different types of relations between biomedical concepts in the gut microbiome domain . we describe The first dataset , MicrobioRel-cur creation process , annotation guidelines , and key statistics . On The first dataset , MicrobioRel-cur , we evaluated different architectures for relation extraction and identify PubMedBERT as the most effective model for relation extraction . we also created a second dataset , MicrobioRel-pred , by generating relation predictions on other journal articles using the fine-tuned PubMedBERT model . we demonstrate a second dataset , MicrobioRel-pred potential to extract meaningful interactions . MicrobioRel , a corpus of two datasets to study the relations between biological entities in the gut microbiome is a crucial resource for advancing tasks like automatic knowledge extraction in specialised domains such as the gut microbiome , facilitating hypothesis generation and supporting scientific discovery .

title: Varied mutual growth inhibition between commensal yeasts and E. coli strains
abstract: Interkingdom interactions between bacteria and fungi are an emerging research field that provides insights into pathological , environmental , and microbiota-related relationships . However , the mechanisms governing Interkingdom interactions between bacteria and fungi , particularly in the context of microbial resistance , remain largely unknown . This study aims to enhance our understanding of the complex interactions between different Candida , Nakaseomyces and Sacharomyces species from the human microbiota and two not isogenic strains of Escherichia coli ( antibiotic-susceptible E. coli-ATCC and multidrug-resistant E. coli-OXA48 ) . Forty-nine Candida strains were co-cultured with two not isogenic strains of Escherichia coli ( antibiotic-susceptible E. coli-ATCC and multidrug-resistant E. coli-OXA48 ) . Both bacterial and yeast growth was monitored using flow cytometry and compared to monocultures . The effect of yeast culture supernatants on Escherichia coli proliferation was also investigated . Metabolomic fingerprints and metabolite identification were performed using mass spectrometry-based approaches followed by multiblock statistical analyses . The inhibitory powers ( IP ) of yeasts against Escherichia coli and vice versa varied significantly among fungal species . N. glabrata exhibited the strongest inhibition against E. coli-ATCC , while Candida lusitaniae , C. kefyr , C. krusei , C. tropicalis , and C. dubliniensis showed lower IPs . C. parapsilosis and Saccharomyces cerevisiae had no inhibitory effects . Against E. coli-OXA48 , most yeasts displayed no inhibition , except for N. glabrata . Conversely , Escherichia coli inhibited yeast growth more effectively , particularly Candida albicans . Fungal supernatants from Saccharomyces cerevisiae , Candida lusitaniae , and N. glabrata showed the highest inhibitory effects on E. coli-ATCC , while Saccharomyces cerevisiae , C. krusei , and Candida lusitaniae were most effective against multidrug-resistant E. coli-OXA48 . Unsupervised metabolite profiling data analysis with multiblock approach highlighted a clustering of samples according to yeast species . Regarding inhibitory power on Escherichia coli , active supernatants tend to cluster together suggesting the presence of similar metabolites ; some were further characterized . This study highlights the diverse interactions between Escherichia coli and commensal yeasts . From an applied perspective , these findings pave the way for identifying probiotics or postbiotics with potential applications in combating multidrug-resistant bacteria through novel antimicrobial compounds .

title: Convexity of the annualized cost of energy systems with usage-dependent component lifetimes
abstract: An energy system optimization ( joint sizing & dispatch ) which accounts for the effect of component aging on the annualized cost of the system is proposed . Despite being nonlinear , An energy system optimization ( joint sizing & dispatch ) which accounts for the effect of component aging on the annualized cost of the system is proved to be convex under a generalized “ lifetime = size / usage ” hypothesis . a generalized “ lifetime = size / usage ” hypothesis is shown to cover the classical energy counting model for battery cycling aging , while a linear approximation is needed to account for the operating hours of dispatchable generators . The convexity of An energy system optimization ( joint sizing & dispatch ) which accounts for the effect of component aging on the annualized cost of the system allows for a piecewise linear approximation which is solved efficiently with linear programming solvers . On an illustrative open-source microgrid sizing test case , An energy system optimization ( joint sizing & dispatch ) which accounts for the effect of component aging on the annualized cost of the system significantly reduces the levelized cost of energy compared to the classical fixed-lifetime approaches . Solving time is kept within the same order of magnitude , thanks to The convexity of the model . An energy system optimization ( joint sizing & dispatch ) which accounts for the effect of component aging on the annualized cost of the system also compares favorably with the more advanced “ usage penalty ” approaches , even though an improved variant of the more advanced “ usage penalty ” approaches is formulated and used .

title: Contributions to the development and simulations of generic, modular and multiphysics greenhouses dynamic models, evaluated with a whole year study case dataset
abstract: North-Western Europe heated greenhouses need to address heated greenhouses high fossil energy dependency while heated greenhouses start to face with climate change . In this context , physics-based greenhouses dynamic models can be used for prospective assessments of innovative shapes , equipment , control , etc . A prerequisite for such model-based evaluation is a review of existing implementations , the improvement and development of suitable sub-models in a generic and modular approach that do not require calibration , and the evaluation of a use case global model with a solid experimental dataset . First , this paper details contributions to existing models regarding several aspects : solar gain , boundaries effects , airflows and leakages , heat and mass transfer . The second part is dedicated to the evaluation of an experimental tomato greenhouse global model for an 11-month period . an experimental tomato greenhouse global model assessment is multiphysics : indoor climate , utilities consumptions , yield and Leaf Area Index . The resulting 5 min sampling indoor air climate Root Mean Square Error is 1.3 ° C ( temperature ) and 8.1%RH ( relative humidity ) . The tomato yield Mean Absolute Error is 1.1 kg m-2 . Mass balances also quantify the losses and potentials for water and CO2 . The global model outputs are compared with literature , and it is demonstrated that assessing the accuracy of models based only on statistical indicators is questionable . This approach is compatible with assessments of prospective solutions , This approach increases the confidence for scaling results from small to large commercial greenhouses , and This approach constitutes a base from which simpler and black box models can be derived for other applications such as predictive control .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Unfolded primal-dual algorithm estimating time-varying COVID-19 reproduction numbers
abstract: During an epidemic outbreak , accurate real-time monitoring of the intensity of the pathogen propagation is key to implement efficient countermeasures rapidly enough to avoid dramatic epidemic waves . However , accurate real-time monitoring of the intensity of the pathogen propagation represents an immense challenge for two main reasons . First , for an emerging disease such as COVID-19 , very few prior knowledge is available . Second , in a crisis context , the quality of collected data might be very low . One popular indicator to quantify the pathogen transmissibility , is the time-varying reproduction number , defined as the average number of infections generated by a typical contagious individual if all conditions remained the same . Recently , a variational estimator of the time-varying reproduction number , defined as the average number of infections generated by a typical contagious individual if all conditions remained the same robust to low data quality has been proposed , relying on a customized primal-dual minimization algorithm . This work proposes to unfold a customized primal-dual minimization algorithm into a residual convolutional neural network . a residual convolutional neural network , is trained on genuinely crafted synthetic data . a residual convolutional neural network is then compared to state-of-the art estimators and shown to produce very consistent estimates of the time-varying reproduction number , defined as the average number of infections generated by a typical contagious individual if all conditions remained the same when tested on real COVID-19 counts from several countries at different phases of the pandemic . A documented Python toolbox is publicly available to reproduce all presented results .

title: RealPaver 1.1: A C++ Library for Constraint Programming over Numeric or Mixed Discrete-Continuous Domains
abstract: Constraint Programming ( CP ) is a paradigm for solving constraint satisfaction and optimization problems ( Rossi et al . , 2006 ) . Although CP mainly addresses combinatorial problems , CP can also handle continuous problems by approximating real numbers with intervals ( Benhamou & Granvilliers , 2006).RealPaver is a C++ library for CP over numeric or mixed discrete-continuous domains . Constraint Satisfaction Problems ( CSPs ) can be described either in C++ with the API or in a text file using the syntax of RealPaver specific language . Then , Constraint Satisfaction Problems ( CSPs ) can be solved using the API or using the CSP solver from the command line . the CSP solver is pre-configured , but various parameters can be modified in another text file .

title: Mechanized Metatheory and Certified Compilation for The Rocq Prover
abstract: The work presented in this habilitation thesis focuses on the verification of the logical core of the Rocq Prover , as well as the Rocq Prover original mechanism for compiling to usual functional programming languages . The objective of The work presented in this habilitation thesis is to obtain formal safety guarantees for the underlying theory of the Rocq Prover , for the implementation of the proof verifier for the underlying theory of the Rocq prover , and for the procedure of program extraction that enables the efficient execution of code verified by the Rocq Prover . The work presented in this habilitation thesis lies at the intersection of the meta-theory of type theory and the formal verification of type inference and compilation algorithms . We present MetaRocq , a formal development of specifications and verified programs , representing a large fragment of the Rocq Prover within the Rocq Prover . MetaRocq , a formal development of specifications and verified programs , representing a large fragment of Rocq within Rocq itself combines techniques for meta-programming and large-scale language metatheory proofs , as well as certified compilation techniques . We formally develop in the Rocq Prover a formal specification of the Rocq Prover type theory and Rocq 's type theory equivalent algorithmic variant , a typing algorithm that is correct and complete with respect to a formal specification of Rocq 's type theory and its equivalent algorithmic variant , a correct proof erasure algorithm , and a compilation chain from the Rocq Prover to OCaml that preserves the semantics of the source language . The results obtained here allow We to shift the paradigm regarding the safety of the results obtained in the proof assistant and produced by extraction , moving from a notion of a trusted code base — the current unverified kernel — to a notion of trusted theory base — the formal specification of Rocq 's type theory in the Rocq Prover that We have introduced . We discuss the impact and limitations of We work to obtain maximal correctness guarantees for the formal developments carried out in the proof assistant .

title: Deductively Verifying Functional Scalable Parallel Programs with Why3
abstract: Bulk Synchronous Parallelism ( BSP ) is a simple , yet realistic , model of scalable parallel computing . BSML is a pure functional library for the multi-paradigm language OCaml that embodies the principles of BSP . We propose a formalization of BSML primitives with WhyML , the specification language of Why3 and specify and prove the correctness of a set of parallel functions forming a standard library . We develop and verify the correctness of small BSML applications based on transformation theorems and the correspondence of a set of sequential functions on lists with algorithmic skeletons , i.e. functions implemented in parallel and manipulating distributed lists . Leveraging the Why3 feature generating the multi-paradigm language OCaml code from WhyML , the specification language of Why3 code , We experiment small BSML applications on parallel machines .

title: Sliding Mode Differentiator versus Sliding Mode Observer: the third way for particular cases
abstract: This paper highlights the comparison , in terms of advantages and drawbacks , between sliding mode differentiators and sliding mode observers . Beyond the case where the signal to be derived comes from an unknown system , for which a differentiator is obviously required , the choice between a differentiator and an observer is not so simple . This is even more true considering that , in information theory , any unused information is lost information , e.g. time scale , structural properties ... This issue has been addressed indirectly in Kalman filtering , where both the degree of confidence in the model and the quality of the signal are taken into account . However , Kalman filtering , where both the degree of confidence in the model and the quality of the signal are taken into account still relies on the availability of a model and on some assumptions of linearity . In this note , we focus on nonlinear settings and discuss several scenarios illustrating how differentiators and observers can be combined or selected to optimally exploit available information .

title: Enhanced Near-Field Coherent Source Localization via Alternating Oblique Projection and Polynomial Root-Finding
abstract: Near field ( NF ) source localization plays an essential role in the field of array signal processing . However , for coherent sources , conventional SSP and Topelitz matrix reconstruction algorithms can not be applied directly , because of the nonlinear phase variations in near-field source . Although probability model-based methods like enhanced maximum likelihood method ( EML ) can deal with coherent near-field sources , probability model-based methods like enhanced maximum likelihood method ( EML ) are fundamentally constrained by computational complexity or resolution performance . To address these issues , this paper proposes an enhanced method for near-field coherent source localization using a two-step alternating oblique projection ( AOP ) and polynomial root-finding , comprising a coarse localization stage followed by a fine estimation . Firstly , the coarse estimates of DOA and range parameters are derived by applying the anti-diagonal components of the covariance matrix through root-MUSIC and root-Capon , respectively , followed by an iterative refinement process that alternately applies the AOP method and root-finding to achieve fine estimation . The performance of an enhanced method for near-field coherent source localization using a two-step alternating oblique projection ( AOP ) and polynomial root-finding is validated through simulations . Results demonstrate that an enhanced method for near-field coherent source localization using a two-step alternating oblique projection ( AOP ) and polynomial root-finding achieves accurate localization of NF coherent sources with reduced computational complexity and improved resolution . The accuracy of an enhanced method for near-field coherent source localization using a two-step alternating oblique projection ( AOP ) and polynomial root-finding is also validated by a filed experiment .

title: On the Design of an Optimal Multi-Tone Jammer Against the Wiener Interpolation Filter
abstract: In the context of civilian and military communications , anti-jamming techniques are essential to ensure information integrity in the presence of malicious interference . A conventional time-domain approach relies on computing the Wiener interpolation filter to estimate and suppress the jamming waveform from the received samples . It is widely acknowledged that A conventional time-domain approach is effective for protecting wideband systems against narrowband interference . In this work , A conventional time-domain approach is questioned through the design of a [ EQUATION]-tone jamming waveform that is intrinsically difficult to estimate assuming a [ EQUATION]-tap Wiener interpolation filter . the design of a [ EQUATION]-tone jamming waveform that is intrinsically difficult to estimate assuming a [ EQUATION]-tap Wiener interpolation filter relies on an optimization procedure that maximizes the analytical Bayesian mean squared error associated with the jamming waveform estimate . Additionally , an analytical proof is provided showing that a multi-tone jamming waveform composed of [ EQUATION ] tones is sufficient to render a [ EQUATION]-tone jamming waveform that is intrinsically difficult to estimate assuming a [ EQUATION]-tap Wiener interpolation filter completely ineffective . The analytical results are validated through Monte Carlo simulations assuming both perfect knowledge and practical estimates of the correlation functions of the received signal .
keywords: narrowband interference multi tone jammer anti jamming techniques wiener filter wideband system dsss communication

title: Collaborative Action on Timing InterferenCes: Summary and Perspectives at Mid-term
abstract: CAOTIC is an ambitious initiative aimed at pooling and coordinating the efforts of major French research teams working on timing analysis of multicore real-time systems , with a focus on interference due to shared resources . The objective is to enable the efficient use of multicores in critical systems . Based on a better understanding of timing anomalies and interference , considering the specificities of applications ( structural properties and execution model ) , and revisiting the links between timing analysis and synthesis processes ( code generation , mapping , scheduling ) , CAOTIC target significant progresses in timing analysis models and techniques for critical systems , as well as in methodologies for timing analysis models and techniques for critical systems application in industry . In this paper , at project mid-term , CAOTIC show the progress of CAOTIC . CAOTIC also present some original work , about the use of a Tricore plaform and a Tricore plaform timing model , and discuss open questions and future work .

title: Interferences within a certifiable design methodology for high-performance multi-core platforms
abstract: The adoption of high-performance multi-core platforms in avionics and automotive systems introduces significant challenges in ensuring predictable execution , primarily due to shared resource interferences . Many existing approaches study interference from a single angle — for example , through hardware-level analysis or by monitoring software execution . However , no single abstraction level is sufficient on its own . Hardware behavior , program structure , and system configuration all interact , and a complete view is needed to understand where interferences come from and how to reduce interferences . In this paper , we present a methodology that brings together several tools that operate at different abstraction levels . At the lowest level , PHYLOG provides a formal model of the hardware and identifies possible interference channels using micro-architectural transactions . At the program level , machine learning analysis locates the exact parts of the code that are most sensitive to shared-resource contention . At the compilation level , MLIR-based transformations use this information to reshape memory access patterns and reduce pressure on shared resources . Finally , at the system level , Linux cgroups enforce static execution constraints to prevent highly interfering tasks from running together . The goal of a methodology that brings together several tools that operate at different abstraction levels is to reduce memory interference and improve the system 's predictability , thereby easing the certification process of multi-core systems in safety-critical domains .
keywords: memory interferences mlir framework machine learning linux cgroups
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: The role of tensegrity in the diversity of avian postural stability
abstract: Abstract Like humans , all birds adopt a strictly bipedal posture . However , unlike humans , birds have such good balance that birds can sleep while standing up , which must require minimal energy . have makes birds an interesting model for studying bipedalism in robotics . In this study , we examine balance and postural stability via a tensegrity system ( assembly in parallel of rigid bodies and cables ) . To test this hypothesis , we created mathematical models based on anatomical observations of the legs of various birds ( zebra finch , little egret , mallard and military macaw ) to investigate different configurations . Building on a previous model , we demonstrate that tensegrity systems can achieve passive stability under simplified loading . Here , we aim to establish whether a previous model can be generalized , to determine stability , and to identify the impact of certain kinematic , dynamic and material parameters . we results enabled we to identify the parameters that allow a previous model to be generalized . we determined that adding two cables corresponding to tendinous and muscular sets generalizes a previous model to a varied range of configurations and exploits the rear part of the foot when present . These findings offer new insights into avian bipedalism and could inspire the design of bipedal robots with passive stability for greater autonomy .

title: ChatGPT, a colonialist agent of lifeworlds: A Habermassian analysis of conversations
abstract: Conversational generative AI-based systems ( CGAIS ) , like ChatGPT , seem capable of taking part in conversations with such fluidity that we may not distinguish Conversational generative AI-based systems ( CGAIS ) from a human . The global integration of CGAIS , however , bears various risks , including the one of colonizing the social through data . In this article , we are interested in the colonization of a new territory : that of conversations . We therefore investigate the nature of conversations individuals have with these technologies . Following Habermas , the realm of the communicative is what enables to construct a common social world , a lifeworld . Conflating the communicative and the instrumental threatens lifeworld construction and more broadly our democracy . We explore CGAIS technical and conceptual properties , and show that CGAIS do not support communicative action . Rather , CGAIS should remain confined to the realm of instrumental action . Yet , as CGAIS give the impression to belong to the realm of the communicative , we conceptualize CGAIS as colonialist agents . Notably , CGAIS are imperialist agents because CGAIS are increasingly used for all types of activities at work and in the private and public spheres . used reduces the space for communicative action . In addition , CGAIS are derealization agents as CGAIS distort conversation , by giving the illusion of communicative action . As a result , CGAIS threaten the co-construction of a common lifeworld , that forms the basis of our democratic societies .
keywords: conversational generative ai systems communicative action colonialist agent lifeworld derealization habermassian validity claims

title: Design and Voltage-Controlled Reconfigurability of an Interdigital Bandpass Filter
abstract: This paper presents the design of a highly reconfigurable interdigital bandpass filter ( BPF ) developed through a three-stage design approach . In the first stage , the influence of four low-loss dielectric substrates on the filter response is systematically analyzed to identify the optimal configuration . The selected substrate demonstrates excellent performance , achieving an input return loss of −38 dB , an insertion loss of −0.9 dB at 4.30 GHz , and a wide passband corresponding to a bandwidth ( BW ) of 2.20 GHz . In the second stage , two variable capacitors were incorporated into the baseline geometry , enabling manual tuning of the center frequency ( f0 ) from 5.10 to 6.34 GHz , with ( S11 ) better than −25 dB and ( S12 ) close to −0.60 dB. In the final stage , two variable capacitors were replaced by SMV1413 varactor diodes , transforming the design of a highly reconfigurable interdigital bandpass filter ( BPF ) developed through a three-stage design approach into a fully voltage-controlled tunable filter . a fully voltage-controlled tunable filter provides continuous frequency agility from 4.70 to 5 GHz without modifying the physical structure , while achieving ( S11 ) levels down to −40 dB and insertion loss as low as −0.7 dB. the design of a highly reconfigurable interdigital bandpass filter ( BPF ) developed through a three-stage design approach offers a compact , low-loss , and electrically reconfigurable solution , making the design of a highly reconfigurable interdigital bandpass filter ( BPF ) developed through a three-stage design approach a promising solution for next-generation RF front-ends , adaptive wireless systems , and cognitive radio applications . Two independent Electromagnetic solvers ( EM ) were employed to validate a fully voltage-controlled tunable filter performance : Two independent Electromagnetic solvers ( EM ) . The close agreement between the results produced by Two independent Electromagnetic solvers ( EM ) confirms the accuracy and robustness of the design of a highly reconfigurable interdigital bandpass filter ( BPF ) developed through a three-stage design approach .

title: Cramér–Rao bound analysis of nested arrays under impulsive noise with coarrays and FLOSs
abstract: Nested arrays are extensively employed in array signal processing to augment the degrees of freedom and enhance estimation precision , and the Cramér – Rao Bound ( CRB ) for nested arrays in a Gaussian noise environment has been established . Nevertheless , in a practical wireless communication environment , noise usually exhibits an impulsive characteristic . The impulsive noise applied in a uniform linear array ( ULA ) has been extensively studied in the literature , but only closed-form expressions of CRB with Cauchy and Gaussian noise distributions are given . Although nested arrays have garnered significant attention recently , research on the CRB under impulsive noise conditions remains scarce . In this paper , we provide the CRB expression for direction of arrival ( DOA ) estimation with nested arrays in an impulsive noise environment , which indicates that CRB is formulated in terms of the fractional low-order statistics ( FLOSs ) of received data . Moreover , we also calculate the CRB results for different FLOSs as well as various sparse arrays and validate that the derived CRB makes an important contribution to the performance analysis of sparse arrays in impulsive noise .
keywords: sparse arrays doa fractional low order statistics floss cramér–rao bound crb coarrays

title: Programmable wave-domain computing in wireless communications
abstract: Future wireless networks must achieve large gains in data rate , energy efficiency and latency while integrating sensing and computation . Programmable wave-domain computing ( pWDC ) , which processes signals directly through reconfigurable wavematter interactions , offers a way to offload part of this burden from electronic processors . In this Perspective , we review historical roots and recent work on Programmable wave-domain computing ( pWDC ) , which processes signals directly through reconfigurable wavematter interactions , and discuss Programmable wave-domain computing ( pWDC ) , which processes signals directly through reconfigurable wavematter interactions , promise and challenges . we focus on three challenges : prototype-aware runtime optimization of Programmable wave-domain computing ( pWDC ) , which processes signals directly through reconfigurable wavematter interactions , hardware , enriching functionalities beyond linear continuouswave operation , and integrating Programmable wave-domain computing ( pWDC ) , which processes signals directly through reconfigurable wavematter interactions , into network-level resource management . Finally , we outline open questions regarding expressivity , practicality , and security that will arise in the transition of Programmable wave-domain computing ( pWDC ) , which processes signals directly through reconfigurable wavematter interactions , to real-life deployment in future wireless infrastructures .

title: Evaluating the sustainability of pv technologies and their cooling systems: a life cycle assessment review
abstract: Life cycle environmental consequences of photovoltaic systems , from raw material extraction to end-of-life ( EoL ) management , have attracted more interest in recent years . Life Cycle Assessment ( LCA ) is a vital tool to analyze the sustainability of PV panels based on parameters such as energy payback time ( EPBT ) , greenhouse gas emissions ( GHG ) , and cumulative energy demand ( CED ) . Several studies have considered standalone PV technologies , while the environmental ramifications of integrating cooling systems have not been adequately investigated , even with cooling systems increasing relevance in enhancing PV efficiency and lifespan . This review fills the identified gap by systematically assessing the life cycle performance of the PV technologies considered here , alongside several cooling methods-air-based , liquid-based , phase change materials ( PCM ) , radiative , and hybrid systems-for their combined performance , economic , and environmental trade-offs . Results show that Cadmium Telluride and Copper Indium Gallium Selenide technologies exhibit low energy payback times and global warming potential ( GWP ) . Water-based cooling shows the lowest GWP , although water use remains a cause for concern . PCM cooling provides long-term energy savings but comes with recyclability issues . High-value EoL management with recycling would lower GWP . With Results , This review provides a common framework for assessing the PV technologies considered here and also provides a case of the need for consolidated datasets and harmonized methodologies . Future research needs to enhance the LCA databases relating to PV cooling systems and establish policy-driven steps to support circularity and sustainable pathways for PV technology .

title: Model-based learning for high-dimensional wireless systems
abstract: The field of wireless communications has traditionally relied on signal processing techniques , based on mathematical models , to describe and optimize wireless transmission of information . When the assumptions underlying mathematical models are not fully met , conventional methods often yield suboptimal performance . Recently , machine learning methods have been used to address this issue , owing to machine learning methods strong adaptation capabilities . However , machine learning methods also introduce significant challenges in terms of interpretability and complexity . This thesis focuses on the use of the model-based machine learning paradigm in wireless communication or sensing systems . the model-based machine learning paradigm leverages mathematical models used in classical signal processing approaches to structure , initialize , or optimize learning methods , thereby combining the structure and interpretability of classical methods with the adaptability of machine learning . the model-based machine learning paradigm is studied through three specific use cases : location-to-channel mapping learning , hardware impairments compensation , and channel compression .

title: Gradient-based NMR pulse sequences for real-time reaction monitoring
abstract: Real-time reaction monitoring requires NMR methods that meet several stringent requirements . NMR spectra used for reaction monitoring need to be sensitive , well resolved , solvent-suppressed , and compatible with flow , and the experimental duration must match the timescale of the monitored reaction . Therefore , most NMR reaction monitoring studies rely on one-dimensional experiments which are rapid and simple , but are often limited by overlap between multiple peaks from reactants and products . While the NMR toolbox offers a great diversity of 1D and 2D experiments that can resolve individual components from complex mixtures , 1D and 2D experiments that can resolve individual components from complex mixtures are often time-consuming and not compatible with flow . We have developed and optimized a set of NMR experiments that make it possible to analyse complex reacting mixtures in real time . Most of a set of NMR experiments that make it possible to analyse complex reacting mixtures in real time rely on spatially-encoded pulse sequences that combine frequency-swept pulses with magnetic field gradients . a set of NMR experiments that make it possible to analyse complex reacting mixtures in real time include ultrafast 2D NMR methods,1 whose application to reacting mixtures under flow conditions was optimized by using gradients orthogonal to the sample flow combined with solvent-suppression schemes.2 We successfully applied ultrafast 2D NMR methods,1 whose application to reacting mixtures under flow conditions was optimized by using gradients orthogonal to the sample flow combined with solvent-suppression schemes.2 to online and in-line reaction monitoring , both at high magnetic field and on benchtop NMR spectrometers.3,4,5 Other recent developments include pure-shift NMR experiments in continuous flow,6 as well as time-resolved diffusion NMR experiments that provide clean , individual spectra of newly formed compounds in reacting mixtures.7 We will describe a set of NMR experiments that make it possible to analyse complex reacting mixtures in real time , and a set of NMR experiments that make it possible to analyse complex reacting mixtures in real time application to the online study of chemical reactions and to the in-line optimization of flow chemistry processes . The integration of a set of NMR experiments that make it possible to analyse complex reacting mixtures in real time into autonomous flow chemistry settings also offers an interesting perspective.8 1 . title: Paying for Training to Make Training Pay Off: Evidence From France
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of increased financial compensation during training on jobseekers ' labor market outcomes . We exploit a reform implemented in France in May 2021 that raised training allowances exclusively for non-­ recipients of unemployment benefits . Using administrative longitudinal data , We compare the trajectories of trainees affected and unaffected by a reform implemented in France in May 2021 that raised training allowances exclusively for non-­ recipients of unemployment benefits . We empirical strategy combines a synthetic triple-­ difference estimator with an event-­ study framework . We find no evidence that a reform implemented in France in May 2021 that raised training allowances exclusively for non-­ recipients of unemployment benefits increased employment rates within 24 months of training entry , but a reform implemented in France in May 2021 that raised training allowances exclusively for non-­ recipients of unemployment benefits did enhance job quality , improving both stability and alignment with the training field .
labels: Preparation for New Jobs in the Future Industry

title: Quantization-aware training: a tradeoff between training and fine-tuning for domain-specific language models
abstract: Quantization is a widely adopted technique to reduce memory footprint and computational cost in neural networks . While quantizing pre-trained models is effective , retraining is often required for extreme quantization formats . Fine-tuning , on the other hand , enables the adaptation of general-purpose models to specific domains , but quantization can significantly degrade general-purpose models performance . In this work , we investigate the training cost of finetuned and quantized language models . By formalizing the computational trade-off between domain adaptation and fine-tuning , we demonstrate that domain-specialized checkpoints exhibit greater robustness to quantization noise . we findings establish a viable blueprint for deploying high-performance biomedical NLP models in resource-constrained , edge environments .

title: Identification of rare missense variants reducing cathepsin O secretion in families with intracranial aneurysm
abstract: AimsIntracranial aneurysm ( IA ) is a common cerebrovascular abnormality characterized by localized dilation and wall thinning in cerebral arteries , which can rupture and lead to fatal subarachnoid haemorrhage . Although genetic factors can contribute to IA , the genetic pre-disposition of IA is largely unknown . This study aims to identify rare functional variants associated with IA in families with multiple affected subjects and explore rare functional variants associated with IA in families with multiple affected subjects impact on IA pathophysiology . Methods and resultsBy combining whole-exome sequencing and identity-by-descent analyses , we have identified two rare missense variants in the CTSO gene associated to IA in two large families with multiple affected subjects . we found that the cysteine-type papain-like cathepsin O ( CTSO ) encoded by CTSO is expressed in the circle of Willis of mice and in the wall of human IA domes . Stretching of vascular smooth muscle cells ( VSMC ) induced CTSO secretion . CTSO controls VSMC migration and adhesion to the extracellular matrix , and directly interacts with fibronectin ( FN ) . CTSO depletion , or expression of two rare missense variants in the CTSO gene associated to IA in two large families with multiple affected subjects , increased the amount of fibronectin ( FN ) . Moreover , CTSO depletion augmented VSMC stiffness , which was reduced by the addition of exogenous CTSO.ConclusionCollectively , we findings identify CTSO as a potential new player in arterial remodelling , regulating fibronectin ( FN ) deposition and VSMC function , supporting the causal role of rare coding CTSO variants in familial forms of IA .

title: Training for Mixed-Precision Integer Weights, Activations and Embeddings in BERT
abstract: Pre-trained language models ( LMs ) deliver strong performance across a wide range of Natural Language Processing ( NLP ) tasks but remain costly to deploy on embedded devices due to Pre-trained language models ( LMs ) high memory and compute requirements . A widely used strategy for adapting LMs to resource-constrained devices is aggressive quantization . At low bit-widths , mixed-precision schemes , where different components of the model use different numerical precisions , offer an effective balance between compression and accuracy . In this work , we evaluate the impact of mixed-precision quantization for inference on the BERT language model . Unlike prior studies that often overlook activation quantization , evaluate systematically explores mixed-precision configurations for both weights and activations . we also examine the effects of quantizing the embedding layer , which is commonly limited to token-weight quantization . Evaluated on the SQuAD and GLUE benchmarks , we approach achieves substantial reductions in memory and computational cost without sacrificing accuracy .

title: An Adaptive Multiphase Finite Element Framework for Simulating Two-Dimensional Rotational Molding
abstract: Rotational molding , also known as rotomolding , is a widely used manufacturing process for composite tank liners . Developing Rotational molding , also known as rotomolding to obtain high-quality liners is usually a long and delicate step . The implementation of numerical simulation can facilitate and expedite Developing . It is challenging to obtain information about polymer movement through experimental methods . In this paper , we present a two-dimensional thermo-fluid simulation of Rotational molding , also known as rotomolding using the immersed boundary approach with the level-set technique . Numerical simulation using the Eulerian approach with the finite element method with anisotropic mesh refinement and the immersed boundary approach has proven to be a powerful tool for analyzing and optimizing the molding processes with the help of implicit boundary and adaptive anisotropic meshing techniques . the finite element method is a valuable tool that allows us to combine several physical elements . the finite element method enables us to identify critical process variables and optimize design choices . To verify we methodology , we first simulated a 2D crosssection of the mold by incorporating a two-phase flow problem involving the polymer / air interface .

title: Parallel Robot with Proprioceptive Actuation for Low-Impedance Sensorless pHRI
abstract: This paper presents a kinematically redundant 9-DoF parallel robot engineered for seamless , sensorless physical humanrobot interaction . a kinematically redundant 9-DoF parallel robot engineered for seamless , sensorless physical humanrobot interaction features three identical 3-DoF RU/2-RUS legs that connect a reconfigurable platform to the base via spherical joints . By configuring all actuators on the base , a kinematically redundant 9-DoF parallel robot engineered for seamless , sensorless physical humanrobot interaction achieves significantly lower moving mass and inertia . By employing backdrivable direct-drive motors , a kinematically redundant 9-DoF parallel robot engineered for seamless , sensorless physical humanrobot interaction realizes proprioceptive actuation , enabling an intuitive , low-impedance , and high-bandwidth interaction . An impedance control strategy is developed on SE(3 ) × R 3 , and a stability analysis using singular perturbation theory highlights the crucial role of actuator dynamics and thus the significance of the choice of the actuation strategy . Experimental results confirm a kinematically redundant 9-DoF parallel robot engineered for seamless , sensorless physical humanrobot interaction stability , extended workspace , and effective human-robot interaction performance .

title: Effect of a Surficial Porous Brittle Layer on the Dynamics and Equilibrium Thickness of Europa’s Ice Shell
abstract: Abstract Tectonic and cryovolcanic features on Europa suggest a dynamically active ice shell with a highly deformable near-surface brittle layer . Shell thickness estimates based on geological interpretation and thermal modeling vary from 10 km to more than 30 km . The surface activity is probably caused by Jupiter ’s tidal forces , whose interplay with heat transfer processes still remains poorly understood . We modeled the dynamics and heat transfer of a dynamically active ice shell with a highly deformable near-surface brittle layer , consistently including a variety of ice / ocean crystallization / melting processes and the effect of a superficial brittle porous layer . For tidal heat production corresponding to current orbital eccentricity , We obtained equilibrium thicknesses between 20 and 80 km depending on the assumed reference viscosity values . We show that the presence of a 1–2 km surficial porous layer reduces the average equilibrium thickness by 5–20 km while simultaneously enhancing the convective dynamics , resulting in much steeper near-surface thermal gradients and higher surface heat flux . The 240 K isotherm is predicted to shift closer to the surface , reaching depths of 10–15 km in the presence of a surficial porous layer , favoring the possible generation of eutectic brines at shallow depths and lithospheric breakups . For highly convecting models , the depth of The 240 K isotherm can be as shallow as 3–4 km , with surface heat flux exceeding 70 mW m −2 . We anticipate that any lateral variation in the porous layer thickness should result in significant variations in the overall a dynamically active ice shell with a highly deformable near-surface brittle layer thickness and convective dynamics , which could be revealed by future measurements by Europa Clipper and JUICE .

title: TPUTrap: Hardware-Based USB Man-in-the-Middle Attack on Coral Edge TPU
abstract: AI-based hardware accelerators , such as the Coral USB Accelerator , enable the use of AI in embedded systems without relying on the cloud , offering advantages like low latency , reduced power consumption , and enhanced privacy . the Coral USB Accelerator connects to the host via USB , which lacks encryption and authentication checks , raising security concerns in critical applications . This paper demonstrates a man-in-the-middle attack on the Coral USB Accelerator USB interface , utilizing a Raspberry Pi 5 and a USB Proxy for real-time interception and manipulation of USB traffic . a man-in-the-middle attack on the Coral USB Accelerator 's USB interface successfully exfiltrated sensitive data and caused misclassification . Despite an added latency overhead , all attacks achieved 100 % success , underscoring the need to address this security issue .

title: Integrating ethical, societal and environmental issues into algorithm design courses
abstract: This document , intended for computer science teachers , describes a case study that puts into practice a questioning of ethical , societal and environmental issues when designing or implementing a decision support system . a case study that puts into practice a questioning of ethical , societal and environmental issues when designing or implementing a decision support system is based on a very popular application , namely road navigation software that informs users of real-time traffic conditions and suggests routes between a starting point and a destination , taking real-time traffic conditions into account ( such as Waze ) . The approach proposes to intertwine technical considerations ( optimal path algorithms , data needed for location , etc . ) with a broader view of the ethical , environmental and societal issues raised by the tools studied . Based on the authors ' experience conducting sessions with students over several years , This document , intended for computer science teachers discusses the context of such a study , suggests teaching resources for implementing such a study , describes ways to structure discussions , and shares scenarios in different teaching contexts .

title: In vivo OCT angiography of mouse ovary
abstract: The ovary undergoes cyclic development for follicle formation and regression , a hormonally regulated process that is key to pregnancy . Angiogenesis and vascular remodeling play critical roles in cyclic development for follicle formation and regression , a hormonally regulated process that is key to pregnancy , but a detailed and dynamic follicle-vascular relationship remains to be elucidated . Simultaneous imaging of the ovarian vascular network and follicular structure is essential for studying a detailed and dynamic follicle-vascular relationship , and studies have largely relied on fluorescence imaging with optically cleared ovary samples from the mouse model . The lack of high-resolution in vivo imaging to probe the mouse model is a major hurdle for studying the dynamic interaction between vasculature and follicles under physiological conditions . Here , we addressed a major hurdle for studying the dynamic interaction between vasculature and follicles under physiological conditions by establishing in vivo angiography of the mouse model with optical coherence tomography and an intravital window . establishing opens the possibility to study a detailed and dynamic follicle-vascular relationship in vivo in the mouse model .

title: Microwave-assisted desorption of CO<sub>2</sub> from ethanolamine solvent in a porous hollow fiber membrane - numerical modeling
abstract: In our previous work , microwave regeneration of 30 wt . % ethanolamine solvents in a hollow fiber gas-liquid contactor was studied . In microwave regeneration of 30 wt . % ethanolamine solvents in a hollow fiber gas-liquid contactor , the solvent was heated by microwaves as the solvent traversed a microwave applicator while passing through the lumen of a hollow fiber gas-liquid contactor . Experimental results do not provide insight into the operation of microwave regeneration . The aim of studied is therefore to develop a model to simulate the microwave solvent regeneration in the single fiber system . The numerical approach is based on coupling 3D microwave heating of solvent flow , and 1D chemical desorption of CO2 applicable to non-isothermal conditions along a hollow fiber gas-liquid contactor . The numerical approach was successful in reproducing with reasonable accuracy the global desorption data from the regeneration experiments , assuming a low wetting fraction of the membrane . The effects of operating conditions were explored : results show that increasing the solvent flow rates induces higher temperature gradients at the boundary of the fiber lumen thus increasing desorption rates . It has been found that increased fiber radius leads to better desorption rates at the expense of lowering the interfacial surface density . On another note , numerical results show that isothermal regeneration performs better than microwave mode although microwave mode is able to outperform where hotspots persist along a hollow fiber gas-liquid contactor . With regards to flow configurations during microwave regeneration , counter-current mode performed better than co-current one : the sweeping gas in counter-current mode passes from the hot solvent side to the cold solvent side which encourages reabsorption of the desorbed CO2 .
