title: Laser based surface texturing and PA6 powder interlayering for joining enhancement of DP600/PA6GF47 hybrid joints via induction welding
abstract: This study investigates a novel approach combining laser surface microtexturing with PA6 powder interlayering to enhance the joining performance of DP600 steel / PA6GF47 thermoplastic composite hybrid joints via induction welding . Four joining conditions were evaluated : no texture-no powder ( NT-NP ) , no texture-powder ( NT-P ) , texture-no powder ( T-NP ) , and texture-powder ( T-P ) . Laser texturing parameters were optimized to create controlled micro-groove patterns with uniform depth and periodicity on DP600 steel surface . A thin PA6 powder layer was applied at the bonding interface prior to induction welding . Mechanical testing revealed that a novel approach combining laser surface microtexturing with PA6 powder interlayering to enhance the joining performance of DP600 steel / PA6GF47 thermoplastic composite hybrid joints via induction welding achieved the highest shear strength of 19,5 MPa , representing a 170 % improvement over untreated joints ( 7,2 MPa ) . Microscopic analysis demonstrated that the synergistic effect of laser texturing and powder interlayering promotes complete polymer infiltration into surface microstructures , creating robust mechanical interlocking . Thermal analysis confirmed optimal processing temperatures for PA6 melting without degradation . The fracture mode shifted from interfacial failure to mixed-mode failure with fibre pull-out , indicating superior metal-composite bonding . a novel approach combining laser surface microtexturing with PA6 powder interlayering to enhance the joining performance of DP600 steel / PA6GF47 thermoplastic composite hybrid joints via induction welding offers a promising solution for lightweight structural assemblies in automotive and aerospace applications .

title: HT-NoC: A Throughput Adaptive Multi Dataflow Network on Chip for AI Accelerators
abstract: Communication often represents a critical bottleneck in the execution of Deep Neural Networks ( DNNs ) on Artificial Intelligence ( AI ) accelerators . To improve communication efficiency , we propose HT-NoC ( High Throughput Network-on-Chip ) , a dynamically reconfigurable NoC that adapts its throughput to optimize internal resource utilization , thereby enabling the simultaneous transmission of more packets . Extensive evaluations across diverse DNN layers demonstrate that its consistently outperforms the baseline non reconfigurable mesh NoC. Specifically , its accelerates input parameter propagation by up to 4× in Fully Connected ( FC ) and Pointwise ( PW ) layers , while reducing dynamic energy by 2.6×. For Convolutional ( CONV ) and Depthwise ( DEPTH ) layers , its achieves speedups of up to 2.3× and energy savings of 2.15×. Finally , when integrated into an AI dataflow accelerator , its delivers a 3.2× speedup over Systolic Array ( SA ) based accelerators in executing Feed Forward Network ( FFN ) blocks of Transformers . Importantly , these performance and energy improvements are achieved with minimal area , latency , and energy overhead introduced by the reconfiguration mechanism .

title: Decentralized multi-agent multi-armed bandits for smart electric vehicles charging
abstract: Smart charging of electrical vehicles can help in avoiding congestion and peak load demands in an electrical distribution network . On the consumer 's side , the advantage lies in minimizing the daily charging cost . the consumer 's may also benefit from cheap photovoltaic electricity from local sources and therefore reduce the consumer 's environmental impact . However , cheap photovoltaic electricity from local sources is variable and uncertain . In many research works , this has been formulated and solved as a centralized or hierarchical optimization problem . However , such systems may suffer from lack of scalability , single point of failures , and privacy breaches . We propose a fully decentralized and fair multi-agent system combined with reinforcement learning called " Decentralised multi-armed bandit ( 2-armed bandit ) based on Thompson sampling"(D-MAB2AB-TS ) to control the charging of electrical vehicles under uncertainties . this is formulated as a two-armed bandit ( charging or not ) for each instant . The proposed algorithm , based on Thompson Sampling , takes into account the uncertainties in the choice of arms combination of other players . The proposed algorithm , based on Thompson Sampling finds the best combination of arms to play with a computational complexity O(m ) linear with the number of arms . The proposed algorithm , based on Thompson Sampling is also model-free , as The proposed algorithm , based on Thompson Sampling does not assume the model of the environment to be perfectly known , which is a common assumption in many of the existing centralized optimization strategies for smart charging .
keywords: multi armed bandits decentralized smart charging thompson sampling

title: DS-Mamba: Dynamic snake visual state space model for vessel segmentation
abstract: Accurately segmenting vascular networks holds significant clinical implications for disease diagnosis and analysis . However , the intrinsically elongated , serpentine , and multi-scale nature of vascular networks poses a significant challenge , with existing methods often struggling to preserve both global connectivity and local morphological fidelity . To address this challenge , we propose a novel deep-learning architecture , termed Dynamic Snake Mamba ( DS-Mamba ) , inspired by the sinuous morphology of vessels . a novel deep-learning architecture , termed Dynamic Snake Mamba ( DS-Mamba ) , inspired by the sinuous morphology of vessels first leverages a Mamba backbone , composed of Residual Visual State Space ( ResVSS ) blocks , to establish a topologically coherent global representation of the vascular network . Subsequently , Dynamic Snake Convolutions ( DSC ) are strategically embedded to enhance the feature extraction of local serpentine details . To further improve a novel deep-learning architecture , termed Dynamic Snake Mamba ( DS-Mamba ) , inspired by the sinuous morphology of vessels capabilities , a novel deep-learning architecture , termed Dynamic Snake Mamba ( DS-Mamba ) , inspired by the sinuous morphology of vessels incorporates three key components : ( 1 ) a Multi-scale Information Mamba Fusion ( MIMF ) mechanism that aggregates features from all encoder stages ; ( 2 ) a Snake Tokenized Kolmogorov-Arnold Network ( STK ) at the bottleneck to manage complex feature interactions ; and ( 3 ) Global-Local Information Fusion ( GLIF ) blocks that merge the global context with serpentine details . The efficacy of a novel deep-learning architecture , termed Dynamic Snake Mamba ( DS-Mamba ) , inspired by the sinuous morphology of vessels was validated through comprehensive experiments on eight diverse tubular structure datasets . Results demonstrate that we approach not only achieves state-of-the-art performance in connectivity and morphological fidelity but also exhibits superior accuracy in segmenting thin , low-contrast vessels and robust resilience against high-intensity image noise . Furthermore , rigorous capacity-controlled ablation studies confirm that the performance gains stem from the synergistic architectural design rather than parameter scaling . Finally , inference speed analysis verifies a novel deep-learning architecture , termed Dynamic Snake Mamba ( DS-Mamba ) , inspired by the sinuous morphology of vessels feasibility for real-time clinical applications .

title: Ambiguity-Aware Segmented Estimation of Mutual Coupling in Large RIS: Algorithm and Experimental Validation
abstract: Optimizing a real-life RIS-parametrized wireless channel with a physics-consistent multiport-network model necessitates prior remote estimation of the mutual coupling ( MC ) between RIS elements . The number of MC parameters grows quadratically with the number of RIS elements , posing scalability challenges . Because of inevitable ambiguities , independently estimated segments of the MC matrix can not be easily stitched together . Here , by carefully handling inevitable ambiguities , we achieve a separation of the full estimation problem into three sequentially treated sets of smaller problems . We partition RIS elements into groups . First , we estimate the MC for one group as well as the characteristics of the available loads . Second , we separately estimate the MC for each of the remaining groups , in each case with partial overlap with an already characterized group . Third , we separately estimate the MC between each distinct pair of groups . Full parallelization is feasible within the second and third sets of problems , and the third set of problems can furthermore benefit from efficient initialization . We experimentally validate We algorithm for a 4 × 4 MIMO channel parametrized by a 100-element RIS inside a rich-scattering environment . We experimentally calibrated 5867-parameter multiport-network model achieves an accuracy of 40.5 dB , whereas benchmark models with limited or no MC awareness only reach 16.9 dB and 13.8 dB , respectively . Based on Our experimentally calibrated 5867-parameter multiport-network model , We optimize a 100-element RIS for five wireless performance indicators . Experimental measurements with the optimized RIS configurations demonstrate only moderate benefits of MC awareness in RIS optimization in terms of the achieved performance . However , We observe that limited or no MC awareness markedly erodes the reliability of model-based predictions of the expected performance .

title: Design, Equivalent Circuit Analysis, and Verification of A 400-Cell Broadband Dual-Polarized Reconfigurable Transmit-Array at Ka-Band
abstract: A broadband 1-bit reconfigurable transmit-array ( TA ) featuring independent dual-polarized beam-scanning capability is reported at Ka-band . Bandwidth enhanced transmissive elements based on the current reversed mechanism are developed , which are optimized based on an equivalent circuit model . Bandwidth enhanced transmissive elements based on the current reversed mechanism are further miniaturized and aligned orthogonally in an end-to-middle scheme for dual-polarized operation . A broadband 1-bit reconfigurable transmit-array ( TA ) featuring independent dual-polarized beam-scanning capability is fabricated and measured . A broadband 1-bit reconfigurable transmit-array ( TA ) featuring independent dual-polarized beam-scanning capability exhibits a peak gain of 24.8 dBi , a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 18 % , as well as an aperture efficiency of 26 % . Moreover , A broadband 1-bit reconfigurable transmit-array ( TA ) featuring independent dual-polarized beam-scanning capability supports sum beams scanning up to 60 ° and difference beams steering up to 50 ° . A broadband 1-bit reconfigurable transmit-array ( TA ) featuring independent dual-polarized beam-scanning capability can be a promising candidate for millimeter-wave communication and radar systems .

title: Reproduction of Data-Driven Identification on real experimental data
abstract: This document extends the work developed in the PhD thesis of Hachem ( 2025 ) through the application of the recommended DDI workflow to real experimental full-field measurements .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: One-sided truncated EWMA control charts for monitoring two-parameter exponential distributed data
abstract: The two-parameter exponential distribution offers greater flexibility and suitability than the classical exponential distribution with a single scale parameter for modelling product lifetimes in reliability analysis and inventory management . Unlike existing schemes designed based on order statistics , new one-sided EWMA schemes using the truncation method are developed in this paper to monitor data following a two-parameter exponential distribution with sample sizes n = 1 as well as n > 1 , indifferently . Furthermore , detailed instructions for constructing the Markov chain model and the Monte Carlo simulation are provided to investigate the detecting properties of the recommended schemes , along with cross-validation to verify the recommended schemes effectiveness . Meanwhile , detecting performance comparisons between the proposed lower-sided scheme and the latest relevant scheme are carried out . The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed chart is not only superior to the comparative chart in monitoring efficiency and the proposed chart resistance to biases in average run length ( ARL ) and average time to signal ( ATS ) , but the proposed chart is also more straightforward and accessible for practitioners . Finally , two illustrative examples are presented to demonstrate the implementation of the recommended schemes .

title: Ising superconductivity in noncentrosymmetric bulk NbSe2
abstract: Ising superconductivity allows in-plane upper critical magnetic fields to vastly surpass Pauli limit by locking the antiparallel electron spins of Cooper pairs in the out-of-plane direction . Ising superconductivity was first explicitly demonstrated in fully two-dimensional monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides with large spin-orbit coupling and broken inversion symmetry . Since then , several studies have shown that Ising superconductivity can be present in layered bulk materials , too . In our previous study , our have clarified the underlying microscopic mechanism of Ising superconductivity in bulk , based on a reduced electronic coupling between superconducting layers due to intercalation by insulating layers and restricted inversion symmetry . But earlier studies suggest that in some transition metal dichalcogenide polytypes Pauli limit is violated even without intercalation . Here , using heat capacity measurements our unambiguously demonstrate , that the pristine noncentrosymmetric bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 polytype significantly violates Pauli limit . The band structure parameters obtained from ab initio calculations using the experimentally determined crystal structure are used in the theoretical model which provides the microscopic mechanism of the Ising protection based solely on broken inversion symmetry .

title: Better understanding of the maleinization of oils using model fatty compounds: Insights from NMR, SEC, and HRMS analyses
abstract: The chemical modification of vegetable oils through maleinization reaction offers a promising route to sustainable bio-based materials for diverse industrial applications . However , the underlying mechanisms of The chemical modification of vegetable oils through maleinization reaction such as the ene , Diels-Alder , and radical pathways , remain insufficiently understood , limiting process optimization and broader adoption . In this study , we employed a model compound approach using methyl oleate ( C18:1 ) , methyl linoleate ( C18:2 ) , and their corresponding triglycerides to systematically investigate The chemical modification of vegetable oils through maleinization reaction under controlled conditions . Advanced analytical techniques , including nuclear magnetic resonance ( NMR ) spectroscopy , size-exclusion chromatography ( SEC ) , and Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry ( FT-ICR MS ) were performed to elucidate reaction mechanisms , quantify product distributions ( when possible ) , and assess structural modifications . we results demonstrated that the ene reaction is the predominant pathway for C18:1 substrates while radical mechanisms contribute to minor products . The Diels-Alder cycloaddition is negligible under the studied conditions . The extent of maleinization increases with maleic anhydride ( MA ) equivalents , as confirmed by quantitative 13C NMR and FT-ICR MS analyses while size-exclusion chromatography ( SEC reveals some polymerization .

title: Influence of grain size distribution type on statistical moments of ultrasonic attenuations and phase velocities in random polycrystals
abstract: This study investigates the sensitivity of ultrasonic phase velocity and attenuation statistics to grain size distribution types , specifically monomodal and bimodal , in cubic finite-sized polycrystals with identical overall arithmetic or volumetric grain size statistics . A large ensemble of synthetic polycrystalline microstructures was generated , and A large ensemble of synthetic polycrystalline microstructures ultrasonic responses were computed using a modified spectral function method . a modified spectral function method enables estimation of both effective phase velocities and attenuation coefficients while rigorously accounting for finite specimen dimensions and statistical variabilities across different samples . When samples share identical grain size statistics based on arithmetic averages , bimodal and monomodal specimens exhibit pronounced differences in the first-order statistical moments of ultrasonic attenuation , while bimodal and monomodal specimens mean phase velocities remain virtually similar . In contrast , the second-order statistical moments of the phase velocities exhibit more pronounced differences , primarily influenced by the number of grains interacting with the waves . Typically , the bimodal sample shows intermediate standard deviations of the ultrasonic phase velocities , while monomodal samples with matching volumetric and arithmetic grain size statistics yield the highest and lowest variabilities , respectively . These findings suggest that the statistical analysis of ultrasonic responses offers a promising non-destructive methodology for identifying subtle microstructural variations , particularly higher-order characteristics beyond the average grain size , such as the shape of the grain size distribution .

title: Multi-period replenishment planning with supplier assignment under a dynamic demand and stochastic lead-times
abstract: We consider a multi-period replenishment planning problem with dynamic demand and multiple suppliers . Each supplier has Each supplier own selling price and random lead time . The objective is to decide how the demands for different periods are distributed among the pre-selected suppliers while minimising the expected total cost , which comprises holding and backlogging costs , as well as the selling price . This statement highlights the trade-off between supplier prices and uncertain lead times in replenishment planning . Two scenario-based stochastic programmes , one linear and one non-linear , are provided to simultaneously consider dispatching orders between suppliers , order crossover , and order release flexibility . The non-linear model , which relies on power sets to reduce the number of aggregated scenarios , is coupled with two approximate solution methods . The numerical experiments prove the computational effectiveness of The non-linear model , which relies on power sets to reduce the number of aggregated scenarios , . These results can be helpful for decision-makers when negotiating prices with suppliers . For instance , we can determine the purchasing cost at which we order almost 100 % from a given supplier . If we now turn to the uncertainty of lead times , this study can also help negotiate with suppliers whose firms can not decrease their selling prices and advise their , thereby reducing the variance of their lead times .

title: New directions for interconnector research: drawing from social sciences and humanities perspectives to explore the Celtic Interconnector
abstract: The current discourse on interconnectors primarily centers on the technical and economic aspects necessary for delivering a stable grid infrastructure powered by renewable sources and for integrating energy markets . This article , therefore , explores opportunities to broaden definitions of energy grid interconnectivity beyond the techno-economic sphere . This article considers multidisciplinary perspectives and presents novel exploratory viewpoints from the social sciences and humanities . This article examines ideas of interconnection by drawing on the Celtic Interconnector , an Irish-French initiative , to explore the cultural , historical , political , and geographical dimensions of interconnectivity . Insights are derived from two workshops with academics in Ireland and France , encouraging a more contextual understanding of energy interconnections beyond energy interconnections physical and economic dimensions . This article builds on Insights to set out an agenda for future research and reflect on frames of reference for describing , analysing , and engaging with emerging interconnector processes and the multiple stakeholders involved .
keywords: celtic interconnector grid infrastructure social science and humanities ireland france

title: Regular outdoor access decreases stress with positive effects on the health of growing pigs raised on a conventional farm
abstract: Conventional pig production systems are characterized by fully slatted floors and space restrictions , hindering pigs from foraging and roaming . In contrast , providing pigs with outdoor access allows pigs to express a wide range of behaviors , but might challenge pigs health . In this context , we hypothesized that giving pigs regular outdoor access might lower stress exposure with positive impacts for health and welfare . A total of 145 male and 148 female pigs , housed in a conventional barn , were provided ( OUT ) or not ( IN ) with access to a grassy paddock twice a week from the age of 77 days to slaughter . The OUT pigs had lower salivary cortisol levels than the IN pigs . Regular access to a pasture also lowered the severity of body lesions . While Regular access to a pasture had no consequences on animal growth , Regular access to a pasture was associated with a reduced frequency of diarrhea in pigs . Despite lower leukocytes counts in The OUT pigs compared to the IN pigs , higher proportion of The OUT pigs developed humoral response against L. intracellularis . Thus , providing regular access to a paddock for growing pigs had positive impacts on growing pigs health and welfare , with no consequence on growing pigs performance .

title: Thiophene-Grafted Cyclo-Carbazole Nanohoop as a Semiconducting Layer in OFETs
abstract: Nanohoops are a class of fascinating curved materials that have started to show Nanohoops potential in organic electronics . Now , the next step consists of going deeper in Nanohoops rational design in order to reach high performance materials . However , at the next step , the Nanohoops properties and Nanohoops device performance are far more complicated to forecast than those of Nanohoops linear counterparts , and systematic studies dealing with the incorporation of functional units have to be carried out . Herein , we report a [ 4]cyclo-2,7-carbazole , possessing an electron-rich thiophene unit grafted on a [ 4]cyclo-2,7-carbazole , possessing an electron-rich thiophene unit grafted on its nitrogen atoms nitrogen atoms . Incorporation in Organic Field-Effect Transistors ( OFET ) provides a saturated mobility of 3.2 × 10–5 cm2 V–1 s–1 , among the highest reported to date for nanohoops . The other characteristics such as the low subthreshold swing ( 0.72 V / dec ) or the high on / off values of the drain-source current ( 2.8 × 105 ) appear even to be the highest reported to date for a nanohoop .

title: Sustainable biodiesel production from waste cooking oil: Process design and techno-economic comparison of homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis
abstract: This study aims to design and model four different semi-continuous process scenarios for biodiesel production , using virgin oil ( VO ) as a reference feedstock and waste cooking oil ( WCO ) collected from restaurants in Beirut . Both heterogeneous and homogeneous catalyst configurations were assessed by a thorough techno-economic analysis to identify the most efficient and cost-effective approach . A total collectable quantity of 22,740 kg / week of WCO was processed for biodiesel production , representing a collection rate of 45 % . This study was developed with a 15 years lifetime and a target payback period ( PBP ) of 5 years . CaO and Amberlyst 46 were chosen as heterogeneous catalysts for transesterification and esterification , respectively , while KOH and H₂SO₄ were identified as reference homogeneous catalysts . Technical evaluations revealed that heterogeneous configurations were simpler , requiring fewer treatment steps compared to homogeneous ones , which necessitate catalyst neutralization and extensive purification of biodiesel and glycerol . The economic impact of the catalyst regeneration section was analyzed , particularly for the heterogeneous configurations examined without the catalyst regeneration section . The economic feasibility of each setup was evaluated with focus on production capacity and how production capacity impacts a target payback period ( PBP ) of 5 years , using a 5-year payback as the reference . Among all configurations , the heterogeneous process without CaO regeneration required the lowest feedstock input of 5600 kg / day to achieve a target payback period ( PBP ) of 5 years . However , as production capacity increased , the economic difference between configurations with and without catalyst regeneration decreased , indicating that catalyst regeneration becomes economically advantageous at larger scales .

title: Guiding waves through chaos: Universal bounds for targeted mode transport
abstract: Controlling wave propagation in complex environments is a central challenge across wireless communications , imaging , and acoustics , where multiple scattering and interference obscure direct transmission paths . Coherent wavefront shaping enables precise energy delivery but typically requires full knowledge of the medium . Here , we introduce a universal statistical framework for targeted mode transport ( TMT ) that circumvents requires and validate a universal statistical framework for targeted mode transport ( TMT ) that circumvents this limitation on various platforms including microwave networks , two-dimensional chaotic cavities , and three-dimensional reverberation chambers . TMT quantifies the efficiency of transferring energy between specified input and output channels in multimode wave-chaotic systems . we develop a diagrammatic theory that predicts the eigenvalue distribution of the TMT operator and identifies the macroscopic parameters — coupling strength , absorption , and channel control — that govern performance . a diagrammatic theory that predicts the eigenvalue distribution of the TMT operator and identifies the macroscopic parameters — coupling strength , absorption , and channel control — that govern performance provides explicit bounds for optimal TMT wavefronts and captures phenomena like statistical transmission gaps and reflectionless states . These findings establish design principles for energy delivery and information transfer in complex environments , with broad implications for adaptive signal processing and wave-based technologies .

title: An approximate dynamic programming approach for multi-stage stochastic lot-sizing under a Decision-Hazard-Decision information structure
abstract: This work studies a combinatorial optimization problem encountered in industrial production planning : the single-item multi-resource lot-sizing problem with inventory bounds and lost sales . The demand to be satisfied by the production plan is subject to uncertainty and only probabilistically known . We consider a multi-stage decision process with a Decision-Hazard-Decision information structure in which decisions are made at each stage both before and after the uncertainty is revealed . Such a setting has not yet been studied for stochastic lot-sizing problems , and the resulting problem is modeled as a multi-stage stochastic integer program . We propose a solution approach based on an approximate stochastic dynamic programming algorithm . a solution approach based on an approximate stochastic dynamic programming algorithm relies on a decomposition of the resulting problem into single-stage sub-problems and on the estimation at each stage of the expected future costs . Due to a Decision-Hazard-Decision information structure in which decisions are made at each stage both before and after the uncertainty is revealed , each nested single-stage sub-problem is itself a two-stage stochastic integer program . We therefore introduce a Benders decomposition scheme to reduce the computational effort required to solve each nested sub-problem , and present a specialpurpose polynomial-time algorithm to efficiently solve the single-scenario second-stage sub-problems involved in a Benders decomposition scheme . The results of extensive simulation experiments carried out on large-size randomly generated instances are reported . The results of extensive simulation experiments carried out on large-size randomly generated instances demonstrate the practical benefit , in terms of the actual production cost , of using a solution approach based on an approximate stochastic dynamic programming algorithm as compared to a naive deterministic optimization approach based on the expected demand .

title: Reduced-Rank Mutual Coupling Representation and Experimental Estimation for Large RIS
abstract: Physics-consistent optimization of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces ( RISs ) is thwarted in practice by the difficulty of experimentally estimating the mutual coupling ( MC ) between RIS elements . For large RISs , experimental MC estimation is fundamentally challenging because of the quadratic scaling of the number of unknowns with the number of RIS elements . In this letter , we present a generic and flexible reduced-rank MC representation that allows wireless practitioners to choose a trade-off between model complexity and accuracy . we experimentally validate the direct reduced-rank MC estimation for a 100-element RIS in three radio environments ( rich scattering , attenuated scattering , free space ) . We observe a strong environmental dependence of the influence of rank reduction on accuracy . Model-based performance evaluations highlight that the importance of MC awareness in optimization depends strongly on the radio environment .

title: Dual-Polarized Array of Triangular Leaky-Wave Antennas for Compact Water Radar Instruments
abstract: This paper presents a compact dual-polarized leaky-wave antenna array for water remote sensing . a compact dual-polarized leaky-wave antenna array for water remote sensing employs a triangular slotted waveguide to achieve high gain and slanted pointing . a compact dual-polarized leaky-wave antenna array for water remote sensing cross-section supports two orthogonal propagation modes to enable dual-linear polarization and a highly slanted beam without exciting higher-order modes . A tailored slot shape is introduced to provide high leakage for two orthogonal propagation modes while efficiently controlling the aperture illumination to reduce sidelobe levels . a compact dual-polarized leaky-wave antenna array for water remote sensing consists of a three-layer monolithic structure , where a triangular slotted waveguide supports two stacked beamforming networks ( one per polarization ) . An array of orthomode transducers connects the beamformers to the radiating elements . Unconventional waveguide sections are employed to ensure self-supporting additive manufacturing . The design is validated through a progressive methodology that increases complexity in steps , allowing separate validation of key features and incorporating feedback from the manufacturing process to minimize deviations . Both the antenna concept and the experimental methodology are confirmed through prototyping of a 4-element array and a 32-element array . The final design achieves realized gains above 37 dB , high cross-polarization discrimination and isolation , and reduced sidelobe levels . Moreover , high slanted angles are attained without generating grating lobes or exciting higher-order modes , meeting the specifications of an airborne water monitoring radar instrument .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Autonomous flow reaction optimization guided by NMR spectroscopy and advanced Bayesian optimization algorithms
abstract: Efficient algorithmic strategies are essential for autonomous self-optimization in flow , where multiple , often conflicting , objectives must be balanced under strict experimental budgets . In this work , we compared two optimization approaches . The first is the Pareto-oriented approach , which focuses on identifying all trade-off solutions . The second is the constraint-oriented approach , where a single objective is optimised while constraining the others so that the search remains focused on the region of interest . we first evaluated two optimization approaches in an in silico study by optimising six analytical functions and showed the advantage of the constraint-oriented approach , where a single objective is optimised while constraining the others so that the search remains focused on the region of interest . we then applied two optimization approaches in the continuous-flow synthesis of 3-phenyl-5-trifluoromethyl-1,2,4-oxadiazole monitored by compact NMR spectroscopy . In the experimental study , we used constraint within the adaptive boundary constraint Bayesian optimization , a strategy we developed recently to avoid futile experiments ( experiments that do not improve the current best objective value theoretically ) . While the Pareto-oriented approach , which focuses on identifying all trade-off solutions is able to identify a diverse range of solutions , ABC-BO directed the search more efficiently towards the conditions of interest . this work demonstrates the complementarity of Pareto-oriented and constraint-based optimization strategies and underscores the importance of algorithm selection in autonomous chemical development .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Definitional Proof Irrelevance Made Accessible
abstract: A universe of propositions equipped with definitional proof irrelevance constitutes a convenient medium to express properties and proofs in type-theoretic proof assistants such as Lean , Rocq , and Agda . However , allowing accessibility predicates---used to establish semantic termination arguments---to inhabit such a universe yields undecidable typechecking , hampering the predictability and foundational bases of a proof assistant . To effectively reconcile definitional proof irrelevance and accessibility predicates with both theoretical foundations and practicality in mind , we describe a type theory that extends the Calculus of Inductive Constructions featuring observational equality in a universe of strict propositions , and two variants for handling the elimination principle of accessibility predicates : one variant safeguards decidability by sticking to propositional unfolding , and the other variant favors flexibility with definitional unfolding , at the expense of a potentially diverging typechecking procedure . Crucially , the metatheory of this dual approach establishes that any proof term constructed in one variant can be soundly embedded into one variant , while preserving the decidability of one variant . Moreover , we prove this dual approach to be consistent and to satisfy forms of canonicity , ensuring that programs can indeed be properly evaluated . we present an implementation in Rocq and compare an implementation in Rocq with existing approaches . Overall , this work introduces an effective technique that informs the design of proof assistants with strict propositions , enabling local computation with accessibility predicates without compromising the ambient type theory .

title: Effects of composition and process on the performance of thermopressed materials prepared from model and real-life biomass
abstract: There is growing interest in turning the by-products of agricultural processes into biobased and biodegradable materials . The complexity of composition and structure of biomass makes it difficult to understand the mechanisms involved in biomass transformation into materials , requiring model systems . In this study , solid materials were obtained from model cellulosic fibers ( modulus of 5.5-5.8 GPa ) and biomass from brewery co-products ( modulus of 2.2-2.6 GPa ) using uniaxial compression . solid materials properties were comparable to or exceeded those reported for conventional binderless cellulosic materials processed at higher temperatures ( ~200 • C ) , thus highlighting the efficiency of our low-temperature process . The effect of the fiber size and composition , of the processing temperature on the resulting samples mechanical properties was assessed . We show that longer initial fibers , with higher aspect ratio , led to improved flexural modulus and strength due to a higher degree of fiber entanglement , which translated into better performance for the less transformed biomass . While purely cellulosic samples displayed better mechanical properties than those prepared from biomass at a pressing temperature of 100 • C , the increase to 140 • C closed the gap between the two biomasses particularly in terms of water resistance due to a reduced porosity . Finally , model cellulosic polymers improved the water resistance of purely cellulosic samples due to the formation of water tight matrix . our low-temperature process is promising for the green transformation of biomass coproducts .

title: Statistical Multiport-Network Modeling and Efficient Discrete Optimization of RIS
abstract: This Letter addresses the physics-consistent optimization of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces ( RISs ) with mutual coupling ( MC ) and 1-bit-programmable RIS elements . This combination of constraints is typical of current prototypes but unexplored in theoretical work . First , we present a simple statistical generator for multiport-network-theory ( MNT ) parameters of rich-scattering , RIS-parametrized channels . we account for reciprocity , passivity , and coherent backscattering ; then , we add a simple hyper-parameter to control the MC strength . Second , we benchmark model-agnostic ( dictionary search , coordinate descent , genetic algorithm ) and model-based ( temperature-annealed back-propagation ) strategies under varying MC strength , with and without intelligent initialization . Except when MC is negligible , coordinate descent with random initialization offers the best trade-off in performance , runtime , and memory . we insights can guide wireless practitioners who optimize RIS prototypes and other reconfigurable wave systems .

title: A comprehensive review of time between events control charts: models, applications, and future directions
abstract: The increasing demand for high-quality processes has driven growing interest in control charts designed for monitoring rare events . Among control charts designed for monitoring rare events , Time Between Events control charts have emerged as powerful tools , yet a comprehensive literature review dedicated to this field has been lacking until now . This gap has limited the ability of researchers and practitioners to identify key methodological advances , unresolved challenges , and emerging research directions . To address this need , the present study provides the first extensive review of TBE control charts , covering 113 studies published between 2000 and 2025 . A multi-dimensional classification framework is introduced , which organizes the literature according to distributional assumptions , monitoring techniques , performance metrics , monitoring phases , event polarity ( positive vs. negative events ) , and data structures ( univariate , multivariate , and combined TBE with amplitude ) . the present study further analyzes publication outlets and presents comprehensive reference tables to support quick identification of relevant methods . Finally , the present study highlights critical research gaps — including limited work on positive events , nonparametric multivariate monitoring , adaptive and hybrid methods , and machine learning integration — and proposes a forward-looking agenda to advance statistical process monitoring in increasingly complex environments .

title: Topological Spatial Graph Coarsening
abstract: Spatial graphs are particular graphs for which the nodes are localized in space ( e.g. , public transport network , molecules , branching biological structures ) . In this work , we consider the problem of spatial graph reduction , that aims to find a smaller spatial graph ( i.e. , with less nodes ) with the same overall structure as the initial one . In this context , performing the graph reduction while preserving the main topological features of the initial one is particularly relevant , due to the additional spatial information . Thus , we propose a topological spatial graph coarsening approach based on a new framework that finds a trade-off between the graph reduction and the preservation of the topological characteristics . The coarsening is realized by collapsing short edges . In order to capture the topological information required to calibrate the reduction level , we adapt the construction of classical topological descriptors made for point clouds ( the so-called persistent diagrams ) to spatial graphs . the construction of classical topological descriptors made for point clouds ( the so-called persistent diagrams ) relies on the introduction of a new filtration called triangle-aware graph filtration . The coarsening is parameter-free and we prove that The coarsening is equivariant under rotations , translations and scaling of the initial one . we evaluate the performances of The coarsening on synthetic and real spatial graphs , and show that The coarsening significantly reduces the graph sizes while preserving the relevant topological information .

title: The interplay between the marine diazotroph Vibrio diazotrophicus and its prophage shapes both biofilm structure and nitrogen release
abstract: ABSTRACT Marine environments are frequently oligotrophic , characterized by low amount of bioassimilable nitrogen sources . At the global scale , the microbial fixation of N₂ , or diazotrophy , represents the primary source of fixed nitrogen in pelagic marine ecosystems , playing a key role in supporting primary production and driving the export of organic matter to the deep ocean . However , given the high energetic cost of N₂ fixation , the active release of fixed nitrogen by diazotrophs appears counterintuitive , suggesting the existence of alternative passive release pathways that remain understudied to date . Here , we show that the marine non-cyanobacterial diazotroph Vibrio diazotrophicus is endowed with a prophage belonging to the Myoviridae family , whose expression is induced under anoxic and biofilm-forming conditions . we demonstrate that a prophage belonging to the Myoviridae family , whose expression is induced under anoxic and biofilm-forming conditions can spontaneously excise from the genome of a prophage belonging to the Myoviridae family , whose expression is induced under anoxic and biofilm-forming conditions host and that a prophage belonging to the Myoviridae family , whose expression is induced under anoxic and biofilm-forming conditions forms intact and infective phage particles . Moreover , phage-mediated host cell lysis leads to increased biofilm production compared with a prophage-free derivative mutant and to increased release of dissolved organic carbon and ammonium . Altogether , the results suggest that viruses may play a previously unrecognized role in oceanic ecosystem dynamics by structuring microhabitats suitable for diazotrophy and by contributing to the recycling of ( in)organic matter . IMPORTANCE Diazotrophs are key players in ocean functioning by providing fixed nitrogen to ecosystems and fueling primary production . However , from a physiological point of view , the active release of fixed nitrogen by diazotrophs is paradoxical , since diazotrophs would invest in an energy-intensive process and supply nutrient to non-sibling cells , with the risk of being outcompeted . Therefore , alternative ways leading to the release of fixed nitrogen must exist . Here , we show that the marine non-cyanobacterial diazotroph Vibrio diazotrophicus possesses one prophage , whose activation leads to cell death , increased biofilm production , and the release of dissolved organic compounds and ammonium . Taken together , we results provide evidence that marine phage – diazotroph interplay leads to the creation of microhabitats suitable for diazotrophy , such as biofilm , and to nutrient cycling , and contributes to better understanding of the role of viruses in marine ecosystems .

title: Prediction of moisture diffusion kinetics during cyclic hygrothermal aging of epoxy resin by an improved finite element modeling approach
abstract: Epoxy resins , frequently employed in composite structures in industries like water transport systems , are known for Epoxy resins , frequently employed in composite structures in industries like water transport systems superior mechanical properties and resistance to chemical degradation . However , Epoxy resins , frequently employed in composite structures in industries like water transport systems long-term durability and performance are considerably affected by Epoxy resins , frequently employed in composite structures in industries like water transport systems ability to absorb water under cyclic hygrothermal conditions , resulting in the severe material degradation . Herein , this work aims to elucidate the moisture diffusion mechanisms within an epoxy resin subjected to extreme environmental conditions by incorporating both experimental investigations and Finite Element Modeling ( FEM ) . Experimentally , epoxy resin samples were subjected to two complete cycles of moisture absorption and desorption in a controlled Temperature Humidity Test Chamber . Continuous gravimetric measurements were recorded every 24 h , revealing a transition from complex Dual-Fickian behavior in the initial absorption cycle to typical Fickian behavior in subsequent resorption cycles . To validate these findings , numerical simulations using FEM Analysis were conducted . The results demonstrated the importance of finer meshes , particularly in the initial Dual-Fickian absorption stage , to significantly improve the fidelity of the model to experimental data . Eventually , this work highlights the need for advanced modeling approach to effectively predict moisture diffusion kinetics in epoxy resins , thereby ensuring epoxy resins long-term durability in industrial applications .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Evaluation of cadmium’s impact on marine mussels: insights from Raman spectroscopy and chemometric analysis
abstract: Raman spectroscopy allows rapid , non-invasive characterization of molecular changes in biological tissues , making Raman spectroscopy apromising tool for ecotoxicology . This study evaluates the potential of Raman spectroscopy combined with chemometricsfor detecting changes induced by cadmium in the tissues of Mytilus edulis , a mussel species widely used in environmentalmonitoring . Adult mussels were exposed to two cadmium concentrations ( 50 μg / L and 500 μg / L ) for 7 days . The cadmiumconcentrations in water and tissues of mussels ( gills and mantle ) were quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry(ICP-MS ) to determine bioavailability and bioaccumulation , with mantle cadmium levels reaching 3.94 ± 0.35 μg / gat 50 μg / L and 57.49 ± 7.16 μg / g at 500 μg / L. Raman spectroscopy spectra were collected from mantle and gill tissues , and were analyzedusing principal component analysis ( PCA ) and K-means clustering . The mantle tissue exhibited a distinct molecular profilein response to cadmium exposure , with spectral variations indicating impairments in lipid , protein , nucleic acid , and carbohydratemetabolism . In contrast , the spectra of gill tissues did not show any discrimination among exposure treatments . These findings indicate that Raman spectroscopy with chemometric analysis could effectively detect early cadmium-inducedbiochemical alterations in Mytilus edulis , a mussel species widely used in environmentalmonitoring tissues , especially in mantle . detect highlights Raman spectroscopy with chemometric analysis potential as a sensitive , noninvasivebiomonitoring tool in ecotoxicological studies .

title: Listening to Forms, Sensing Formants
abstract: Writing about the work of someone who has been a supervisor , a colleague and a friend is never simple . Instead of attempting an overview of someone who has been a supervisor , a colleague and a friend whole scientific and academic work – well beyond the scope of this paper – we propose to revisit several moments in which sound shaped someone who has been a supervisor , a colleague and a friend conceptual and methodological developments . This text should be understood as a navigation through someone who has been a supervisor , a colleague and a friend ideas , gradually leading us to the notions of forms , formants and formalities , which someone who has been a supervisor , a colleague and a friend first developed during someone who has been a supervisor , a colleague and a friend PhD research ( someone who has been a supervisor , a colleague and a friend , 1996 ) and later presented in an article translated into English here . While the works discussed here gravitate around the emergence of forms , formants and formalities , the works discussed here belong to a wider set of scientific and pedagogical inquiries that we do not claim to retrace in full . Our aim is simply to put selected elements into perspective , offering a humble introduction and contextualisation to This text .
keywords: writing about the work of someone who has been a supervisor, a colleague or a friend

title: On the unit hypercube, the tightest convex relaxation of the ℓ0 pseudonorm is the ℓ1 norm
abstract: Convex relaxations of cardinality-constrained optimization problems can be used in many applications requiring sparsity . We consider the case of optimization problems where the feasible domain is restricted to the unit hypercube and includes an ℓ0-norm cardinality constraint . Finding the tightest convex relaxation amounts to finding the convex hull of this feasible set . It is a well-known result [ 1 ] that for K = 1 , the convex hull of the ℓ0 " ball " of radius K on [ 0,1]^P is the ℓ1 ball of radius K on [ 0,1]^P . The property holds for any K ∈ N * , yet The property proof may not be derived in the same fashion , hence this short contribution .

title: “Steps” towards a corpus of SCOTUS opinions annotated using a Swalesian approach
abstract: In the tradition of Moreno and Swales ( 2018 ) , this paper presents the creation of a manually annotated resource for supporting teaching English for Legal Purposes ( ELP ) and for Natural Language Processing ( NLP ) purposes . After justifying the use of Supreme Court of the United States opinions , we define we coding scheme by adapting the move model of rhetorical structure in specialized discourse . we describe the methodology and the implementation of the annotation campaign . we analyze how the methodology and the resulting annotation scheme diverge from those described in the literature as well as the advantages that diverge afford . In addition to this paper , we release several supplementary materials which aim to make the process transparent and serve other researchers aiming to annotate specialized discourse with the help of machine learning techniques .

title: End –to –End Learning for Hardware Impaired Downlink Cell –Free Massive MIMO
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output ( CF-mMIMO ) promises macrodiversity and high spectral efficiency through cooperation among many distributed access points ( APs ) . However , hardware imperfections such as power amplifier ( PA ) nonlinearities become a limiting factor when many low-cost radio-frequency chains operate in parallel . Conventional mitigation techniques either rely on accurate distortion models or require expensive digital pre-distortion ( DPD ) at each transmitter . In this paper we propose a hardware-aware end-to-end ( E2E ) learning framework for the downlink of a Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output ( CF-mMIMO ) network . The transmitter employs a neural network ( NN ) encoder hosted at the central processing unit that encodes each user data symbol . each user data symbol are then locally precoded by a full-pilot zero-forcing ( FZF ) matrix at each AP and transmitted before being received and classified by a second NN decoder at each user terminal . The encoders and decoders are trained jointly in an offline phase to minimize the categorical cross-entropy loss on a large dataset of randomly drawn quadrature amplitude modulation ( QAM ) symbols and channel realizations . Once trained , the solution operates without requiring any knowledge of the PA model . Simulation results show that a hardware-aware end-to-end ( E2E ) learning framework for the downlink of a CF-mMIMO network achieves lower symbol error rate ( SER ) than a conventional FZF precoder with and without expensive digital pre-distortion ( DPD , especially in the hardware-impairment-dominated regime . Furthermore , a hardware-aware end-to-end ( E2E ) learning framework for the downlink of a CF-mMIMO network is scalable and operates without backpropagation over the fronthaul during inference .

title: Named Data Networking for Scalable Distributed Storage and Indexation
abstract: With the exponential growth of data exchanged across geo-distributed infrastructures , the management , storage , and retrieval of such data have become major technical and economic challenges . One of the fundamental issues in data management systems is enabling users to quickly and efficiently access relevant information within massive and geographically dispersed datasets . In the geo-distributed context , several approaches have been proposed , including centralized and decentralized architectures , each with its own strengths and limitations . Centralized approaches simplify coordination but introduce single points of failure , potential bottlenecks , and limited tolerance to network partitioning . Centralized approaches can also increase data discovery costs , which may sometimes exceed the cost of retrieving the data . In contrast , decentralized approaches offer greater resilience and fault tolerance but often incur higher network overheads because of the need to propagate updates across the network whenever new data are created or modified . Therefore , designing an efficient indexing system remains challenging . Such a system should enable data discovery at a minimal cost without generating excessive network flooding while ensuring fault tolerance , high scalability , and independence from the geographical location of nodes . To address these challenges , we propose a fully distributed NDN-based storage architecture that integrates four complementary components : ( 1 ) VectorSync , a lightweight synchronization protocol that enables selective and dynamic update propagation across clusters ; ( 2 ) NDNS , an indexation service that registers and resolves named content , enabling efficient replica discovery without network flooding ; ( 3 ) AS-cast , a partitioned dissemination mechanism that localizes the closest replica , thereby reducing inter-cluster traffic and overall network overhead ; and ( 4 ) Hyperbolic Routing ( HR ) , which guides packet forwarding decisions based on geometric coordinates , reducing routing table size and improving scalability . Together , four complementary components ensure efficient data availability , consistent synchronization , and low-latency content retrieval across geo-distributed infrastructures , while minimizing network overhead .

title: Capacity Approximations for Insertion Channels with Small Insertion Probabilities
abstract: Channels with synchronization errors , exhibiting deletion and insertion errors , find practical applications in DNA storage , data reconstruction , and various other domains . The presence of insertions and deletions renders the channel with memory , complicating capacity analysis . For instance , despite the formulation of an independent and identically distributed ( i.i.d . ) deletion channel more than fifty years ago , and proof that an independent and identically distributed ( i.i.d . ) deletion channel is information stable , hence an independent and identically distributed ( i.i.d . ) deletion channel Shannon capacity exists , calculation of the capacity remained elusive . However , a relatively recent result establishes the capacity of an independent and identically distributed ( i.i.d . ) deletion channel in the asymptotic regime of small deletion probabilities by computing the dominant terms of an independent and identically distributed ( i.i.d . ) deletion channel capacity expansion . This paper extends a relatively recent result to binary insertion channels , determining the dominant terms of the channel capacity for small insertion probabilities and establishing capacity in the asymptotic regime of small deletion probabilities . Specifically , we consider two i.i.d . insertion channel models : the simple insertion channel , where a random bit may be inserted after each transmitted bit , and the Gallager insertion model , for which a bit is replaced by two random bits with a certain probability . To prove our results , we build on methods used for an independent and identically distributed ( i.i.d . ) deletion channel , employing Bernoulli(1/2 ) inputs for achievability and coupling this with a converse using stationary and ergodic input processes , and show that the channel capacity differs only in the higher order terms from the achievable rates with i.i.d . inputs . The results , for instance , show that the capacity of the simple insertion channel , where a random bit may be inserted after each transmitted bit is higher than that of the Gallager insertion channel , and quantify the difference in the asymptotic regime of small deletion probabilities .
keywords: channels with synchronization errors insertion channel gallager insertion channel channel capacity information stability deletion channel

title: Taking Advantage of Emergent Properties of a Transformer for Music Representation Learning
abstract: Self-supervised learning ( SSL ) has proven effective for music information retrieval ( MIR ) , yet contrastive and equivariant methods excel on different tasks : contrastive learning on tagging , equivariant learning on structured predictions . We propose a multi-class-token multitask model ( MT2 ) using multiple class tokens to optimize both contrastive and equivariant pretext tasks simultaneously , taking advantage of the emergent properties of a transformer . Averaging class tokens improves performance across diverse MIR tasks , while sequence tokens capture local musical information using emergent properties in a transformer . a multi-class-token multitask model ( MT2 ) using multiple class tokens achieves competitive results with far fewer parameters than existing masked modeling approaches .

title: Energy-latency attacks: A new adversarial threat to deep learning
abstract: The growing computational demand for deep neural networks ( DNNs ) has raised concerns about deep neural networks ( DNNs ) energy consumption and carbon footprint , particularly as the size and complexity of the models continue to increase . To address these challenges , energy-efficient hardware and custom accelerators have become essential . Additionally , adaptable DNNs are being developed to dynamically balance performance and efficiency . The use of these strategies became more common to enable sustainable AI deployment . However , these strategies may also introduce vulnerabilities , as attackers can potentially exploit these strategies to increase latency and energy usage by triggering attackers worst-case-performance scenarios . This new type of attack , called energy-latency attacks , has recently gained significant research attention , focusing on the vulnerability of DNNs to This new type of attack , called energy-latency attacks . This paper provides a comprehensive overview of current research on energy-latency attacks , categorizing energy-latency attacks using the established taxonomy for traditional adversarial attacks . We explore different metrics used to measure the success of energy-latency attacks and provide an analysis and comparison of existing attack strategies . We also analyze existing defense mechanisms and highlight current challenges and potential areas for future research in this developing field . The GitHub page for this work can be accessed at [ URL ]

title: Lost in narration? Metropolises in transition seek narrative(s) - Introduction
abstract: What is a metropolis ? An institutional area , an accumulation of networks and flows , an unusual concentration of higher urban functions , activities , and habitats for the living . All of these at once . However , a metropolis is also a perceptible , lived-in space , the physical ( infrastructures ) , geographical ( hydrography , topography ) , and symbolic ( representations ) encounter of several scales ( landscapes , uses , etc . ) and the result of a permanent tension between ordinary and spectacular , local and global , humans and non-humans . How can such complexity be planned and projected other than by recounting such complexity ? Whilst , over the past thirty or so years , narrative has indeed imposed narrative as one of the favoured tools for territory-making , what are narrative manifestations in the construction of metropolitan transitions ?

title: Unveiled Impact of 211 At-Labeled Compounds' Ability to Form Halogen Bonds on their In Vivo Stability
abstract: At is a radionuclide of great interest in nuclear medicine for cancer therapy , provided At is firmly bound to an appropriate targeting agent . In recent year , original 211 At-labeled compounds have shown promising in vivo stability , without the underlying logic being identified . Herein , molecular modeling ( two-component relativistic DFT ) is used to assess the hypothesis that the degradation mechanism(s ) , leading to the release of At , is related to the ability of labeled compounds to form halogen-bond interactions involving astatine . We highlight inhibition phenomena at play for a variety of compounds , in line with observations of enhanced stability , paving the way for a potentially applicable strategy to access robust radiopharmaceuticals .

title: Novel structures of chaos-based parallel multiple image encryption and FPGA implementation
abstract: Image data has been generated massively by devices in medical imaging modalities , cameras , and even by artificial intelligence . Encryption is the powerful method to keep the image content confidential , in which an encryption algorithm must include the confusion and diffusion properties . For massive images , a efficient method of encryption must be chosen to meet the demands of encryption speed and confidentiality . So far , chaos-based image encryption has been an active topic of research because chaos-based image encryption is considered an effective method to remove the correlation in image data as well as to keep confidential by the involvement of chaotic system in the encryption process . Besides , multiple image encryption algorithms encrypt multiple images in parallel , and chaos-based image encryption provides highly efficient performance in term of speed if chaos-based image encryption is implemented on a parallel computing platform such as multiple core processing as well as digital hardware design . Chaos-based multiple image encryption is constructed by integrating a chaotic system into multiple image encryption . Recently , many algorithms of chaos-based multiple image encryption have been proposed , and many algorithms of chaos-based multiple image encryption are proved to have high efficient in terms of both speed and confidentiality . However , many algorithms of chaos-based multiple image encryption require images of the same size and of the same number of bits representing pixels . Further , many algorithms of chaos-based multiple image encryption encrypt a cohort of plain images at the same time , and all ciphertext images of a cohort must also be decrypted at the same time . It means that if It does not allow to decrypt one or some selected ciphertext images from a cohort separately ; and as a result , It wastes time and energy to decrypt unwanted images . In this paper , three novel structures of chaos-based multiple image encryption are proposed which overcome the drawbacks of existing algorithms . That is , three novel structures of chaos-based multiple image encryption accept cohort images of different sizes ; pixels of images can be represented by different numbers of bits ; and any selected ciphertext images from a cohort can be decrypted separately . The security is improved by using the session keys of image-content dependency . three novel structures of chaos-based multiple image encryption consist of permutation , substitution , and diffusion processes . The difference between three novel structures of chaos-based multiple image encryption is the order of such processes . A perturbed chaotic map and a linear-feedback shift register are employed to generate pseudo-random bit sequences for session keys . The simulation results for the exemplar designs using three novel structures of chaos-based multiple image encryption show the effectiveness by means of the statistical analysis for the session keys using the NIST randomness test , information entropy , histogram , and correlation coefficients of adjacent pixels in ciphertext images , and security analysis by means of space and sensitivity of the secret key . The hardware implementation on the FPGA platform demonstrates the feasibility of three novel structures of chaos-based multiple image encryption by means of throughput and hardware efficiency .

title: Probing Structural Confinement in Organic Nanoparticles by Intertwining Photochromism and Nanomechanics
abstract: Functional organic nanoparticles , largely praised for optoelectronics and bioimaging applications , are usually manufactured upon mere self-assembly of molecular dyes . Undesirable dissociation due to non-covalent interactions between the molecular constituents can be prevented by further photocrosslinking . In order to study the reactivity within nanoparticles and the impact of photocrosslinking on the mechanical properties of nanoparticles , we elaborate nanoparticles and films , based on a photoactivatable network issued from reacting bis-acrylate functionalized azo photochromic units and bis(dithiolane ) crosslinkers of variable flexibility . Photochromic studies , recording azo relaxation dynamics after photoisomerization , are combined to force spectroscopy investigations , using atomic force microscopy following a nanocompression method , to give access to elastic modulus at the single nanoparticle level . we find that the average thermal relaxation of the azo units in crosslinked nanoparticles is largely enhanced by comparison to that in crosslinked films , whereas close values are obtained for both the more flexible and stiffer networks . While the elastic modulus slightly increases for thin films incorporating stiffer crosslinkers , increases is tenfold amplified in nanoparticles . These results first demonstrate that high structural confinement in nanoparticles upon nanoprecipitation favors large reactivity and thereby large incorporation of the crosslinkers in the final three-dimensional networks . Secondly , These results point out that nanoparticle elasticity is mainly ruled by the stiffness of the crosslinkers . The enhanced discrepancy in elasticity at the nanoparticle level is thus tentatively interpreted as nanoconfinement effects , impacting free volume distribution and chain mobility .

title: Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition with Graph Neural Networks and Tree-based Language Models
abstract: Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition ( HMER ) aims to translate handwritten formulas into machine-readable representations , bridging visual perception and symbolic reasoning . Despite progress in deep learning , Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition ( HMER ) remains challenging due to handwriting ambiguity , 2D spatial complexity , and intricate mathematical syntax . This thesis addresses Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition ( HMER ) from a structural perspective by modeling mathematical expressions as graphs and trees in 2D structure . We propose an Edge-weighted Graph Attention Network ( EGAT ) for joint symbol and relation classification , and a Tree-Structured Transformer ( TST ) Decoder for hierarchical structure prediction . To facilitate evaluation , the CROHME 2023 competition was organized with newly collected handwritten and large-scale synthetic data . Contextual extensions of CROHME were further introduced to assess the role of textual and visual context using vision-language models . The proposed approaches achieve competitive performance and contribute new insights and resources toward more structured and context-aware mathematical expression recognition .

title: Deep learning combines MRI texture and clinical factors to predict early efficacy in TACE for hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Objectives : Hepatocellular carcinoma ( HCC ) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide , and transarterial chemoembolization ( TACE ) represents the standard treatment for patients with intermediate-stage disease . However , early prediction of post-transarterial chemoembolization ( TACE ) response remains challenging due to tumor heterogeneity and limited interpretability of existing models . This study aimed to develop and validate a deep learning ( DL ) framework that integrates multi-sequence MRI texture features with preoperative clinical factors to predict early postoperative efficacy following transarterial chemoembolization ( TACE ) . Methods : In This study , 178 Hepatocellular carcinoma ( HCC ) patients who underwent transarterial chemoembolization ( TACE ) were enrolled from two institutions . Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI data and clinical variables were analyzed to construct a deep learning ( DL ) framework that integrates multi-sequence MRI texture features with preoperative clinical factors to predict early postoperative efficacy following TACE . a deep learning ( DL ) framework that integrates multi-sequence MRI texture features with preoperative clinical factors to predict early postoperative efficacy following TACE prediction probability and significant clinical factors were further combined through logistic regression to generate a nomogram for individualized response estimation . Results : a deep learning ( DL ) framework that integrates multi-sequence MRI texture features with preoperative clinical factors to predict early postoperative efficacy following TACE achieved robust predictive performance , with an area under the curve ( AUC ) of 0.90 in the internal testing set and 0.79 in the external validation set . Incorporating clinical variables improved predictive accuracy , yielding AUCs of 0.98 and 0.86 for the in-house and external datasets , respectively . Calibration and bootstrap analyses confirmed model stability , while decision curve analysis demonstrated superior clinical utility compared with conventional approaches . Attention-weight analysis revealed that T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted sequences contributed most to prediction , consistent with T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted sequences biological relevance in tumor viability assessment . Conclusions : a nomogram for individualized response estimation provides an interpretable , noninvasive tool for predicting early transarterial chemoembolization ( TACE ) response in Hepatocellular carcinoma ( HCC ) , potentially aiding in personalized therapeutic decision-making and optimizing treatment strategies .

title: Viruses in multi-scale ocean models: challenges and opportunities
abstract: While viruses affect the flow of elements and energy at a planet-wide scale through lysis , gene transfer , and metabolic reprogramming , viruses are yet to be included in planetary-scale models of ecosystem function and nutrient cycling . Here , we review recent advances incorporating viruses into ocean models and ask : what barriers remain ? To address these challenges , we argue for a new generation of ocean models that are fully representative of the multifaceted influences of viruses across scales of organization . we describe ways to achieve this by integration of existing models built across scales , from molecules to ecosystems and the Earth System . To accelerate these advances , we emphasize the need for systematic , intercalibrated datasets for diverse experimental virus-host systems , wider application of new technologies to monitor in situ viral infections , and new software to integrate models across scales . Resolution of viruses within multi-scale models will open the door to assessing current biological uncertainties related to the impact of viral infection on nutrient retention in the surface ocean , carbon sequestration to depth , and the sensitivity of these processes to climate change .

title: Combining physics-based models and machine learning for multi-energy system modeling
abstract: The massive integration of intermittent renewable energy sources necessitates more complex energy systems with stronger coupling between energy sectors , expanded storage capacities , and more dynamic operation . Model-based decision-making is essential to efficiently design and operate more complex energy systems with stronger coupling between energy sectors , expanded storage capacities , and more dynamic operation . However , pure physics-based models are often too computationally expensive for real-time applications . Machine Learning ( ML ) offers high speed and accuracy but suffers from limited interpretability and generalizability . This thesis explores hybrid modeling approaches that combine physics-based and ML models to achieve both speed and accuracy while maintaining interpretability and generalizability . This thesis provides a classification of the fundamental building blocks and design patterns of hybrid modeling , then proposes novel hybrid models for Thermal Energy Storage ( TES ) and Heat Pump ( HP ) systems . The hybrid TES model runs approximately 1250x faster with overall mean squared error below 0.48 ° C2 , while the hybrid HP model achieves a 271× speed-up with error below 0.4 % . novel hybrid models for Thermal Energy Storage ( TES ) and Heat Pump ( HP ) systems demonstrate improved accuracy and generalizability while requiring less training data than pure ML models . In the second part , novel hybrid models for Thermal Energy Storage ( TES ) and Heat Pump ( HP ) systems are evaluated on two case studies , ( 1 ) the operation of charging and discharging a TES in a solar power plant , and ( 2 ) the operation of a HP coupled with a hot water tank to provide heating for a building . These studies demonstrate the usability of novel hybrid models for Thermal Energy Storage ( TES ) and Heat Pump ( HP ) systems for real-time applications . novel hybrid models for Thermal Energy Storage ( TES ) and Heat Pump ( HP ) systems were successfully integrated into Model Predictive Control workflows to optimally operate more complex energy systems with stronger coupling between energy sectors , expanded storage capacities , and more dynamic operation .

title: Hybrid Reaction–Diffusion Epidemic Models: Dynamics and Emergence of Oscillations
abstract: ABSTRACT In this paper , we construct a hybrid epidemic mathematical model based on a reaction – diffusion system of the SIR ( susceptible‐infected‐recovered ) type . a hybrid epidemic mathematical model based on a reaction – diffusion system of the SIR ( susceptible‐infected‐recovered ) type integrates the impact of random factors on the transmission rate of infectious diseases , represented by a probabilistic process acting at discrete time steps . a hybrid epidemic mathematical model based on a reaction – diffusion system of the SIR ( susceptible‐infected‐recovered ) type couples a continuous reaction – diffusion system , which describes the spatiotemporal dynamics of the infectious disease , with a discrete probabilistic process that models potential change in the transmission rate . we establish properties of both biological and mathematical interest in a hybrid epidemic mathematical model based on a reaction – diffusion system of the SIR ( susceptible‐infected‐recovered ) type , including the existence of global solutions , stability analysis of equilibrium points , and the emergence of oscillatory behaviors . Additionally , we extend a hybrid epidemic mathematical model based on a reaction – diffusion system of the SIR ( susceptible‐infected‐recovered ) type by including vaccination . The dynamics and emergence of oscillations in a hybrid epidemic mathematical model based on a reaction – diffusion system of the SIR ( susceptible‐infected‐recovered ) type are investigated under various scenarios , which are illustrated through numerical simulations .

title: Development of a microwave heating treatment as a substitute for the classical retort sterilization process
abstract: This research investigates the development of a microwave-based heat treatment process as a sustainable alternative to conventional sterilization , focusing on the thermo mechanical behavior of food packaging during high-temperature processing of a model food product ( mashed potato ) . Conventional sterilization studies on rigid metal containers combined experiments and numerical modelling using COMSOL Multiphysics ® to analyze temperatures within a model food product ( mashed potato ) and pressure evolution within the head space , showing that dry air contributes to total internal pressure mainly during the early heating stage , while vapour pressure becomes dominant during the rest of the process . Flexible polypropylene ( PP ) trays ( empty and filled with mashed potato ) were then examined under different mechanical constraints to evaluate Flexible polypropylene ( PP ) trays ( empty and filled with mashed potato ) structural response under air injection , convective heating treatment , and microwave heating . Although the application of mechanical constraints increased internal pressure tolerance of Flexible polypropylene ( PP ) trays ( empty and filled with mashed potato ) , rupture consistently occurred at the heat-seal interface . The final study was conducted with a rigid Polyether ether ketone ( PEEK ) container designed to withstand internal pressure during microwave heating , achieving internal temperatures above 118 ° C . Overall , This research lays the groundwork for understanding the thermo – mechanical dynamics of food packaging during heat treatment , providing a foundation for designing safer and more energy-efficient food processing systems .
