title: Deep Neural Strategies for Regularization Parameters Estimation and Image Parameterization in PET Reconstruction
abstract: Positron Emission Tomography ( PET ) is a functional imaging technique widely used in oncology , enabling quantitative analysis of radiopharmaceuticals distribution . The reconstruction of PET images from raw data is an ill-posed inverse problem that requires regularization due to intrinsic high noise level . As a result , image quality strongly depends on the regularization method and the choice of regularization parameters . Current methods used in clinics apply the same setting to all patients . In this thesis , we explore two deep learning-based strategies to adapt regularization automatically for each individual scan with the aim of getting optimal image quality . The first approach uses a supervised residual neural network to predict optimal parameters for an established regularization method directly from raw data . A simulation pipeline was developed to efficiently generate realistic PET datasets and corresponding optimal parameters , allowing to build the training database . The second approach leverages Implicit Neural Representations ( INRs ) , modeling the image as a continuous function represented by a cartesian coordinate-based network , which is optimized directly from raw data via a physics-informed loss . The second approach introduces regularization implicitly and does not require training data .

title: LP4P: Link Prediction over Annotated Knowledge Graphs with Four Patterns
abstract: Initially designed for Knowledge Graphs ( KG ) containing plain ( s , p , o ) triples , research on link prediction has evolved to address more complex structures such as hypergraphs , hyper-relational graphs , and bi-level graphs . evolved push link prediction to handle annotation patterns , where a triple is annotated with another ( t , p , t ) , or where triples are annotated with qualifiers ( t , p , o ) . However , each approach focuses on a single annotation pattern , and the case where a triple is annotated with a subject ( s , p , t ) has never been explored . In this paper , we propose LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns . LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns captures the information expressed in annotations through a four-pattern attention layer , and LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns loss function further leverages the ontological information of KGs . Moreover , we built WD4P , an RDF KG derived from baseline datasets , which includes three annotation patterns . Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns outperforms relevant state-of-the-art models on knowledge graphs with three annotation patterns , and achieves comparable performance on standard benchmarks .

title: Friction in Motion Systems: A Systematic Approach to LuGre Model Identification, from Experimental Design to Parameter Calibration
abstract: Friction-induced disturbances degrade the accuracy of positioning systems . The LuGre model balances physical fidelity and parameter parsimony , but poses identification challenges due to The LuGre model nonlinearity and parameter coupling . This paper presents a systematic LuGre friction identification methodology combining a gradient-based optimization algorithm and a friction-guided experimental plan . a systematic LuGre friction identification methodology combining a gradient-based optimization algorithm and a friction-guided experimental plan integrates a single-objective optimization criterion with a two-step initialization strategy . a systematic LuGre friction identification methodology combining a gradient-based optimization algorithm and a friction-guided experimental plan is validated through simulation and experiments on a motorized linear stage from MKS Instruments , demonstrating a systematic LuGre friction identification methodology combining a gradient-based optimization algorithm and a friction-guided experimental plan experimental effectiveness for positioning industrial applications .

title: Hierarchical Data-enabled Predictive Control for Building Thermal Management
abstract: Building thermal management accounts for a significant share of global energy consumption . The application of Model Predictive Control ( MPC ) in Building thermal management remains limited by the complexity of modeling . Data-enabled Predictive Control ( DeePC ) , which replaces explicit models with data-driven trajectory predictions , offers a promising alternative . However , Data-enabled Predictive Control ( DeePC ) , which replaces explicit models with data-driven trajectory predictions , reliance on quasi-linear dynamics limits Data-enabled Predictive Control ( DeePC ) , which replaces explicit models with data-driven trajectory predictions , direct control of nonlinear HVAC actuators . This work proposes a hierarchical framework : Data-enabled Predictive Control ( DeePC ) , which replaces explicit models with data-driven trajectory predictions , optimizes thermal power allocation at the supervisory level , while decentralized PI controllers , tuned via the model-free Virtual Reference Feedback Tuning method , regulate power . Validated on the Building Optimization Testing Framework ( BOPTEST ) , this approach eliminates explicit modeling and achieves superior energy efficiency and comfort management compared to conventional resistance-capacitance model MPC .

title: Friction in Motion Systems: A Systematic Approach to LuGre Model Identification, from Experimental Design to Parameter Calibration
abstract: Friction-induced disturbances degrade the accuracy of positioning systems . Although the LuGre model balances physical fidelity and parameter parsimony , the LuGre model identification remains challenging due to nonlinear dynamics and parameter coupling . This paper proposes a systematic LuGre friction identification methodology combining a gradient-based optimization algorithm with a friction-guided experimental design . a systematic LuGre friction identification methodology combining a gradient-based optimization algorithm with a friction-guided experimental design relies on a single-objective cost function and a two-step parameter initialization strategy . a systematic LuGre friction identification methodology combining a gradient-based optimization algorithm with a friction-guided experimental design is validated through simulation and experimental results obtained on an MKS Instruments motorized linear stage , illustrating a systematic LuGre friction identification methodology combining a gradient-based optimization algorithm with a friction-guided experimental design suitability for accurate friction modeling in industrial positioning applications .

title: Hub location for waterborne transportation networks in the context of the physical internet
abstract: This dissertation addresses optimization models for the design of logistics networks under the emerging paradigm of the Physical Internet ( PI ) , with a focus on river-based and multimodal transportation . Building on hub location theory and network design , This dissertation extends classical formulations to better reflect the structural and operational features of real logistics systems . The first contribution introduces the Tree-of-Hub Location Problem with Stopovers , which allows intermediate stopovers along inter-hub routes . A mixed-integer linear programming model , strengthened by valid inequalities , demonstrates the cost and flexibility benefits of extends . The second contribution develops hub location models for multimodal networks combining rivers and roads , illustrated through a case study on Colombia ’s Magdalena River . The third contribution adapts liner shipping service network design to the the emerging paradigm of the Physical Internet ( PI ) context , adding set-partitioning constraints to capture modular and interoperable flows . To address scalability , a Large Neighborhood Search ( LNS ) metaheuristic is implemented , providing high-quality solutions for large instances .

title: Stabilizing non-discerning control design for discrete-time linear switched systems
abstract: The distinguishability between the modes of a switched system is an essential concept , particularly for the synthesis of observers . In this paper , we propose to use The distinguishability between the modes of a switched system opposite , specifically to protect against cyber-physical attacks that aim to obtain information about a switched system . More precisely , we focus on synthesizing non-discerning control laws that stabilize a switched system . we establish the conditions for the existence of such a law and propose a procedure for such a law design . The academic examples demonstrate the described application .

title: Willems’ Lemma Reformulations: Which Operators Preserve LTI System Behavior?
abstract: In the behavioral approach , dynamical systems are abstracted as sets of trajectories . the behavioral approach gave birth to the celebrated Willems ’ Fundamental Lemma , for which various reformulations have been proposed in the literature , for instance , using frequency-domain data . In this note , we show that all reformulations are necessarily based on linear shift-invariant transformations , which have the fundamental property that linear shift-invariant transformations , which have the fundamental property that they preserve the trajectory space of all LTI systems preserve the trajectory space of all LTI systems . we results unify the existing reformulations and provide guidelines for designing novel ones .

title: Design of Heavy-Atom Free Dipyridomethene Boron Complexes for Singlet Oxygen Emission with Induced Chirality
abstract: The straightforward synthesis of the first difluoro dipyridomethene boron complexes as heavy-atom-free photosensitizers is described . the first difluoro dipyridomethene boron complexes as heavy-atom-free photosensitizers show good singlet oxygen generation ( phi Delta = 10 to 47 % ) and significant nonplanar arrangement , inducing axial and boron-centered chirality .

title: LP-4P : Link Prediction over Annotated Knowledge Graphs with Four Patterns
abstract: Initially designed for Knowledge Graphs ( KG ) containing plain ( s , p , o ) triples , research on link prediction has evolved to address more complex structures such as hypergraphs , hyper-relational graphs , and bi-level graphs . evolved push link prediction to handle annotation patterns where a triple is annotated with another ( t , p , t ) , or where a triple is annotated with qualifiers ( t , p , o ) . However , each approach focuses on a single annotation pattern , and the case where a triple is annotated with a subject ( s , p , t ) has never been explored . In this paper , we propose LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns . LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns captures the information expressed in annotations through a four-pattern attention layer , and LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns loss function further leverages the ontological information of KGs . Moreover , we built WD4P , an RDF KG derived from baseline datasets , which includes three annotation patterns . Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns outperforms relevant state-of-the-art models on knowledge graphs with three annotation patterns , and achieves comparable performance on standard benchmarks .
keywords: knowledge graph and prediction and machine learning

title: Augmented Adaptive Observer for a Differentiable Regressor
abstract: We show that constructing an augmented adaptive observer , where the extended state is a mix of the original states and the original states derivatives , we can enhance the transient performance and obtain robust estimation results for the original state and the unknown parameters . The convergence of an augmented adaptive observer , where the extended state is a mix of the original states and their derivatives , is shown under the persistence of excitation assumption by constructing a Lyapunov function and using the input-to-output stability framework . The performance of the design is illustrated via numerical simulations .

title: Effect of sintering on aeolian snow erosion
abstract: The quantitative description of aeolian snow transport remains a challenging issue for theoretical modelling but also for environmental concerns . Drifting snow is crucially dependent on snow cover properties , including cohesive force and snow type . Snow transport is particularly impacted by cohesive processes in contrast to wind-blown sand . Our study explores in particular the effect of snow sintering on both the aerodynamic and impact erosion processes . Our propose here an original experimental set-up to determine both the aerodynamic and impact erosion rate in the context of snow packs . The experiments were carried out in the cold wind-tunnel at the Cryopsheric Environment simulator in Shinjo with snow packs of various sintering times . Our results reveal that as sintering time is increased , impact erosion efficiency – which is determined by the number of particles ejected per impact – is decreased . Our preliminary findings are in line with recent experiments made with moist sand , suggesting similarities between snow and moist sand .

title: Aeolian transport of cohesive sand
abstract: The influence of moisture on wind-driven sand transport is particularly important in coastal environements . While moisture is generally low in desert sands , moisture significantly affects sand transport on beaches or in coastal dune dynamics . Studies on The influence of moisture on wind-driven sand transport are far from yielding consistent results because it is difficult to control and measure moisture levels due to evaporation . We circumvent this difficulty by using sand-oil mixtures which offers the advantage to get rid of evaporation . With sand-oil mixtures which offers the advantage to get rid of evaporation , We conducted wind-tunnel experiments and documented with an unprecedented accuracy the effects of cohesion on wind-blown sand .

title: Simulation of a Semiconductor Manufacturing Research and Development Cleanroom
abstract: This paper focuses on a Research and Development ( R&D ) semiconductor manufacturing system . By virtue of their vocation , R&D facilities tolerate much more variability in processes and outcomes than industrial-scale ones . In such environments , operating under conditions characterized by high uncertainty and occurrences of ( un)knowns corresponds to normal operating conditions rather than abnormal ones . This paper characterizes the key entities and operational aspects of a semiconductor R&D cleanroom and introduces a discrete-event simulation model that captures the key entities and operational aspects of a semiconductor R&D cleanroom . a discrete-event simulation model that captures these elements is grounded in empirical data and reflects real-life operations management practices observed in actual R&D cleanroom settings . Preliminary computational results based on real-life instances are presented , and future research directions are outlined to support resilient decision-making in environments where high levels of uncertainty are part of normal operating conditions .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Towards Process Optimization by Leveraging Relationships Between Electrical Wafer Sorting and Complete-Line Statistical Process Control Data
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing , Statistical Process Control ( SPC ) ensures that products meet the Electrical Wafer Sort ( EWS ) tests performed at the end of the manufacturing flow . In this work , we model the Electrical Wafer Sort ( EWS ) tests performed at the end of the manufacturing flow using inline Statistical Process Control ( SPC ) data from the Front-End-Of-Line ( FEOL ) to the Back-End-Of-Line ( BEOL ) . Statistical Process Control ( SPC ) data tend to be inherently sparse because measuring all wafers , lots , and products is both costly and can significantly impact the throughput . In contrast , EWS data is densely collected at the die level , offering high granularity . we propose to model the problem as a regression task to uncover interdependencies between Statistical Process Control ( SPC ) and EWS data at the lot level . By applying two learning strategies , mono-and multi-target , we demonstrate empirically that leveraging families of EWS tests enhances model performance . The performance and practical relevance of the approach are validated through numerical experiments on real-world industrial data .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Babel-formal: Translation of Proofs between Lean and Rocq
abstract: In this work , we investigate using proof terms ( the low-level representation of formal proofs ) as a pivot language for translating proof scripts between proof assistants and across tactic sets . Unlike direct proof translation , using does not require an aligned training corpus ; using only needs aligned context at inference time so that both systems elaborate comparable terms . we compare two strategies : ( 1 ) direct script-to-script translation with an off-the-shelf LLM ( GPT-5 ) , and ( 2 ) proof term translation , where an LLM turns a proof term into a proof script in the target language . we build a small benchmark of aligned sources ( 14 files , 117 lemmas ) across Lean and Rocq , and train models to map Lean and Rocq proof terms back to Lean and Rocq proof terms native proof scripts . we experiments show that proof term translation works for cross-assistant translation and for translation between tactic sets . proof term translation is complementary to using a SoTA off-the-shelf LLM for direct proof script translation ( combining both performs best ) , scales easily in terms of training data , and handles tactic-set translation better ( e.g. , vanilla Rocq → SSReflect ) .

title: On Self-stabilizing Sharing of Multicast Transmission in Overlays
abstract: Overlay networks enable flexible and scalable communication in distributed systems by constructing logical topologies above the physical Internet . A fundamental operation in Overlay networks is multicast transmission , where data is efficiently delivered from a source to multiple receivers via a logical tree . Maintaining such multicast overlays , however , incurs transmission costs at intermediate nodes , making fair cost sharing essential to prevent selfish behavior and ensure system sustainability . While cost-sharing mechanisms and self-stabilizing protocols have been studied separately , existing approaches do not jointly address both challenges . Current solutions either assume fault-free networks or overlook economic incentives , leaving multicast overlays vulnerable to faults and unfairness . In this paper , we propose a self-stabilizing algorithm for multicast transmission overlays that integrates structural recovery with faithful cost sharing . a self-stabilizing algorithm for multicast transmission overlays that integrates structural recovery with faithful cost sharing autonomously reconstructs a correct multicast tree following transient faults while fairly distributing transmission costs among receivers using a Shapley-based mechanism . Lightweight cryptographic techniques are employed to prevent manipulation and ensure strategyproofness . we formally prove that a self-stabilizing algorithm for multicast transmission overlays that integrates structural recovery with faithful cost sharing guarantees convergence , budget balance , and resilience against selfish deviations . Simulations on dynamic overlays demonstrate rapid stabilization , low overhead , and robust fairness even under frequent faults and churn . This work advances reliable distributed systems by bridging fault tolerance and economic fairness in multicast overlays .

title: Exploring the computational and psychological aspects of a human-centered decision-making process for nurse rostering
abstract: This thesis aims to integrate human-centered ethical aspects into nurse rostering . We argue that classical operations research approaches to nurse rostering , which fix objectives and constraints within a mathematical model , fail to capture the procedural rationality of human decision-makers and raise ethical issues of autonomy and responsibility . We propose a contextualized approach that draws on insights from occupational health and organizational justice . insights from occupational health and organizational justice help identify essential aspects related to well-being and fairness . We then design an interactive tool that enables decision-makers to iteratively adjust constraints and objectives , thereby exploring different trade-offs and reinforcing decision-makers autonomy . The implementation , based on an integer linear programming model , incorporates a catalog of additional constraints and provides recommendations drawn from the literature . An experiment with participants demonstrates progressive learning , improved efficiency , and a preserved sense of autonomy . This research thus highlights the importance of designing interactive and multidisciplinary tools to foster responsible decision-making that is better aligned with organizational needs .

title: Automatic Text Revision for Scientific Writing Assistance
abstract: Writing a scientific article is a challenging task as Writing is a highly codified genre , consequently proficiency in written communication is essential for effectively conveying research findings . In the writing process , text revision involves substantial modifications to improve clarity , coherence , and adherence to academic standards . This thesis investigates scientific text revision with a focus on the development of resources and evaluation strategies for automated writing assistance . Our main contributions are as follows : To support empirical research , Our introduce CASIMIR , a large-scale dataset of scientific article revisions , aligned at the sentence level and enriched with edit operations and inferred revision intentions . Recognising the limitations of sentence-level scope , Our propose a paragraph-level definition of the task , supported by ParaRev , a dataset of revised scientific paragraphs annotated with finegrained revision instructions . Our experiments reveal that finegrained revision instructions improve automated revisions . Finally , Our address the limitations of current similarity-based evaluation metrics which inadequately reflect the quality of scientific text revisions . Our explore alternative approaches , including reference-free metrics and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation , finding that a hybrid strategy combining LLM-based and task-specific metrics most reliably captures revision quality .

title: Coupled vs. Decoupled Motion Planning for Four-Robotic Arm Manipulation in a Shared Workspace: An Empirical Study
abstract: Multi-robot manipulator systems are increasingly used in industrial settings for tasks like coordinated assembly and pick-and-place operations . In such shared workspaces , multiple robotic arms must plan collision-free motions that account for each other ’s movements . plan is computationally challenging , as the joint configuration space grows exponentially with the number of degrees of freedom ( DoF ) . We study motion planning for a four-arm industrial cell ( KUKA KR6 , KUKA KR10 , UR10 , UR5 ) operating in a shared workspace under ROS / Gazebo / MoveIt . We compare a coupled planner in a 24-DoF composite space using OMPL RRT-Connect against a decoupled pipeline that plans per arm and then time-coordinates trajectories with a Detect-and-Pause heuristic . a Detect-and-Pause heuristic discretizes a 24-DoF composite space into voxels , builds a spatio-temporal occupancy matrix , detects inter-arm conflicts in advance , and resolves inter-arm conflicts by pausing the robot with larger remaining execution time . To ensure a fair comparison , task allocation and grasp configurations are fixed across methods , and identical controller and planning parameters are used . Benchmarks span three clutter levels defined by minimum interobject distance dmin ∈{30,20,10}cm . We generate 10 randomized instances per level . Results show a decoupled pipeline that plans per arm and then time-coordinates trajectories with a Detect-and-Pause heuristic dominates : 100 % success at all clutter levels ( vs. ∼81.7 % for coupled ) , a −28.9 % reduction in median planning time on average , and −26.1 % median makespan on average . Gains are largest at 20 cm , where interactions are frequent . Results suggest that time-based coordination on fixed single-arm paths is a simple , robust , and scalable alternative to centralized planning for multi-arm manipulation in shared workspaces .

title: FIDAVL: Fake Image Detection and Attribution Using Vision-Language Model
abstract: We introduce FIDAVL : Fake Image Detection and Attribution using a Vision-Language Model . FIDAVL : Fake Image Detection and Attribution using a Vision-Language Model is a novel and efficient multitask approach inspired by the synergies between vision and language processing . Leveraging the benefits of zero-shot learning , FIDAVL : Fake Image Detection and Attribution using a Vision-Language Model exploits the complementarity between vision and language along with soft prompt-tuning strategy to detect fake images and accurately attribute fake images to fake images originating source models . We conducted extensive experiments on a comprehensive dataset comprising synthetic images generated by various state-of-the-art models . We results demonstrate that FIDAVL : Fake Image Detection and Attribution using a Vision-Language Model achieves an encouraging average detection accuracy of 95.42 % and F1-score of 95.47 % while also obtaining noteworthy performance metrics , with an average F1-score of 92.64 % and ROUGE-L score of 96.50 % for attributing synthetic images to synthetic images respective source generation models . The source code of this work will be publicly released at [ URL ]

title: SW3T-IoT : Smart Water Monitoring Based on a Three-Tier IoT Architecture
abstract: The growing impacts of climate change on water resources demand innovative monitoring and management strategies . This paper presents SW3T-IoT , an innovative water monitoring system leveraging Internet of Things ( IoT ) technologies to enhance water resource management under dynamic conditions . SW3T-IoT , an innovative water monitoring system leveraging Internet of Things ( IoT ) technologies to enhance water resource management under dynamic conditions adopts a three-tier architecture — edge , fog , and cloud — integrating a custom-designed LoRa-WDS node optimized for low power consumption and long-term autonomous operation . edge , fog , and cloud collect real-time data on water level , flow , pressure , temperature , and quality from distribution networks and reservoirs . Data are locally processed at edge , then transferred to the cloud for advanced analysis and visualization . A Geographic Information System ( GIS ) enhances spatial awareness and decision-making . To ensure adaptability , SW3T-IoT , an innovative water monitoring system leveraging Internet of Things ( IoT ) technologies to enhance water resource management under dynamic conditions integrates a continual learning ( CL ) framework for Biochemical Oxygen Demand ( BOD ) forecasting . a continual learning ( CL ) framework for Biochemical Oxygen Demand ( BOD ) forecasting allows models to incrementally update with new environmental data without catastrophic forgetting , maintaining accuracy and robustness as water quality dynamics evolve . A hybrid CNN – BiLSTM – Attention model , reinforced with PER , AER , LwF , and EWC strategies , supports adaptive prediction and knowledge retention . SW3T-IoT , an innovative water monitoring system leveraging Internet of Things ( IoT ) technologies to enhance water resource management under dynamic conditions delivers intuitive dashboards for engineers and water managers , providing a holistic , scalable , and intelligent solution for sustainable water resource management .

title: Measuring gentrification through commercial amenities: The case of Paris
abstract: Understanding gentrification in cities remains a significant challenge for sustainable planning and for the struggle against inequalities . Change in neighbourhoods happens holistically and stems from a multitude of different factors . Here , we introduce an original measure to tackle the challenge of deciphering change : the Amenity Configuration Index ( ACI ) . an original measure to tackle the challenge of deciphering change : the Amenity Configuration Index ( ACI ) separates neighbourhoods depending on neighbourhoods present commercial amenities . we apply an original measure to tackle the challenge of deciphering change : the Amenity Configuration Index ( ACI ) to Paris from 2014 to 2023 and argue that we are locating consumers with differentiated spending levels by proxy . we show that we index relates strongly to local socio-economic conditions and reflects known Parisian realities . we approach provides a near real-time and scalable tool to monitor urban dynamics and allows for an adapted approach to the holistic issue of gentrification .

title: A Planar Rectenna at 2.45 GHz With Circular Polarization for Wireless Power Transmission
abstract: This study presents the design and analysis of a compact circularly polarized rectenna operating at 2.45 GHz , intended for wireless power transmission ( WPT ) applications . a compact circularly polarized rectenna operating at 2.45 GHz , intended for wireless power transmission ( WPT ) applications includes a 2x2 patch array antenna and a voltage doubler rectifier circuit , both optimized to maximize RF-DC conversion efficiency . Simulations , carried out using ADS and another electromagnetic solver show excellent performance with a reflection coefficient ( S₁₁ ) below-10 dB , an axial ratio below 3 dB in the ISM band , and a maximum gain of 11.14 dB for a 2x2 patch array antenna . The RT5880 substrate ( εᵣ = 2.2 , tanδ = 0.0009 ) and 35 μm metal thickness were chosen to balance performance and simplicity of design . The results show an RF-DC conversion efficiency of up to 73.69 % at 27 dBm , confirming the potential of a compact circularly polarized rectenna operating at 2.45 GHz , intended for wireless power transmission ( WPT ) applications for mobile WPT applications such as powering drones .

title: Influence of the nutriome, exposome, and microbiome of breast milk on early growth in infants in the context of prematurity.
abstract: Introduction : The health benefits of breastfeeding for premature infants are clear , including improved postnatal growth , but the underlying mechanisms remain complex due to the rich composition of breast milk . Objective : To explore the interaction between breast milk nutrients , breast milk microbiological components , and breast milk level of exposure to environmental chemicals in relation to the growth of premature infants . Patients / Methods : In the prospective LACTACOL cohort ( NCT014930 ) , Z-scores for discharge weight and lean mass were measured in 137 exclusively breastfed premature infants . breast milk was analyzed to characterize the nutriome , using targeted ( amino acids and fatty acids and derivatives ) and untargeted ( lipidome ) approaches , the exposome ( persistent organic pollutants , POPs ) , and the microbiome ( 16s rRNA sequencing ) . A correlation analysis between the three components of breast milk followed by an e-learning analysis identified the molecular determinants of early growth in children . Results : the nutriome appeared to be the main contributor to postnatal growth in premature infants . Choline-containing lipids ( sphingolipids , phosphatidylcholines , and plasmalogens ) contributed positively to weight Z-score . Nervonic acid-enriched sphingomyelin was positively associated with lean mass Z-score , in contrast to oxylipins . the exposome ( persistent organic pollutants , POPs ) showed complex effects : the dioxin-like compound 1,2,3,7,8-PeCDD had a negative impact on weight , while polychlorinated biphenyl 123 positively influenced weight and lean mass gain . Brominated flame retardants were associated with a decrease in lean mass Z-score . Despite a minor impact , the microbiome varied with POP levels and postnatal growth tertiles , highlighting co-dependencies between milk components . Conclusions : This pilot study provides new evidence on the interaction of the the nutriome , the exposome ( persistent organic pollutants , POPs ) , and microbiome of breast milk and the nutriome , exposome , and microbiome of breast milk joint influence on the early development of premature infants .

title: Biosynthetic studies on a promising anticancer drug, cryptophycin-1 produced by the cyanobacterium Nostoc sp. ATCC 53789
abstract: Cryptophycins are a group of cyclodepsipeptides that are among the most potent anti-proliferative agents ever described . The parent compound , cryptophycin-1 was isolated from two Nostoc cyanobacterial strains ( ATCC 53789 and GSV224 ) , and it binds tightly to tubulin , inhibits microtubule polymerization , and depolymerizes preformed microtubules in vitro . it is a powerful antitumor agent and shows cytotoxicity against several cancer cell-lines , with IC50 in the pM range . Our aim is to microbiologically produce cryptophycin-1 using a Nostoc cyanobacterium ( ATCC 53789 ) , as a green alternative to chemical synthesis . However , the use of cyanobacteria as biological factories for the production of a metabolite is not straightforward : the culture of photosynthetic microorganisms requires specific adjustments and the cryptophycin-1 biosynthesis is complex ( involving polyketide synthases PKS , non-ribosomal peptide synthases NRPS , hybrids thereof and tailoring enzymes ) and not fully understood . An issue relies on the complete description of the biosynthesis of cryptophycin-1 . Indeed , the actual precursor is derived from phenylalanine but the actual precursor structure is unknown . In this work , Our developed the qualitative and quantitative analysis of cryptophycin-1 production directly from the cyanobacterial culture medium . Through isotopic incorporation experiments , Our have precisely identified the origin of the atoms incorporated into cryptophycin-1 .

title: Prediction Fairness with respect to Sensitive Networks
abstract: Algorithmic fairness is an important axis of ethical AI . We propose a novel approach to assess and mitigate the unfairness of classification models with respect to a given sensitive networks , such as social networks or professional networks . In this context , the fairness of a model correspond to the absence of correlation between the model predictions and the existence / absence of relations in a given sensitive networks , such as social networks or professional networks . We formalize criteria based on known concepts of group fairness using the assortativity coefficient , and We derive a regularization framework to mitigate the unfairness of a supervised model . Preliminary experiments on real-world case studies suggests that a regularization framework to mitigate the unfairness of a supervised model can be useful to explore the trade-off between accuracy and fairness . However , the use of GNN architectures may be required to find good compromises .

title: Exploring Ownership of an Avatar's Cat Ears through Visual, Auditory, and Haptic Multimodal Feedback
abstract: Extensions of body parts that humans are not innately endowed with , such as supernumerary limbs , have attracted attention . Since Extensions of body parts that humans are not innately endowed with , such as supernumerary limbs resemble existing ones , Extensions of body parts that humans are not innately endowed with , such as supernumerary limbs movements and sensations can be inferred from existing ones . However , the sense of ownership for imaginary body parts , such as cat ears , which humans have never possessed , has not been sufficiently investigated . This paper proposes an experiment to examine the changing sense of ownership of cat ears , a body part that humans are not innately endowed with , through multimodal feedback that integrates visual , auditory , and haptic stimuli . Using an avatar with cat ears attached to the top of the head , we suggest presenting visual stimuli of an avatar with cat ears attached to the top of the head cat ears along with spatially congruent auditory and haptic feedback to enhance the sense of ownership over imaginary cat ears .

title: Biomechanically consistent real-time action recognition for human-robot interaction
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for real-time human action recognition in industrial contexts , using standard 2D cameras . We introduce a complete pipeline for robust and real-time estimation of human joint kinematics , input to a temporally smoothed Transformer-based network , for action recognition . We rely on a new dataset including 11 subjects performing various actions , to evaluate We approach . Unlike most of the literature that relies on joint center positions ( JCP ) and is offline , We uses biomechanical prior , eg . joint angles , for fast and robust real-time recognition . Besides , joint angles make a novel framework for real-time human action recognition in industrial contexts , using standard 2D cameras agnostic to sensor and subject poses as well as to anthropometric differences , and ensure robustness across environments and subjects . We proposed learning model outperforms the best baseline model , running also in real-time , along various metrics . Our proposed learning model achieves 88 % accuracy and shows great generalization ability , for subjects not facing the cameras . Finally , We demonstrate the robustness and usefulness of a novel framework for real-time human action recognition in industrial contexts , using standard 2D cameras , through an online interaction experiment , with a simulated robot controlled in real-time via the recognized actions .

title: Design of Robust Multi-Robot Formations for Collaborative Localization and Navigation
abstract: This thesis focuses on the joint navigation of a heterogeneous aerial / terrestrial multi-robot system . The objective is to ensure accurate localization of a target robot by using inter-robot range measurements to reconstruct a target robot position . This thesis focuses on the optimal placement of collaborative robots around a target robot to be localized in the presence of measurement noise with heterogeneous standard deviations . A local robustness analysis is then performed on collaborative robots to assess collaborative robots sensitivity in the presence of positioning errors of collaborative robots . This allows us to state the necessary and sufficient conditions on collaborative robots in order to maximize collaborative robots robustness against positioning errors of collaborative robots . An experimental scenario is implemented and confirms the value of robust formations in the presence of positioning uncertainties . In addition , the experimental results highlight the importance of accurately estimating the standard deviation of UWB sensor noise to improve the accuracy of a target robot localization . Finally , a formation control architecture based on nonlinear predictive control is formulated and implemented experimentally . The cost function incorporates the necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality in order to maximize localization accuracy while ensuring obstacle avoidance and target robot tracking .

title: Load balancing in the mail sorting process: a case study at the French postal company La Poste
abstract: This paper investigates a load balancing problem within the context of postal sorting operations at La Poste , the French postal service . Faced with declining mail volumes , La Poste , the French postal service must reorganize La Poste , the French postal service processes to maintain service quality and operational efficiency . Mail sorting is modeled as a Simple Assembly Line Balancing Problem ( SALBP-2 ) , where mail items ( tasks ) are assigned to containers ( stations ) in a way that minimizes load imbalances while respecting precedence constraints . precedence constraints take the form of independent chains , as each mail route follows a fixed delivery sequence . We propose three resolution methods : an exact approach based on a Mixed Integer Linear Programming ( MILP ) formulation , a metaheuristic algorithm based on simulated annealing , and a fast heuristic designed for industrial deployment which exploits the precedence constraint structure for faster convergence . a metaheuristic algorithm based on simulated annealing and a fast heuristic designed for industrial deployment which exploits the precedence constraint structure for faster convergence are tested on academic and real-world datasets much larger than those commonly used in the literature . In order to use academic and real-world datasets much larger than those commonly used in the literature several times a day , the resolution method needs to be fast in terms of calculation time . Due to a fast heuristic designed for industrial deployment which exploits the precedence constraint structure for faster convergence strong performance and low computation time , a fast heuristic designed for industrial deployment which exploits the precedence constraint structure for faster convergence has been implemented on industrial platforms at La Poste , the French postal service and is now used daily .
keywords: precedence constraint structure for faster convergence

title: A Novel 3D Hemispherical Reconfigurable Antenna with Switchable Radiation Patterns Using a Butler Matrix
abstract: This paper presents a compact 3D hemispherical reconfigurable antenna for sub-6 GHz 5 G applications . a compact 3D hemispherical reconfigurable antenna for sub-6 GHz 5 G applications integrates a four-element Vivaldi antenna array with a 4×4 Butler matrix and a PIN-diode switching network to enable beam steering toward three primary directions . Measurements confirm a stable gain of 4.7 dBi , radiation efficiency above 85 % , and hemispherical coverage of about 67 % in both elevation and azimuthal planes . The compact and low-power architecture makes a compact 3D hemispherical reconfigurable antenna for sub-6 GHz 5 G applications attractive for dynamic wireless environments .

title: Fresnel Lens Antenna with smooth phase compensation in the 220 -330 GHz band using highly cost-effective manufacturing process
abstract: In this work is presented the performance of a Fresnel Lens Antenna ( FLA ) in the 220-330 GHz band for future wireless communication systems with high-data-rate . The lens of the system is manufactured using an innovative and highly low-cost process , based on a thermally pressed foam material . an innovative and highly low-cost process , based on a thermally pressed foam material permits the manufacturing of fully dielectric , inhomogeneous lenses made from a single material , allowing smooth phase compensation the wavefront distortion introduced by a primary feed , in this case a standard horn antenna , realized with electric discharge machining . a primary feed , in this case a standard horn antenna , realized with electric discharge machining is first designed then experimentally validated , demonstrating excellent agreement between simulation and measurements in terms of radiation patterns and gain . The lens of the system is then fabricated , confirming the effectiveness of the pressed foam approach over the 220-330 GHz band . a Fresnel Lens Antenna ( FLA ) , achieves a narrow beam-width of 2 ° beam-width and a peak gain of 32 dBi , and is implemented using three stacked sub-lenses .
