title: Improving Vulnerable Road-Users Detection through Hybrid Collaborative Perception and Detection Refinement
abstract: Ensuring the safety of autonomous vehicles in complex urban environments critically depends on accurate 3D object detection . While LiDAR sensors provide reliable depth information , LiDAR sensors effectiveness is limited by sparsity at long distances and occlusions , particularly in intersection scenarios . Collaborative perception addresses these challenges by enabling information sharing among vehicles and infrastructure sensors , with intermediate fusion offering a balance between communication efficiency and detection accuracy . However , existing collaborative perception frameworks exhibit a notable performance gap between detecting vehicles and vulnerable road users such as cyclists and pedestrians . In this work , we propose a novel hybrid collaboration framework designed to reduce a notable performance gap between detecting vehicles and vulnerable road users such as cyclists and pedestrians . a novel hybrid collaboration framework designed to reduce this gap leverages late-stage information from communicating agents to augment the ego agent 's point cloud , then applies a standard intermediate fusion strategy , followed by a refinement stage that further improves the detection accuracy of various objects . Experiments on the Mixed Signals dataset demonstrate that a novel hybrid collaboration framework designed to reduce this gap sets a new state-of-the-art in the detection of vulnerable road users in urban V2X scenarios

title: Failures and Cyberattacks on IoT Devices: Interactions and Challenges.
abstract: The internet of things ( IoT ) has gained significant interest since the miniaturization of electronics , the development of low power networks and low power networks educed costs . However , while the literature flourishes with The internet of things ( IoT ) applications across multiple domains , such as industry , home automation , healthcare , and military operations , security practitioners have raised serious concerns about The internet of things ( IoT ) vulnerabilities . By nature The internet of things ( IoT ) is made up of low-power physical components sending large amount of data to a network , with the objective of providing application specific services . However , what makes The internet of things ( IoT ) devices unique ( i.e. low-power , heterogeneity , positioned in the environment ) also makes IoT devices particularly vulnerable to cyberattacks and failures . For instance , the lack of computational power of The internet of things ( IoT ) nodes reduces the possibility of implementing strong attack mitigations , unlike personal computers or servers . Additionally , by installing IoT devices in outdoor environments , IoT devices become vulnerable to harsh conditions and may deteriorate faster . Such environmental faults may then cause critical failures in the The internet of things ( IoT ) network , potentially triggering cascading effects . The rapid growth of The internet of things ( IoT ) necessitates the identification of all possible vulnerabilities , all possible vulnerabilities sources , and the implementation of robust mitigations . In recent years , significant efforts have been made to identify and mitigate security concerns within The internet of things ( IoT ) Numerous academic and industrial works focus on addressing security for particular The internet of things ( IoT ) layers [ 5 ] . On the other hand , the identification and mitigation of faults and failures impacting The internet of things ( IoT ) devices have been less documented . This is problematic , as underestimating reliability threats might lead to serious hazards . However , we believe that the greatest threats come from undetected interactions between failures and cyberattacks . The safety-cybersecurity-reliability interactions have been documented by numerous works in the literature . numerous works in the literature highlight the potentially catastrophic effects that interactions between failures and attacks might have on safety . To the best of our knowledge , the identification of interactions between The internet of things ( IoT )-specific failures and cyberattacks has not yet been studied . This leads to an incomplete knowledge of all existing threats that might impact The internet of things ( IoT ) devices . Having a partial knowledge of all existing threats that might impact IoT devices leaves a large number of vulnerabilities in products , waiting to be exploited . Therefore , we will present the results of a systematic literature review ( SLR ) dedicated to identifying all the known threats that may impact The internet of things ( IoT ) devices . Specifically , we performed one SLR to identify all failures impacting The internet of things ( IoT ) devices and a second to identify all cyberattacks targeting The internet of things ( IoT ) devices . we also analyzed the possible interactions between faults and attacks to provide a comprehensive knowledge of threats at the The internet of things ( IoT ) perception layer . With this poster , we will briefly present the process of the review , and highlight the major findings of we work .

title: An AI-Based Sensorless Force Feedback in Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Surgery
abstract: ( 1 ) Background : Most robotic MIS platforms lack native haptic feedback , leaving surgeons to infer tissue loads from vision alone — an especially risky limitation in esophageal procedures . ( 2 ) Methods : We develop a sensorless , image-only force-estimation pipeline that maps endoscopic video to tool – tissue forces using a lightweight EfficientNetV2B0 CNN . a sensorless , image-only force-estimation pipeline that maps endoscopic video to tool – tissue forces using a lightweight EfficientNetV2B0 CNN is trained on 9691 labeled frames from in vitro esophageal experiments and validated against an FT300 load cell . For intraoperative feasibility , a sensorless , image-only force-estimation pipeline that maps endoscopic video to tool – tissue forces using a lightweight EfficientNetV2B0 CNN is deployed as a plug-in on PARA-SILSROB , consuming the existing laparoscope feed and driving a commercial haptic device . The runtime processes every 10th frame of a 60 FPS stream ( ≈6 Hz updates ) with ~15–20 ms per-prediction latency . ( 3 ) Results : On held-out tests , a sensorless , image-only force-estimation pipeline that maps endoscopic video to tool – tissue forces using a lightweight EfficientNetV2B0 CNN achieves MAE = 0.017 N and MSE = 0.0004 N2 , outperforming a recurrent CNN baseline while maintaining real-time performance on commodity hardware . Integrated evaluations confirm stable operation at the deployed update rate and low latency compatible with closed-loop haptics . ( 4 ) Conclusions : By avoiding distal force sensors and preserving sterile workflow , the approach is readily translatable and retrofit-friendly for current robotic platforms . The results support the practical feasibility of real-time , sensorless force feedback for robotic esophagectomy and related MIS tasks , with potential to reduce tissue trauma and enhance operative safety .

title: Persistent Luminescence in Highly Nonstoichiometric GAGG Garnets Gd 3+x [Al 2 Ga 3 ] 1‐x/5 O 12 (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.6) Doped with Ce 3+ /Cr 3+
abstract: The gadolinium garnet Gd 3 Al 2 Ga 3 O 12 co‐doped with Ce 3 + and Cr 3 + ( GAGG‐Ce , Cr ) has been widely studied due to The gadolinium garnet Gd 3 Al 2 Ga 3 O 12 unusual bright yellow long‐lasting persistent luminescence properties . Here , rapid containerless melt‐quenching is used as part of a two‐step glass‐crystallisation synthesis process to obtain a new highly nonstoichiometric form of The gadolinium garnet Gd 3 Al 2 Ga 3 O 12 , of composition Gd 3+x [ Al 2 Ga 3 ] 1‐x/5 O 12 with 0 ≤ x ≤ 0.6 ( ns‐GAGG ) . For compositions x > 0 , powder X‐ray diffraction analysis confirms that excess Gd 3 + is accommodated at the Al 3 + /Ga 3 + sublattice in octahedral coordination , by substituting up to 30 % of these sites . substituting complexifies the local structure of the garnet host , which is shown to influence certain luminescence properties in the analogous highly nonstoichiometric Y 3+x Al 5‐x O 12 ( 0 < x < 0.4 ) and Gd 3+x Al 5‐x O 12 ( 0 < x < 0.6 ) systems . Co‐doping ns‐GAGG with Ce 3 + and Cr 3 + produces green‐yellow persistent luminescence when x = 0 , which undergoes a redshift to yellow‐orange as the Gd 3 + content increases to x = 0.4 . However , Co‐doping does not strongly affect the afterglow kinetics . These results demonstrate an effective and high‐precision way of decoupling color and kinetics in persistent luminescent garnets , which is usually hard to achieve using the standard stoichiometric material engineering approach .

title: Human Manure as Activism: Composting Excrement as an Alternative Approach to Soil Fertilization
abstract: Following a period of intense interest in the use of human excrement as fertilizer in nineteenth-century Europe , this type of manure was largely sidelined by the rise of synthetic fertilizers . However , interest in human excreta as manure has seen a resurgence in recent decades thanks to the growing use of composting toilets at the domestic level , particularly in France . In this chapter , we explore how the practice of returning human excrement to the soil relates to agricultural production at different points in recent history . Specifically , we examine how the practice of returning human excrement to the soil provide a basis for a political and economic critique of the prevailing extractive model and serve as a means of inquiry into the ( re)production of soil fertility .

title: Coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems and applications
abstract: This paper proposes a procedure for constructing a coercive ISS-Lyapunov functional for regular infinite-dimensional systems that are exponentially stable . Indeed , as already known , Lyapunov functionals for infinite-dimensional systems does not need to be \color{black } coercive . Under the assumption that there exists an exactly observable output , we are able to modify any non-coercive Lyapunov functional into a coercive one . We also discuss the potential applications of such a Lyapunov functional in singular perturbation theory and output regulation . The results are illustrated on a non-trivial equation , namely , a linearized version of the Korteweg-de Vries equation .

title: Finite Volume Discretization Preserving Energy Estimates for a Compressible THM Model
abstract: In this work , we investigate a Thermo-Hydro-Mechanical ( THM ) model describing compressible flow in deformable porous media . Such models play a significant role in various areas of geomechanics , with applications ranging from underground energy storage to oil and gas reservoir engineering . The simulations of THM models are essential for the analysis and design of safe and efficient energy storage cavities . we begin by presenting the mathematical formulation of a Thermo-Hydro-Mechanical ( THM ) model describing compressible flow in deformable porous media . First , we derive energy estimates for a Thermo-Hydro-Mechanical ( THM ) model describing compressible flow in deformable porous media . Next , we focus in particular on the development of numerical discretizations that preserve the energy estimates of the continuous system at the discrete level . To this end , we employ the backward Euler scheme for the time discretization together with the finite volume two-point flux approximation ( TPFA ) method for the spatial discretization . Numerical experiments are presented to validate the proposed approach and to illustrate the proposed approach accuracy , efficiency , and robustness .
keywords: thermo hydro mechanical thm model energy estimates compressible flow finite volume method
finite volume two-point flux approximation ( tpfa)

title: FC-CONAN: An Exhaustively Paired Dataset for Robust Evaluation of Retrieval Systems
abstract: Hate speech ( HS ) is a critical issue in online discourse , and one promising strategy to counter Hate speech ( HS ) is through the use of counter-narratives ( CNs ) . Datasets linking HS with CNs are essential for advancing counterspeech research . However , even flagship resources like CONAN ( Chung et al . , 2019 ) annotate only a sparse subset of all possible HS-CN pairs , limiting evaluation . We introduce FC-CONAN ( Fully Connected CONAN ) , the first dataset created by exhaustively considering all combinations of 45 English HS messages and 129 CNs . A two-stage annotation process involving nine annotators and four validators produces four partitions-Diamond , Gold , Silver , and Bronze-that balance reliability and scale . None of the labeled pairs overlap with CONAN ( Chung et al . , 2019 ) , uncovering hundreds of previously unlabelled positives . FC-CONAN ( Fully Connected CONAN ) , the first dataset created by exhaustively considering all combinations of 45 English HS messages and 129 CNs enables more faithful evaluation of counterspeech retrieval systems and facilitates detailed error analysis . FC-CONAN ( Fully Connected CONAN ) , the first dataset created by exhaustively considering all combinations of 45 English HS messages and 129 CNs is publicly available 12 .
keywords: hate speech counter narrative exhaustive annotation fully paired dataset dataset creation benchmark creation quality graded partition label sparsity lower bound bias retrieval system evaluation recommender systems information retrieval bias in evaluation evaluation metrics annotation quality argumentation counterspeech natural language processing nlp

title: Vesicle impact electrochemistry shows the irreversible destructive effect of rhamnolipid biosurfactants on living cells
abstract: Amperometric measurements coupled to optical microscopy monitoring are used to detect the exocytosis process of a living cell in the presence of rhamnolipids in the medium . Chromaffin and pheochromocytoma cells are studied in the presence of the biosurfactant , without stimulation , in order to quantify the release of vesicular content at the ultramicroelectrode . The microscopy imaging of the target single cell during the amperometric measurement allows for the observation of the progressive disruption of the target single cell in the presence of rhamnolipids in the medium . The data collected show the irreversible action of rhamnolipids on the living cell , from the beginning of vesicular release , measured by the appearance of current spikes in amperometry , to cell death monitored by microscopy . An important change in cellular structure is observed in the microscopy images of the target single cell , suggesting that the membrane is dissolved and ruptured , or becomes very permeable and swells . This initial work shows that the presence of rhamnolipids in the medium leads to stimulation of exocytosis , followed by premature cell death .

title: Mobilization and Dissent On Blogs and Social Media
abstract: In Russia , digital technologies have impacted the world of activism and ways of protesting . The extent of impacted is of such global magnitude that reflection on the internet and digital social networks is now essential to any research on activism ( Desroches 2011 ) . Like other aspects of the social world , collective mobilization has increasingly been mediated by computerized technological media , especially on handheld devices , even in the most remote parts of Russia . Most protesters have moved from emails , mailing lists , and blogs ( LiveJournal ) to Web 2.0 systems ( social networking sites and social media such as YouTube ) . Users and types of use differ : Facebook , Instagram , Telegram , and X ( formerly Twitter ) are the main means of communication for political activists and urban and educated populations , while the Russian networks VKontakte and Odnoklassniki remain the main medium for laypeople and ordinary citizens .

title: Integrated resonant structure for colloidal dispersion stability: Development of a resonant optical zetameter
abstract: Long-term storage of colloidal solutions presents significant challenges in maintaining the physical and mechanical properties of manufactured products over extended periods . Ensuring stability is critical for agro-alimentary products , pharmaceutical formulations , and petroleum applications to preserve product quality and longevity during storage . Monitoring the stability of colloidal dispersions is essential for anticipating potential degradation over time . This study explores the evaluation of stability criteria using quasi-surface resonant analysis . Specifically , the zeta potential of colloidal solutions is investigated via resonant optical parameter , the Free Spectral Range ( FSR ) , to distinguish between stable and unstable dispersions . For investigated , sensors based on organic UV210 Micro-Resonators ( MRs ) were fabricated using deep UV photolithography . organic UV210 Micro-Resonators ( MRs ) were integrated into an optical test platform , enabling real-time data collection with a spectrometer and dedicated MATLAB processing . This study focuses on black carbon nanopowders dispersed in water and in water plus an anionic surfactant ( Sodium Dodecyl Sulfate , SDS ) . The findings show that unstable solutions exhibit an increasing FSR over time , which is indicative of sedimentation , whereas stable dispersions maintain a constant FSR . The findings are validated through complementary rheological and zeta potential measurements , establishing a clear correlation between FSR variations and colloidal dispersion stability . This study demonstrates the potential of resonant optical measurements as a novel tool for assessing colloidal dispersion stability , functioning as a " zeta-meter " on a surfacic platform .

title: Investigation of marennine quality throughout the main culture phases of Haslea ostrearia in a membrane photobioreactor
abstract: Marennine is a blue pigment excreted by the diatom Haslea ostrearia . Marennine is renowned for Marennine antioxidant and antibacterial properties , which have raised research interest . The standard method for obtaining Marennine is by harvesting the supernatant from cultures of the diatom Haslea ostrearia and applying a double ultrafiltration approach . Marennine concentration is then assessed by another standard method ( UV-visible spectrophotometry ) . The resulting “ blue water ” may however contain Marennine along with a variety of other molecules , not detectable by spectrophotometry . As changes in supernatant composition are likely to occur depending on culture conditions and modes of operation , it is wondered whether changes in supernatant composition affects the marennine extract ’s quality . This work aims to assess such fluctuations across the exponential , stationary , and senescent phases of a the diatom Haslea ostrearia culture in a membrane photobioreactor ( MPBR ) . Antioxidant and antibacterial bioassays , in conjunction with spectral analyses of marennine extracts , were used to characterize marennine extracts . Results showed that marennine production peaked during exponential growth phase of a H. ostrearia culture in a membrane photobioreactor ( MPBR ) and that the resulting extract exhibited the highest antibacterial activity . Antioxidant activity was however unaffected throughout the different growth phases , being solely a function of the marennine concentration as assessed by a double ultrafiltration approach .

title: Quantitative assessment of the validity range of radiative transfer approximations of acoustic wave energies in unbounded and bounded random media
abstract: This paper reports a series of numerical experiments comparing solutions of the 3D acoustic wave equation in a ( randomly-fluctuating ) heterogeneous medium to solutions of the radiative transfer equation . Parameters of the two equations are first chosen such that the radiative transfer solution is expected to provide an accurate approximation of the energy of the wave ( weak-coupling regime ) , and the comparisons are excellent . Further simulations indicate that radiative transfer provides accurate approximations not only in the expected regime , but also for a wide range of frequencies and fluctuation levels of the propagation medium parameters , as long as the background velocity is appropriately selected . A particular attention is devoted to comparing wave solutions and radiative transfer approximations close to boundaries , where the accuracy of the radiative transfer equation has not been evaluated before .

title: LLM as a Guide: an Approach for Unsupervised Economic Relation Discovery in Administrative Documents
abstract: Effective relation extraction ( RE ) from unstructured text is critical , especially when the target relations are unknown . In this case , we can leverage Large Language Models ( LLMs ) to perform Effective relation extraction ( RE ) from unstructured text . In this paper , we present an LLM as a guide approach for identifying economic relations . This novel methodology , based on sentence clustering and an LLM , is used to identify previously unknown economic relations in French administrative documents . This novel methodology , based on sentence clustering and an LLM addresses the challenge of extracting actionable knowledge without predefined relation labels . we evaluate we approach on French and English RE datasets , demonstrating high precision and recall in detecting previously unknown relations . we results suggest that clustering and LLM-based methods can effectively discover and categorize economic relations , with potential applications to private corpora .

title: Invited Paper: On the Equivalence of Snapshot/Append Objects and Broadcast Abstractions under Byzantine Failures
abstract: Abstractions play a central role in distributed computing , as Abstractions capture essential synchronization properties . Equivalence results among abstractions clarify abstractions relative computational power . While many such equivalences are well established in crash-prone systems , far less is known about Byzantine-prone environments , where faulty processes may behave arbitrarily . This paper revisits the equivalence landscape in Byzantine systems , with a particular focus on shared registers and broadcast abstractions . We establish three new reductions . Specifically , We prove that the broadcast abstraction called Byzantine Set-Constrained Delivery Broadcast ( BSCD-Broadcast ) can implement a Snapshot / Append object and vice versa ( I.e. , a two-way reduction ) , and that the FIFO variant of the renowned Byzantine Reliable Broadcast ( BRB-Broadcast ) can implement the broadcast abstraction called Byzantine Set-Constrained Delivery Broadcast ( BSCD-Broadcast ) under a majority of correct processes . Interestingly , this assumption mirrors the one required in crash-prone systems for a similar transformation .

title: An abstract setting for the Fredholm backstepping transformation: self-adjoint case
abstract: In this paper we address the existence of a Fredholm backstepping transformation for self-adjoint operators A. we prove , under assumptions on the control operator B and A , that there exists a Fredholm backstepping transformation for operators A of order strictly greater than 1 . One of the main contribution of this paper is to exhibit the underlying isomorphism used to construct T . the underlying isomorphism used to construct T allows to deduce sharp estimates on ∥T ∥ L(H;H ) and ∥T-1 ∥ L(H;H ) with respect to the damping parameter λ > 0 . sharp estimates on ∥T ∥ L(H;H ) and ∥T-1 ∥ L(H;H ) with respect to the damping parameter λ > 0 allow we to prove the finite-time stabilization for a large class of self-adjoint operators .

title: 13C position-specific isotopic analysis of fatty acid methyl esters using NMR with intramolecular isotopic referencing
abstract: Among stable isotope measurement strategies at natural abundance , Position-Specific Isotope Analysis ( PSIA ) is a valuable approach for food authentication and metabolism understanding . In this context , carbon-13 Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectroscopy ( irm-13C NMR ) has emerged as an efficient tool It enables the determination of the absolute 13C intramolecular composition ( δ13Ci ) when all NMR signals are well-resolved and the global 13C content ( δ13Cg ) is known . However , in the case of fatty acids with eight carbons or more , It can only resolve six carbon signals . δ13Ci values are thus not attainable without specialized methods . To overcome resolve , we developed a novel methodology that leverages the concept of isotopic intramolecular referencing by using the methoxy group in the fatty acid methyl esters ( FAMEs ) as a reference . we thus determined δ13Ci values with improved trueness and repeatability without requiring δ13Cg measurement . Combining determined with the acquisition of 13C NMR spectra using an adiabatic INEPT pulse sequence offered a more time-efficient , sample-efficient , and sustainable approach , rendering the entire process greener . we successfully applied a novel methodology that leverages the concept of isotopic intramolecular referencing by using the methoxy group in the fatty acid methyl esters ( FAMEs ) as a reference to FAMEs from butter and coconut oil . Subsequent studies will evaluate the effectiveness of the novel isotopomic biomarkers derived from a novel methodology that leverages the concept of isotopic intramolecular referencing by using the methoxy group in the fatty acid methyl esters ( FAMEs ) as a reference in authenticating foodstuffs and elucidating metabolic differences among fatty acids . Additionally , a novel methodology that leverages the concept of isotopic intramolecular referencing by using the methoxy group in the fatty acid methyl esters ( FAMEs ) as a reference will be of interest for studying other molecules and isotopes .

title: A generalized hybrid machine learning framework for predicting biohydrogen production via dark fermentation of organic wastes
abstract: The rising global demand for sustainable energy has directed significant attention towards biohydrogen production via dark fermentation of organic wastes . Accurate yield prediction is crucial for optimizing process conditions and enhancing overall process . This study aims to develop a robust and interpretable predictive framework that integrates kinetic modeling with a hybrid Bayesian Optimization-Artificial Neural Network ( BO-ANN ) approach for precise biohydrogen yield prediction . The core novelty lies in representing each substrate not as a simple category , but by each substrate quantitative kinetic parameters from the Modified Gompertz equation , providing a biologically meaningful input . A comprehensive database compiled from the literature incorporates key process variables , including temperature , pH , residence time , and substrate concentration , along with kinetic parameters from the Modified Gompertz equation characterizing each substrate . The BO algorithm was employed to optimize the ANN architecture , and 5-fold cross-validation was used to evaluate model generalization ability . The proposed hybrid model achieved outstanding predictive performance ( R² = 0.9980 , RMSE = 0.0117 , MAE = 0.0062 ) , confirming The proposed hybrid model accuracy and robustness . Furthermore , SHAP analysis and correlation metrics provided interpretable insights into feature contributions , particularly the relevance of kinetic descriptors . Overall , The proposed hybrid model offers a scalable , interpretable , and biologically grounded tool to improve predictive accuracy and support the design of more efficient and sustainable biohydrogen production systems .

title: Enhancing Photovoltaic Performance through Water-Based Cooling: A Comprehensive Review of Passive and Active Techniques
abstract: The use of renewable energy is being advanced in large part by photovoltaic ( PV ) panels . photovoltaic ( PV ) panels effectiveness is severely reduced by high working temperatures , though , underscoring the necessity for efficient cooling systems to improve performance and sustainability . Photovoltaic panels have a decline in efficiency when operating temperatures increase , with crystalline silicon cells exhibiting a 0.45-0.6 % reduction in efficiency for each degree Celsius rise . This study offers a comprehensive assessment of water-based cooling strategies , recognised as highly effective methods for improving photovoltaic performance and sustainability . water-based cooling strategies , recognised as highly effective methods for improving photovoltaic performance and sustainability are categorised as passive systems ( immersion , floating photovoltaic , evaporative cooling ) and active systems ( water spraying , photovoltaic / thermal collectors , micro-channels , jet impingement , geothermal exchangers ) . Reported findings indicate that water-based cooling can reduce PV module temperatures by up to 46 % , enhance electrical efficiency by 6-38 % , and increase power output by as much as 47 % , depending upon the design . Active systems provide superior cooling but elevate operational expenses ; passive systems are more straightforward and energy efficient . This paper presents the inaugural comprehensive review exclusively addressing water-based photovoltaic cooling , supplemented with a section on hybrid water cooling systems that integrates technical performance with a succinct assessment of the economic and environmental impacts . This paper delineates critical research deficiencies , such as long-term reliability and urban integration , while providing strategic recommendations for the advancement of more sustainable photovoltaic systems .

title: Topochemical synthesis of lanthanide phosphor-doped La2O2S with a metastable orthorhombic polymorph
abstract: The layered oxysulfide La₂O₂S is well known as a host matrix for a wide range of luminescent applications over the past five decades . While La₂O₂S adopts a hexagonal primitive ( hP ) lattice as the lowest-energy polymorph , we recently discovered a metastable form of La₂O₂S with an orthorhombic A-centred lattice ( oA ) through the topochemical deintercalation of sulfur atoms from the La₂O₂S precursor . Compared to the conventional structure of hP-La₂O₂S containing a single inequivalent lanthanum environment , a metastable form of La₂O₂S with an orthorhombic A-centred lattice ( oA ) is characterized by the presence of two inequivalent lanthanum environments . This paper reports on the preparation and optical characterisation of Ce-, Pr-, and Eu-doped oA-La₂O₂S phases . The principal contributions to the luminescence spectra of Ce-, Pr-, and Eu-doped oA-La₂O₂S phases are situated in the green , green and red , and red regions of the visible spectrum for Ce , Pr-, and Eu , respectively . By contrast , the emissions observed for the corresponding doped hP-La₂O₂S phases occur in the violet , green and red , and orange regions , respectively .

title: Development of a smart experimental system for the measure and manipulation of the hydrodynamic state of a water tank with immersed bodies
abstract: This work presents the development of a novel tool for biologists to investigate how hydrodynamic signals generated by swimming fish influence the behavior of nearby specimens . Two information sources are leveraged : video recordings of laboratory experiments and pressure sensors sensitiveto the disturbances generated by the motion of a swimming fish . Using artificial intelligence , apipeline has been developed to automatically generate digital twin Computational Fluid Dynamics ( CFD ) simulations from video data , offering a low-fidelity but spatially rich estimation of the hydrodynamic state . Data fusion techniques , currently in an exploratory phase , aim to integrate digital twin Computational Fluid Dynamics ( CFD ) simulations with sensor data for a more comprehensive understanding of the tank environment . A custom smart dataset was created to support and evaluate the performance of these methods .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Average and Worst-case Analysis of MIMO Beamforming Loss due to Hardware Impairments
abstract: In this paper , we investigate the impact of hardware impairments in antenna arrays on the beamforming performance of multi-input multi-output ( MIMO ) communication systems . we consider two types of imperfections : per-element gain mismatches and inter-element spacing deviations . we analytically determine the impairment configurations that result in the worst-case degradation . In addition , the analytical expression of the average-case performance is also derived for comparison . Simulation and theoretical results show that the average SNR degradation remains relatively limited , whereas the worst-case scenarios can exhibit substantially higher losses . These findings provide clear insight into the robustness limits of MIMO systems under practical hardware imperfections .

title: Towards Scalable O-RAN Resource Management: Graph-Augmented Proximal Policy Optimization
abstract: Open Radio Access Network ( O-RAN ) architectures enable flexible , scalable , and cost-efficient mobile networks by disaggregating and virtualizing baseband functions . However , this flexibility introduces significant challenges for resource management , requiring joint optimization of functional split selection and virtualized unit placement under dynamic demands and complex topologies . Existing solutions often address functional split selection and virtualized unit placement under dynamic demands and complex topologies separately or lack scalability in large and real-world scenarios . In this work , we propose a novel Graph-Augmented Proximal Policy Optimization ( GPPO ) framework that leverages Graph Neural Networks ( GNNs ) for topology-aware feature extraction and integrates action masking to efficiently navigate the combinatorial decision space . we approach jointly optimizes functional split and placement decisions , capturing the full complexity of O-RAN resource allocation . Extensive experiments on both small-and large-scale O-RAN scenarios demonstrate that Our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines , achieving up to 18 % lower deployment cost and 25 % higher reward in generalization tests , while maintaining perfect reliability . These results highlight the effectiveness and scalability of Our approach for practical O-RAN deployments .

title: A Novel Approach for DoA Estimation of Coherent Sources with Leaky-Wave Antennas
abstract: Leaky-wave antennas ( LWAs ) enable cost-effective DoA estimation but struggle with coherent sources due to Leaky-wave antennas ( LWAs ) non-Vandermonde steering matrix . Thus , this paper proposes a spatially filtered interpolation ( SFI ) method , which first divides the whole field of view into several angular sectors . Then , in each sector , the actual Leaky-wave antennas ( LWAs ) directional matrix is transformed into a Vandermonde matrix while reducing interference from sources in other sectors . Simulation results show the effectiveness of a spatially filtered interpolation ( SFI ) method , which first divides the whole field of view into several angular sectors .

title: Immunomodulation by extracellular vesicles from mature or mesenchymal stem cells in the lymph node microenvironment
abstract: Small extracellular vesicles ( sEV ) with immunomodulatory properties are promising candidates for therapeutic innovation , primarily with the use of mesenchymal stem cells-derived EV ( MSC-EV ) carrying immune regulatory and regenerative signals . Unlike EV produced by differentiated cells , EV from mesenchymal stem cells-derived lack antigen expression required for the induction of long-lasting immune memory ; lack hinders the application of mesenchymal stem cells-derived EV ( MSC-EV ) carrying immune regulatory and regenerative signals to autoimmune and antigen-specific immune diseases . Growing evidence shows that a continuous lymphatic drainage of EV derived from mature cells contributes to the immune surveillance and maintenance of tolerance to self and innocuous foreign antigens . Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune disease caused by the targeted destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic beta cells . EV derived from naïve beta cells ( beta-EV ) have been reported to exert immune-protective effects . Here , we are interested in the mechanisms of immune modulation induced by beta-EV , carrying beta cell auto-antigens , or tolerogenic MSC-EV , on immune responses in the lymph node . For this purpose , sEV from the MIN-6 murine pancreatic beta cell line or from a human BM-MSC immortalised cell line were isolated by tangential flow filtration and size exclusion chromatography . Characterization included NTA , cryo-EM , flow cytometry and protein cargo analyses , in compliance with the MISEV2023 guidelines . sEV function was studied in vitro using an allogenic mixed lymphocyte reaction ( MLR ) . In vivo , sEV injected intradermally were analysed for sEV injected intradermally aptitude to target lymphoid organs : lymph nodes were analysed by imaging with light sheet microscopy and transcriptomic arrays , and in parallel serum cytokines were measured . we found that MIN-6 sEV express an immuno-active cargo , with beta cell antigens as well as molecules involved in cell recruitment , metabolic control , integrin signalling and immune-regulation . In an MLR assay , beta-EV showed a dose-dependent reduction of T lymphocyte proliferation and cytokine secretion , in support of a regulatory function . Moreover , intradermal administration of sEV allows the targeting of secondary lymphoid organs through lymphatic drainage . Targeted transcriptomic analysis revealed significant down-regulation of molecular pathways involved in the recruitment and activation of innate and adaptive immune cells . This ongoing study paves the way for future clinical developments of EV-based antigen-specific immune therapy .

title: Convergence analysis of crack features extraction using conjugate work integral
abstract: Background : The extraction of Williams higher-order terms ( n>1 ) is crucial , since Williams higher-order terms ( n>1 ) control the crack stability and propagation , among other phenomena . Nevertheless , current numerical methods strongly depend on the projection domain and/or are unstable , and thus not suited to analysing experimental data . Purpose : This paper aims to investigate the method based on the Bueckner-Chen conjugate work integral , which provides a bilinear form in which Williams series terms are orthogonal , to retrieve all Williams higher-order coefficients . We reformulate the original path-independent integral into an Equivalent Domain Integral ( EDI ) , more robust when dealing with experimental data or finite element discretisation , and compare the convergence of both approaches . Methods : Williams fields are imposed on a meshed body with decreasing element sizes . The different error sources , i.e. numerical integration , stress interpolation and Finite Element ( FE ) discretisation , are decoupled by applying relevant boundary conditions to the linear elastic problem . Results : Predictably , the error due to FE discretisation is higher than the other types of errors . the Bueckner-Chen conjugate work integral , which provides a bilinear form in which Williams series terms are orthogonal converges markedly faster than the J-integral on the same domain and provides a better approximation of the Stress Intensity Factor ( SIF ) . As expected , an Equivalent Domain Integral ( EDI ) , more robust when dealing with experimental data or finite element discretisation is more accurate and efficient to retrieve Williams higher-order terms . Conclusion : This paper presents a convergence analysis on a robust and efficient method based on the Bueckner-Chen conjugate work integral , which provides a bilinear form in which Williams series terms are orthogonal to retrieve Williams higher-order coefficients .

title: Laves phase observed by transmission electron microscopy in a natural Brazilian opal
abstract: The bidisperse structure of a natural Brazilian opal was revealed using transmission electron microscopy ( TEM ) . Since transmission electron microscopy ( TEM ) enables observation through the transparency of a few layers of silica spheres , the lamellar observation produced a complex image suggesting a flower-like repeating pattern generated by superimposed discs more or less opaque to the electron beam . Analysis of superimposed discs more or less opaque to the electron beam revealed that The bidisperse structure of a natural Brazilian opal was a hexagonal Laves phase of MgZn 2 type . The cutting plane is parallel to ( 11 2 0 ) . A simulation over the thickness of the lamella matched a complex image suggesting a flower-like repeating pattern generated by superimposed discs more or less opaque to the electron beam very well . The synthesis of such binary colloids is the aim of many experimental and theoretical studies with a variety of industrial applications . This study aims to prove that determining the structure of ordered natural opals can be performed by analysing transmission electron microscopy ( TEM ) images .

title: Test methods for chloride diffusivity of blended cement pastes: a review by RILEM TC 298-EBD
abstract: Abstract The use of supplementary cementitious materials ( SCM ) is an important part of the roadmap for reducing CO 2 emissions and extending the service life of reinforced concrete structures . To accelerate the adoption of SCMs , the RILEM Technical Committee 298-EBD evaluates scaled-down cement paste test methods to assess the effect of SCM on resistance to chloride and sulfate ingress and reactivity , which are critical to concrete durability . evaluates focuses on methods for measuring chloride diffusivity and is divided into four sections : diffusivity models and parameters , diffusion test methods ( including NMR and chloride measurements ) , migration test methods and implications for future research . Key insights highlight the complexities of multi-species ionic and molecular diffusion / migration , including various binding interactions , and compares the different measurement methodologies . evaluates also addresses the test scale and aggregate effects , noting the pros and cons of testing at the paste , mortar , and concrete scales . evaluates underscores the need for further investigation into testing protocols and the influence of SCM on chloride diffusion , emphasizing that comprehensive testing across different scales provides complementary information for assessing durability performance .

title: Design of Astatine(I) chelates for applications in targeted alpha therapy
abstract: Astatine ( Z=85 ) is a radioelement of major interest for targeted alpha-therapy owing to the short half-life of Astatine ( Z=85 ) 211At isotope ( 7.2 hours ) as well as Astatine ( Z=85 ) decay process leading to the emission of a single alpha particle . Stability of Astatine ( Z=85 ) radiolabeled complexes has been a challenge towards Astatine ( Z=85 ) medical application due to a significant degree of deastatination in vivo.1 Binding “ metallic ” astatine , At+ , could be an alternative approach to existing radiolabeling strategies relying on Astatine ( Z=85 ) halogen character . Our goal is to guide the synthesis of multidentate ligands that specifically capture At+ , and establish an understanding of Astatine ( Z=85 ) coordination chemistry . Given the nature of Astatine ( Z=85 ) , a specific methodology has been established based on 2-component relativistic DFT calculations , taking into account the influence of the solvent . From 2-component relativistic DFT calculations , complexation constants have been reported across a series of simple ligands containing oxygen , sulfur , selenium , nitrogen and/or phosphorus heteroatoms . Depending upon the heteroatom , the nature of the bond formed by Astatine ( Z=85 ) can have varying degrees of covalency or ionicity . To characterize the bonds , partial charges ( NPA , Hirschfeld ) were calculated but also combined with quantum chemical topology descriptors ( QTAIM , ELF ) that provide a deeper analysis of the total electron density . Furthermore , it has been demonstrated experimentally that there can be a formation of complexes with a 1:2 stoichiometry revealing a connection with Astatine ( Z=85 ) property of being the strongest halogen bond donor.2 Taking advantage of Astatine ( Z=85 ) metallic and halogen properties , various chelating agents have been designed [ Figure 1 ] . title: Experimental evaluation and analytical prediction of effects of skin defect size on the long-term durability of bio-based balsa core sandwich structures
abstract: This work focuses on the characterization of the cyclic moisture absorption-desorption aging behavior of balsa wood core sandwich structures with two-dimensional defects in Glass-Fiber-Reinforced-Polymer ( GFRP ) skins . Experimental investigations and analytical predictions were compared to evaluate the effects of skin defect size on the moisture diffusion kinetics during long-term aging cycles , in terms of the moisture diffusion coefficients and maximum moisture content capacity . Two distinct protocols were employed to investigate the effects of hygroscopic aging history on the moisture diffusion kinetics , including complete-cycle and incomplete-cycle absorption conditions , respectively . The Dual Fickian model proves to be admissible in predicting the moisture absorption behavior , while the moisture desorption process is in good agreement with the classical Fickian model , regardless of the skin defect size . Furthermore , the results reveal that the main moisture diffusion coefficient D I of The Dual Fickian model in the first complete absorption cycle could be doubled with a twofold increase in the skin defect size , while the larger skin defect has resulted in a slight decrease in the moisture diffusion coefficient D during all desorption cycles , which is mainly due to the transport of more bound water . In addition , the predicted maximum moisture content capacity is nearly three times higher for all absorption and desorption cycles as the skin defect size is doubled .

title: An intelligent data-driven model for sustainable-resilient supplier scrutiny and selection in sustainable reconfigurable manufacturing systems
abstract: In the research stream of sustainable reconfigurable manufacturing systems , sustainable and resilient supplier scrutiny and selection emerges as a key strategy , emphasising the imperative of integrating sustainability and resiliency into the supply chain fabric . sustainable and resilient supplier scrutiny and selection extends beyond mere economic evaluations by incorporating environmental stewardship , social responsibility , and resilience against disruptions into the supplier assessment processes . While studies in these fields have made significant strides , there remains a scarcity of research investigating and providing performance appraisal approaches for sustainable-resilient suppliers within such systems . Motivated by addressing the recognised gap , this study aims to identify key criteria for scrutinising sustainable-resilient suppliers through a state-of-the-art review and develop an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems . To this end , this study presents an illustrative case to demonstrate the practical configuration of an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems as well as a case study to corroborate an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems validity . The case studies confirmed that an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems effectively assesses sustainable-resilient suppliers , improving precision and execution time while providing insights for informed decision-making through an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems analytical depth and computational efficiency . Furthermore , sensitivity analysis and sensitivity analysis integration into an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems are discussed .

title: STRATA: Unruly Ethnographies of Troubled Worlds
abstract: STRATA is a collective book that rethinks how we narrate , inhabit , and experience ethnographic encounters through visual and sensory editorial experimentation . Created by anthropologist-artists , a collective book that rethinks how we narrate , inhabit , and experience ethnographic encounters through visual and sensory editorial experimentation weaves together images , texts , and sounds from six research projects conducted in France , Portugal , Romania , and Congo . a collective book that rethinks how we narrate , inhabit , and experience ethnographic encounters through visual and sensory editorial experimentation explores human and non-human relationships , colonial memory , thermoception , temporality , and sensory experience , allowing narrative form to serve as a mode of knowledge .

title: Listening is Better Understood with: Minds, Milieux, Machines and; Musics
abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual framework for understanding listening as a four-way interaction in-and-between minds , milieux , machines , and musics . Building on cognitive , ecological , computational , and cultural approaches to sound , we explore how each of minds , milieux , machines , and musics contributes uniquely to auditory experience and interpretation . minds bring perceptual , cognitive , and emotional grounding ; milieux provide ecological and sociocultural contexts ; machines offer tools for sensing , modeling , and synthesis in sonic environments ; and musics embody structured forms of human expression and shared aesthetic meanings . Through pairwise and three-way analyses , we identify the pitfalls of excluding any one component — leading to disembodiment , inefficiency , or cultural disconnection . We advocate for a transdisciplinary synthesis that situates listening within networks of perception , technology , and environment . We goal is to recenter listening as a reflexive , situated , and multiscalar practice across disciplines .

title: Modeling OCL Collection Types and Type Casting using Constraint Programming
abstract: In Model-Driven Engineering ( MDE ) , the Unified Modeling Language ( UML ) is often combined with the Object Constraint Language ( OCL ) to express constraints on models . While constraints on models are typically used for validation , certain tasks-such as model search , completion , repair , or explorationrequire the automatic generation of models that satisfy certain tasks-such as model search , completion , repair , or explorationrequire . Due to the combinatorial nature of certain tasks-such as model search , completion , repair , or explorationrequire , even small models can lead to computationally complex problems . Constraint Programming ( CP ) offers a powerful paradigm for modeling and solving such combinatorial challenges , notably through the use of global constraints , which enable concise models supported by efficient algorithms . Although previous approaches have tackled model search using tools like Alloy or ATLc , previous approaches often rely on simplified subsets or avoid the use of global constraints . In this paper , we extend the ATLc approach by leveraging Constraint Programming ( CP ) to the expressiveness and coverage of the Unified Modeling Language ( UML ) . we introduce a Constraint Programming ( CP ) model for representing the Unified Modeling Language ( UML ) instances and evaluating queries , along with global constraint formulations for the Unified Modeling Language ( UML ) collection types ( Sequence , Bag , Set , OrderedSet ) and UML collection types ( Sequence , Bag , Set , OrderedSet ) corresponding the Object Constraint Language ( OCL ) casting operations ( asSequence , asBag , asSet and asOrderedSet ) . Finally we provide an implementation allowing we to test we model for this subset of the Object Constraint Language ( OCL ) and compare with related work .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Embodiment Curve: a Graphical Method to Visualize the Temporal Evolution of the Sense of Embodiment in VR
abstract: The Sense of Embodiment ( SoE ) in VR is a psychological state which naturally fluctuates over time . Embodiment questionnaires are commonly used in research as assessment tools . Yet , Embodiment questionnaires inherently limit the range of expression and are ill-suited to capture the temporal dynamics of embodied experiences . Building on the UX curve method used in user experience research , we propose the Embodiment Curve method . we conducted a user study with 12 participants in VR , who embodied an avatar to complete four tasks in a virtual hair salon . we assessed 12 participants in VR , who embodied an avatar to complete four tasks in a virtual hair salon SoE using both the Embodiment Curve and a classical embodiment questionnaire . the Embodiment Curve shows the temporality of the embodiment . we observed two distinct drawing strategies for constructing the Embodiment Curve : task-oriented or trend-oriented . A majority of participants preferred the Embodiment Curve due to the Embodiment Curve task-by-task form and the Embodiment Curve freedom . Moreover , the Embodiment Curve facilitates the verbalization of their SoE the Embodiment Curve thus appears to be a promising qualitative method for studying their SoE

title: Immersed boundary formulation for complex geometries in hypersonic flows: Application to atmospheric reentry
abstract: This article discusses the challenges of modeling atmospheric reentry using computational fluid dynamics ( CFD ) due to computational fluid dynamics ( CFD ) complexity and practical industrial applications . Ablation phenomena caused by high energy make it difficult and time-consuming to use a " high-fidelity " CFD method to accurately measure forces and heat flux . As a result , methods based on Newton 's theory are used to model aerodynamic forces , incorporating statistical correlations from CFD results to estimate heat fluxes . However , methods based on Newton 's theory sacrifice accuracy for CPU and engineering time and have difficulty representing realistic physics when complex phenomena occur , such as shock interactions . To bridge the gap between approximate and high-fidelity methods , we propose a new approach using an automatic grid generation method of the octree Cartesian type coupled to a solver solving Euler 's equations . we compare two boundary condition imposition methods : the Direct-Forcing-Method ( DFM ) and the Ghost-Point-Forcing-Method ( GPFM ) in hypersonic flow configurations . we present a comparative study of two boundary condition imposition methods : the Direct-Forcing-Method ( DFM ) and the Ghost-Point-Forcing-Method ( GPFM ) on verification and validation phases , including an academic test case and an industrial case on a real reentry spacecraft .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Thirty Years of Antenna Characterization in the Millimeter Wave Range at IETR
abstract: Since more than 30 years , IETR has been designing antennas for millimeter wave range applications . Coupled with this main topic , characterization capabilities have been developed in order to validate research work by measuring Electro-Magnetic radiation of the prototypes used as proof of concept . Of course , over such a long period of time , the different antenna test facilities have been improved , in correlation with the research needs and the evolution of the different equipment . In this paper , the different improvements performed are presented , as well as the objectives which shaped the different improvements performed . The guidelines cover the RFsystems , the measurement techniques , the different processing used , and the possible next steps . Indeed , to be consistent with research activities , the different antenna test facilities must meet two main criteria : the systems have to be dimensioned to offer sufficient capabilities to characterize proof of concept prototypes ; the versatility of the systems have to allow set-ups and measurement techniques to be tailored to short-and long-terms research needs . This historical overview of IETR millimeter wave range antenna test facilities shows the evolution of Vector Network Analyzers from the historic HP8510 to those of the latest generation , the integration of Compact Antenna Test Ranges eligible for millimeter and submillimeter wave characterization , the development of nearfield scanners for Electro-Magnetic probing or antenna characterization . For each category , a discussion is carried out to assess the advantages and disadvantages of the evolution choices made . To illustrate the key steps of these improvements , several experimental results are presented giving as well an overview of characterization needs in the millimeter wave-range .
keywords: millimeter wave range antenna test ranges

title: Fraw : Sampling-Based Approximate Query Processing for Federations of SPARQL Endpoints
abstract: SPARQL federation engines allow users to query multiple SPARQL endpoints as if all RDF data were available through a single virtual endpoint . However , executing complex SPARQL queries over federations while maintaining fast response times remains a major challenge . In this demonstration , we present Fraw , a SPARQL federation engine that supports sampling-based approximate query processing . sampling-based approximate query processing is particularly useful in scenarios where response time is essential and approximate results are acceptable . we showcase the effectiveness of Fraw , a SPARQL federation engine that supports sampling-based approximate query processing through an interactive SPARQL query autocompletion use case , where users receive timely suggestions during query authoring , despite the complexity of federated querying .

title: Modelling a single-mode 915 MHz microwave applicator for low-moisture food treatment: comparison between COMSOL Multiphysics ® and CST Studio Suite ®
abstract: Two computational models were developed by using COMSOL Multiphysics ® and CST Studio Suite ® to simulate the microwave heating process of paprika and to compare the electromagnetic results obtained from each modelling software . The dielectric properties of paprika were initially measured at room temperature using the cavity perturbations technique and then estimated as a function of temperature . Experimental validation was performed in a rectangular waveguide with iris openings of 125 ( Configuration 1 ) and 88 mm ( Configuration 2 ) . The impact of variations in both dielectric constant and dielectric loss on temperature prediction was examined , along with the sensitivity of the results to the positioning of probes . Simulated and experimental temperatures were compared at two positions inside paprika : the centre ( T1 ) and the bottom ( T2 ) . Additionally , the distribution of the electromagnetic field and the microwave reflected power were examined . the results highlight the strong impact of dielectric property variations on local temperature prediction and provide valuable insights for optimizing industrial microwave heating processes for food powders .
keywords: 915 mhz microwave modelling electric field simulation low moisture food powder dielectric properties

title: Continuation Queries: Embracing Timeouts on Public SPARQL Endpoints
abstract: Public SPARQL endpoints , such as Wikidata , provide essential access points to large-scale knowledge graphs . However , Public SPARQL endpoints , such as Wikidata often suffer from strict timeouts that prevent the retrieval of complete query results . This demonstration presents the first public deployment of passage , a SPARQL query engine that guarantees query completeness through continuation queries . Instead of failing upon timeout , passage , a SPARQL query engine that guarantees query completeness through continuation queries returns partial results along with a SPARQL continuation query capable of retrieving the missing results . a SPARQL continuation query capable of retrieving the missing results can be chained iteratively until complete results are obtained . For This demonstration , attendees can interact with a passage loaded with 13B triples from Wikidata , and observe in detail a passage loaded with 13B triples from Wikidata 2025 operation during attendees query execution .

title: 3D Joint Reconstruction of Activity and Attenuation in PET by Diffusion Posterior Sampling
abstract: Attenuation correction ( AC ) allows to accurately quantify activity in positron emission tomography ( PET ) . However , traditional AC methods using computed tomography ( CT ) scans can suffer from mismatch artifacts and introduce additional radiations to the patient . CT-less reconstruction methods solve both those issues . We leverage diffusion models ( DMs ) to jointly reconstruct the activity and the attenuation from the emission data . Scaling DMs to handle three-dimensional ( 3D ) data is a challenging task which we solve by performing diffusion in a wavelet-decomposed image space . Comparison to iterative joint reconstruction algorithm maximum likelihood activity and attenuation ( MLAA ) shows that iterative joint reconstruction algorithm maximum likelihood activity and attenuation ( MLAA ) achieves higher peak signal-to-noise ratio ( PSNR ) and structural similarity index measure ( SSIM ) . Undergoing work seems to validate iterative joint reconstruction algorithm maximum likelihood activity and attenuation ( MLAA ) for lower-count data and non-time-of-flight ( TOF ) data .
keywords: maximum likelihood activity and attenuation ( mlaa )

title: Optimizing Nanoparticle Design for Selective Targeting of Breast Cancer Cells
abstract: Recent efforts in cancer targeting have focused on nanoparticle ( NP ) drug delivery , yet the complexity of NP uptake makes experimental studies challenging . To streamline NP uptake , numerical models help identify key parameters . This study 's model , focusing on elliptical NPs , aims to optimize NP aspect ratios for selective uptake by breast cancer cells . Mechanical properties of cells were taken from literature , and This study 's model , focusing on elliptical NPs , suggests that non-deformable NPs with aspect ratios between 1/3 and 1/2 are optimal for selective cancer cell internalization . These promising results require experimental validation .

title: Building a hydrogen economy: Does France have the industrial capacity for a low-carbon transition?
abstract: The energy transition towards low-carbon hydrogen ( H2 ) in France is expected to require deep industrial planning to develop electrolysis and H2 production infrastructure . This study employs an input – output method to simulate a new sector of electrolysis-produced hydrogen ( e-H2 ) that supplies two-hydrogen intensive sectors , petroleum refining and ammonia . We construct two input – output models , a demand-driven model for e-H2 sector development ( the investment phase ) and a mixed model for H2 production ( the operation phase ) . The results demonstrate that a new sector of electrolysis-produced hydrogen ( e-H2 ) that supplies two-hydrogen intensive sectors , petroleum refining and ammonia depends on industries such as machinery , electrical equipment , construction and metal products manufacturing in the investment phase , with strong backward linkages to the power sector in the operation phase . The results reveal that the energy shock ( 350 kt of e-H2 per year ) generates significant growth ( € 1.3 Bn of gross domestic product ) and jobs ( 3600 ) , but strongly depends on industries ’ capability to expand and recruit . Recommendations advise public policy development to address the need to reinforce key industries to support e-H2 production due to inter-industry dependence and the need for more attractive skilled and technician jobs in sectors that are already experiencing recruitment tensions . At much higher e-H2 shocks in the steel sector ( 700 kt e-H2 ) and other industries ( 415 kt e-H2 ) , even greater amounts of domestic resources would be required . Therefore , de-carbonising the entire H2 sector require ambitious policy planning to support industrial empowerment , research programmes and labour training so that H2 becomes an enabling technology of The energy transition towards low-carbon hydrogen ( H2 ) in France .
labels: Preparation for New Jobs in the Future Industry

title: Is it possible to valorize bicarbonates from reclaimed wastewater by CO2 electroreduction into formic acid? Investigation under low bicarbonate concentration and low-conductivity solutions
abstract: The electroreduction of CO 2 into value-added compounds from low bicarbonate concentration solutions typical of treated wastewater has been explored for the first time , unlike existing studies that focus on high bicarbonates concentrations and pressurized gas CO 2 as sources . This study investigates the feasibility of producing formic acid ( FA ) from low initial total inorganic carbon ( TIC 0 ) concentration referring to total inorganic carbon ( TIC ) after acidification to pH 4 ( 15-50 mg-C L-1 ) under microfluidic conditions in a filter press cell , from simulated to real reclaimed wastewaters . The effect of TIC 0 demonstrated that an optimal TIC 0 of 20 mg-C L-1 at j app = 5 mA cm-2 balanced the conversion yield ( 56 % ) , faradaic efficiency ( FE ) ( 9 % ) , and specific energy consumption ( E sp ) ( 1.96 kWh mol CO 2-1 ) .Reducing j app = 5 mA cm-2 from 5 to 2 mA cm-2 resulted in a 14 % increase in FE , although accompanied by a decrease in an overall conversion efficiency , highlighting the compromise that exists between selectivity and productivity . A kinetic model based on TIC degradation and FA formation accurately captured experimental trends . Results from real effluents showed successful FA production . These findings highlighted the interdependence between mass transport ( k m ) limitations , TIC availability , and competing reactions such as hydrogen evolution reaction ( HER ) . The observed variations in k m ( 1.4-1.6 × 10-5 m s-1 ) indicated that mass transport constraints played a critical role in CO 2 reduction efficiency , where an increased diffusion layer ( ) at higher TIC 0 limited CO 2 availability to the cathode surface shifting the balance between CO 2 reduction and HER . FTIR analyses further revealed an intensification of FA bands with increasing current .
labels: Reduction and Treatment of Effluents and Waste

title: A measurement-based calibration approach for highly scalable timing and energy modeling of EdgeAI multi-core systems
abstract: Deploying Artificial Neural Networks ( ANNs ) on embedded multi-core platforms requires precise models for estimating and optimizing timing and energy , which is crucial for enabling novel Artificial Intelligence ( AI ) applications . However , predicting non-functional properties ( timing , power ) is challenging due to degrees of parallelism in ANNs and complex effects in execution platforms ( e.g. contentions at shared resources , dynamic power management ) . This article presents an Electronic System-Level ( ESL ) timing and energy modeling flow and the associated calibration methodology for optimizing ANN deployment on multi-core platforms . an Electronic System-Level ( ESL ) timing and energy modeling flow leverages SystemC simulation to offer both speed and accuracy while ensuring high scalability in many dimensions , such as platform resources modeling . Analytical models are used for ANN layer computation and communication delays as well as power consumption and energy cost . We propose a measurement-based calibration approach to Analytical models which enables high prediction accuracy while guaranteeing high re-usability . Analytical models can be used across different settings without the need to re-perform a calibration phase . We validate We flow against real measurements of ANN implementations on a prototype multi-core platform . Results demonstrate over 97 % accuracy in timing and 93 % in energy for 54 mappings of different ANNs tested with and without the use of power management on a prototype multi-core platform , with an evaluation time under 2s per mapping . Furthermore , We illustrate that We flow is suitable for Design Space Exploration ( DSE ) , allowing up to 24 % improvement in inference time and 16 % in energy compared to baseline implementation .
keywords: electronic system-level ( esl ) timing and energy modeling
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Design and fabrication of a novel millimeter-wave bandstop filter using transversal signal interference technique
abstract: This paper presents the design , simulation , and fabrication of a miniaturized millimeter-wave band-stop filter ( BSF ) on microstrip technology . The proposed arrangement is based on the concept of transversal interference of signals , and is realized as a pair of parallel transmission lines with the appropriate characteristic impedance and electrical length . Such scheme provides sharpening signal discrimination without resonator structures additional to the filter . the filter is fabricated on a ROGERS RT / Duroid 5880 substrate , selected for its favorable properties at high frequencies , including a thickness of 0.13 mm , a relative dielectric constant of 2.2 , and a loss tangent of 0.0009 . The optimized design was validated through electromagnetic simulations by two types of electromagnetic solvers , and then fabricated and measured by coplanar waveguide ( CPW ) probe to confirm the filter practical performance .

title: Online measurement of differential drain to source voltage for SiC MOSFETS power module
abstract: The on-state resistance RDSON is a key aging indicator of silicon carbide MOSFETs power module . The on-state resistance RDSON can provide information on both chip and packaging degradation allowing more reliable power electronic converter . The on-state resistance RDSON can be determined using both the on-state current and voltage of the power semiconductor . This paper focuses on an on-state voltage measurement circuit for SiC MOSFET power module . In the literature , power module bondwires resistance can not be measured due to high switching voltage oscillations . An on-state voltage measurement circuit that can withstand such oscillations is proposed . An on-state voltage measurement circuit that can withstand such oscillations is characterized using the ISO 5725 standard over a wide temperature range . Finally , An on-state voltage measurement circuit that can withstand such oscillations is successfully tested on a double pulse bench for various module base plate temperatures and compared to data obtained with a static curve tracer Keysight B1505 .

title: Enhanced Simultaneous Automatic Synthesis (SAS) of 2-DOF QFT Based Robust PID Controller Design for Servo Systems
abstract: This article presents a simultaneous automatic synthesis ( SAS ) of robust controller and the pre-filter , 2-degree of freedom ( DOF ) , involved in the quantitative feedback theory ( QFT ) approach to address the large setpoint tracking for the motion control problem of dc servo uncertain systems with disturbances , sensor noise and control effort constraint . The traditional QFT based 2-DOF design being manual , time consuming and tedious , involves two step design process which results in nonoptimal solution . The merits of the proposed SAS approach are : 1 ) formulation of the robust proportional – integral – derivative ( PID ) controller and the pre-filter design as a single step nonlinear optimization problem with an enhanced objective function and performance constraints ; 2 ) inclusion of the controller and pre-filter terms in an enhanced objective function to obtain the optimal controller and pre-filter ; 3 ) enforcing various performance constraints such as robust tracking , input disturbance rejection , control effort and robust stability constraints ; 4 ) minimization of closed-loop system bandwidth with an inclusion of optimal pre-filter ; 5 ) free from actuator saturation while tracking the large setpoints . The effectiveness of the proposed SAS approach is demonstrated on a QUBE dc servo system . The experimental validation of the proposed SAS approach exhibits the fast and accurate robust tracking performance with a minimum control input .

title: Direction-of-Arrival Estimation of Coherent Sources with Leaky-Wave Antennas using Spatially Filtered Interpolation
abstract: With their frequency-beam scanning behavior , their are promising solutions to develop accurate and cost-effective direction-of-arrival ( DoA ) estimation systems . However , DoA estimators such as MUSIC face challenges with coherent sources due to the non-Vandermonde LWA steering matrix . Leveraging the unique radiation properties of their , this paper first divides the entire field of view into several angular sectors , and then introduces a robust and accurate sectorized spatially-filtered interpolation ( SFI ) method to transform the non-Vandermonde LWA steering matrix into a Vandermonde matrix in each sector while minimizing the issue of out-of-sector interference . The proposed method allows thus the estimation of DoAs of coherent sources with their . The simulation results show that the DoAs of multiple coherent sources across the entire field of view , regardless multiple coherent sources angular sector , can be correctly estimated . The performance of The proposed method is shown be close to the Cramér-Rao Bound .

title: Development and Experimental Evaluation of the Athena Parallel Robot for Minimally Invasive Pancreatic Surgery
abstract: This paper presents the development and experimental evaluation of the Athena parallel robot , a novel system designed for robot-assisted pancreatic surgery . The development of the Athena parallel robot , a novel system designed for robot-assisted pancreatic surgery based on the kinematic scheme , including the command and control system ( hardware and software ) , the calibration procedure , and the performance measurements of the Athena parallel robot , a novel system designed for robot-assisted pancreatic surgery based on finite element analyses of the 3D model , are also detailed in This paper . Based on finite element analyses of the 3D model , a region of the Athena parallel robot , a novel system designed for robot-assisted pancreatic surgery that introduces clearance during the operation of the Athena parallel robot , a novel system designed for robot-assisted pancreatic surgery is found . This paper also presents the methodology used for mapping the Athena parallel robot , a novel system designed for robot-assisted pancreatic surgery workspace with an optical system , which enabled improvements to ensure coverage of the entire pancreas area . The results obtained before and after the mechanical improvements are presented , demonstrating a reduction in clearance by up to 4.1 times following part replacement , as well as a workspace extension that enables the active instrument to reach the entire pancreas area .
