In a second step , conditions obtained by standard convex analysis , subdifferential and directional derivative , applied to uniform approximation are formulated . conditions obtained by standard convex analysis , subdifferential and directional derivative , applied to uniform approximation relationship to previous conditions is investigated , providing sometimes enlightening interpretations of the laters , e.g. , relating Kolmogorov criterion with directional derivative , and strong uniqueness with sharp minimizers . Finally , numerical applications of the two-step approach to three uniform approximation problems are presented , namely the approximation of the multidimensional Runge function , the approximation of the two dimensional inverse model of the DexTAR parallel robot , and the approximation problem consisting in minimizing the sum of both the polynomial approximation error and the polynomial evaluation error in Horner form .

title: Using virtual reality to study preference and restorativeness for streetscape vegetation design
abstract: The presence of small urban green spaces , such as streetscape vegetation , plays a significant role in the daily exposure to nature for a considerable proportion of urban inhabitants across the globe . This study examines how specific design elements ( vegetal and non-vegetal ) of small urban green spaces influence human preferences and human preferences alignment with perceived restorativeness dimensions . In each of the 30 trials , participants selected participants preferred option and gave reasons for participants choice based on the four aspects of the Attention Restoration Theory ( fascination , coherence , being away , compatibility ) . The results demonstrate that the absence of a fence was the most preferred option , irrespective of the fence type . Shorter fences and fences that include greenery were found to be significantly more favored than other types , primarily due to fascination . Conversely , attributes such as metal and high fences were selected less frequently , with coherence identified as the primary reason for selected . The most preferred vegetation type was trees , which were selected primarily due to trees , which were selected primarily due to their capacity to evoke fascination capacity to evoke fascination . In contrast , bushes and grass , which were less favored , were chosen for bushes and grass , which were less favored contribution to coherence . A medium level of diversity was preferred over high or low levels when the arrangement of vegetation was not regular . Furthermore , random and regular arrangements were less favored than an intermediate level of arrangement . With regard to the Attention Restoration Theory dimensions , fascination was the primary motive for all options except for the regular arrangement . These findings could assist designers of small urban green spaces in creating more restorative environments . Additionally , This study illustrates the value of employing virtual environments in environmental preference research .

title: Advances in automata theory for optimization problems involving multi-period personnel scheduling
abstract: This thesis lies within the field of operations research applied to personnel scheduling problems ( PSP ) . This thesis introduces a formalism based on regular languages , and more specifically on deterministic finite automata ( DFA ) , to represent a wide range of contractual or operational work rules in a generic and flexible manner . This modeling approach leads to mixed-integer programming ( MIP ) formulations in which the number of variables is directly related to the number of transitions in the automata . To make mixed-integer programming ( MIP ) formulations in which the number of variables is directly related to the number of transitions in the automata easier to solve , This thesis explores the use of unambiguous finite automata ( UFA ) to reduce the number of variables in the MIP while avoiding symmetry issues . Since minimizing the number of transitions in such UFA is NP-hard , a polynomial-time reduction heuristic is proposed , and a polynomial-time reduction heuristic practical efficiency is demonstrated on benchmark PSP from the literature . Finally , This thesis extends This modeling approach to integrated problems combining PSP and vehicle routing problems ( VRP ) through a branch-and-price method that leverages the automata structure to efficiently solve generic problems involving both PSP and vehicle routing problems ( VRP ) .

title: Phase-field and lip-field approaches for fracture with extreme mesh deformation (X-Mesh): a one-dimensional study
abstract: We consider a one-dimensional fracture problem modelled using either the phase-field or lip-field approach . In either the phase-field or lip-field approach , we optimise the incremental potential with respect to the displacement and damage fields and the nodal coordinates of the mesh . This is thus a variational mesh study . We observe that , as the damage reaches the damage maximum value , optimise drives the most damaged element to zero size as the damage reaches the damage maximum value . the most damaged element provides a precise displacement jump representation as the bar breaks . The overall solution is also shown to be much more accurate than the fixed mesh solution . This work forms part of an exploration into the capabilities of extreme meshes in computational mechanics ( X-Mesh ) .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: TST: Tree Structured Transformer for Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition
abstract: Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition ( HMER ) is a challenging task due to the complexity of mathematical symbols and the variability of handwriting styles . Tree Structured Transformer ( TST ) is proposed to recognize handwritten mathematical expressions by predicting the Symbol Layout Tree ( SLT ) of handwritten mathematical expressions . The proposed method is based on an Encoder-Decoder architecture , where the Decoder is designed to predict the tree structure of handwritten mathematical expressions , which predicts the node labels , edge labels , and parent index of each node . the Decoder can be combined with different Encoder to handle both online or offline handwritten mathematical expressions with CNN-based Encoder for offline HMER and Graph-based Encoder for online HMER . Both the online and offline systems are evaluated on the CROHME 2023 dataset , and evaluated by the standard evaluation tools , achieving competitive results compared to the state-of-the-art methods .
keywords: handwritten mathematical expression recognition tree transformer handwriting recognition encoder decoder architecture

title: Boosting Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition through Contextual Reasoning with Vision Large Language Models (vLLMs)
abstract: Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition ( HMER ) has traditionally relied on dedicated models specifically designed for Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition ( HMER ) . With the emergence of Vision Large Language Models ( vLLMs ) , we investigate Vision Large Language Models ( vLLMs ) potential for HMER tasks . This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark study evaluating various state-of-the-art vLLMs on the CROHME dataset . we develop an experimental pipeline that includes language model inference , cleaning and conversion to structural graphs , and evaluation using graph-based metrics . we experiments explore two prompting strategies : without context ( image-to-text only ) and with context ( image-to-text with surrounding contextual information ) . Results show that while vLLMs demonstrate promising capabilities , dedicated models still outperform general-purpose vLLMs on HMER tasks . we analyze the performance gaps and discuss future directions for improving vLLM-based mathematical expression recognition .

title: Processing Complex Oxide Ceramics Toward Printable DRA Applications
abstract: To meet the demands of mobile and satellite communication devices , microwave dielectric ceramics must possess a moderate relative permittivity ( 50 ≲ εr ≲ 100 ) for miniaturization , low dielectric losses ( tan δ ≲ 10-3 ) for high radiation efficiency , and a near-zero temperature coefficient of resonant frequency ( τf ) for thermal stability [ 1 ] . Moreover , the emergence of ceramic 3D printing now enables net-shape parts with complex geometries unachievable by conventional methods . However , current research into the use of ceramic 3D printing remains limited to basic , commercially available compositions , that do not meet all of the requirements mentioned above . The objective of this study is to develop new dielectric ceramic materials with an elaboration technique transferable to slurries for 3D printing . Our previous work on ( Sr2Ta2O7)1-x(La2Ti2O7)x and β'-SrTa2O6 ceramics achieved εeff = 80-120 and low losses ( ~10-3 ) , but ' τf ' of a few hundred [ 2,3 ] . this study focuses , first , on the La2Ti2O7 compound yet not characterized in high frequencies , and , secondly , on lithium niobate and calcium titanate-based compositions , lithium niobate and calcium titanate-based compositions being chosen for expected very low ' τf ' . Here , emphasis is placed on ceramic processing control at each step , to achieve consistent dielectric properties at lab scale and enabling scaleup to meet the demanding requirements for loaded resin slurry formulation for photolithography-based ceramics 3D manufacturing . Key aspects addressed will include optimizing particle size distribution through grinding and ball milling for efficient synthesis and sintering , maximizing relative density through tailored debinding and sintering schedules , and managing conditions during high-temperature treatments to reduce contamination .
keywords: dielectric materials ceramics dra's characterization processing additive manufacturing

title: Overcoming the Technical Hurdles of IoT Adoption: the FITNESS Project Vision and Insights
abstract: The Internet of Things ( IoT ) has emerged as a transformative force , enabling seamless connectivity and data exchange between diverse devices and networks . However , the realization of a truly interoperable , secure , and energy-efficient The Internet of Things ( IoT ) ecosystem remains a significant challenge . In this paper , we present the vision and the first key findings of the FITNESS project , a comprehensive research initiative funded by the French Research Agency ( ANR ) as part of the France 2030 program . the FITNESS project , a comprehensive research initiative funded by the French Research Agency ( ANR ) as part of the France 2030 program work aims to develop solutions that enable The Internet of Things ( IoT ) full potential , emphasizing scalability , interoperability , security , and sustainability , and enabling seamless connectivity and efficient data transmission between diverse The Internet of Things ( IoT ) devices and networks . the FITNESS project , a comprehensive research initiative funded by the French Research Agency ( ANR ) as part of the France 2030 program focus in this paper on three critical areas : The Internet of Things ( IoT ) architecture and interoperability , the place of Artificial Intelligence in The Internet of Things ( IoT ) , and energy efficiency . Additionally , the FITNESS project , a comprehensive research initiative funded by the French Research Agency ( ANR ) as part of the France 2030 program identify and analyze key use cases that demonstrate the practical applications of the FITNESS project , a comprehensive research initiative funded by the French Research Agency ( ANR ) as part of the France 2030 program research , highlighting the importance of real-world implementation to validate and refine the FITNESS project , a comprehensive research initiative funded by the French Research Agency ( ANR ) as part of the France 2030 program solutions . Through the FITNESS project , a comprehensive research initiative funded by the French Research Agency ( ANR ) as part of the France 2030 program dedicated research efforts , the FITNESS project , a comprehensive research initiative funded by the French Research Agency ( ANR ) as part of the France 2030 program have made significant advances across several key areas , while also laying the groundwork for further development in others . These contributions support the emergence of a more secure , efficient , and interoperable The Internet of Things ( IoT ) ecosystem , and provide a foundation for adoption by stakeholders seeking to harness The Internet of Things ( IoT ) transformative potential .

title: Categorial Dependency Grammars Extended with Typed Barriers
abstract: We consider the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) , as computational grammars for language processing . the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) are a class of categorial grammars defining dependency structures . The formalism can be viewed as a formal proof system on the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) types , with a finite set of rules , combining the classical categorial grammars ’ elimination rules with valency pairing rules that are able to define non-projective ( discontinuous ) dependencies . A the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) lexicon attaches types to words . A sentence is said correct when a sequence of types attached to A sentence words entails a particular type , the proof derivation then reflects the sentence dependency structure as in the given example . This article is motivated by a need to limit the scope of non-projective dependencies . A previous proposal extended the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) with a single barrier to give an AFL ( Abstract Family of Languages ) . In This article we introduce typed barriers . Typed barriers should be more convenient to model some fine-grained linguistic phenomenon in a simple and modular way , while preserving good theoretical properties . This proposal allows to prevent some undesired analysis and also may guide the parsing more efficiently . We provide a new type language and rule system that generalize previous the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) formulations and consider a new type language and rule system that generalize previous CDG formulations in terms of expressivity , parsing and efficiency .

title: Assessment of Hybrid RANS-LES and WALE Formulations for Wake and Resistance Prediction of the BB2 Submarine
abstract: Submarine hydrodynamics presents unique challenges in accurately predicting flow separation , wake structure , and resistance due to complex geometry and turbulent behaviour at high Reynolds ( Re ) numbers . Traditional Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes ( RANS ) approaches are often limited in resolving unsteady flow structures and turbulence in the near and far regions . To address these limitations , hybrid RANS-LES models such as Detached Eddy Simulation ( DES ) and Large Eddy Simulation ( LES ) offer improved performance in capturing near-wall vortical structures . The capturing of turbulent vortices and wake structures significantly contributes to conduct hydrodynamic noise analysis . Detailed resolution and understanding of turbulent vortices and wake structures help minimize hydroacoustic signatures , essential for submarines ' stealth characteristics . Based on prior studies , Breuer et al . ( 2003 ) reported that RANS failed to capture unsteady vortex shedding , producing only steady results even in 3D simulations . In contrast , Detached Eddy Simulation ( DES ) and Large Eddy Simulation ( LES ) successfully resolved asymmetric shedding across different grid resolutions . Spalart ( 2009 ) reported that Detached Eddy Simulation ( DES ) is more effective than RANS or Large Eddy Simulation ( LES ) for high Re flows , although Detached Eddy Simulation ( DES ) suffers from challenges related to ambiguous grids and nonmonotonic grid refinement behaviour . Whereas Liang & Xue ( 2014 ) found that Detached Eddy Simulation ( DES ) predicts tip vortex flow characteristics more accurately than RANS and can capture complex 3D vortex structures . In addition , Guilmineau et al . ( 2018 ) demonstrated that the IDDES model accurately predicts recirculation bubbles and aligns more closely with experimental data for flow prediction . Long et al . ( 2021 ) confirmed the capability of IDDES in simulating cavitating flows around hydrofoils and marine propellers . Lungu ( 2022 ) highlighted the efficiency and accuracy of the IDDES model in DARPA submarine simulations . Zhang et al . ( 2023 ) also noted that URANS struggles with resolving small-scale turbulence structures , whereas IDDES is better suited for predicting complex phenomena such as ship air wake asymmetry . Nevertheless , capturing the unsteadiness and turbulence fluctuations scales is extremely challenging because the cell size requirements should suit each turbulence model employed . Thus , as a continuation of the prior work of Abidin et al . ( 2024 ) , the unsteady simulation with high mesh resolution at U_m=1.8235 m / s and Re of 3.6×10 ^ 6 to generate the asymmetrical wake dynamic and vortical structure . The current research expands the methodology by parameterizing the meshes and numerical scheme based on Taylor microscale refinement with respect to the characteristic length of ( L , B and D ) of submarine , particularly focusing on hybrid turbulence model and WALE to observe the ability to resolve turbulence in the wake region . The transient simulations were performed initially using wall-resolved mesh ( 76×10 ^ 6 cells ) at y^+ < 5 and then wall-modelled mesh ( 56×10 ^ 6 to 74×10 ^ 6 cells ) at y^+ > 30 , which produced notably different and more detailed results ( vortices and turbulence fluctuation ) than previous steady-state RANS simulations without risking the accuracy of quantity of interest ( global resistance ) .

title: Effect of Printing Temperature on the Microstructure and Tensile Properties of Polylactic Acid–Magnetic Iron Composites Manufactured by Material Extrusion
abstract: In this study , we examined how printing temperature affects the microstructure and mechanical properties of polylactic acid ( PLA ) composite reinforced with iron oxide i.e. , magnetite manufactured using a material extrusion technique . polylactic acid ( PLA ) composite reinforced with iron oxide i.e. , magnetite manufactured using a material extrusion technique was printed at temperatures from 185 • C to 215 • C. Microstructure analysis via synchrotron radiation Xray microtomography revealed changes in both iron oxide and porosity contents within the printed structures . Mechanical testing results demonstrated a limited effect of the printing temperature on tensile performance . Finite element computation is considered to predict the elasticity behavior of polylactic acid ( PLA ) composite reinforced with iron oxide i.e. , magnetite manufactured using a material extrusion technique by converting 3D images into 3D structural meshes . When implementing a two-phase model , the predictions show a leading role of the iron oxide content , and an overestimation of the stiffness of polylactic acid ( PLA ) composite reinforced with iron oxide i.e. , magnetite manufactured using a material extrusion technique . A three-phase model demonstrates a better matching of the experimental results suggesting a limited load transfer across the PLA-iron oxide interface with Young 's moduli in the interphase zone as small as 10 % of Young 's modulus . Magnetic actuation demonstrates that experiments on PLA-iron oxide plates reveal a pronounced thickness-dependent limitation , with the maximum deflection observed in thin strips of 0.4 mm .
keywords: polylactic acid composite reinforced with iron oxide
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Compact and wide-scanning connected-slot array for Ku/K/Ka band applications
abstract: Emerging applications such as satellite communications on the move are boosting research on wide-angle scanning phased arrays operating over multiple bands with a single radiating aperture , up to millimeter wave ( mm-wave ) frequencies . The realization of cost-effective and robust designs , suitable for low-loss integration with integrated circuits ( ICs ) , is a key objective to enable wide-angle scanning phased arrays operating over multiple bands with a single radiating aperture , up to millimeter wave ( mm-wave ) frequencies massive deployment . In the last decade , several ultra-wideband architectures have been proposed and demonstrated , mainly in the microwave spectrum . several ultra-wideband architectures leverage on the high mutual coupling among several ultra-wideband architectures elements to attain uniform current distributions and comprise wide-angle impedance matching ( WAIM ) layers to enhance several ultra-wideband architectures field view . This thesis presents a compact and cost-effective design of connected-slots arrays operating in Ku-, K-and Ka-band and scanning up to ±60 ° . A two-section hybrid superstrate directly loading the radiating aperture is proposed to achieve wide-angle impedance matching and enhanced cross-polarization discrimination . The first section is an artificial dielectric comprising three stacked subwavelength patch layers , two of which connected by vias , while the second one is an isotropic dielectric slab . a compact and cost-effective design of connected-slots arrays operating in Ku-, K-and Ka-band and scanning up to ±60 ° comprises a reduced number of layers with respect to the state of the art . Moreover , a compact and cost-effective design of connected-slots arrays operating in Ku-, K-and Ka-band and scanning up to ±60 ° does not require special manufacturing steps , e.g. foam spacers or substrate drilling . The small array pitch and the possibility to fabricate a compact and cost-effective design of connected-slots arrays operating in Ku-, K-and Ka-band and scanning up to ±60 ° in a robust , multilayer PCB is attractive for future integration with ICs . 8x8 arrays are fabricated and measured .

title: Transformers Can Admit Mistakes and Backtrack
abstract: Transformer models excel in language processing but lack intrinsic logical reasoning . Our proposed solution equips generative models with enhanced logical inference via integrated backtracking capabilities for multiple algorithms . Our proof-of-concept Transformer learn efficient tree structure traversal , demonstrating backtracking feasibility . This foundational work aims to establish trustworthy AI systems that can critically think and revise assumptions , with potential implications for precise decision-making in various fields .

title: Style-FG: A Style-based Framework for Film Grain Analysis and Synthesis
abstract: Film grain which used to be a by-product of the chemical processing in the analog film stock is a desirable feature in the era of digital cameras . Besides participating to the artistic intent during content creation , film grain has also interesting properties in the video compression chain such as film grain ability to mask compression artifacts . In this article , we use a deep learning-based framework for film grain analysis , generation , and synthesis . a deep learning-based framework for film grain analysis , generation , and synthesis consists of three modules : a style encoder performing film grain style analysis , a mapping network responsible for film grain style generation , and a synthesis network that generates and blends a specific grain style to a given content in a content-adaptive manner . three modules are trained jointly , thanks to dedicated loss functions , on a new large and diverse dataset of pairs of grain-free and grainy images that we made publicly available to the community . 1 Quantitative and qualitative evaluations show that fidelity to the reference grain , diversity of grain styles as well as a perceptually pleasant grain synthesis are achieved , demonstrating that each module outperforms the state-of-the-art in the task each module was designed for . To contribute further to the sustainability necessary effort of the digital information and communication field , a light-weight version of a deep learning-based framework for film grain analysis , generation , and synthesis is also proposed , which demonstrates similar quantitative and qualitative performances , while reducing the number of network parameters by a factor of 92 % .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Attochemical Control of Nuclear Motion Despite Fast Electronic Decoherence
abstract: Short-in-time , broad-in-energy atto-or few-femtosecond pulses can excite coherent superpositions of several electronic states in molecules . excite results in ultrafast charge oscillations known as charge migration . A key open question in the emerging field of attochemistry is whether these electron dynamics , which due to decoherence often last only for a few femtoseconds , can influence longer-timescale nuclear rearrangements . Herein , we address A key open question in the emerging field of attochemistry through full-dimensional quantum dynamics simulations of the coupled electron-nuclear dynamics initiated by ionization and coherent excitation of ethylene . full-dimensional quantum dynamics simulations of the coupled electron-nuclear dynamics initiated by ionization and coherent excitation of ethylene predict electronic coherences with half-lives of less than one femtosecond . Despite electronic coherences with half-lives of less than one femtosecond brevity , electronic coherences with half-lives of less than one femtosecond induce vibrational coherences along the derivative coupling vectors that persist for at least 50 fs . These results suggest that short-lived electronic coherences can impart long-lasting legacies on nuclear motion , a finding of potential importance to the interpretation of attosecond experiments and the development of strategies for attochemical control .

title: Synthesis and Characterization of Proton Conducting Ceramic Electrolyte Materials for Hydrogen Production Devices by Water Electrolysis
abstract: Proton-conducting ceramics , particularly the BaZrₓCe₀‚₈−ₓY₀‚₁Yb₀‚₁O₂‚₉ ( 0 ≤ x ≤ 0.8 ) perovskite family , have emerged as key materials for next-generation energy systems , including protonic ceramic fuel cells and electrolysis cells . Characterizing both hydrated and dehydrated phases is essential , as both hydrated and dehydrated phases proton conductivity is strongly influenced by hydration . In this thesis , pure-phase nano-powders were synthesized via the glycine-nitrate method and characterized using neutron diffraction ( ND ) , X-ray diffraction ( XRD ) , thermogravimetric analysis ( TGA ) , and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy ( EIS ) . Hydrated phases were analyzed in Hydrated phases as-synthesized form , while dehydrated phases were obtained by high-temperature treatment under vacuum . Based on the ND and XRD results , two phase diagrams were developed : one for hydrated BaZrₓCe₀‚₈−ₓY₀‚₁Yb₀‚₁O₂‚₉ ( H₂O)₀‚₁ in a nitrogen atmosphere and another for dehydrated BaZrₓCe₀‚₈−ₓY₀‚₁Yb₀‚₁O₂‚₉ in vacuum . two phase diagrams reveal the influence of Zr / Ce ratio and hydration state on structural symmetry , phase transition temperatures , and thermal expansion . Mass loss due to dehydration ( TGA ) was correlated with unit cell volume changes ( XRD ) , allowing quantification of chemical expansion caused by water uptake . Additionally , Zn-based sintering aids and internal doping strategies were used to improve the densification of BaZr₀‚₄Ce₀‚₄Y₀‚₁Yb₀‚₁O₂‚₉ ( x = 0.4 ) . Zn-based sintering aids and internal doping strategies enabled sintering at 1400 ° C to > 90 % relative density while maintaining high ionic conductivity , reaching 0.9 × 10⁻ ²S·cm⁻¹ at 700 ° C in humidified N₂.
keywords: mass loss due to dehydration ( tga )

title: Operational Game Semantics for Generative Algebraic Effects and Handlers
abstract: We present a sound operational game semantics model ( w.r.t . contextual equivalence ) of a typed language with algebraic effects and handlers and dynamic generation of effect instances à la [ 5 , 11 ] . We exhibit the interactive aspect of effect propagation , and to address the interactive aspect of effect propagation precisely , we identify the adequate granularity of the operational semantics ( akin to [ 15 ] ) and the decomposition of normal forms into normal forms interactive and normal forms observational part . To account for this additional form of interaction , we extend the standard pure interaction interface of game semantics consisting of questions and answers with effectful moves that involve the propagation of effects and the yielding of delimited continuations . Finally , we extend the well-bracketed constraint on the behavior of the environment , from the use of continuations as is standard in game semantics , to fragments of captured delimited continuations .

title: The ambiances are the message: Transects, project, and urban situations
abstract: For geographers , the term transect designates “ a field observation device or the representation of a space , along a linear path and in the vertical dimension , intended to identify a superposition , a spatial succession or relationships between phenomena ” according to geographer Marie-Claire Robic . Applied to the development of a territory , the transect is a practice whose elements were theorized and applied at the beginning of the twentieth century , in particular by the urban planner and botanist Patrick Geddes in Scotland . A technique of representation as much as a field practice , the transect is now being revisited . For us , the transect is presented as a hybrid device between the technical section and the sensitive route : the transect is constructed through drawing , photography , measurement , text , and video , as much as the transect is practised in situ , by perception , speech , wandering , generally by walking . By rehabilitating the atmospheric dimension in urban representations and enabling the inclusion of inhabitants ’ stories in the specialized debates between disciplines , the transect becomes a tool of interrogation and expression of the sensitive space and of lived practices . As such , the transect helps articulate two usually dissociated postures , those of analysis and of conception . Although the transect borrows the transect capacity to identify and collect the most different situations from the notion of an inventory , and even though the transect refers to Aby Warburg ’s Mnemosyne atlases and Carlo Ginzburg ’s indexical paradigm , the passage from the plan to the cross-section reveals the social , environmental , historical , and project-based thickness of the city . Through graphic representations , life stories , and perceptions of ambiances , the transect becomes a workspace that can be shared and amended between the actors of the territory : inhabitants , experts , as well as decision-makers and designers . In Deleuzian terms , we make the transect the symbol of an approach to the city “ through the middle ” . Between the great historical narrative of a city and the pragmatic micro-narratives of a city use , the transect becomes an ideal narrative instrument for designing the urban ambiences of tomorrow as well as for situating the urban project within a larger “ heritage ” dynamic .

title: Experimental validation of the analytic-centre based tension distribution algorithm for cable driven parallel robots
abstract: Cable-Driven Parallel Robots ( CDPRs ) offer several advantages over traditional parallel robots . Guiding Cable-Driven Parallel Robots ( CDPRs ) accurately and safely requires fast Tension Distribution Algorithms ( TDAs ) able to work in real-time . This paper proposes the experimental validation of our previous TDA namely , the Analytic Centre . The contribution consists of comparing the simulated results with the measured tension profiles to infer the validity of the theoretical outcome . In other words , the idea is to find evidence of the predictions made in simulations . Experiments confirm simulated results supporting the theoretical advantages of our previous TDA namely , the Analytic Centre , proving our previous TDA namely , the Analytic Centre usefulness .

title: Implicit Shape-Prior for Few-Shot Assisted 3D Segmentation
abstract: The objective of this paper is to significantly reduce the manual workload required from medical professionals in complex 3D segmentation tasks that can not be yet fully automated . For instance , in radiotherapy planning , organs at risk must be accurately identified in computed tomography ( CT ) or magnetic resonance imaging ( MRI ) scans to ensure organs at risk are spared from harmful radiation . Similarly , diagnosing age-related degenerative diseases such as sarcopenia , which involve progressive muscle volume loss and strength , is commonly based on muscular mass measurements often obtained from manual segmentation of medical volumes . To alleviate the manual-segmentation burden , this paper introduces an implicit shape prior to segment volumes from sparse slice manual annotations generalized to the multi-organ case , along with a simple framework for automatically selecting the most informative slices to guide and minimize the next interactions . The experimental validation shows the method 's effectiveness on two medical use cases : assisted segmentation in the context of at risks organs for brain cancer patients , and acceleration of the creation of a new database with unseen muscle shapes for patients with sarcopenia .

title: Circadia: Checkpointing for Intermittent Computing in AI Driven Applications
abstract: Battery-less embedded systems powered by energy harvesting eliminate the need for battery maintenance and enable Battery-less embedded systems powered by energy harvesting deployment in remote environments . However , Battery-less embedded systems powered by energy harvesting intermittent execution , disrupted by unpredictable power failures , complicates data processing . Solutions for intermittency management gravitate around one key technique : checkpointing volatile data before power failures , and retrieving data at system reboot . Moreover , since data transmission is a major source of energy consumption , performing computations directly ondevice is essential . Initially used for simple tasks such as goods identifications , battery-less systems are now being applied to more energy-intensive tasks such as image recognition leveraging machine learning algorithms such as Convolutional Neural Networks ( CNNs ) . In this paper , we introduce Circadia , a checkpointing strategy dedicated to CNN inference in battery-less systems . By leveraging the structured dataflow and control flow of CNNs , Circadia , a checkpointing strategy dedicated to CNN inference in battery-less systems strategically places checkpoints within the CNN code to ensure task termination , data consistency , and low energy consumption . By design , Circadia , a checkpointing strategy dedicated to CNN inference in battery-less systems has a linear complexity relative to model size , a significant improvement over the closest state-of-the-art checkpointing method , which has cubic complexity . has enables Circadia , a checkpointing strategy dedicated to CNN inference in battery-less systems to handle much larger CNNs . Experimental results , on both generated and state-of-the-art embedded CNNs , show that Circadia , a checkpointing strategy dedicated to CNN inference in battery-less systems checkpoint placement time is several orders of magnitude lower than existing approaches , while Circadia , a checkpointing strategy dedicated to CNN inference in battery-less systems energy consumption at runtime remains nearly identical .

title: Crafting Visibility and Solidarity
abstract: This paper investigates how micro-task platform workers construct and mobilize micro-task platform workers professional digital identity to influence sourcing decisions , navigate platform control , and foster forms of solidarity . In contexts where workers are largely invisible to clients and algorithmic decision-making prevails , we explore how identity work operates as a subtle but meaningful form of resistance . We specifically ask : How do workers portray workers in ways that shape visibility , signal credibility , and build collective ties under conditions of isolation and precarity ? Collective digital identity is the shared identity that emerges from the interactions and collaborations of groups within digital spaces . We draw on professional identity theory and collective identity literature to theorize digital identity as a contested space where visibility , legitimacy , and solidarity are co-produced .
labels: Preparation for New Jobs in the Future Industry

title: Influence of the Initial Clay Fabric on the Progressive Destructuring Process under One-Dimensional Compression
abstract: This study aims to show how the interactions between clay particles and clay particles environment can influence the fabric structuring of clayey soils , as well as to highlight the consequences on clayey soils mechanical behavior . For aims , samples of kaolinite clay sedimented within solutions at different pHs , which may induce either flocculated or dispersed clay fabric , were prepared and analyzed . The approach consists of using sedimentation tests to form different microstructures at the slurry state of samples of kaolinite clay sedimented within solutions at different pHs , which may induce either flocculated or dispersed clay fabric ; then , oedometric tests and the scanning electron microscopy ( SEM ) technique were used to analyze both mechanical behavior and clay microfabric features at different loading levels . It was found that during the sedimentation , low pH values produced flocculated clay particles forming aggregates with edge-to-face ( EF ) associations , resulting in a clay fabric with large voids . In contrast , at high-pH conditions , kaolinite particles were dispersed with face-to-face ( FF ) associations , resulting in denser fabric and reduced poral spaces . By increasing the one-dimensional compression load , the initially flocculated-structured clay showed a higher compression capacity than the initially dispersed-structured clay , due to the reduction of both interaggregate and intra-aggregate pores , leading to the progressive convergence of the stress – strain curves . Consequently , at high stress levels , the fabric of the initially flocculated-structured clay progressively converges toward the initially dispersed-structured clay . High-resolution the scanning electron microscopy ( SEM ) technique photographs showed at the microscale a progressive transition under loading from a flocculated clay fabric , a card-house-like structure , to aligned particle stacks that are quite similar to the microfabric observed in the case of initially dispersed-structured clay . Quantitative analysis of the pore size distribution ( PSD ) , based on the scanning electron microscopy ( SEM ) technique observations and image processing , highlights the distinct initial fabrics and the distinct initial fabrics evolution under mechanical loading .

title: Designing Object Detection Models for TinyML: Foundations, Comparative Analysis, Challenges, and Emerging Solutions
abstract: Object detection ( OD ) has become vital for numerous computer vision applications , but deploying Object detection ( OD on resource-constrained internet of things ( IoT ) devices presents a significant challenge . resource-constrained internet of things ( IoT ) devices struggle to handle the computational load of deep learning-based object detection ( OD ) models . struggle is compounded by the rapid proliferation of IoT devices , predicted to surpass 150 billion by 2030 . TinyML offers a compelling solution by enabling Object detection ( OD on ultra-low-power devices , paving the way for efficient and real-time OD at the edge . Although numerous survey articles have been published on this topic , numerous survey articles often overlook the optimization challenges associated with deploying Object detection ( OD models in TinyML environments . To address the optimization challenges associated with deploying OD models in TinyML environments , this survey article provides a detailed analysis of key optimization techniques for deploying Object detection ( OD models on resource-constrained devices . key optimization techniques for deploying OD models on resource-constrained devices include quantization , pruning , knowledge distillation , and neural architecture search . Furthermore , we explore both theoretical approaches and practical implementations , bridging the gap between academic research and real-world edge artificial intelligence ( AI ) deployment . Finally , we compare the key performance indicators ( KPIs ) of existing Object detection ( OD implementations on microcontroller devices , highlighting the achieved maturity level of existing OD implementations on microcontroller devices in terms of both prediction accuracy and efficiency . we also provide a public repository to continually track developments in this topic : Link .

title: Cattle, architecture, and the Bureau of Animal Industry: Institutional documents for the production and dissemination of a new model of dairy farm (1884–1910)
abstract: In 1884 , the Bureau of Animal Industry was established within the US Department of Agriculture , with the aim of preventing the spread of zoonotic diseases in livestock production , especially cattle . This paper investigates the nature and diversity of the documentation produced by the Bureau of Animal Industry , ranging from health , technical , and commercial recom-mendations to the use of architectural plans and photography as edu-cational tools for dairy farmers . The aim is to examine the production of institutional sources from the top down , which allows us to grasp some of the transformations at work in US cattle economy between the end of the nineteenth century and the beginning of the twentieth century . This paper sheds light on the active role played by the Bureau of Animal Industry in the production and dissemination of a new industrial model for dairy farms in the years before the First World War .

title: Hybrid Approach for Logo Segmentation in Videos
abstract: This work focuses on the segmentation of fixed overlay logos in videos . Although state-of-the-art video semantic segmentation models achieve good results , state-of-the-art video semantic segmentation models often rely on complex architectures with high memory and computational costs . high memory and computational costs are even more critical in video processing , where models must handle temporal consistency and efficiently process multiple frames . However , applications such as discriminating overlay content from scene elements have specific constraints and exploitable priors that make generalist models less suitable . We present a hybrid approach that addresses this task by combining the adaptability of deep learning with handcrafted spatio-temporal features . a hybrid approach that addresses this task by combining the adaptability of deep learning with handcrafted spatio-temporal features outperforms traditional models that process frames directly or rely solely on isolated cues , while maintaining competitive inference times . Extensive experiments confirm a hybrid approach that addresses this task by combining the adaptability of deep learning with handcrafted spatio-temporal features effectiveness . We code is available at [ URL ]

title: Ambiances Integration in the HBIM Process Towards an Ambient Twin: A Literature Review
abstract: This paper discusses new methods for digitally valorizing a heritage by proposing the inclusion of sensory and atmospheric dimensions within Heritage Building Information Modeling ( HBIM ) workflows . The age of digital transformation has afforded unprecedented tools through immersive technologies and Information and Communication Technologies ( ICT ) , with which to enrich heritage beyond heritage geometric documentation . Instead of reframing or transforming the experiences of cultural heritage , we propose to turn to a poetic-sensory model with an awareness of the ambient as the mediation between the physical and experiential dimensions . Through a critical literature review and analysis of HBIM projects in Tunis ( Tunisia ) and Nantes ( France ) , we take stock of current practices and suggest future possibilities for defining ambient and in-tangible knowledge using HBIM as the modality . Importantly , we Research supports the evolution of digital twins to encompass ambient twins , to document , capture and ultimately portray emotional attachments and cultural significance of heritage places . a poetic-sensory model with an awareness of the ambient as the mediation between the physical and experiential dimensions is currently being developed within the framework of a joint PhD. The case studies in Tunis ( Tunisia ) and Nantes ( France ) aim to identify relevant tools and methods to capture , store , and integrate atmospheric data into HBIM environments .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: The future of our contemporary sensitivity
abstract: The social sciences must fully adress the issue of sensitivities because sensitivities participate in how the world is constructed and organized . sensitivities are not minor aspect of our society 's workings , and there are multiple scales and objects for understanding and documenting sensitivities . Here we have dwelled on the body and what affects the body , the multiple sensory relations in inhabited environments , and the fabriation of the city as the fabrication of sensitivities .

title: Human Body Shadowing Modeling based on Rotatable Screens and Uniform Theory of Diffraction
abstract: Nowadays , human body effect on electromagnetic waves propagation , known as Human Body Shadowing ( HBS ) , is of prevalent interest , especially for indoor environments , Wireless Body Area Networks ( WBANs ) , pedestrian crowds in dense urban environments and millimeter waves ( mmWaves ) . In this paper , HBS propagation models , based on rotatable screens for the human body geometrical model and Uniform Theory of Diffraction ( UTD ) for the associated electromagnetic theory , are described . HBS propagation models , based on rotatable screens for the human body geometrical model and Uniform Theory of Diffraction ( UTD ) for the associated electromagnetic theory are compared to measurements based on both Motion Capture ( MoCap ) and 2.4 GHz radio systems [ 1 ] , and to Uniform Theory of Diffraction ( UTD elliptic cylinder models [ 2 ] because of HBS propagation models , based on rotatable screens for the human body geometrical model and Uniform Theory of Diffraction ( UTD ) for the associated electromagnetic theory human body orientation inclusion .
keywords: human body shadowing rotatable screen uniform theory of diffraction propagation modeling

title: BOGausS: Better Optimized Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Gaussian Splatting ( 3DGS ) proposes an efficient solution for novel view synthesis . Gaussian Splatting ( 3DGS ) framework provides fast and high-fidelity rendering . Although less complex than other solutions such as Neural Radiance Fields ( NeRF ) , there are still some challenges building smaller models without sacrificing quality . In this study , we perform a careful analysis of Gaussian Splatting ( 3DGS ) training process and propose a new optimization methodology . we Better Optimized Gaussian Splatting ( BOGausS ) solution is able to generate models up to ten times lighter than the original 3DGS with no quality degradation , thus significantly boosting the performance of Gaussian Splatting compared to the state of the art .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Efficient surface impedance modeling of conformal metasurfaces for RCS reduction of drones
abstract: This work investigates a surface impedance-based modeling approach for conformal metasurfaces ( CMS ) applied to curved geometries , with the objective of reducing computational costs and enabling faster simulations compared to full-wave volumetric methods . As a case study , a cylindrical drone section is considered to evaluate the potential of a surface impedance-based modeling approach for conformal metasurfaces ( CMS ) applied to curved geometries to analyse and synthetize conformal metasurfaces for Radar Cross Section ( RCS ) reduction applications .. a surface impedance-based modeling approach for conformal metasurfaces ( CMS ) applied to curved geometries combines the equivalent circuit model and ABCD matrix formalism to compute the angular variation of surface impedance along the curved geometry .
keywords: radar cross section rcs conformal meta surface cms equivalent circuit model ecm

title: The Conformational Electrostatic Potential as Predictor for the Influence of Fluorination on Alcohol Hydrogen Bonding: Identification of a CF 2 H‐Mediated Cooperative Effect
abstract: Hydrogen bonding is the most important noncovalent interaction involved in molecular binding events . Herein , how γ ‐fluorination alters the hydrogen bond ( HB)‐donating capacities of aliphatic alcohol groups is described . Herein , it is shown that the increase in HB‐donating capacity due to the fluorine electronegativity can be significantly attenuated by 6‐membered F•••HO intramolecular HB ( IMHB ) , to the point where even in acyclic structures a decrease in alcohol HB‐donating capacity is observed . The correlation of experimental HB‐donating capacities ( p K AHY ‐scale ) with an easily computed descriptor , the Kenny molecular electrostatic potential V α ( r ) , is discussed . It is shown that F•••HO IMHB leads to a V α ( r ) reduction which , in the case of highly populated IMHB conformers , leads to an underestimation of HB‐donating capacities . The use of conformational electrostatic potentials , however , was found to be very useful to describe OH•••F IMHB , as well as to explain variations in experimental alcohol HB‐donating capacities . Notably , V α ( r)‐analysis allowed the identification of the importance of conformational equilibria in explaining HB‐donating capacity variations of identical fluorohydrin motifs , and notably The use of conformational electrostatic potentials also reveals a cooperative effect involving a difluoromethyl group ( CF 2 H ) on alcohol HB‐donating capacity .

title: Gradient Clipping Improves Neural Network Optimization for Perceptual Sound Matching
abstract: Perceptual Sound Matching ( PSM ) learns the optimal synthesizer input to replicate a target sound perceptually . To achieve so , Perceptual Sound Matching ( PSM ) adopts learning objectives reflective of auditory perceptual distance to derive perceptually informed gradients via automatic differentiation . Yet , learning objectives of Perceptual Sound Matching ( PSM ) are often ill-conditioned , since not all synthesizer and perceptual representation are invertible . To address this challenge , state of the art methods adopt multi-stage training to foster convergence , rendering the training objective non-stationary . In this paper , we show that autoregressive optimization methods like Adam is unsuited to readily reflect the discrepancy in gradient conditions caused by nonstationary objectives , as well as updating weights informed by large gradients from ill-conditioned objectives . we demonstrate empirically how , with a simple formulation of weight decay and gradient clipping , one can optimize Perceptual Sound Matching ( PSM ) with more probable convergence and better generalization . we provide possible reasoning by comparing evolutions of summarized gradient norm and gradient roughness under different optimization setups .

title: Design of Low-Profile Scanning Transmitarrays by Virtual Focus Synthesis
abstract: A novel approach for designing low-profile transmitarray antennas is presented , optimizing phase taper of the primary feed to emulate a spherical wavefront originating from a virtual focal point . The feed aperture is smaller than the transmitarray and placed at a distance H=2λ from the transmitarray . The performance of a 24×24-elements TA with H / D=0.17 is analyzed . A novel approach for designing low-profile transmitarray antennas improves broadside directivity from 28.5 dBi to 32 dBi and reduces 1-bit quantization losses at 60 ° from 4.8 dB to 3 dB as compared to a similar configuration where no phase taper is applied on the aperture field . Finally , the effectiveness of A novel approach for designing low-profile transmitarray antennas is validated using an 8×8 array of open-ended waveguides as a focal array , demonstrating a 2.5 dB gain improvement and significant suppression of quantization lobes in a low-profile TA for beam steering at 40 ° .

title: Branch-and-bound algorithm for exact ℓ0 -norm sparse spectral unmixing
abstract: We propose an algorithm that exactly solves the cardinality-constrained sparse spectral unmixing problem . Based on recent works on ℓ0-norm exact optimization , a branchand-bound architecture is specifically developed for sparse unmixing , under nonnegativity and sum-to-one constraints . an algorithm that exactly solves the cardinality-constrained sparse spectral unmixing problem boils down to solving a finite number of sum-to-one constrained nonnegative least-squares problems for upper-and lower-bounding the global optimal value , which are solved efficiently . Numerical simulations show that We method outperforms competing ones in terms of support identification and estimation , and that an algorithm that exactly solves the cardinality-constrained sparse spectral unmixing problem remains computationally tractable as long as the problem size is limited or the signal-to-noise ratio is high enough . A free C++ implementation is made available .

title: Ambiances. A Sensitivity to Ordinary Situations
abstract: How do ambiances shape our sensory , social , and built environments ? This book offers interdisciplinary perspectives to understand the profound ways in which ambiances redefine our experiences and perceptions of ordinary spaces . The study of ambiances is part of an important trend in the contemporary urban world , where increasing attention is given to the sensitive and affective dimensions of space and experience . Beginning with an exploration of foundational concepts , This book then delves into the sensory , philosophical , and cultural dimensions of ambiances at the intersection of sensory environments and lived experiences . This book explores the role that ambiances play in architectural design , urban spaces , and daily life . This book engages with questions of contemporary sensibility , the sensitive experience of architectures and urban spaces , and the dialogue between the notion of ambiances and that of affective atmospheres . This book connects diverse perspectives of architects , philosophers , anthropologists and geographers to map the conceptual and practical territories of ambiances , from ambiances roots in Francophone research to ambiances broader global implications . This book offers an essential guide to the study of ambiances , providing a foundational and forward-looking exploration , valuable for researchers and upper level undergraduates of architecture , urban studies , urban planning , human geography , anthropology and philosophy .

title: Phoneme-Level Speech Intelligibility Reduction
abstract: As noise masking is central to reducing fatigue in open-plan offices , identifying which elements of speech contribute to intelligibility is essential . This paper employs phoneme-level noise masking techniques to examine how the intelligibility of consonants and vowels degrades under noisy conditions , and to determine which aspects of the speech signal are truly compromised . We introduce and compare two methods : one that applies noise between all phoneme boundaries and another that respectively applies noise to consonants and vowels , based on phonemespecific signal-to-noise ratios . Evaluations on Harvard sentence corpora , using both automatic speech recognition systems and objective intelligibility metrics , reveal that although aggregated word error rates indicate significantly higher degradation for consonants compared to vowels , the direct phoneme error rate analysis does not reflect significantly higher degradation for consonants compared to vowels . reflect suggests that the marked decline in word-level intelligibility may not be solely due to differences in phone class , but also to other factors such as ASR contextual compensation mechanisms .

title: A Tensor-Based Modulation Scheme with Hybrid Optimization for Unsourced Random Access
abstract: This paper extends the idea of tensor-based modulation ( TBM ) for unsourced random access by introducing a new small sub-constellation , enabling a hybrid continuous-discrete optimization approach on the tensor factors . a hybrid continuous-discrete optimization approach on the tensor factors enhances the detection process and extends the tensor decomposition ability , allowing the separation of more active users . Furthermore , a hybrid continuous-discrete optimization approach on the tensor factors can be combined with a preamble-based architecture that partitions bits and resources into unsourced and coherent components . a preamble-based architecture that partitions bits and resources into unsourced and coherent components improves decoding efficiency and detection accuracy , providing a robust solution for unsourced random access scenarios . The energy efficiency of a hybrid continuous-discrete optimization approach on the tensor factors is evaluated under various tensor configurations and compared with state-of-the-art approaches under a quasi-static Rayleigh fading channel model .

title: Diffusion-based spectral super-resolution of third octave acoustic sensor data: is privacy at risk ?
abstract: Third octave spectral recording of acoustic sensor data is an effective way of measuring the environment . While there is strong evidence that slow ( 1s frame , 1 Hz rate ) and fast ( 125ms frame , 8Hz rate ) versions lead by-design to unintelligible speech if reconstructed , the advent of high quality reconstruction methods based on diffusion may pose a threat , as high quality reconstruction methods based on diffusion can embed a significant amount of a priori knowledge when learned over extensive speech datasets . This paper aims to assess this risk at three levels of attacks with a growing level of a priori knowledge considered at the learning of the diffusion model , a ) none , b ) multi-speaker data excluding the target speaker and c ) target speaker . Without any prior regarding the speech profile of the speaker ( levels a and b ) , our results suggest a rather low risk as the worderror-rate both for humans and automatic recognition remains higher than 89 % .

title: TP37 - Tracking Fish Trajectories through Dynamic Pressure Signals: A Dual-Sensor System for Hydrodynamic Cues Monitoring
abstract: Accurate characterization of hydrodynamic cues produced during fish locomotion is essential for understanding behavioral dynamics . In this work , a novel pressure sensor system is presented to isolate the dynamic pressure components associated with fish movements , while compensating for wave induced p ressure . a novel pressure sensor system combines a differential pressure sensor and a water level sensor . a novel pressure sensor system accuracy has been demonstrated through experimental validation against a classical potential flow model around a cylinder , confirming the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed approach .
keywords: sensors dynamic pressure instrumentation wave hydrodynamic model embedded systems

title: Experimental and theoretical investigation of the low velocity impact response of CFRP composite beams
abstract: This paper presents an investigation into the low-velocity impact ( LVI ) behavior of carbon fiber reinforced polymer ( CFRP ) composite beams . The main goal is to explore the experimental and theoretical responses of woven CFRP composites under LVI loading . To simplify the typically complex geometries of composite structures , This paper focuses on beam configurations rather than plates . The effects of impact energy on damage characteristics , peak load , and energy absorption are comprehensively analyzed . The force and energy curves exhibit three distinct behaviors across varying impact levels . Elastic behavior is evident at impact energies of 2 , 5 , and 7.5 J. The damage threshold in terms of force , displacement , and energy for the composite beam is demonstrated at intermediate impact levels of 10 , 12.5 , and 15 J. At the highest impact levels of 17.5 and 20 J , the composite beam undergoes complete collapse , as indicated by a sharp drop in the force-time curves , open-loop force-displacement curves , and a continuous increase in the energy-displacement curves without a descending path . The absorbed energy by the composite beam demonstrates distinct behaviors across the low , intermediate , and high impact energy ranges . A damage-based theoretical model has been proposed that effectively captures the key characteristics of the composite beam impact response . In addition to the damage mechanism , A damage-based theoretical model reveals the presence of an auxiliary energy absorption mechanism that operates concurrently . Notably , an auxiliary energy absorption mechanism that operates concurrently persists across all levels of impact energy , including those within the lowest range . The findings provide valuable insights for enhancing simulation accuracy for impact-resistant composite structures .
keywords: carbon fiber reinforced polymer cfrp composite

title: Cohomologically tropical varieties
abstract: Given the tropicalization of a complex subvariety of the torus , we define a morphism between the tropical cohomology and the rational cohomology of a complex subvariety of the torus respective tropical compactifications . We say that a complex subvariety of the torus is cohomologically tropical if a morphism between the tropical cohomology and the rational cohomology of their respective tropical compactifications is an isomorphism for all closed strata of the tropical compactification . We prove that a schön subvariety of the torus is cohomologically tropical if and only if a schön subvariety of the torus is wunderschön and a schön subvariety of the torus tropicalization is a tropical homology manifold . The former property means that the open strata in the boundary of a tropical compactification are all connected and the mixed Hodge structures on the open strata in the boundary of a tropical compactification cohomology are pure of maximum possible weight ; the latter property requires that , locally , the tropicalization of a complex subvariety of the torus verifies tropical Poincaré duality . We study other properties of cohomologically tropical and wunderschön varieties , and show that in a semistable degeneration to an arrangement of cohomologically tropical varieties , the Hodge numbers of the smooth fibers are captured in the tropical cohomology of the tropicalization of a complex subvariety of the torus . This extends the results of Itenberg , Katzarkov , Mikhalkin and Zharkov .

title: Citizen preferences for risk communication associated with emerging food risks linked to climate change
abstract: Climate change is significantly disrupting weather patterns , resulting in negative impacts on the resilience of agrifood systems . One consequence is an increase in emerging food safety risks driven by climate change to humans , animals , and plants resulting from newly identified hazards , which requires policy action to both mitigate , and adapt to , emerging food risks . Although there is evidence that risk perception associated with novel threats may result in heightened citizen concerns , it is not known whether people 's concerns about emerging food safety hazards necessitate specific risk communication strategies . A semi-structured interview protocol was developed to understand citizen priorities for risk communication in relation to emerging food safety risks , and to understand if citizen priorities for risk communication in relation to emerging food safety risks differed from people 's preferences and priorities for communication about established risks . Twenty participants from each of the UK , France , Germany , and Hungary were recruited into the study . The results indicated that , although study participants did not distinguish emerging food safety risks specifically from existing food safety risks , study participants categorised systemic risks ( which were potentially associated with climate change drivers ) as distinct from acute risks ( which had immediately impacted public health and were not categorised as systemic risks , despite the possibility of being caused by climate change ) . It is concluded that dedicated emerging food safety risk communication is needed to only engage citizens in developing protective behaviours in relation to emerging food safety risks . In addition , dedicated emerging food safety risk communication is also relevant to both adaptive and mitigatory actions to reduce the impacts of emerging food safety risks associated with climate change .

title: Dual-Mirror Wide Angle Quasi-Optical Beamformer in PCB Technology for Satcom Applications
abstract: This paper presents a novel quasi-optical beamformer in multi-layer PCB technology for feeding Low Earth Orbit ( LEO ) arrays to generate multiple beams over wide fields of view in K-band ( 17.3-20.2 GHz ) . The quasi-optical system adopts a dual-mirror configuration to reduce the size of The quasi-optical system and provides the required amplitude and phase illumination to the array . A Physical Optics tool is adopted for the optimization of the shape of The quasi-optical system and location of the input sources . To each source in the focal plane of The quasi-optical system corresponds a pointing direction of the radiated beam in the far field . The quasi-optical system feeds in phase and amplitude 28 elements of a linear array with 23 independent beams over ±55 ° field of view with side lobe levels below-15 dB and beam crossover above-3.9 dB. The true time delay behavior of The quasi-optical system guarantees stable pointing directions in the considered band of operation . The reflection coefficients at the input sources are below-10 dB whereas mutual couplings remain below-19 dB.

title: Formal Modelling of Information System Evolution using B
abstract: In this paper , we explore the problem of predictable evolution of Information System ( IS ) . In this context , a part of the Information System evolution is modelled through phases and interphases in order to specify evolution rules . A formal model is provided using the B language to check the rule effectiveness .
keywords: is modelling predictable system evolution phases formal methods b

title: Scalable Process for Embedding Strain Gauge Sensors in Epoxy-Fiberglass Composites: Toward Next-Generation Smart Fiber-Reinforced Polymers
abstract: Structural health monitoring ( SHM ) is a rapidly advancing field that focuses on the detection and analysis of defects in engineering structures . To meet the demand for lightweight and high-performance materials , composites are increasingly used in place of metals or plastics . This study introduces a manufacturing process based on transfer printing to embed strain gauge sensors into epoxy-fiberglass composites . a manufacturing process based on transfer printing ensures minimal intrusiveness ( < 15 μm ) , low-cost processing , and high scalability . a manufacturing process based on transfer printing enables gentle integration of thin-film sensors directly onto fiber preforms , prior to composite infusion . The sensor architecture ranges from a single layer to multilayer configurations , including silver electrodes and a carbon-based sensing layer with a gauge factor of ∼30 under tensile and compressive strains between −1.5 and 1.5 % . Electrical tests reveal excellent linearity ( R2 > 0.995 ) , mechanical stability over more than 700 cycles , and negligible drift during curing , confirming the robustness of the embedded devices . a manufacturing process based on transfer printing demonstrates the feasibility of integrating functional electronics into fiber-reinforced composites , paving the way for next-generation intelligent structures in SHM applications .

title: Training of physical neural networks
abstract: Physical neural networks ( PNNs ) are a class of neural-like networks that make use of analogue physical systems to perform computations . Although at present confined to small-scale laboratory demonstrations , PNNs could one day transform how artificial intelligence ( AI ) calculations are performed . Could we train AI models many orders of magnitude larger than present ones ? Could we perform model inference locally and privately on edge devices ? Research over the past few years has shown that the answer to these questions is probably \"yes , with enough research\ " . Because PNNs can make use of analogue physical computations more directly , flexibly and opportunistically than traditional computing hardware , PNNs could change what is possible and practical for AI systems . To do change , however , will require notable progress , rethinking both how AI models work and how AI models are trained-primarily by considering the problems through the constraints of the underlying hardware physics . To train PNNs , backpropagation-based and backpropagation-free approaches are now being explored . backpropagation-based and backpropagation-free approaches have various trade-offs and , so far , no method has been shown to scale to large models with the same performance as the backpropagation algorithm widely used in deep learning today . However , this challenge has been rapidly changing and a diverse ecosystem of training techniques provides clues for how PNNs may one day be used to create both more efficient and larger-scale realizations of present-scale AI models .

title: Frequency Domain Identification of a 1-DoF and 3-DoF Fractional-Order Duffing System Using Grünwald–Letnikov Characterization
abstract: Fractional-order models provide a powerful framework for capturing memory-dependent and viscoelastic dynamics in mechanical systems , which are often inadequately represented by classical integer-order characterizations . This study addresses the identification of dynamic parameters in both single-degree-of-freedom ( 1-DOF ) and three-degree-of-freedom ( 3-DOF ) Duffing oscillators with fractional damping , modeled using the Grünwald – Letnikov characterization . 1-DOF includes a cubic nonlinear restoring force and is excited by a harmonic input to induce steady-state oscillations . For both systems , time domain simulations are conducted to capture long-term responses , followed by Fourier decomposition to extract steady-state displacement , velocity , and acceleration signals . steady-state displacement , velocity , and acceleration signals are combined with a GL-based fractional derivative approximation to construct structured regressor matrices . System parameters — including mass , stiffness , damping , and fractional-order effects — are then estimated using pseudoinverse techniques . both systems are validated through a comparison of reconstructed and original trajectories in the phase space , demonstrating high accuracy in capturing the underlying dynamics . The proposed framework provides a consistent and interpretable approach for frequency domain system identification in fractional-order nonlinear systems , with relevance to applications such as mechanical vibration analysis , structural health monitoring , and smart material modeling .

title: Optimization of latent heat storage system performance in food packaging
abstract: Latent heat storage ( LHS ) systems can be utilized at all stages of the cold chain distribution to control the temperature fluctuations in food products . However , Latent heat storage ( LHS ) systems application in food packaging is limited by the low heat transfer rate . This study aims to develop and validate a numerical model to optimize LHS systems in food cold chain distribution , such as food delivery systems , by considering fins of varying thicknesses , numbers , shapes , and locations . The parameters analyzed include the number of fins ( 2–16 ) , thickness ( 0.325 mm , 0.625 mm , and 1.3 mm ) , shape , and location ( branched , lateral , and central types ) . Tetradecane was used as the phase change material ( PCM ) , while aluminum served as the the phase change material ( PCM ) container . The heat transfer and melting process of the phase change material ( PCM ) were numerically solved using the finite element method with COMSOL software 5.4 . The developed model , with an RMSE of 0.35 and an R2 of 0.99 , demonstrated that the LHS system with 8 fins exhibited the best heat absorption performance , achieving a stability percentage of 97.7 % when using tylose gel as a food model . The shape and location of 8 fins had no significant impact on the results due to the low heat transfer rate within the food packaging system . Increasing the fin thickness from 0.325 mm to 1.3 mm altered the aluminum-to-the phase change material ( PCM ) ratio from 0.13 to 0.33 . Consequently , the PCM quantity significantly influenced the results , making it difficult to isolate the effect of fin thickness alone .
