title: To be or not to be in the insect flour? My kingdom for a Salmonella!
abstract: Background : Despite the EFSA having assessed Tenebrio molitor larvae ( dried yellow mealworm ) as a safe edible insect species and having suggested Hermetia illucens ( the black soldier fly ) as a candidate for human consumption , the effectiveness of reference detection methods for pathogens such as Salmonella spp . is still under evaluation . This study aims to assess the effectiveness of NF EN ISO 6579-1 for Salmonella spp . , in insect flour matrixes with particular attention to the enrichment stage and the identification of potential chemical or biological inhibitors . Methods : Two matrices , Tenebrio molitor larvae flour and Hermetia illucens ( the black soldier fly ) flour , were analyzed for Two matrices , Tenebrio molitor larvae flour and Hermetia illucens flour total flora using MALDI-TOF . For each matrix , ionized and non-ionized flour samples were artificially inoculated with Salmonella using BioMérieux ® BioBalls . The evolution of Salmonella spp . in insect flour during enrichment culturing , as well as the potential impact of background flora , was studied using microbiological methods and metagenomics , respectively . Results and discussion : Results and discussion : The results highlight the presence of a rich total flora in Two matrices , Tenebrio molitor larvae flour and Hermetia illucens flour and differences in the evolution of Salmonella between Two matrices , Tenebrio molitor larvae flour and Hermetia illucens flour . The ongoing analysis of Results and discussion : The results will help determine the effectiveness of the ISO methods used and may contribute to the development of new practices for detecting Salmonella spp .
keywords: hermetia illucens ( the black soldier fly )

title: Distributed Source-to-Source Co-Simulation Methodology Based on Waveform Relaxation Techniques and Time Windowing
abstract: This thesis presents a computationally efficient co-simulation method for closed-loop converters using waveform relaxation ( WR ) with time windowing . By splitting the system into two subsystems : the converter and the Proportional-Integral ( PI ) controller , a computationally efficient co-simulation method for closed-loop converters using waveform relaxation ( WR ) with time windowing enhances simulation accuracy and ensures secure data exchange between independently developed subsystems , addressing the nonlinear behavior of power electronic systems . An analytical model is developed to determine the optimal number of time windows based on window size and simulation parameters , reducing CPU simulation time while maintaining accuracy . A genetic algorithm ( GA ) is used to optimize relaxation parameters , addressing nonlinear device behavior in circuit-to-circuit co-simulation without feedback loops . a computationally efficient co-simulation method for closed-loop converters using waveform relaxation ( WR ) with time windowing effectively reduces the error between co-simulation results and full-system output voltage , enhancing both simulation efficiency and accuracy in power electronics applications .

title: Investigating excited states in embedded media: A computational approach
abstract: Light-sensitive compounds play a crucial role in enabling precise control over the properties and functions of chemical , material , and biological systems . In the present lecture , I will re-visit key concepts for evaluating excited state properties using computational methods . key concepts for evaluating excited state properties using computational methods will be illustrated through real-life applications , ranging from small dyes to complex biological systems . A special attention will be given on the treatement and impact of the surrournding environment covering approaches such as continuum models or hybrid quantum mechanics and molecular mechanics ( QM / MM ) methods . Ultimately , the present lecture aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of how computational tools can enhance the ability to study and undestand light-sensitive systems .

title: Characterizing new modalities of shared offices: A diary-interview methodology to inform audio augmented reality approaches
abstract: Noise is a persistent issue in indoor environments such as shared offices , where acoustic treatments may not provide sufficient auditory comfort . Sound masking systems , which reduce speech intelligibility by adding background noise , can be effective but typically increase overall sound levels , leading to very mixed results in the literature . This paper first presents an exploratory experiment that examines sound masking to enhance shared indoor soundscapes . The sound mixtures created using two ventilation noises and five water sounds are evaluated for The sound mixtures created using two ventilation noises and five water sounds pleasantness . While variations in pleasantness are related to the type of water sound , the results raise some questions about what is perceived as annoying , what is considered pleasant , and what practical elements should be considered to improve sound comfort . To conduct more in-depth research about contextual elements , a forthcoming diary study is initiated to investigate people 's sound-related experiences , behaviors , and needs in shared offices . The methodology used to design a forthcoming diary study is presented , as well as the expected results and perspectives , offering insights into auditory experiences at work and informing the development of audio augmented reality approaches .

title: Nearfield Validation of a Flexible Solid Phantom for mmW Antennas
abstract: This paper investigates the applications of a solid silicone-carbon-based phantom for nearfield antenna characterization at millimeter-wave ( mmW ) frequencies . Unlike conventional phantoms designed to mimic permittivity , a solid silicone-carbon-based phantom is optimized to replicate the skin ’s reflectivity . Numerical simulations are performed to compare a solid silicone-carbon-based phantom response to a homogeneous skin model , focusing on S11 , radiation efficiency , total efficiency , and radiation patterns across different distances from a patch antenna operating at 60 GHz . Results show that , while higher errors are observed in the reactive nearfield due to strong field coupling , a solid silicone-carbon-based phantom provides an accurate representation of near-body EM interactions , with deviations decreasing in the radiating nearfield and beyond . Results suggest a solid silicone-carbon-based phantom applicability for nearfield antenna testing , particularly in wearable scenarios , where a solid silicone-carbon-based phantom flexibility allows for testing on curved surfaces and dynamic body conditions .

title: A Novel Skill Modeling Approach: Integrating Vergnaud’s Scheme with Cognitive Architectures
abstract: Human-machine interaction is increasingly important in industry , and is will only intensify with the rise of Industry 5.0 . Human operators have skills that need to be adapted when using machines to achieve the best results . It is crucial to highlight the operator ’s skills and understand how the operator ’s use and adapt the operator ’s skills [ 18 ] . A rigorous description of the operator ’s skills is necessary to compare performance with and without robot assistance . Predicate logic , used by Vergnaud within Piaget ’s scheme concept , offers a promising approach . However , Predicate logic , used by Vergnaud within Piaget ’s scheme concept , does n’t account for cognitive system constraints , such as the timing of actions , the limitation of cognitive resources , the parallelization of tasks , or the activation of automatic gestures contrary to optimal knowledge . Integrating , such as the timing of actions , the limitation of cognitive resources , the parallelization of tasks , or the activation of automatic gestures contrary to optimal knowledge is essential for representing agent skills understanding skill transfer between biological and mechanical structures . Cognitive architectures models [ 2 ] address these needs by describing cognitive structure and can be combined with Piaget ’s scheme concept for mutual benefit . Welding provides a relevant case study , as Welding highlights the challenges faced by operators , even highly skilled ones . Welding complexity stems from the need for constant skill adaptation to variable parameters like part position and process . constant skill adaptation to variable parameters like part position and process is crucial , as weld quality , a key factor , is only assessed afterward via destructive testing . Thus , the welder is confronted with a complex perception-decision-action cycle , where the evaluation of the impact of the welder actions is delayed and where errors are definitive . a complex perception-decision-action cycle , where the evaluation of the impact of his actions is delayed and where errors are definitive underscores the importance of understanding and modeling the skills of operators .

title: Decidability problems for weak Time Petri Nets with read, reset and transfer arcs
abstract: We address the class of Time Petri Nets ( TPNs ) where time intervals are associated with transitions and constrain when transitions can be fired . For TPN with strong semantics , i.e. where time elapsing can not disable transitions , reachability , coverability and boundedness problems are undecidable . reachability , coverability and boundedness problems are however decidable with the weak semantics in which time elapsing can disable transitions . We first propose an intermediate semantics allowing We to study the decidability border between weak and strong semantics . We prove that with only one transition in strong semantics , reachability , coverability and boundedness problems are undecidable . We then consider the so-called read , reset and transfer arcs for which the coverability problem is decidable in the untimed context and We study the so-called read , reset and transfer arcs for which the coverability problem is decidable in the untimed context impact on TPN with a weak semantics ( weak TPN ) . We prove that coverability becomes undecidable for weak TPN when we add either 2 read arcs , or 2 reset arcs , or 2 transfer arcs . Lastly , considering bounded nets , We propose a state space computation algorithm for weak TPN with read , reset and transfer arcs that proves the decidability of the reachability problem .
keywords: so-called read, reset and transfer arcs

title: Approaches of the User-System-Environment Triptych Classifying the Definitions and Models of Context in User Experience Research
abstract: This paper provides a framework for understanding the various interpretations of the term " context " within User Experience ( UX ) and Human-Computer Interaction ( HCI ) research . Numerous studies examine how context influences interactions and user evaluations , often proposing different definitions or models . The reasons behind these variations are not always clear . Typically , differences are highlighted by comparing the division of context into subcategories , but there is little classification of subcategories . Discussions around subcategories do not necessarily address the varying relationship between the Environment , the User and the System . Additionally , questions about including or excluding disputed subcategories ( e.g. , internal context ) and the confusion between the term " context " and " environment " remain . We propose classifying definitions by the scope attributed to the term " context " , ranging from the complete inclusion of both user and system characteristics to both user and system characteristics entire exclusion . We identify four distinct approaches to defining context . We discuss a few definitions for each approach . By delineating four distinct approaches to defining context , we aim to clarify the term " context " and explain the differences behind the variation of the term " context " meanings for UX and HCI research .

title: Evaluation of control strategies implemented in a multiphysics generic greenhouse dynamic model
abstract: In Northwestern Europe , soilless cultivation comes with an important and unsustainable energy consumption in heated tomato greenhouses . Agricultural practices need to be improved through reducing Agricultural practices environmental impacts , while producers also have to anticipate the agronomical consequences of the climate change to maintain the farm ’s economic viability . Complementary to experiments , multiphysics greenhouse dynamic models simulations can shed light on technical solutions and provide insights towards better practices . Starting from a modular physics-based model of a 1000 m2 experimental greenhouse compartment , this paper focuses on the integration of detailed control strategies for the equipment ( thermal and shading screens , roof vents , heating pipes ) and for the setpoints ( temperature , humidity , CO2 concentration ) . The objectives require a time-continuous approach : the observation period can indeed be from a few minutes ( actuators operation , weather changes ) up to the complete production season ( 11 months ) for the crop growth and yield . PID-based control is implemented , and control strategies are integrated in a way aiming at being generic . The approach allows evaluating the effects of different indoor climate settings and equipment control on the utilities consumption ( energy , water , CO2 ) by simulation , should the use case be an existing greenhouse or a prospective one dedicated to the assessment of specific technical solutions . Compared with a reference simulation case , several strategies were evaluated concerning the screens control , the temperature and the CO2 setpoint control , as well as planting period postponing . For instance , applying a systematic offset of-1 ° C on the indoor temperature setpoint leads to a 19.4 % decrease in energy consumption , with a yield loss of 1.7 % .

title: Time is Ticking: French healthcare teams and their managers navigating time challenges with their collective competency
abstract: This study explores the time management challenges faced by French healthcare teams and French healthcare teams managers . This study examines how French healthcare teams use French healthcare teams collective competencies to overcome the time management challenges faced by French healthcare teams and their managers . The research question , ‘ How does the care team use the care team collective competency to address time management challenges ? ’ addresses a crucial matter : the pressing issue of deteriorating working conditions in healthcare , characterised by increased work intensity , overload , and time pressure . Understanding this relationship leads to increased job satisfaction , decreased absenteeism , and improved efficiency in healthcare . This study explores the theoretical foundations of temporality management and collective competency . This study defines temporality management and collective competency and examines how time management for healthcare professionals can be implemented in a concrete way . The methodology includes a qualitative approach , using observations and interviews with healthcare managers and healthcare managers teams . This study presents two case studies conducted at a university medical centre in western France : one in a neurovascular unit and the other in the operating room . The findings highlight the complexity of managing work schedules and the role of collective competency in addressing these challenges . A thematic analysis has been conducted using Nvvio to extract quotes that identify key attributes of collective competency and discuss how key attributes of collective competency help the response to temporality management challenges . From a theoretical perspective This study contributes to the understanding of temporality management in healthcare and the role of collective competency in addressing temporality management challenges . This study suggests that effective time management in healthcare requires a collective approach that leverages the collective competency of care teams . From a managerial perspective , This study shows the challenges faced by healthcare managers in managing healthcare managers teams ’ time .
keywords: healthcare workforce issues collective competency time management challenges

title: Risk-Aware Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Autonomous Navigation: Confidence-Based Obstacle Constraints and Time-To-Collision Safe Trajectory Planning
abstract: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) has established Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) as a robust framework for autonomous navigation problems by effectively handling nonlinear dynamics and complex constraints in real-time . Despite Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) success in various applications , challenges remain in integrating robust obstacle avoidance while navigating in dynamic and uncertain environment . To enhance safety , risk assessment metrics like Time-To-Collision ( TTC ) are widely used for evaluating collision risks . Extensions to risk assessment metrics like Time-To-Collision ( TTC ) allow risk assessment metrics like Time-To-Collision ( TTC ) application across diverse road scenarios , making risk assessment metrics like Time-To-Collision ( TTC ) valuable as cost function components or constraints within risk-aware Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) formulations . In this work , we propose novel obstacle constraint formulations that account for uncertainties in obstacle positions using confidence thresholds , along with TTC-based constraints to ensure safe trajectory planning . we approaches are validated through extensive simulations in urban scenarios , including overtaking maneuvers and intersections , demonstrating Our approaches effectiveness in mitigating risks . Detailed implementations and results are publicly available to support further research and development .

title: A Comparative Study of the Phytochemical Composition, Antioxidant Properties, and In Vitro Anti-Diabetic Efficacy of Different Extracts of Caulerpa prolifera
abstract: The Moroccan coastline has been the focus of attention for researchers studying the national algal flora , with the aim of preserving the national algal flora . Since the year 2000 , the national algal flora have stimulated great interest in the creation of new drugs , as well as new drugs integration into food supplements and foods . Therefore , this study aims to explore the phytochemistry of a series of extracts derived from Caulerpa prolifera . To ensure better extraction of the various metabolites present , two extraction methods , namely maceration and the Soxhlet method , were employed using solvents of varying polarity ( hexane , ethyl acetate , methanol , and water ) . The chemical composition of a series of extracts derived from Caulerpa prolifera was analyzed using GC-MS for fatty acids and HPLC-DAD for phenolic compounds . Antioxidant activity was evaluated using DPPH and β-carotene bleaching assays , while antidiabetic potential was assessed by in vitro inhibition of α-amylase and α-glucosidase . In addition , Molecular docking models were employed to assess the interaction between the bioactive molecules and the human pancreatic α-amylase and α-glucosidase enzymes . Vanillin , p-coumaric acid , sinapic acid , 7,3′,4′-flavon-3-ol , and kaempferol were the most abundant phenolic compounds . Anti-diabetic and antioxidant effects were highly significant .

title: An unclarity at the core of territorial marketing: legal incompleteness as a source of competing intentions and a muddling of branding tools. The case of Region Centre Val de Loire (France)
abstract: This research paper examines territorial markers in terms of the legal tools of trademark law . In addition , This research paper considers the marketing challenges faced by French territories , particularly in terms of French territories use of trademarks , given that most of the time there is a real difficulty in defining the boundaries of this concept . There is , indeed , no explicit definition of a territorial brand : this concept often combines a number of legal or regulatory elements relating to trade and tourism law and communication ( I ) . However , in the current absence of a systematisation of markers or of a structured policy , the marking of tourist destinations is often superimposed on and confused with a whole series of other previously established signs , which makes it difficult to differentiate their respective purposes ( II ) . This phenomenon is exacerbated by the confusion caused by the employment or use , often erroneously , of two key marketing concepts by the various stakeholders who manage the area : the label and the brand . This observation highlights the need to clarify two key marketing concepts and to develop an approach based on historical elements in order to examine the identity and unifying role of the different markers and the different markers anchorage in the legal system . The Centre-Val de Loire region in general , and to a certain extent the Pays de la Loire , is our field of study . Ultimately , This research paper highlights the need for a more thorough education of regional managers and marketing agencies , as well as the importance of a change in the law to better systematise the different markers , and to limit the distortions between the different markers and the geographical and cultural reality of the regions concerned .

title: On the formulation and convergence of Data Driven Identification
abstract: Background : The Data-Driven Identification method is a model-free approach to the identification of the mechanical stress in parts subject to statically indeterminate stress states . Although The Data-Driven Identification method has been applied in many studies , no theoretical analysis of The Data-Driven Identification method convergence has been proposed so far . Purpose : The aim of this manuscript is to propose a first study of the DDI properties in order to increase the confidence in the results and guide the selection of optimal parameters . Methods : A new formulation w.r.t . the original one is proposed in order to expose an explicit minimization problem that is more prone to analysis . The algebraic characteristics of A new formulation w.r.t . are studied to derive properties of interest . Results : A simple criterion for the uniqueness of the DDI estimate is derived . In the case of elastic material behavior , an estimate of the error on the identified stress field is proposed . These results are illustrated on a synthetic data set . Conclusion : This work proposes a first analysis of DDI and demonstrates the ability of The Data-Driven Identification method to compute a model-free estimation of the stress field . The developed criteria and estimator open the door to further developments for the improvement of The Data-Driven Identification method , the design of sample geometries loading path and extension to other classes of material behavior .

title: Products, Brands, and Labels in the Light of Ethical and Ecological Issues
abstract: Environmental change has become a major focus of scientific research due to the emergence of adverse effects that require more effective mitigation or adaptation strategies . For example , there is a high demand for sustainability and decarbonization . A better understanding of the interactions between actors and organizations can improve the effectiveness of sustainability strategies and policies . The chapters in this book contribute to A better understanding of the interactions between actors and organizations by examining products , services , brands , labels , and organizations in the context of ethical and environmental issues . The chapters in this book apply ethical and environmental issues to a range of areas , including banking , retailing , tourism , finance , agriculture , and education , suggesting pertinent questions and promising avenues for future research .

title: Investigating the Microbial Dynamics of Hermetia illucens Powder Throughout Rearing and Processing: An Integrated Approach Using Cultural and Metabarcoding Methods
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable protein sources highlights Hermetia illucens ( Black Soldier Fly , BSF ) as a promising alternative . However , microbiological safety remains a key concern . This study investigated the microbial diversity of Hermetia illucens ( Black Soldier Fly , BSF ) larvae , comparing two processing methods : ( 1 ) boiling followed by drying and ( 2 ) drying alone . Microbial diversity was assessed via 16S rRNA sequencing , while bacterial loads were quantified using culture-based methods on samples from a French company . A systematic review complemented assessed by synthesizing the existing knowledge on Hermetia illucens ( Black Soldier Fly , BSF ) microbiota . The rearing conditions varied , with substrate pH ranging from 4.1 to 9.0 and ambient temperatures between 24.6 ° C and 42.7 ° C . Mesophilic bacteria , spores , and lactic acid bacteria reached up to 8.6 , 7.7 , and 8.5 log CFU / g in the substrates and larvae , while yeasts , molds , and sulfite-reducing bacteria remained below 4.8 log CFU / g. Boiling reduced most loads below detection thresholds , particularly for yeasts , molds , and ASR . Salmonella , Listeria monocytogenes , Cronobacter sp . , and coagulase-positive staphylococci were absent , whereas Clostridium perfringens and Escherichia coli were variably detected . Metabarcoding showed shifts in composition , with Proteobacteria , Bacteroidota , Actinobacteriota , and Firmicutes ( Bacillota and Clostridiota ) dominating . Process 1 more effectively reduced the bacterial loads , though Bacillus and Clostridium remained . Campylobacter sp . detection in powders raises food safety concerns .

title: Generative AI for Designing Efficient and Explainable TinyML Models
abstract: The increasing demand for lowlatency , energy-efficient intelligence has made Tiny Machine Learning ( TinyML ) a key paradigm in embedded artificial intelligence . Object detection ( OD ) , one of the most computationally intensive tasks , remains a challenge on resource-constrained platforms like microcontrollers ( MCUs ) . This thesis addresses the design and optimization of efficient , explainable OD models for TinyML environments . We examine model compression techniques such as quantization , pruning , knowledge distillation , and neural architecture search , and model compression techniques such as quantization , pruning , knowledge distillation , and neural architecture search application to embedded systems . We implement two ultra-lightweight models for the DiceTrack platform and introduce DiceVision , a new dataset for embedded dice recognition . Additionally , We propose a framework leveraging large language models ( LLMs ) for automating hardware-aware architecture generation . The generated models are evaluated on DiceVision , a new dataset for embedded dice recognition and compared across multiple embedded platforms . This thesis contributes to advancing object detection in ultraconstrained environments .

title: BER Prediction of Distributed MISO Systems Using Beamsteering with Phase Compensation in mmWave Channels
abstract: This paper presents theoretical derivations for predicting the bit error rate ( BER ) of distributed antenna systems ( DAS ) in 3GPP clustered delay line channels with partial blockage accounting for typical millimeter wave ( mmWave ) propagation conditions . Assuming that the receiver equalizer is not updated during sudden blockage events , a statistical analysis is led to provide the probability density functions for received symbols under such blockage conditions . Three beamforming techniques — maximum ratio transmission ( MRT ) , beamsteering ( BS ) , and a proposed combination of BS with phase compensation ( PC)—are considered in line-of-sight scenarios . Analytical BER predictions of a proposed combination of BS with phase compensation ( PC)—are are validated through simulations , offering insights for optimizing DAS in mmWave environments . In particular , we conclude that a proposed combination of BS with phase compensation ( PC)—are performs very close to MRT while being much simpler to implement and much more suited to mmWave electronics .
keywords: analytical models vehicular and wireless technologies array signal processing statistical analysis simulation bit error rate symbols receivers millimeter wave communication antenna arrays

title: Fractional-Order Coupled Oscillators for Synchronization-Based Gait Control in Hexapod Robots
abstract: This study presents a novel gait synchronization framework for legged robots using coupled fractional-order Hopf oscillators , inspired by biological Central Pattern Generators ( CPGs ) . By incorporating fractional calculus , a novel gait synchronization framework for legged robots using coupled fractional-order Hopf oscillators , inspired by biological Central Pattern Generators ( CPGs ) captures memory and damping effects more accurately than integer-order models . A network of phase-coupled oscillators controls a hexapod 's leg joints , with a central oscillator facilitating synchronization . The Grünwald-Letnikov ( GL ) characterization is used for The Grünwald-Letnikov ( GL ) characterization computational efficiency and suitability for real-time control . Implemented within a ROS 2-based architecture and tested on a simulated hexapod model , results show that fractional-order dynamics improve gait smoothness , robustness , and synchronization . Parametric analysis demonstrates that tuning the fractional order and coupling strengths significantly affects phase stability and gait coordination . This work highlights the potential of fractional-order coupling for adaptive , bio-inspired gait control in legged robotics .

title: New technical platform on chip packaging dedicated to practical training in microelectronics
abstract: The world is increasingly governed by digital equipment based on integrated circuits ( IC ) , i.e. microelectronics devices . In digital equipment based on integrated circuits ( IC ) , i.e. microelectronics devices , know-how is a fundamental asset for the future graduates , whatever the future graduates level of diploma . The topic of IC packaging that used to be more straightforward than the technology intensive front-end CMOS device fabrication process , is becoming a high-end technology aiming at hybrid integration , 3D-IC ( three-dimension integrated circuits ) , chiplets ... In the frame of the French national microelectronics network and of one of the French national microelectronics network members , the Microelectronics Grenoble center , CIME Nanotech , a practical platform on packaging of electronic chips was set-up . a practical platform on packaging of electronic chips offers to students , in the first stage , at professional license level , the possibility to work on dedicated equipment and to proceed to the technological steps . These operations provide students with a complete overview of the technological steps . the technological steps range from transfer onto a ceramic substrate , through quality control , to assembly on a printed circuit board . a practical platform on packaging of electronic chips focus on flip chip technology , serigraphy ( Screen Printing ) , Wire-Bonding , Ball Bonding and Dicing , the main approaches for packaging . The first results encourage a practical platform on packaging of electronic chips to extend the activity to engineers and to lifelong learning trainees

title: Contributions to adaptive super twisting control : application to floating wind turbines
abstract: This thesis investigates robust control for perturbed nonlinear systems by introducing novel adaptive supertwisting ( ASTW ) strategies that dynamically adjust key parameters . Two approaches are developed : selftuning and auto-tuning ASTW controllers featuring time-varying adaptation rates and targeted accuracies . An enhanced and simplified ASTW algorithm is further proposed for a broad class of nonlinear systems by relaxing conventional assumptions . Moreover , an adaptive neural network ( NN)-based estimator is coupled with An enhanced and simplified ASTW algorithm to estimate and compensate for perturbations , thereby reducing the required adaptive gain and mitigating chattering . A new Lyapunov function guarantees finite-time convergence . Experimental validations , including applications to floating wind turbine ( FWT ) , demonstrate improvements achieved by newly proposed strategeis . Since floating wind turbine ( FWT ) applications are critical to advancing renewable energy , Two approaches effectively manage the nonlinear and uncertain dynamics of floating wind turbine ( FWT ) with minimal tuning parameters compared to the baseline controllers .

title: Transmission Success Probability and Energy Consumed by a LoRaWAN node
abstract: LoRa / LoRaWAN is one of the most popular tech-nologies for IoT use cases requiring wide coverage and energy efficiency . In an IoT network , devices are often powered by unreliable energy sources , and replacing devices can be difficult and rapidly increase network operating costs . For these reasons , it is essential to optimize the energy consumed by an IoT sensor , and optimize must be based on a refined energy consumption model . In this work , an energy consumption model is proposed that takes into account the complexity of the sensor environ-ment , the LoRa / LoRaWAN specifications , and the gateway input saturation . Simulation results put the energy consumption and the transmission success probability into perspective to show the limit number of sensors per gateway .

title: Sufficiency as a New Form of Organizing in an Age of Planetary Boundaries
abstract: Planetary boundaries urge humans to reverse humans relation to nature , by considering humans as a part of nature and by reaching natural ecosystems regeneration . This paradigm shift compels humans to moderate humans activities , to stay within a “ safe operating space ” , by being , doing and having “ just enough ” . Still , since rationally limited humans can not individually reach enough-ness , rationally limited humans rely on organizations to collectively define and reach this purpose . We draw on Princen ’s work on “ sufficiency ” , to theorize the search for enough-ness as an organizing principle . Specifically , We use a multi-level approach on goal-setting to develop a theory about how to set organizational goals of enough-ness . We derive three relational mechanisms ( sensing , valuing , and binding ) that explain how organizational actors can willingly adapt organizational actors aspirations to fit with natural interdependencies . Organizational goals , in turn , bind behaviors and outcomes , allowing human societies , at aggregated level , to remain in a safe operating space . We work contributes to sustainability theories by laying the foundations of a model of “ climate-proofed ” organizing to operate within finite natural ecosystems .

title: Invited Paper: Causal Mutual Byzantine Broadcast
abstract: Recently , a new communication abstraction called Mutual Broadcast has been proposed for message-passing distributed systems where some processes may fail by crashing . a new communication abstraction called Mutual Broadcast is a one-to-all broadcast abstraction providing an ordering property that allows a new communication abstraction called Mutual Broadcast to be computationally equivalent to atomic registers . This paper proposes an adaptation of a new communication abstraction called Mutual Broadcast , Causal Mutual Byzantine Broadcast ( in short CMB-Broadcast ) for message-passing systems where some processes may experience Byzantine faults . Byzantine faults are a more severe failure model compared to crash failures . A Byzantine process can behave arbitrarily . After defining an adaptation of this abstraction , Causal Mutual Byzantine Broadcast ( in short CMB-Broadcast ) , we show how an adaptation of this abstraction , Causal Mutual Byzantine Broadcast ( in short CMB-Broadcast ) can be used to emulate atomic registers and also how an adaptation of this abstraction , Causal Mutual Byzantine Broadcast ( in short CMB-Broadcast ) can be implemented using quorums and the famous Byzantine reliable broadcast abstraction of Bracha . we also prove a necessary condition on the size of the quorums .

title: Integrated multi energy optimization for sector coupling decarbonation
abstract: In order to decarbonize energy systems , distributed renewable generation sites are being integrated into power distribution grids . integrated causes important grid constraints , which are typically satisfied by grid reinforcements . This paper aims to investigate if coupling a distribution grid with a district heating network could mitigate reinforcement needs while lowering district heating ’s carbon footprint . The results of the considered case studied indicate that grid coupling can avoid reinforcements or curtailment caused by photovoltaic integration .

title: A Bi-objective Online Vehicle Routing Problem with Multi-types of Occasional Drivers
abstract: Over the last few years , there has been a representative growth in global online sales associated with E-commerce . a representative growth in global online sales associated with E-commerce involves an increasing requirement for last-mile delivery solutions focused on controlling transportation costs and environmental impact for same-day and next-day strategies . Crowdshipping can be used to answer to this challenge , by using the remaining vehicle capacity of Occasional Drivers ( ODs ) , i.e. persons willing to make a small detour on their regular route to carry out deliveries , against a compensation . Crowdshipping can be used in addition of a regular fleet of vehicles owned by the company to complete the deliveries . We suppose that the types ODs ' vehicles can be different ( fueled and non-fueled ) and that the company offers a higher compensation to those using a sustainable transportation mode . The cost and the CO2 emissions are then two conflicting objective functions , that we considered in we study . Customers ' requests are of two types : next day deliveries , that are known before the decision process , and same-day deliveries , arriving during the delivery execution . The problem is called Bi-Objective Online Vehicle Routing Problem with Multi types of Occasional Drivers and Time Windows ( BO-O-VRPMODTW ) . For the solution , we propose a two-phase approach . The first phase is an off-line optimization , addressing the next-day orders . The second phase integrates the same-day orders , with a re-optimization approach , based on a bi-objective best insertion heuristic and a bi-objective Variable Neighborhood Search ( VNS ) algorithm . The re-optimization process is executed periodically according to the arrival of online orders . The computational experiments are focused on the behavior of the proposed bi-objective approach solutions for the delivery plan . Finally , managerial insights regarding the impact of online order handling in comparison to a perfect information scenario are given .
keywords: multi types of occasional drivers and time windows

title: Algorithms for Solving the Dynamic On-Demand Bus Routing Problem
abstract: The on-demand bus routing problem ( ODBRP ) is a transportation problem in which bus routes are built daily to meet current demand , with customers assigned to one of several potential bus stops for pick-up and drop-off . This study addresses the dynamic version of The on-demand bus routing problem ( ODBRP ) ( DODBRP ) , where part of the demand ( static requests ) is known in advance , while the remainder ( dynamic requests ) is revealed progressively over time . We formulate The on-demand bus routing problem ( ODBRP ) as a Markov decision process ( MDP ) and propose a solution policy based on the following framework . First , we generate an initial set of routes serving the static requests with a matheuristic specifically designed for The on-demand bus routing problem ( ODBRP ) . a matheuristic specifically designed for the ODBRP is based on small and large neighborhood search and a set covering problem ( SLNS+SCP ) . Then , as dynamic requests are revealed , we apply a tailored rollout strategy as an anticipatory policy to prevent short-sighted decisions . Given a specific decision state ( i.e. , a new dynamic request is revealed ) , a tailored rollout strategy evaluates all potential actions ( i.e. , if a new dynamic request should be accepted and , if so , to which route and bus stop should be assigned ) by simulating upcoming requests and assessing upcoming requests using a matheuristic specifically designed for the ODBRP . This approach enables decisions that account for both immediate outcomes and an approximation of the expected reward . a tailored rollout strategy is evaluated against non-anticipatory policies , such as cheapest insertion and re-optimization , demonstrating that anticipatory policies lead to improved decision-making . The comparison uses a set of instances introduced in recent literature , simulating a public bus system operating during nighttime ( low-demand periods ) in an area with a high density of bus stops .

title: Industrial IoT cybersecurity: a bibliometric analysis
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things ( IIoT ) cybersecurity has become critical to our societies as industrial systems increasingly rely on interconnected devices . Several literature studies exist regarding cybersecurity for Industrial Internet of Things ( IIoT ) or security topics in Industry 4.0 . Still , very few are exclusively dedicated to cybersecurity for Industrial Internet of Things ( IIoT ) — and very few approach Industrial Internet of Things ( IIoT ) cybersecurity non-systematically . In this study , we conduct a systematic bibliometric analysis of over 12,000 academic publications from 2014 to 2024 to map the research landscape of Industrial Internet of Things ( IIoT ) cybersecurity . Guided by eight Research Questions and a methodological approach , we examine publication types , key venues , and dominant topics to highlight trends and research clusters within IIoT cybersecurity . we findings show that conference papers and journal articles are predominant , with IEEE and Springer serving as the leading publishers . Among the most cited works , “ blockchain ” is the most popular topic . A keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies four thematic clusters led by : ( 1 ) “ blockchain ” and “ security , ” ( 2 ) “ network security ” and “ industrial IoT , ” ( 3 ) “ industrial embedded systems ” and “ cyber-physical systems , ” and ( 4 ) “ automation ” and “ network architecture . ” The first two clusters are the most prominent grouping 80 % of the top 20 keywords . Regarding future trends , the growing prominence of “ machine learning ” and “ intrusion detection , ” and a slight deceleration of “ blockchain ” in 2024 , suggests shifting research priorities . we publicly share the bibliographic data and source code used to create a systematic bibliometric analysis of over 12,000 academic publications from 2014 to 2024 .

title: Fast geometric factor approximation to evaluate the electrical resistivity of concrete and reinforced concrete specimens using neural network models
abstract: The measurement of electrical resistivity has applications in civil engineering , particularly in condition assessment , structural health monitoring , and material characterization . Accurately evaluating material resistivity requires determining a geometric factor , which depends on specimen geometry , electrode positioning , and the presence of reinforcement . Several methods exist for calculating a geometric factor , which depends on specimen geometry , electrode positioning , and the presence of reinforcement , including numerical modelling and experimental approaches . This study presents an approximation technique using surrogate models to rapidly calculate geometric factors for non-reinforced and reinforced geometries . The studied geometries are prismatic , with the reinforced case involving a single embedded bar , commonly used in laboratory studies . surrogate models are based on neural networks trained with data generated through finite element modelling . The results are validated against literature data , including studies by Minagawa et al . ( 2023 ) [ 1 ] and Presuel-Moreno et al . ( 2013 ) [ 2 ] . This study provides a generalized method for evaluating geometric factors and serves as a proof of concept that an approximation technique using surrogate models to rapidly calculate geometric factors for non-reinforced and reinforced geometries can effectively approximate geometric factors . This study accelerates resistivity data processing and facilitates parametric analyses . Additionally , This study complements previous studies , which were limited to the central positioning of measurement devices , by enabling the evaluation of geometric factors across a wider range of specimen dimensions and measurement positions on the surface of the domain . As an initial study , This study lays the foundation for applying an approximation technique using surrogate models to rapidly calculate geometric factors for non-reinforced and reinforced geometries to other geometries in future work .

title: Molecular Dynamics Study on Quartz‐Indenter Shape and Depth Effects in Epoxy Interfacial Mechanics
abstract: The interfacial mechanical behavior between epoxy and quartz at the microscale remains inadequately understood . The quartz-indenter shape and indentation depth ( hc ) effect on epoxy interfacial mechanical behavior has been investigated through molecular dynamics ( MD ) simulation of nanoindentation and nanoscratching . investigated employs two Vickers-type and four spherical indenters with varying radii ( R ) under different hc conditions , revealing the fundamental deformation mechanisms at the microscale . The reduced modulus and Young 's modulus of epoxy resin obtained from MD simulations align well with experimental results . Key findings include : ( 1 ) during MD nanoindentation , the elastic-plastic deformation of epoxy and the indentation force increased with rising R and hc , due to the enhanced interfacial interactions between epoxy and quartz . ( 2 ) A negative indentation force was observed during the unloading stage , attributed to adhesion effects . ( 3 ) In nanoscratching , the forces in the y-and z-directions increased with rising R and hc , which was due to a greater contact zone and elastic – plastic deformation . ( 4 ) The friction coefficient could increase with rising indentation depth , exceeding 1.0 at hc / R > 0.75 . ( 5 ) The classic Coulomb 's law of friction was not applicable at the microscale or nanoscale . These results provide a foundation for developing interfacial models at the macroscopic scale for engineering applications .

title: Generalised social norms in water consumption networks
abstract: According to the last IPCC report ( AR6 , 2022 ) , ’ roughly half of the world ’s population are assessed as currently subject to severe water scarcity for at least some part of the year due to climatic and non-climatic factors , and severe water scarcity is projected to be exacerbated at higher levels of warming ’ . Due to this rise of the water scarcity , there has been an increase of small-scale systems managed by local authorities or companies such as smart meters which provide information on similar household consumption to help consumers reduce consumers water use . Many theoretical papers use the average consumption of others to define the social norm information provided to agents ( Ushchev and Zenou 2020 ; Pedehour and Richefort 2022 ) . New to this approach , we use a more general definition of the social norm following the recent paper of Boucher et al . ( 2024 ) who consider that social norm can be based on other measures . For example , median or minimum consumption could be used as a new reference point for water consumers . In this context , the recent paper of Boucher et al . ( 2024 ) who consider that social norm can be based on other measures develops a model of water extraction with endogenous social norms to study the different effects of this informaƟon provision and calibraƟon on the networks of water consumers . We consider a territory where water consumers are connected to a unique shared resource that can be overexploited in case of water scarcity . Preferences of individuals are guided by individuals extraction values and individuals taste for conformity to follow individuals norm . Depending on the calibration of the norm , the position in the network of agents , and the connections between water consumers , some definitions of social norms appear more optimal than others for reducing water consumption . We find conditions for uniqueness and interior solutions of the equilibrium . We then establish welfare and social-opƟmal properties to characterise social norms that could avoid the tragedy of the commons and suboptimal water consumption . Preliminary results highlight the strategic interaction between consumptions and can be used to derive interesting policy implications about the optimal norm information to set .

title: Monitoring the electrical resistivity profiles of ordinary and slag concrete samples subjected to artificial tidal cycles
abstract: Instrumented concrete specimens of two formulations , an ordinary and a BFS concrete , were subjected to long term artificial tide cycles . An embedded resistivity sensor was tested in this study to monitor resistivity profiles in concrete . Resistivity values in a BFS concrete are several times greater than values in an ordinary , which confirms the effect of BFS addition on the microstructure of concrete . this study clearly shows the ingress of salt water into concrete , at different depths in the samples . Finally , resistivity profiles from An embedded resistivity sensor compare well with resistivity profiles from surface resistivity measurements , thus validating this application of An embedded resistivity sensor .

title: Scalable Multiport Antenna Array Characterization With PCB-Realized Tunable Load Network Providing Additional “virtual” VNA Ports
abstract: We prototype a PCB-realized tunable load network whose ports serve as additional “ virtual ” VNA ports in a “ Virtual VNA ” measurement setup . a PCB-realized tunable load network whose ports serve as additional “ virtual ” VNA ports in a “ Virtual VNA ” measurement setup enables the estimation of a many-port antenna array 's scattering matrix with a few-port VNA , without any reconnections . We experimentally validate the approach for various eight-element antenna arrays in an anechoic chamber in the 700−900 MHz regime . We also improve the noise robustness of a step of the “ Virtual VNA ” post-processing algorithms by leveraging spectral correlations . Altogether , We PCB-realized VNA Extension Kit offers a scalable solution to characterize very large antenna arrays because of a PCB-realized tunable load network whose ports serve as additional “ virtual ” VNA ports in a “ Virtual VNA ” measurement setup low cost , small footprint , fully automated operation , and modular nature .

title: Progressive Hedging for the Freight Transportation Network Scheduling Problem with uncertain travel times
abstract: We consider a parcel transportation network planning problem in the context of the activities of a carrier for e-commerce suppliers . Packages are picked-up at suppliers , sorted and transferred at hubs in order to be routed to Packages destination terminals . The demand is modeled as commodities , having a release date at Packages origin , a due date at Packages destination , and a path in the network decided at a more strategic level . Each arc on the network is associated with a cost per truck move . a parcel transportation network planning problem consists of planning truck moves in the network , deciding truck moves in the network departure time , and the dispatch of commodities among trucks such that The demand is satisfied and the transportation cost is minimized . This research investigates how uncertain travel times affect network performance . We formulate a parcel transportation network planning problem as a two-stage stochastic program in which routing decisions for commodities in the network are determined after both truck departure times are set and actual travel times become known . We establish a chance constraint that ensures delivery of at least ( 100-[ EQUATION ] ) % of the demand on time , with a confidence level of 1-[ EQUATION ] . Here , ( 100-[ EQUATION ] ) represents the quality of service metric , while [ EQUATION ] denotes the risk of encountering severely disrupted traffic conditions . We solve a parcel transportation network planning problem using the \textit{Progressive Hedging } metaheuristic , for which We propose a new aggregation strategy . The aim of the \textit{Progressive Hedging } metaheuristic , for which we propose a new aggregation strategy is to find a consensus for the trucks ' departure time decisions by iteratively solving a scenario-wise decomposition of the stochastic program extensive formulation using an augmented Lagrangian relaxation . A reference solution is computed at each iteration with an aggregation strategy to guide the resolution of the subsequent iterations toward a consensus . the \textit{Progressive Hedging } metaheuristic , for which we propose a new aggregation strategy allows to efficiently find solutions compliant with a chance constraint that ensures delivery of at least ( 100-[ EQUATION ] ) % of the demand on time . We validate the \textit{Progressive Hedging } metaheuristic , for which we propose a new aggregation strategy on real data from an industrial partner .
keywords: delivery of at least ( 100-[ equation ] ) % of the demand on time

title: CHARACTERIZATION OF CYCLIC HYGROTHERMAL SWELLING AND SHRINKAGE BEHAVIOR OF BALSA WOOD AND GFRP-BALSA SANDWICH STRUCTURES
abstract: The objective of developing bio-based composite sandwich structures with greener core materials is to facilitate the decarbonization of industries such as aviation and maritime . This field of research has received increasing attention over the past decades . For example , balsa wood has emerged as a highly promising alternative to foam or honeycomb cores , offering a lightweight , rapidly renewable and cost-effective solution . However , plant fibers such as balsa wood and flax often display high hydrophilic behavior , which could affect plant fibers such as balsa wood and flax mechanical performance and long-term durability . It is therefore imperative to promote further research into the characterization of the cyclic hygrothermal aging behavior of balsa wood core sandwich structures , in particular the identification of moistureinduced strains and internal stresses in the skins and cores , as well as the investigation of moisture desorption processes and the associated thermal shrinkage phenomena in wood fibers , resins and glass fibers . Accordingly , this work employs two complete moisture absorption-desorption cycles to characterize the moisture diffusion behavior of specimens comprising three different materials , including the pure balsa wood , resin-infused balsa and balsa core sandwich structures with two Glass-Fiber-Reinforced-Polymer ( GFRP ) skins . The changes in moisture content and hygroscopic strains in the thickness , length and width directions of all specimens were investigated with a view to identifying the hygroscopic swelling and thermal shrinkage behaviors exhibited during long-term aging cycles .

title: Justin: Hybrid CPU/Memory Elastic Scaling for Distributed Stream Processing ⋆
abstract: Distributed Stream Processing ( DSP ) engines analyze continuous data via queries expressed as a graph of operators . Auto-scalers adjust the number of parallel instances of operators to support a target rate . Current auto-scalers couple CPU and memory scaling , allocating resources as one-size-fits-all packages . couple contrasts with operators ' high diversity of requirements . We present Justin , an auto-scaler that enables hybrid CPU and memory scaling of DSP operators . Justin , an auto-scaler that enables hybrid CPU and memory scaling of DSP operators monitors both CPU usage and the performance of operators ' storage operations . Justin , an auto-scaler that enables hybrid CPU and memory scaling of DSP operators mechanisms enable finegrain memory allocation for tasks upon a query reconfiguration . The Justin , an auto-scaler that enables hybrid CPU and memory scaling of DSP operators policy identifies individual operators ' memory pressure and decides between adjusting parallelism and/or memory assignment . We implement Justin , an auto-scaler that enables hybrid CPU and memory scaling of DSP operators in Apache Flink , extending the Flink Kubernetes Operator and the DS2 CPU-only auto-scaler . Using the Nexmark benchmark , We evaluation shows that Justin , an auto-scaler that enables hybrid CPU and memory scaling of DSP operators identifies suitable resource allocation in as many or fewer reconfiguration steps as the DS2 CPU-only auto-scaler and supports a target rate with significantly fewer CPU and memory resources .

title: Architecture and security for cooperative autonomous systems
abstract: Cooperative Autonomous Systems ( CAS ) , such as intelligent vehicles , are increasingly used in Industrial IoT ( IIoT ) to share tasks and information . Cooperative Autonomous Systems ( CAS ) , such as intelligent vehicles complexity and distributed nature require deployment across diverse hardware along the IIoT-Cloud continuum . Cooperative Autonomous Systems ( CAS ) , such as intelligent vehicles handle sensitive data , making security and privacy essential . While various security countermeasures exist , various security countermeasures must be combined thoughtfully , as various security countermeasures can impact performance and be incompatible . This thesis reviews literature in AI , distributed systems , security and their combination . This thesis proposes a reference architecture ( RACAS ) , identifying CAS cooperation methods and explores distributed AI , especially disaggregated AI . We evaluate the performance and security of key cooperation functions : collaborative learning decentralisation ( FDFL ) and on-demand security ( Ti-skol ) , task delegation ( D-Lambda ) , and status communication ( ReDOSN ) . A simulation framework ( D-ECS ) for secure , decentralized CAS environments is also introduced . We demonstrate that distribution and decentralization across the IoT-Cloud continuum enhances performance , scalability , and resilience . This thesis identifies security requirements for each function and suggests countermeasure composition for applicability .

title: Durability and Efficiency of Energy Piles: A Multi-Year Investigation Under Real Operating Conditions
abstract: Energy piles , which serve both as deep foundations and geothermal heat exchangers , are increasingly used to enhance the energy efficiency of buildings . Understanding Energy piles , which serve both as deep foundations and geothermal heat exchangers , long-term thermo-mechanical behavior is crucial for optimizing Energy piles , which serve both as deep foundations and geothermal heat exchangers , design and operation . This research builds upon a previous study conducted at the wastewater treatment plant in Sept-Sorts ( Seine-et-Marne , France ) , where instrumented energy piles were monitored over multiple years to assess instrumented energy piles response to cyclic thermal loading . Initial observations from the first two years of monitoring-one year prior to geothermal activation and one year after-revealed that geothermal activation induced axial deformations are comparable in magnitude to those caused by natural seasonal temperature variations . Despite these thermal effects , the structural integrity of instrumented energy piles remained intact , with deformations uniformly distributed along the thermally active sections . By incorporating additional years of data , This research offers a more comprehensive analysis of long-term trends , including potential cumulative effects of repeated thermal cycles on pile deformation , soil-pile interactions , and overall energy performance . The findings contribute to refining design guidelines , enhancing the durability and reliability of energy pile systems in practical applications .

title: Multi-provider capabilities in EnOSlib: driving distributed system experiments on the edge-to-cloud continuum
abstract: This paper introduces recent advances in EnOSlib , a Python library that aims at facilitating the design and execution of reproducible experiments across distributed computing infrastructures . Originally developed to simplify experimentation on testbeds such as Grid'5000 and Chameleon Cloud , EnOSlib , a Python library that aims at facilitating the design and execution of reproducible experiments across distributed computing infrastructures now incorporates support multi-provider deployments , including access to edge resources , as well as advanced services . Key contributions include integration with Kwollect for fine-grained energy measurements , a planning service for executing timed events , and enhanced network emulation functionalities . integration with Kwollect for fine-grained energy measurements , a planning service for executing timed events , and enhanced network emulation functionalities enable users to model and study complex , realistic scenarios such as latency-sensitive edge-to-cloud applications . A major new capability is the support for synchronized multi-infrastructure experiments , allowing simultaneous resource reservation and deployment across diverse testbeds . This paper illustrates these capabilities through a distributed video processing use case spanning edge and cloud platforms . This paper is the companion paper of the tutorial presented in DAIS 2025 .

title: Is Selective Masking A Key to Improving Domain Adaptation for Masked Language Model?
abstract: Pre-training and fine-tuning language models have been effective for domain adaptation in various NLP tasks . A key aspect of BERT-based models is the word-masking strategy used during training . However , commonly used random word masking may not fully capture domain-specific linguistic nuances . This paper aims to determine whether domain-dependent masking strategies , informed by thematic relevance or genre specificity , would be more effective than the conventional random strategy in different training phases . Our experiments on legal domain benchmarks reveal that selective masking offers no significant advantage over random masking in continual pre-training . However , domain-specific masking proves more effective in from-scratch pre-training , despite all available pre-trained language models being trained using random masking .
keywords: language modeling masking strategy bert genre tf idf

title: Impact of halogen bonding on stability of astatine-211 labelled compounds
abstract: Astatine-211 is the most promising radionuclide for targeted alpha therapy against cancer , due to its physical properties ( half-life of 7.2 h , emission of a single high-energy alpha-particle ) . Yet , finding a stable 211At-labelled motif that would avoid in vivo astatine release is hampering the application of the most widely labelling strategy : formation of astatoaryl bond as in SAB ( figure 1 ) . The mechanism for the in vivo deastatination of this prosthetic group has been of key interest.[1 ] Because its is seen as the strongest halogen-bond ( XB ) donor atom,[2 ] one possible hypothesis is that the in vivo deastatination of this prosthetic group is triggered by XB interactions with protein residues , especially the selenocysteine present in iodothyrionine deiodinases . one possible hypothesis was proven to explain the improved stability of SAGMB ( figure 1 ) over SAB , thanks to the introduced guanidinium substituent.[1 ] In recent literature , neopentyl glycol having two hydroxyl groups ( AtNpG , figure 1 ) , was found to show improved in vivo stability relative to a SAB analogue,[3 ] while the intrinsic At – C bond strength is significantly weaker with Csp3 carbons.[4 ] We have also observed an improved stability on ortho-functionalization of astatoaryl compounds with benzyl alcohols ( AtPDM , figure 1 : R. Fouinneteau , et al . Sci . Rep. , submitted ) . In another work , 211At-labelling of Au(I ) complexes of N-heterocyclic carbene ( At-Au-IPr , figure 1 ) have shown promising stability against deastatination ( M. Ligeour , et al . Chem . Eur . J. , submitted ) . Could these behaviors be justified by the in vivo deastatination of this prosthetic group ? This was investigated by means of relativistic DFT calculations using the PW6B95 hybrid meta functional and triple zeta dhf-TZVPD-2c basis sets . References : [ 1 ] Yssartier , T. ; et . al . RSC . Med . Chem . 2024 , 15 , 223-233 . [ 2 ] Guo , N. ; Maurice , R. ; Téze , D. ; Graton , J. ; Champion , J. ; Montavon , G. ; Galland , N. Nat . Chem . 2018 , 10 , 428-434 . [ 3 ] Suzuki , H. et . al . J. Med . Chem . 2021 , 64 , 15846-15857 . [ 4 ] Ayed , T. et al . Eur . J. Med . Chem . 2016 , 116 , 156-164 .
