title: Unveiling the link between phytoplankton molecular physiology and biogeochemical cycling via genome-scale modeling
abstract: Earth system models ( ESMs ) highly simplify Earth system models ( ESMs ) representation of biological processes , leading to major uncertainty in the impacts of climate change . Despite a growing understanding of molecular networks from genomic data , describing how changing phytoplankton physiology affects biogeochemical processes remains elusive . Here , we embed genome-scale models within a state-of-the-art ESM to deliver an integrated understanding of how gradients of nutrients modulate the molecular physiology of various plankton . In particular , when applied to Prochlorococcus , we find that glycogen and lipid management can be interpreted in terms of acclimation to different environments . Generalized to other phytoplankton such as the diatom Thalassiosira , we estimate the production of 39 metabolites that constitute hot spots of dissolved organic carbon described by their amount of carbon produced and their diversity of associated metabolites in ESMs . This modeling approach shows how ESMs have the potential to advance our understanding of microbial ecosystem functioning in ocean biogeochemical processes .

title: Near-field focusing at sub-THz frequencies using transmitarray antennas
abstract: Next-generation wireless communications demand innovative architectures and antenna systems to achieve higher data rates , low energy consumption , and broader radio coverage . Exploiting the THz band has appeared as the best choice to overcome higher data rates , low energy consumption , and broader radio coverage . With an intrinsic bandwidth of several tens of GHz , the THz band arises as the most suitable candidate . Furthermore , shifting telecom standards to higher frequencies helps alleviate spectrum saturation occurring until the millimetre-wave range . On the other hand , high-frequency operation faces the challenge of free-space path loss , making near-field radio links more practical . Therefore , upcoming future wireless networks are likely to function within the radiating near-field region . All of the above pushes towards the needs of efficient and wideband near-field focusing antenna . At these frequencies , the design features are tiny , and fabrication constraints often limit the achievable performance , requiring the use of more expensive , high-resolution technologies . Transmitarrays ( TAs ) have emerged as a highly promising solution for versatile beam-forming throughout various spatial dimensions . Transmitarrays ( TAs ) effectively address the inherent bandwidth restrictions of resonant antennas and the lossy feed networks commonly found in phased arrays . Moreover , Transmitarrays ( TAs ) can be easily integrated with planar fabrication processes , such as standard printed circuit boards . These features enable the development of low-cost , low-profile antennas that offer impressive near-field beam-shaping capabilities in the sub-THz region . This dissertation introduces , for the first time , a comprehensive mathematical framework designed for the precise determination of the near-field radiation emitted by a Transmitting Array ( TA ) . a comprehensive mathematical framework designed for the precise determination of the near-field radiation emitted by a Transmitting Array ( TA ) enables the prediction of electric field amplitudes by considering all characteristics of the system 's elementary building blocks . all characteristics of the system 's elementary building blocks include the injected power , the gain of the focal source , the distance between the focal source and each unit cell , as well as the directivity of each unit cell and each unit cell transmission coefficients in both phase and amplitude . A variety of near-field focusing patterns are achieved , allowing for control over both the focal and longitudinal distributions , whether on or off the propagation axis . The corresponding TAs are manufactured using a standard PCB process and experimentally characterized at 300 GHz in a wide variety of scenarios . The empirical results validate the proposed analysis and design approach .

title: How can communication content be adapted depending on consumers’ diet to encourage consumption of insect-based foods?
abstract: Purpose Entomophagy ( eating insects as food ) is an important step in the transition toward alternative sources of protein , but is not culturally accepted in Western countries . This study aims to identify which communication strategies on the benefits of entomophagy resonate most with consumers based on consumers diet . Design / methodology / approach This study was carried out on 720 French adults , who were divided into three groups depending on 720 French adults , who were divided into three groups depending on their diet ( omnivore , flexitarian or vegetarian diet ( omnivore , flexitarian or vegetarian ) and then exposed to a different message on the benefits of entomophagy ( environment , health and animal welfare ) . Findings Flexitarians show the highest level of acceptance toward entomophagy . Communication content has no main effect , but the interaction with diet has a main effect , meaning that the communication content needs to be adapted depending on the consumers ’ diet . The message explaining the environmental benefits of entomophagy seems to be more effective for flexitarians , while the message on health benefits seems to be more effective for vegetarians and omnivores . Practical implications The results can help promoters of insect-based food products ( public organizations and insect food suppliers ) to guide promoters of insect-based food products ( public organizations and insect food suppliers ) marketing campaigns to promote entomophagy in Western food cultures . Originality / value This study contributes to emerging research on alternative food consumption by examining the type of information that needs to be communicated to consumers – depending on consumers current diet – to promote entomophagy . This study highlights Construal Level Theory as essential in understanding the cognitive processes involved in consumers ’ acceptance of entomophagy .

title: Relationship Between Ball Speed and Spin in Elite Youth Table Tennis Players Using Optical Sensors
abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between ball spin and linear speed in table tennis . This paper uses a simple photodiode montage to introduce a methodology for measuring spin based on light reflection on the ball ’s surface . Two optical-based measurement systems were developed to measure either the ball ’s speed or spin . This paper describes sensor calibration and error estimation . Two optical-based measurement systems measured ball kinetic parameters from nine young elite players ( aged 15 ± 1.5 years ) who volunteered to perform 4 exercises . Results showed a strong positive linear relationship between the ball ’s speed and spin ( r = 0.96 , R2 = 0.93 , p < 0.001 ) . The effect of exercise conditions on ball speed has been studied using a statistical test , ANOVA . Results showed a significant main effect of exercise conditions on ball speed ( p < 0.05 ) with a very large effect size ( η2 = 0.82 ) . This paper revealed significant variations in linear speed based on the type of stroke ( backhand , forehand ) and the incoming ball ’s spin ( topspin , backspin ) , with topspin forehand strokes achieving higher speeds compared to backhand strokes . These findings provide valuable knowledge for players to enhance performance in a competitive environment .

title: Turn on light on multiscaling simulation of ligand-protein biological system
abstract: Ligand-protein interactions domain is extremely vast and is an ideal game for computational chemists . Indeed , independentaly of the applications a large set of methods are available going from low cost quantum mechanic methods to robust and accurate molecular mechanic approaches to deal with biological systems . In this talk , I will present results targetting various fields of chemobiology aligned with computational methods that are able to deal with the different scientific questions . Starting from photo(pharmaco)biology and going to the identification of specific biomarkers and protein-protein inhibitors , the goal is to travel accross a multi-scaling computational representation of the different system of interest . Such work will demonstrate the crucial interplay between computational chemists and biologists .

title: Combining mass spectrometric platforms for lipidome investigation - Application to the characterisation of disruptions in the lipid profile of pig serum upon β-agonist treatment
abstract: In the last decade , many mass spectrometric fingerprinting methods dedicated to lipidomics have been proposed : either non-targeted approaches , coupled with annotation methods , or targeted strategies , aiming at specifically monitoring a limited number of substances . In a general public health perspective and through a strategy combining non-targeted and targeted lipidomics MS-based approaches , this study aims at identifying disrupted patterns in serum lipidome upon growth promoter treatment in pig and evaluating the relative contributions of the three platforms involved . Pig serum samples collected during an animal experiment involving control and treated animals , whose food had been supplemented with ractopamine , were extracted and characterised using three MS strategies : Non-targeted RP LC-HRMS ; the targeted Lipidyzer ™ platform ( differential ion mobility associated with shotgun lipidomics ) and a homemade LC-HRMS triglyceride platform . the three platforms involved showed complementarity insight into lipid characterisation , which , applied to a selected set of samples , enabled highlighting specific lipid profile patterns involving various lipid classes , mainly in relation with cholesterol esters , sphingomyelins , lactosylceramide , phosphatidylcholines and triglycerides . Thanks to the combination of both non-targeted and targeted MS approaches , the exploration of various compartments of serum lipidome could be performed , including commonly characterised lipids ( the targeted Lipidyzer ™ platform ( differential ion mobility associated with shotgun lipidomics ) ) , triglyceride isomers ( Triglyceride platform )-whose accurate analysis was considered an analytical challenge , and unique lipid features ( Non-targeted RP LC-HRMS ) . Thanks to the three platforms involved respective characteristics , the complementarity of the three platforms involved could be demonstrated for public health purposes , with enhanced lipidome coverage , level of characterisation and applicability .

title: A Matlab-based program to develop control laws for wind turbines with OpenFAST: study of the pitch control case
abstract: In the framework of wind turbine energy management , control laws allow optimizing globally the energy extraction . The OpenFAST tool is a complete solution to simulate the whole wind turbine dynamics under different wind speed profiles , for which the user can define and experiment the user own controllers . To improve the user experience regarding the design of control algorithms and the management of the simulation cases , we propose a Matlab-based program to facilitate the development of advanced control algorithms and co-simulate the dynamic behavior of specific wind turbine structures . Simulation examples focus on the reduction of the blade fatigue by controlling the aerodynamic lift of the blades using a model-free based control approach .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Polymers of a Transition-State Sialyl Cation Strongly Inhibit Bacterial Sialidases.
abstract: Conjugation of the transitionstate-cation analogue DANA to polymeric scaffolds led to highly potent inhibitors of bacterial sialidases . Each clustered DANA on polymeric scaffolds saw Each clustered DANA on the polymers inhibitory potency for S. pneumoniae or B. thetaiotaomicron sialidases improved by more than four orders of magnitude . led extends the multivalent concept to bacterial sialidases .

title: The Development of Cattle Farming in Cerdagne and Its Socio-Environmental Implications (19th–20th Century)
abstract: This paper explores the development of cattle farming in Cerdagne from the 19th to the 20th century , with a focus on the accompanying social , economic , and agricultural transformations . Without seeking to provide an exhaustive account of the development of cattle farming in Cerdagne from the 19th to the 20th century causes or consequences , This paper proposes a systemic analysis of the development of cattle farming in Cerdagne from the 19th to the 20th century by examining several key dimensions . The central premise is to approach cattle farming in Cerdagne as a “ total social fact . ” approach involves not only interrogating cattle farming in Cerdagne relationship with agriculture up until the 1960s , but also exploring the social bonds that are forged through the presence and practices surrounding cattle .

title: Triazine Mg-Based Phosphonate Metal–Organic Framework for ε-Caprolactone Polymerization
abstract: A novel three-dimensional metal-organic framework ( MOF ) based on magnesium and the triazine triphosphonate ligand has been successfully synthesized via the solvothermal method and fully characterized . Denoted as IEF-31 ( IEF stands for IMDEA energy framework ) , A novel three-dimensional metal-organic framework ( MOF ) based on magnesium and the triazine triphosphonate ligand crystal structure was unveiled by single-crystal X-ray diffraction , exhibiting free P-OH groups in two coordination modes (-PO3H2 and-PO3H ) and an open framework with 1D channels ( 8 x 7 & Aring ;) . its crystal structure shows high thermal and chemical stability ( in several catalytic-relevant organic solvents and water , pH = 2 to 10 ) . Further , this study presents the proof of concept for using an Mg-based P-MOF as a catalyst in the ring-opening polymerization of epsilon-caprolactone ( epsilon-CL ) with relevance in the challenging bioplastic formation . Specifically , IEF-31(Mg ) achieved notable monomer conversions and polymer molecular weights with low dispersity values ( & Dstrok ; approximate to 1.1 ) , paving the way for further design and optimization of robust , efficient , and sustainable Mg P-MOFs for clean polymerization processes .

title: Federated Learning for Secure and Efficient Device Activity Detection in mMTC Networks
abstract: Grant-free random access in massive machine-type communications enables low-latency connectivity with minimal signaling . However , sporadic device activation requires efficient device activity detection . We propose a federated learning-based device activity detection approach , leveraging distributed training to enhance security and privacy while maintaining low computational complexity . Compared to existing methods , a federated learning-based device activity detection approach , leveraging distributed training to enhance security and privacy while maintaining low computational complexity achieves competitive detection performance , addressing scalability and security challenges in mMTC networks .

title: How graphic design on packaging can facilitate the adoption of sustainable food products ? The case of insect-based cereal bars.
abstract: The level of demand for animal-based proteins will soon be unsustainable due to global population growth and the depletion of natural resources ( Thavamani et al . , 2020 ) , making it imperative to find other sources of protein . Insects offer a promising and sustainable protein alternative . Insects offer nutritional and environmental benefits while reducing food production costs ( Van Huis et al . , 2013 ) , but are considered non-edible in Western cultures ( Kröger et al . , 2022 ) . Specifically , the sensory attributes that consumers perceive in insects ( such as slimy , sticky , hairy , dry … ) strongly increase disgust and reduce consumers willingness to taste insects ( Gallen et al . , 2019 ) . Packaging design is a critical tool to overcome the sensory attributes that consumers perceive in insects ( such as slimy , sticky , hairy , dry … ) . For is , this research focuses on how to best visually represent an insect on the front of the package ( FOP ) to reduce disgust and improve the expected taste of the insect-based product . In a first study , we compared French consumers ' reactions to realistic ( photo ) versus less realistic ( drawing ) images of two types of insect ( mealworm , cricket ) on the packaging of an insect-based cereal bar ( Hémar-Nicolas et al . , 2024 ) . The results show that using a less realistic insect image reduces perceived disgust , and increases expected taste and willingness to eat these foods . We extend this research to investigate how the type of insect drawing on the packaging influences consumer perception . We draw on consumer behaviour research on cross-modality , which suggests that there is a correspondence between the shape of a food 's graphic design on the packaging and a food 's perceived taste ( Motoki et al . , 2023 ) . In particular , it has been shown that a round shape is associated with an expected sweet taste , whereas an angular shape is associated with an expected bitter or salty taste . These effects of cross-modality are based on the theory of grounded cognition ( Barsalou , 2008 ; Elder and Krishna , 2014 , 2022 ) , according to which the graphic design of an object generates the formation of mental representations in the consumer 's brain ( " embodied mental simulation " ) , sensory inferences ( taste , flavour , mouthfeel ) and anticipated emotions ( disgust ) associated with the product , which in turn influence attitudes and intentions towards the product . Thus , we assume that a round graphic representation of the insect on the packaging will not have the same cognitive , emotional and conative effects as an angular shape . Therefore , by reducing disgust and increasing expected taste through graphic design , designers can contribute to the promotion of sustainable food and emphasise food serenity . To check this assumption , We worked with a graphic designer who created 5 different graphic designs to represent the insect ( photos ) . The study is currently being carried out in three countries-France , Brazil and Finland-with 400 consumers , to compare cultural differences . The aim of this research is to show how design can play a role in driving food transition , while at the same time suggesting how graphic design can be used on the packaging of novel , sustainable products to influence consumers , reduce consumers disgust and increase consumers expectation of the taste of novel , sustainable products .
authors: Filipe Quevedo Pires de Oliveira E Silva

title: Real-Time Jump Activity Recognition and Jump Height Estimation using IMU
abstract: Accurate recognition of jump activities and estimation of jump height are essential tasks in biomechanical analysis and sports performance research . This study introduces a realtime approach based on a low-cost Inertial Measurement Unit ( IMU ) , to estimate jump height . Two state-of-the-art methods-Time of Flight ( ToF ) and Double Integration ( DI )-are implemented and compared to evaluate Two state-of-the-art methods-Time of Flight ( ToF ) and Double Integration ( DI ) accuracy and applicability in real-world scenarios . Complementary signal processing techniques are also applied to reduce noise and improve reliability . a realtime approach based on a low-cost Inertial Measurement Unit ( IMU ) is developed in collaboration with Les Neptunes de Nantes , a professional women 's volleyball club in France , and aims at serving as a practical tool for field-based analysis . The results support the feasibility of using a wearable IMU to provide accurate real-time jumping activity recognition and jump height estimation .

title: Comparing resistivity measurement approaches for Ge2Sb2Te5 thin films
abstract: This poster presents a new method to precisely characterize the resistivity variation between amorphous and crystalline phases for each chalcogenide composition to ensure optimal use in reconfigurable microwave devices .

title: Methylglyoxal-Induced Glycation of Plasma Albumin: From Biomarker Discovery to Clinical Use for Prediction of New-Onset Diabetes in Individuals with Prediabetes
abstract: Abstract Background Methylglyoxal ( MGO ) is a potent glycating agent that contributes to the pathogenesis of diabetes . However , Abstract Background Methylglyoxal ( MGO ) is unstable in plasma without demanding sample preparation at blood collection , limiting Abstract Background Methylglyoxal ( MGO ) clinical utility as a biomarker . We aimed to discover reliable MGO-glycated albumin ( ALB)-derived biomarkers and to assess reliable MGO-glycated albumin ( ALB)-derived biomarkers association with new-onset diabetes ( NOD ) in people with prediabetes . Methods Bottom-up mass spectrometry-based proteomics was used to discover peptide biomarkers of MGO-glycated ALB , including MGO-derived hydroimidazolone ( MGH)-ALB219–225 , which proved to be biologically stable and reliable for large-scale analyses in human plasma . After assay validation , the IT-DIAB ( Innovation Thérapeutique DIABète ) prospective study , conducted in 300 individuals with impaired fasting plasma glucose ( FPG ) levels ( 110 to 125 mg / dL , 6.1 to 6.9 mmol / L ) , was used to assess the association between plasma MGH-ALB219–225 and NOD , defined as FPG ≥126 mg / dL ( 7 mmol / L ) , using Kaplan – Meier curves and Cox models . Results In total , 113 participants of the IT-DIAB ( Innovation Thérapeutique DIABète ) developed NOD during a median follow-up of 5 years . There was a graded association between the baseline plasma MGH-ALB219–225 concentration and incident NOD ( log-rank P < 0.0001 ) , in contrast to a lack of association for plasma MGO and total or glycated ALB ( commercial kit ) . After adjustment for age , sex , body mass index , FPG , hemoglobin ( Hb ) A1c , and ALB , the plasma levels of MGH-ALB219–225 were associated with NOD ( hazard ratio [ HR ] per one SD [ 95 % CI ] = 1.50 [ 1.26–1.78 ] ; P < 0.0001 ) . Conclusions MGH-ALB219–225 is a novel and stable peptide biomarker of MGO-glycated ALB , whose plasma levels are positively associated with an increased risk of NOD in people with prediabetes , independently of traditional risk factors . ClinicalTrials.gov Registration Number : NCT01218061

title: Pseudo-Random Illumination Microscopy
abstract: Structured illumination microscopy ( SIM ) is a well-established mean to obtain super-resolved images of fluorescent biological samples , with a two-fold resolution gain . However , Structured illumination microscopy ( SIM ) relies on the precise knowledge of the excitation patterns , which is an issue in the presence of uncontrolled pattern distorsions . Random illumination microscopy ( RIM ) is an alternate solution , built upon a larger number of unknown , randomly generated excitation patterns of controlled statistics , and on a variance-matching process for the super-resolved reconstruction step . In this paper , we propose Pseudo-RIM ( PRIM ) , a novel approach where the sample is illuminated with a limited number of structured patterns as in Structured illumination microscopy ( SIM ) , combined with a matching process based on second-order statistics as in RIM . we explore mathematical conditions under which Pseudo-RIM ( PRIM ) , a novel approach where the sample is illuminated with a limited number of structured patterns as in SIM has a provable super-resolution capacity comparable to Structured illumination microscopy ( SIM ) and RIM , and we show how to build valid combinations of pseudo-random illuminations . Several pattern sets commonly used in Structured illumination microscopy ( SIM ) are also compatible with Pseudo-RIM ( PRIM ) , a novel approach where the sample is illuminated with a limited number of structured patterns as in SIM , which allows us to compare the behavior of Pseudo-RIM ( PRIM ) , a novel approach where the sample is illuminated with a limited number of structured patterns as in SIM with that of Structured illumination microscopy ( SIM ) on the same simulated dataset , in the presence of pattern distorsions . This empirical test empirically validates that Pseudo-RIM ( PRIM ) , a novel approach where the sample is illuminated with a limited number of structured patterns as in SIM variance data processing is nearly insensitive to pattern distorsions , compared to Structured illumination microscopy ( SIM ) joint least-squares demodulation .

title: Security of Dynamically Reconfigurable RISC-V Systems: I/O Attack Focus
abstract: Dynamic Partial Reconfiguration ( DPR ) enhances flexibility in modern hardware but introduces security risks . This work demonstrates how a Malicious Hardware Accelerator ( MHA ) can exploit Direct Memory Access ( DMA ) to bypass Input Output Memory Management Unit ( IOMMU ) protections through device ID manipulation , enabling unauthorized memory access . This vulnerability exposes a fundamental security gap in the management of dynamically reconfigurable systems . By highlighting a fundamental security gap in the management of dynamically reconfigurable systems and proposing mitigation strategies , we provide a conceptual framework to guide the development of security mechanisms for dynamically adaptable architectures .

title: Experimental Comparison of Wireless Near-Field Links based on Gaussian and Bessel Beams
abstract: Gaussian beams are considered excellent candidates for wireless near-field links thanks to Gaussian beams well-known focusing properties . their well-known focusing properties , however , are maintained only up to the Rayleigh range because of diffraction . In this context , the limited-diffraction and self-healing properties of Bessel beams gained increasing interest in wireless data links and power transfer applications . Here , we provide for the first time an experimental comparison of the performance of Bessel beams and Gaussian beams for realizing a wireless link in the sub-terahertz range , specifically in the W-band . Bessel beams are generated through all-metal spline horns , whereas Gaussian beams are generated through commercial WR10 horns . Measurements , even in presence of obstacles across the link and a ground plane in proximity , reveal the superior performance of Bessel beams .

title: Sensitivity-based optimization of test configurations for parameters identification using full field measurements
abstract: In dynamic , the material properties are typically established through the implementation of testing methodologies based on homogeneous stress / strain states . Recent advances in optical technology have enabled the identification of dynamic material parameters through the use of full-field measurement and inverse methods . In this approach , the specimen design is crucial , as the specimen design must be sensitive to the various parameters to be identified . Different methodologies have been developed to optimize the geometry of the specimen based on the sensitivity of the material properties [ 1][2 ] . The primary limitation of Different methodologies is the calculation cost that strongly increases with the number of parameters . the calculation cost that strongly increases with the number of parameters becomes prohibitive when identifying complex non-linear laws , commonly used in dynamics . This work proposes an innovative method based on the use of surrogate models and high-performance computing to optimize a specimen geometry by a specimen geometry sensitivity to material parameters . In this purpose , a surrogate model based on a parametrized specimen geometry and a parametrized specimen geometry mechanical response is built . The configurations are then assessed through The configurations sensitivity level , characterized by the covariance matrix of the displacement sensitivity to material parameters to be identified . Finally , a parametrized specimen geometry is modified until the richness is considered sufficient for a robust material parameter identification .

title: Combined social norms: do meters matter ?
abstract: Providing social norm information can decrease consumption , but also generate a non-desirable boomerang effect . Combining information on social norms with other tools has been shown to be efficient . But combining different social norms is still understudied . Literature on green compensatory effects and moral licensing shows that when individuals take a positive environmental action , individuals easily sacrifice another action , but this remains to be studied in combination with the impact of social normal information . Our study aims to provide new insights into the complementarity and subsitution effects of combining social norms , i.e. providing information on peers ' consumption of several resources . Here , Our focus on the effects on water and electricity consumption , using both a theoretical model inspired by Ushchev and Zenou ( 2020 ) and Benjamin et al . ( 2010 ) and an online experimental survey with 1400 French energy and water consumers . Our results provide insights to policy makers and resources distributors on how to inform consumers in a context of energy and water scarcity .

title: Stability analysis of a linear system coupling wave and heat equations with different time scales
abstract: In this paper we consider a system coupling a wave equation with a heat equation through a system coupling a wave equation with a heat equation through its boundary conditions boundary conditions . The existence of a small parameter in a heat equation , as a factor multiplying the time derivative , implies the existence of different time scales between the constituents of a system coupling a wave equation with a heat equation through its boundary conditions . implies suggests the idea of applying a singular perturbation method to study stability properties . In fact , we prove that a singular perturbation method works for a system coupling a wave equation with a heat equation through its boundary conditions . Using a singular perturbation method , we get the stability of a system coupling a wave equation with a heat equation through its boundary conditions and a Tikhonov theorem , which allows us to approximate the solution of a system coupling a wave equation with a heat equation through its boundary conditions using some appropriate uncoupled subsystems .
keywords: system coupling a wave equation with a heat equation

title: Compact parasitically-loaded wideband monopole antenna for sub-6GHz 5G wireless communications
abstract: A thin compact broadband coplanarfed rectangular-ring monopole antenna parasiticallyloaded by three nested concentric rectangle rings and a π-shaped stub is proposed suitable for modern communication needs . A thin compact broadband coplanarfed rectangular-ring monopole antenna parasiticallyloaded by three nested concentric rectangle rings and a π-shaped stub has an overall area of only 25 mm×6 mm ( 0.29λ 0 ×0.07λ 0 at 3.5 GHz ) , which can be the base radiating element of the MIMO array , being easily integrated into any wireless device . A thin compact broadband coplanarfed rectangular-ring monopole antenna parasiticallyloaded by three nested concentric rectangle rings and a π-shaped stub measured ( simulated ) fractional bandwidth is 24.6 % ( 31.6 % ) ranging from 3.25 ( 3.09 ) to 4.16 ( 4.25 ) GHz , being applicable to the 5 G N48 , N77 , and N78 bands . Practical guidelines are also provided to make A thin compact broadband coplanarfed rectangular-ring monopole antenna parasiticallyloaded by three nested concentric rectangle rings and a π-shaped stub operate on some other additional 5 G bands ( e.g. , N41 or N46 ) without compromising A thin compact broadband coplanarfed rectangular-ring monopole antenna parasiticallyloaded by three nested concentric rectangle rings and a π-shaped stub overall size . As far as the radiation properties are concerned , A thin compact broadband coplanarfed rectangular-ring monopole antenna parasiticallyloaded by three nested concentric rectangle rings and a π-shaped stub radiates nearly bidirectionally and omnidirectionally in the Eand H-plane , respectively , and has an average measured ( simulated ) peak realized gain of-0.1 ( 1.8 ) dBi over the band of interest . A thin compact broadband coplanarfed rectangular-ring monopole antenna parasiticallyloaded by three nested concentric rectangle rings and a π-shaped stub is wideband , physically small and relatively easy to manufacture , making A thin compact broadband coplanarfed rectangular-ring monopole antenna parasiticallyloaded by three nested concentric rectangle rings and a π-shaped stub straightforward to integrate with the RF electronics in IoT sensors .
keywords: broadband coplanarfed rectangular-ring monopole antenna parasiticallyloaded by three nested concentric rectangle rings

title: SparqLLM : Retrieval-Augmented SPARQL Query Processing
abstract: SPARQL is essential for querying Knowledge Graphs ( KGs ) , but much information exists in external sources rather than within Knowledge Graphs ( KGs ) . To address exists , we propose SparqLLM , a retrieval-augmented query processing approach that leverages user-defined functions ( UDFs ) and named graphs to augment SPARQL queries with diverse external sources , including search engines , large language models ( LLMs ) , and vector search . By doing so , SparqLLM significantly enhances SPARQL capabilities , enabling a single query to access multiple heterogeneous sources while ensuring query provenance and explainability . This demonstration highlights the potential of SparqLLM to enrich query results with comprehensive , up-to-date information and showcases SparqLLM application in a real-world use case .

title: Optimal design and dynamic trajectory planning of a 2-DOF cable-suspended palletizing robot with parallelogram cable loop
abstract: To achieve energy saving , high speed , vast workspace , and light weight of the logistics equipment , this letter proposes geometric and trajectory optimization methods for the cable-suspended parallel robot ( CSPR ) , which is a two-degree-offreedom ( 2-DOF ) robot with a parallelogram cable loop , carrying out the efficient palletizing operation with dynamic trajectories . Based on kinematic and dynamic models , the Torsion Resistance Ability Index ( TRAI ) and Torsion Resistance Consumption Index ( TRCI ) are proposed for the CSPR to indicate the torsion resistance performance of a parallelogram cable loop . A geometric optimization method is established with the reference dynamic trajectory , which provides an approach to carry out the optimal design of the CSPRs considering dynamic trajectories . Facing the engineering practice , a planning method for the dynamic trajectory is proposed considering the obstacle avoidance based on the Fourier and Polynomial models . A prototype of the CSPR is established , and the proposed methods are verified with the palletizing experiments , which also provide a novel high-efficiency palletizing robot .

title: Using machine learning for timing analysis: where do we stand?
abstract: This paper presents our experience using Machine Learning ( ML ) to predict the Worst-Case Execution Time ( WCET ) of small code snippets on single-core platforms . our provide a concise overview of our work , highlight key observations made throughout our study , and advocate for further exploration of this topic . Keywords Worst-case execution time ( WCET ) estimation • Machine learning ( ML )

title: Topology optimization for dual-flow heat exchangers of moderate conductive material within a narrow design domain: Numerical and experimental investigations
abstract: Heat exchangers ( HXs ) play a critical role in various energy systems , which can largely influence Heat exchangers ( HXs ) overall efficiency . Most recently , the interest in the topology optimization ( TO ) of heat transfer , which can derive innovative thermal designs , is growing rapidly . Therefore , the present work investigates the utility of the densitybased TO for dual-flow HX unit of moderate conductive material ( Stainless Steel ( SS ) ) and narrow design domain , along with CFD ( computational fluid dynamics ) and experimental verifications . The objective of the densitybased TO is to maximize the heat exchange rate , while a pressure drop constraint is imposed on the HX 's flow channels to avoid the blocking issues . An in-depth investigation is conducted to study the effect of various TO 's input parameters on the derived topology . The obtained results reveal that the TOderived design is mainly featured by the solid allocation in proximity to the insulation walls but not at the interface wall that separates hot and cold fluids ( where heat is exchanged ) . Furthermore , high fidelity CFD simulations along with experimental approaches ( including Infrared thermography ) are employed to validate the densitybased TO design methodology and the numerical model . The experimental and numerical results present good agreement between each other , demonstrating the thermo-hydraulic performance superiority of the TOderived design compared to the benchmark case with an intensification in the exchanged heat up to 15 % under the same pumping power . Lastly , a physical interpretation is delivered to analyze the underlying physics behind the TO-acquired topologies .
keywords: topology optimization heat exchangers fins design computational fluid dynamics infrared thermography

title: In-situ partial reduction of biochar by overlaying a syngas stream
abstract: This work focuses on the partial reduction of a hot biochar by a hot syngas coming out of the partial oxidation zone in the Ariane ® pyrolysis prototype . The patented geometry of the Ariane ® pyrolysis prototype , with separate pyrolysis and partial oxidation zones , enables easy management of biochar and syngas flows . The aim is to increase the specific surface area of a hot biochar to achieve more agronomic specifications , while maintaining a high carbon content in a hot biochar . The experimental implementation of the partial reduction of a hot biochar by a hot syngas coming out of the partial oxidation zone in the Ariane ® pyrolysis prototype is achieved by adding a partial reduction zone at the bottom of the reactor , enabling direct contact between biochar and syngas . a partial reduction zone at the bottom of the reactor , enabling direct contact between biochar and syngas now enables biochar and syngas streams to be mixed in a high-temperature zone ( > 500∘C ) . adding increased the specific surface area of a hot biochar by 250 m2 / g and preserved the carbon content of a hot biochar regardless of the biomass flow rate . Around 20 % of the carbon in a hot biochar is consumed by the partial reduction of a hot biochar by a hot syngas coming out of the partial oxidation zone in the Ariane ® pyrolysis prototype and transferred from a hot biochar to a hot syngas coming out of the partial oxidation zone in the Ariane ® pyrolysis prototype . a hot syngas coming out of the partial oxidation zone in the Ariane ® pyrolysis prototype is thus enriched in particular in H2 and CO2 and depleted in CH4 , which opens up a wider range of development opportunities for CH4 ( biomethane , biohydrogen , biokerosene , cogeneration , etc . ) . Thanks to this activation method , a better compromise has been achieved ( compared with the previous version of the Ariane ® pyrolysis prototype ) between quality ( specific surface area and carbon content ) and quantity of biochar produced ( anhydrous yield ) .
keywords: partial reduction activation pine bark high available surface biochar

title: Manufacturing Changeability and Manufacturing as a Service
abstract: As markets and supply chains become more volatile , rapid response to changing demands is crucial . Manufacturing as a Service ( MaaS ) enables quick access to manufacturing assets , while changeable manufacturing designs adaptable systems . This paper investigates how 1 ) manufacturing as a service may support changeability , and 2 ) how changeability may support manufacturing as a service . To do so , a representative literature review on the bidirectional support of changeability and manufacturing as a service is conducted . Consequently , the means changeability provides to enable and/or stimulate manufacturing as a service are studied . Additionally , how manufacturing as a service can support changeability in different levels of a production system is discussed . Findings show Manufacturing as a Service ( MaaS ) fosters manufacturing flexibility , while changeability strengthens Manufacturing as a Service ( MaaS ) in three areas : strategy ( market adaptability ) , technology ( flexible systems ) , and organization ( operational agility ) . Together , three areas : strategy ( market adaptability ) , technology ( flexible systems ) , and organization ( operational agility ) enhance manufacturing resilience and responsiveness .

title: The contribution of mechanoradical reactions to crustal hydrogen generation
abstract: Hydrogen ( H-2 ) generation within the Earth 's crust contributes significantly to abiotic organic synthesis and the sustenance of deep microbial ecosystems . While natural H-2 is recognized as a potential primary energy resource , current exploration models focus solely on two sources , serpentinization and water radiolysis , leaving other H(2)generating processes largely unexplored . This study investigates mechanoradical reactions specifically , H-2 production resulting from mineral grinding in the presence of water , a process analogous to rock abrasion along fault planes during earthquakes . We performed laboratory experiments simulating these conditions by grinding quartz under controlled conditions of fluid pH , ionic strength , water / rock ( W / R ) ratio , and grinding energy . We results show that H-2 production is significantly affected by fluid pH , ionic strength , water / rock ( W / R ) ratio , and grinding energy . Notably , grinding in acidic environments ( 6 < pH < 4 ) tripled H-2 production compared to alkaline conditions ( pH > 8) . Increasing the W / R ratio from 0.1 to 1 resulted in an 18-fold enhancement of H-2 production . Additionally , a linear relationship was observed between H-2 production and the grinding energy applied . Extrapolating We findings to natural fault movements , We estimate that mechanoradical reactions during earthquakes of magnitude greater than 4 generate approximately 1.45 x 10(13 ) mol yr(-1 ) of H-2 . Although this production rate involved significant incertainties related to the model assumptions and may not be directly compared to two sources , serpentinization and water radiolysis-since two sources , serpentinization and water radiolysis operate on different time and space scales-This study underscores the importance of including mechanoradical processes in models of crustal H-2 fluxes . Recognizing mechanoradical processes expands our understanding of subsurface H-2 generation and subsurface H-2 generation contributions to geochemical and microbial processes in the Earth 's crust .

title: Thermal conversion of cellulose fiber under slow pyrolysis: Kinetics, thermodynamics and related chemical species
abstract: This study discusses the thermal conversion of cellulose fiber and the governing kinetic , chemical and thermodynamic phenomena . Activation energy ( ) and pre-exponential factor ( A ) were evaluated for the range of temperature [ 20–600 ° C ] under three low heating rates 1.5 , 2.5 and 5 ° C min−1 using different model-free and model-fitting methods and are around 205 kJ mol−1 and 2.4 × 10 + 20 s−1 , respectively . Coats-Redfern method was used to identify the thermal degradation reaction mechanism . Biobased carbonized fiber yield increases with lower heating rate and goes from 15.5 % for 5 ° C min−1 to 19 % for 1.5 ° C min−1 through a spontaneous endothermic process . The evolution of prominent volatiles and light gases was evaluated by mass spectrometry and gas chromatography combined with Fourier Transform InfraRed spectroscopy . This study may be useful for future research into bio-based carbonized fibers , and bio-based carbonized fibers applicability on an industrial scale with considering all related parameters .

title: Ultrafast 2D benchtop NMR spectroscopy enhanced by flow Overhauser dynamic nuclear polarization
abstract: Benchtop Nuclear Magnetic Resonance ( NMR ) spectroscopy is a powerful analytical technique for the monitoring of reactions and processes due to Benchtop Nuclear Magnetic Resonance ( NMR ) spectroscopy accessibility and lower cost compared to high-field NMR . However , Benchtop Nuclear Magnetic Resonance ( NMR ) spectroscopy often suffers from limited sensitivity and resolution . In this work , we have combined ultrafast ( UF ) 2D NMR with Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization ( ODNP ) to tackle limited sensitivity and resolution . Compared to thermally polarized 1D NMR , ultrafast ( UF ) 2D NMR provides improved spectral resolution in a single scan whereas Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization ( ODNP ) boosts the NMR sensitivity . To demonstrate the possibility of combining ultrafast ( UF ) 2D NMR with Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization ( ODNP ) for process monitoring applications , experiments were carried out at different flow conditions . we results show that Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization ( ODNP ) at least compensated for the losses in sensitivity of ultrafast ( UF ) 2D NMR that are normally induced by high flow velocities . Moreover , under certain flow conditions , Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization ( ODNP ) brings additional sensitivity to ultrafast ( UF ) 2D NMR spectra , with SNR increased by a factor of > 3 compared to thermal equilibrium acquisitions . The methods developed in this article are expected to be beneficial for more informative and sensitive acquisitions in the context of process monitoring .

title: A vector quantized masked autoencoder for audiovisual speech emotion recognition
abstract: An important challenge in emotion recognition is to develop methods that can leverage unlabeled training data . In this paper , we propose the VQ-MAE-AV model , a self-supervised multimodal model that leverages masked autoencoders to learn representations of audiovisual speech without labels . the VQ-MAE-AV model , a self-supervised multimodal model that leverages masked autoencoders to learn representations of audiovisual speech without labels includes vector quantized variational autoencoders that compress raw audio and visual speech data into discrete tokens . discrete tokens are used to train a multimodal masked autoencoder that consists of an encoderdecoder architecture with attention mechanisms . the VQ-MAE-AV model , a self-supervised multimodal model that leverages masked autoencoders to learn representations of audiovisual speech without labels is designed to extract both local ( i.e. , at the frame level ) and global ( i.e. , at the sequence level ) representations of audiovisual speech . During self-supervised pretraining , the VQ-MAE-AV model , a self-supervised multimodal model that leverages masked autoencoders to learn representations of audiovisual speech without labels is trained on a large-scale unlabeled dataset of audiovisual speech , for the task of reconstructing randomly masked audiovisual speech tokens and with a contrastive learning strategy . During self-supervised pretraining , a multimodal masked autoencoder that consists of an encoderdecoder architecture with attention mechanisms learns to extract a representation of audiovisual speech that can be subsequently leveraged for emotion recognition . During the supervised fine-tuning stage , a small classification model is trained on top of a multimodal masked autoencoder that consists of an encoderdecoder architecture with attention mechanisms for an emotion recognition task . the VQ-MAE-AV model , a self-supervised multimodal model that leverages masked autoencoders to learn representations of audiovisual speech without labels achieves state-of-the-art emotion recognition results across several datasets in both controlled and in-the-wild conditions .

title: Facility location based on Adjusted Present Value
abstract: Supply chain network design aims to optimize strategic decisions such as facility location decisions . strategic decisions such as facility location decisions have a major impact on the supply chain , but also on the financial value of the company . However , financial considerations are often omitted from facility location mathematical models . This paper addresses the challenge of identifying a relevant financial indicator that can be practically implemented in facility location models across different industries . This paper makes several contributions : the Adjusted Present Value ( APV ) is identified as such a financial indicator ; we propose a mathematical formulation that embeds the Adjusted Present Value ( APV ) in a facility location model maximizing firm value ; computational experiments demonstrate the tractability of a mathematical formulation that embeds the APV in a facility location model maximizing firm value . Finally , we compare a mathematical formulation that embeds the APV in a facility location model maximizing firm value with a sequential approach that first optimizes logistical decisions and then financial decisions . a mathematical formulation that embeds the APV in a facility location model maximizing firm value improves a sequential approach that first optimizes logistical decisions and then financial decisions up to 5.5 % , increases the market coverage and anticipates facility location decisions .

title: Taylor flow CO 2 chemical absorption in a minichannel: characterization of transport behaviors in the liquid slug and mass transfer modeling
abstract: This paper presents the mass transfer behaviors accompanied by chemical reaction under Taylor flow pattern . Experiments were conducted to study the absorption of CO 2 into MEA aqueous solution in a vertical straight minichannel with square cross-section of 1.5 mm in width . The velocity field in the liquid slug was characterized using particle tracking velocimetry ( PTV ) , revealing a liquid internal recirculation pattern featuring dual vortex symmetry structure . The recirculation intensity increased with higher two-phase velocities and MEA concentration , and was accurately predicted using a proposed empirical correlation . A pH-sensitive colorimetric method was employed to measure the spatial and temporal distribution of CO 2 concentration within the liquid slug . High CO 2 concentration zones were observed near bubble caps and channel walls , while low concentration zones were identified in the liquid bulk . Although liquid recirculation motion significantly enhanced axial convection-driven mass transfer , radial mass transfer remained diffusion-dominated . To better account for these phenomena , a modified unit-cell flow and mass transfer model was developed , incorporating the enhancing effects of liquid flow recirculation and chemical reaction . a modified unit-cell flow and mass transfer model enables the determination of local mass transfer coefficients within the liquid slug , offering new insights into the transport mechanisms at the local level .
keywords: gas liquid taylor flow co chemical absorption two phase mass transfer particle tracking velocimetry ptv ph sensitive colorimetry flow recirculation mode local mass transfer coefficient

title: The reaction of maleic anhydride with alkenes: a review on the mechanisms involved in the reaction of maleic anhydride with lipids
abstract: Maleic anhydride is one of the most widely used anhydrides after acetic and phthalic anhydride and Maleic anhydride market has grown rapidly over the last century . Maleic anhydride is a versatile monomer widely used in industrial and commodity chemicals . It is interesting to note that Maleic anhydride can be obtained from biosourced molecules such as furfural and 5-hydroxymethylfurfural . The maleinization reaction involves the addition of maleic anhydride molecules to unsaturated compounds , particularly lipids , without the need of solvents . This review article provides a comprehensive overview of The maleinization reaction , focusing on the mechanisms involved in The maleinization reaction , providing a state-of-the-art overview . This review article covers various aspects of the maleinization process , including properties and industrial applications of Maleic anhydride , current production methods , experimental setups , and characterization methods for the final products . Different mechanisms involved in The maleinization reaction , such as the Diels – Alder reaction , free radical reaction , and ene reaction , are discussed . The use of additives like catalysts and inhibitors to optimize The maleinization reaction is also explored . This review article aims to consolidate existing knowledge on maleinization reactions , addressing contradictions in earlier literature and highlighting recent developments . By providing a comprehensive understanding of the maleinization process , This review article supports the future development of maleinized compounds for various applications , including biobinders , bioplasticizers , biopolymer synthesis , paints , and coatings .

title: Assessing linkages between supply chain tokens and other assets: Evidence from a time-frequency quantile connectedness approach
abstract: This study assesses return spillovers and hedging dynamics between supply chain tokens and traditional assets , including equities , currencies , bonds , gold , oil , and Bitcoin , using a time-frequency quantile connectedness approach . Findings reveal that while supply chain tokens exhibit weak connectedness with traditional assets during stable periods , heightened market volatility , such as during the COVID-19 pandemic , significantly increases return spillovers , particularly from equities and Bitcoin . Supply chain tokens offer some diversification potential , especially when paired with oil ( WTI ) , but Supply chain tokens effectiveness as hedging instruments varies by time horizon and market conditions . Optimal portfolio weights and hedge ratios suggest that investors should dynamically adjust allocations to mitigate risks effectively , particularly during market instability . These insights emphasize the need for adaptable portfolio strategies when integrating supply chain tokens with traditional assets .

title: Predictive model-based multi-objective optimization with life-long meta-learning for designing unreliable production systems
abstract: Owing to the realization of advanced manufacturing systems , manufacturers have more flexibility in improving manufacturers processes through design decisions . Design decisions in production lines primarily involve two complex problems : buffer and resource allocation ( B&RA ) . The main aim of B&RA is to determine the best location and size of buffers in the production line and optimally allocate production resources , such as operators and machines , to workstations . Inspired by a real-world case from the marine engine production industry , this study addresses B&RA in high-mix , low-volume hybrid flow shops ( HFSs ) with feed-forward quality inspection . high-mix , low-volume hybrid flow shops ( HFSs ) with feed-forward quality inspection can be characterized by uncertainties in demand , material handling , processing times , and quality control . In this study , the production environment is modeled via discrete-event simulation , which reflects the features of the actual system without requiring unreasonable or restrictive assumptions . To replace the expensive simulation runs , five widely used regressor machine learning algorithms in manufacturing are trained on data sampled from the simulation model , and the best-performing algorithm is selected as the predictive model . To obtain high-quality solutions , the predictive model is coupled with an enhanced non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm ( En-NSGA-II ) that incorporates lifelong meta-learning and features a customized representation and a variable neighborhood search . Additionally , a post-optimality analysis using a pattern-mining algorithm is performed to generate knowledge for allocating buffers and operators based on the optimization results , thus providing promising managerial insights .

title: Promoting a master plan by encouraging participation: On the culture of convergence in urban planning
abstract: The aim of this contribution is to help develop a new model of the use of storytelling in planning . To this end , this contribution draws on media studies research as well as literary studies that examine so-called transmedia storytelling devices . The authors use this method to examine the communication strategy around the 2030 Cantonal Master Plan of the Republic and Canton of Geneva ( Switzerland ) . the communication strategy around the 2030 Cantonal Master Plan of the Republic and Canton of Geneva ( Switzerland ) , mobilizes practical regimes that can strengthen the engagement of different audiences with the process of giving narrative form to future urban developments . Communication and public participation in an urban project tend to hybridize , thereby complexifying debates on the use of storytelling in planning , which often contrast storytelling educational use ( explain projects to the general public ) with storytelling manipulative use ( make projects desirable so projects may be accepted ) . By conducting an analysis through the prism of transmedia storytelling , we can simultaneously consider these two aspects of communication in planning .
keywords: cantonal master plan of the republic and canton of geneva ( swiss )

title: A multi-criteria approach to coastal flooding risk assessment: from modelling to crisis response
abstract: With climate change inducing sea-level rise , the vulnerability of buildings and coastal infrastructure facing marine submersion is increasing . To estimate the vulnerability of buildings and coastal infrastructure facing marine submersion , our study analyzes sensitive areas with a view to anticipating these crises and raising public awareness . Any emergency response must therefore be prepared and analyzed in advance . Simulations based on the Xynthia storm and IPCC scenarios were used to identify the areas most at risk , enabling an analysis of the vulnerability of assets located in the municipality . An historical analysis of storms has also enabled recurring problems to be catalogued and crisis management strategies to be refined . At the same time , refuge areas were defined according to precise criteria , to optimize people 's response to the risk , while providing organizational support for the emergency services . To this end , a dynamic mapping tool has been developed to pinpoint areas at risk and facilitate the implementation of preventive measures . The final objective is to create an interactive digital tool to help emergency services to visualize at-risk areas in real time and optimize emergency services response during an event . Initially , this article will set the scene and present the study area . set will be followed by a description of the methodology used to understand a dynamic mapping tool . The last part of this article will be devoted to the results and the analysis of risks and issues .

title: Upon This Quote I Will Build My Church Thesis
abstract: The internal Church thesis ( CT ) is a logical principle stating that one can associate to any function f : ℕ → ℕ a concrete code , in some Turing-complete language , that computes any function f : ℕ → ℕ . While the compatibility of The internal Church thesis ( CT ) in simpler systems has been long known , The internal Church thesis ( CT ) compatibility with dependent type theory is still an open question . In this paper , we answer an open question positively . we define “ MLTT ” , a type theory extending MLTT with quote operators in which The internal Church thesis ( CT ) is derivable . we furthermore prove that MLTT is consistent , strongly normalizing and enjoys canonicity using a rather standard logical relation model . All the results in this paper have been mechanized in Coq . a

title: A framework for risk assessment during natural hazard based on the Choquet integral and MACBETH
abstract: This research is part of a doctoral program in geography , geomatics , and computer science , which began in October 2023 . Risk assessment in the face of natural disasters is an increasingly critical issue with climate change . Evaluating risk involves two distinct assessments : first , the probability of the disaster occurring , and second , the potential stakes or impacts of such an event . the potential stakes or impacts of such an event are generally categorized along several dimensions , notably human factors and infrastructure concerns . However , even when focusing solely on human stakes , characterizing risk — particularly in terms of the potential to prevent casualties — is complex . This complexity arises from multiple factors , including the vulnerability of individuals present in the affected area ( such as the presence of schools or nursing homes ) , the availability of a safe zone , and the ease with which emergency responders can intervene . Assessing risks presents several challenges . First , it is necessary to find ways to objectively analyze the situation through measurable indicators ( e.g. ease to access the victims for first responders , presence of a safe zone or not , vulnerability of the population ) . find includes not only defining measurable indicators ( e.g. ease to access the victims for first responders , presence of a safe zone or not , vulnerability of the population ) but also evaluating measurable indicators ( e.g. ease to access the victims for first responders , presence of a safe zone or not , vulnerability of the population ) consequences . One possible approach would be to create separate maps for each dimension of risk . However , create would result in a large number of maps , making interpretation difficult . Decision-makers would then need to synthesize a large number of maps to identify the most at-risk areas and prioritize interventions accordingly . To account for the various dimensions inherent to risk assessment , it is first necessary to process these metrics through a function that determines the level of risk for each criterion . Once process is completed , these metrics are then combined using aggregation functions , allowing for a comprehensive evaluation of the overall risk based on individual indicators . The most common approach to this problem relies on a weighted sum , which assigns specific weights to each criterion . a weighted sum , which assigns specific weights to each criterion effectively establishes the relative importance of one criterion over another and has the advantage of being linear . However , a weighted sum , which assigns specific weights to each criterion also presents certain limitations . In particular , a weighted sum , which assigns specific weights to each criterion linearity prevents a weighted sum , which assigns specific weights to each criterion from capturing interactions between criteria , such as veto effects ( where failing to meet a single critical criterion results in a severe situation regardless of other factors , but meeting a single critical criterion is not sufficient to ensure a low-risk scenario ) , as well as complementarities or substitutability between criteria ( e.g. ease to evacuate a place can be substituted by the presence of a safe zone ) . In this paper , we propose a risk mapping method that utilizes an alternative aggregation function . Specifically , we rely on the Choquet integral , which allows for the modeling of interactions between criteria , whether in terms of complementarity or substitutability , while maintaining desirable properties such as monotonicity . the Choquet integral , which allows for the modeling of interactions between criteria , whether in terms of complementarity or substitutability , while maintaining desirable properties such as monotonicity has been widely used in multi-criteria decision-making problems ( Grabisch and Labreuche , 2010 ) , as the Choquet integral , which allows for the modeling of interactions between criteria , whether in terms of complementarity or substitutability , while maintaining desirable properties such as monotonicity enables a more refined representation of interactions compared to the weighted sum , which can be seen as a special case of the Choquet integral , which allows for the modeling of interactions between criteria , whether in terms of complementarity or substitutability , while maintaining desirable properties such as monotonicity . Like the weighted sum , which can be seen as a special case of this function , the Choquet integral , which allows for the modeling of interactions between criteria , whether in terms of complementarity or substitutability , while maintaining desirable properties such as monotonicity is a parametric function based on the definition of an underlying function called a capacity . Determining an underlying function called a capacity requires input from a domain expert or decision-maker . However specifying the model parameters or providing an absolute evaluation can be challenging for a domain expert or decision-maker . To address this , we rely on MACBETH ( Measuring Attractiveness by a Categorical Based Evaluation Technique ) ( Bana and Costa et al . , 2010 ) and MACBETH ( Measuring Attractiveness by a Categorical Based Evaluation Technique ) adaptation to the elicitation of the capacity , a widely used method in multi-criteria decision analysis . MACBETH ( Measuring Attractiveness by a Categorical Based Evaluation Technique ) operates through pairwise comparisons and preference levels , making MACBETH ( Measuring Attractiveness by a Categorical Based Evaluation Technique ) more interpretable and accessible for experts . we evaluate we approach by applying MACBETH ( Measuring Attractiveness by a Categorical Based Evaluation Technique ) to the challenge addressed in the MOGEC project : coastal flooding projections under IPCC ’s RCP 8.5 scenario in the Pays-de-la-Loire region , following a storm of similar magnitude to Xynthia . For this assessment , we rely on the expertise of emergency response teams , particularly the SDIS ( Departmental Fire and Rescue Service ) , for whom risk mapping is a key concern . Specifically , we demonstrate the advantages and limitations of we approach in the municipality of Batz-sur-Mer within this projected scenario . title: Independent transitions to fully planktonic life cycles shaped the global distribution of medusozoans in the epipelagic zone
abstract: Life history traits influence marine species dispersal and habitat colonization . Medusozoans ( jellyfish and siphonophores ) exhibit diverse life cycles , evolved from an ancestral cycle alternating between a benthic polyp and a pelagic medusa . Despite their ecological importance , factors shaping medusozoan distribution remain poorly understood . By integrating metabarcoding and environmental data from the Tara Oceans expedition with life history traits , we provide global evidence supporting the longstanding hypothesis that benthic polyp presence / absence is a key factor influencing the distribution and abundance of planktonic medusozoans in the surface ocean . we inferred on a time-calibrated phylogeny of Medusozoa multiple transitions to a fully planktonic ( holoplanktonic ) life cycle , either through polyp loss , acquisition of drifting polyps , or development of polyps parasitizing pelagic organisms . We could associate each transition with a shift toward offshore habitats and the emergence of globally dominant Operational Taxonomic Units ( OTUs ) , whose abundance far exceeds that of any nonholoplanktonic medusozoans in the planktonic realm . The prevalence of holoplanktonic medusozoans in terms of abundance and diversity is broadly observed in coastal and offshore environments , peaking over greater bathymetric depths in tropical and subtropical regions . we show that holoplanktonic and nonholoplanktonic groups interact with distinct yet compositionally similar planktonic communities . Holoplanktonic OTUs occupy more peripheral positions in a plankton interactome , suggesting greater flexibility in biotic interactions , an adaptive trait in rapidly changing planktonic ecosystems . These findings highlight how life cycle evolution shaped the global distribution of medusozoans and suggest that variations in life history may significantly influence how medusozoans respond to global environmental changes .

title: From decision aiding to the massive use of algorithms: where does the responsibility stand?
abstract: In the very large debates on ethics of algorithms , this paper proposes an analysis on human responsibility . On one hand , algorithms are designed by some humans , who bear a part of responsibility in the results and unexpected impacts . Nevertheless , we show how the fact some humans , who bear a part of responsibility in the results and unexpected impacts can not embrace the full situations of use and consequences lead to an unreachable limit . On the other hand , using technology is never free of responsibility , even if there also exist limits to characterise . Massive uses by unprofessional users introduce additional questions that modify the possibilities to be ethically responsible . this paper is structured in such a way as to show how the limits have gradually evolved , leaving unthought of issues and a failure to share responsibility .

title: A multi-criteria approach to coastal flooding risk assessment: from modelling to crisis response
abstract: This research is part of a doctoral program in geography , geomatics , and computer science , which began in October 2023 . In a context where the effects of climate change are becoming increasingly visible in our society , natural hazards represent a growing threat . Early warning systems are therefore essential tools for implementing a proactive and effective response to crises . This research specifically focuses on the spatial analysis of vulnerable areas facing the risk of marine submersion . An increasing number of buildings , road infrastructures , and industrial zones will be affected by such crises . A large-scale awareness campaign must be conducted among populations to help prevent and anticipate such crises . The objective is to provide emergency services with a detailed database identifying all vulnerable assets , thus facilitating the development of an indicator . This work requires an extensive field reconnaissance study , combined with an in-depth bibliographic analysis . This methodology allows for the identification of vulnerability zones at the municipal scale . The impact of marine submersion crises has been analysed in the territories of Batz-sur-Mer and L’Aiguillon-la-Presqu’île . Initially , simulations of marine submersion crises were conducted to identify the most sensitive areas . simulations of these phenomena incorporate both the analysis of past events , such as the 2010 Xynthia storm , and projections derived from the most pessimistic scenarios of the IPCC for the Pays de la Loire region in France . Based on this information , a thorough territorial analysis of the affected municipalities was carried out , enabling the establishment of a list of vulnerable assets . An importance score was also assigned to each asset to better target the areas presenting critical risks . Simultaneously , refuge zones were identified using geographic processing . Any area larger than 100 m² and located more than 30 cm above the projected level in the worst-case scenario was considered a refuge zone . Finally , a historical study made it possible to analyse and catalog past storms , highlighting previous issues that remain relevant for analysing and managing current risk factors . The precise localization of vulnerable assets represents a major advancement in identifying sensitive and submersible areas , offering a better understanding of the risks associated with marine submersion crises . Through This research , it is possible to accurately quantify the impact of marine submersion crises on the territory and anticipate the necessary measures to mitigate marine submersion crises effects . In Batz-sur-Mer , 552 hectares are exposed to the risk of marine submersion , accounting for 59.5 % of the total municipal area . 958 buildings , representing 17.8 % of the urbanized area , would be affected in the event of a crisis . Studies also indicate that the road and railway networks would be severely impacted , leading to significant transportation challenges during evacuations or rescue operations . This substantial proportion underscores Batz-sur-Mer vulnerability to rising water levels and highlights the need for tailored strategies to enhance territorial resilience . To address these challenges and improve crisis management , a dynamic mapping tool has been developed alongside vulnerability analyses . a dynamic mapping tool enables the precise localization of high-risk areas while providing a detailed understanding of high-risk areas composition . With regular data updates , a dynamic mapping tool serves as a crucial resource for local authorities , facilitating the implementation of preventive measures and appropriate actions in case of an emergency . The final perspectives of this work aim to integrate these maps into an advanced digital tool , providing a more refined and precise mathematical analysis . In parallel , the development of This methodology will allow for both fine-scale and comprehensive localization of vulnerable assets across the territory . The ultimate goal is to design a dynamic and interactive decision-support tool , specifically tailored for emergency response teams . a dynamic and interactive decision-support tool , specifically tailored for emergency response teams will provide emergency response teams with a clear , real-time visualization of at-risk areas , thereby optimizing intervention strategies and enhancing emergency response teams effectiveness in managing marine submersion crises .
