title: Hybrid tribo-piezoelectric microgenerator for mechanical energy harvesting
abstract: In the present study , a hybrid triboelectric / piezoelectric generator was proposed to combine simultaneously the piezoelectric and triboelectric effects to improve the device 's performances . When subjected to the shaker motion , a hybrid triboelectric / piezoelectric generator delivers an open circuit voltage of 318 V , a short-circuit current of 4.95 μA and a maximum power of 349 μW dissipated in a load resistance of 40 MΩ under the application of a force of 8.5 N at a frequency of 2 Hz after rectification by two diode bridges . A capacitor of 80 μF capacitance was charged with the piezoelectric , triboelectric and hybrid systems with vibrating shaker . Thanks to combine , the charging time is reduced by 74 % compared to the piezoelectric system alone and 39 % compared to the triboelectric system alone . Finally , a temperature sensor was powered by a 1 mF capacitor charged to 4.5 V by a hybrid triboelectric / piezoelectric generator .

title: A Pillbug-Inspired Morphing Mechanism Covered with Sliding Shells
abstract: This research proposes a novel morphing structure with shells inspired by the movement of pillbugs . Instead of the pillbug body , a loopcoupled mechanism based on slider-crank mechanisms is utilized to achieve the rolling up and spreading motion . a loopcoupled mechanism based on slider-crank mechanisms precisely imitates three distinct curves that mimic the shape morphing of a pillbug . To decrease the degree-of-freedom ( DOF ) of a loopcoupled mechanism based on slider-crank mechanisms to one , scissor mechanisms are added . 3D curved shells are then attached to the tracer points of a loopcoupled mechanism based on slider-crank mechanisms to safeguard a loopcoupled mechanism based on slider-crank mechanisms from attacks while allowing a loopcoupled mechanism based on slider-crank mechanisms to roll . Through type and dimensional synthesis , a complete system that includes shells and a loopcoupled mechanism based on slider-crank mechanisms is developed . A 3D model is created and tested to demonstrate a complete system that includes shells and an underlying morphing mechanism shape-changing capability . Lastly , a robot with two modes is developed based on the proposed mechanism , which can curl up to roll down hills and can spread to move in a straight line via wheels .

title: An exploratory study of touchpoints shaping the phygital shopping experience in France: a thematic and sentiment analysis approach
abstract: Consumers increasingly seek more seamless shopping experiences through “ phygital ” store environments that integrate physical and digital touchpoints . However , managers ’ strategies for digitizing interaction points remain challenging and complex . This study aims to explore and compare the salient touchpoints influencing perceived shopping experiences in traditional versus phygital retail environments , specifically in the French cosmetics and lingerie sectors . By conducting thematic and semantic analyses of user-generated content across both traditional and phygital store contexts , we investigate how digital integration transforms consumer perceptions and interactions . The results reveal that consumers primarily articulate consumers positive and negative experiences through human touchpoints and interactions , highlighting the nuanced impact of digital enhancements on retail experience . This study contributes to the phygital retailing literature by exploring the multidimensional factors that influence phygital shopping experience . The findings provide critical managerial insights helping store owners better understand and strategically implement touchpoints that significantly influence consumer perceptions in emerging phygital retail environments .

title: Characterization of the cyclic hygroscopic aging behavior of balsa wood core bio‐composite sandwich structures with preexisting defects in laminate skins
abstract: Aimed at the decarbonization of marine structures under harsh humid environments , the present study explores the cyclic hygroscopic aging behavior of balsa wood core bio‐composite sandwich structures with manufacturing defects in Glass‐Fiber Reinforced‐Polymer ( GFRP ) skins . Both experimental investigations and analytical predictions are presented . Two distinct protocols were proposed to realize complete‐cycle and incomplete‐cycle absorption conditions of moisture , to characterize moisture diffusion mechanisms due to non‐Fickian effects . The Dual Fickian model was found to be effective in predicting moisture diffusion kinetics during absorption cycles , while The Dual Fickian model demonstrated superior fit with the moisture desorption processes . Furthermore , the maximum moisture content of 13.80 % after 33 days reveals that an 18 mm diameter hole in the skin of balsa wood core bio‐composite sandwich structures with manufacturing defects in Glass‐Fiber Reinforced‐Polymer ( GFRP ) skins could result in a considerable water uptake , which can not be neglected . However , balsa wood core bio‐composite sandwich structures with manufacturing defects in Glass‐Fiber Reinforced‐Polymer ( GFRP ) skins can be fully dried at 35 ° C within 3 days . It indicates that balsa core sandwich structures possess notable repairability . Additionally , the significant impact of the initial desorption cycle on moisture diffusion coefficients in subsequent resorption cycles was highlighted to investigate the long‐term effects of cyclic moisture exposure on the properties of balsa core sandwich structures . Highlights Multiple aging cycles were performed to replicate harsh , humid environments . The Dual Fickian model was employed to characterize moisture desorption behavior . Dual‐Fickian model was proven to predict moisture absorption mechanisms . Balsa wood was found to be a good candidate due to rapid repair capabilities . Effect of the initial desorption cycle on resorption rates can not be ignored .

title: The cutting type of vegetables influences the spontaneous fermentation rate
abstract: Fermented vegetables are mainly produced by the spontaneous fermentation of raw vegetables that are roughly or thinly cut , salted and incubated in an oxygen-free environment . Despite the variety of cutting types and cutting types potential role in the rate of solute diffusion from vegetable tissue , and hence the fermentation rate , the effect of their potential role in the rate of solute diffusion from vegetable tissue , and hence the fermentation rate has been little studied . Our aim was to investigate how cutting and small variations in salt concentrations impact the microbial and biochemical changes that occur during the spontaneous fermentation of vegetables . A 2 × 3 experimental design was set up with vegetable type ( carrot / cabbage ) , cutting type ( thin / rough ) , and salt concentration ( 0.8%/1 % ) as the different factors . The vegetables were pressed down in 500 mL-jars and then filled with brine , and two independent jars used at four stages to characterise microbial dynamics and biochemical changes by combining culturomics , 16S rRNA V5-V7 and gyrB metataxonomics , and targeted metabolomics . Culturomic and metataxonomic results revealed similar successions of the main bacterial groups in The vegetables , with Enterobacteriaceae ( 8 vs 7 log colony-forming units(CFU)/g ) quickly replacing the initial microbiota , further replaced within a few days by lactic acid bacteria ( 9 vs 8 logCFU / g ) , mainly represented by Leuconostoc sp . The pH fell to 3.8 within 40 h in carrot and about two weeks in cabbage . Mannitol , lactic acid and acetic acid were the main metabolites produced in The vegetables . Viable Enterobacteriaceae were no longer detected after two weeks of fermentation , except in some roughly-cut cabbage samples . No pathogenic bacteria were found . Taxonomic profiles varied depending on the marker used , e.g. Leuconostoc sp was only detected with gyrB and vice-versa for Clostridium . gyrB enabled markedly better resolution at the species level ( for 97 % of ASV vs only 20 % for the 16S marker ) . Significant effects of the cutting type , and , to a limited extent , of the NaCl concentration , were observed . Thinly-cut vegetables generally displayed more rapid fermentation compared to roughly-cut vegetables , together with higher titratable acidity , e.g. 0.8 % vs 0.3 % , respectively , in grated and sliced carrot after 64 h incubation . In line with displayed , acids were produced more rapidly and levels of viable enterobacteria fell more quickly in thinly-cut vegetables , and particularly cabbage , where the surface area generated by cutting was ~20-fold greater in shredded cabbage than in leaf cabbage . Some leaf cabbage samples displayed atypical fermentations , with particular taxa and atypical metabolite profiles producing high levels of ethanol . These general trends were modulated by quantitative and qualitative differences between replicate jars . This study therefore confirms the highly diverse microbiota of spontaneously fermented vegetables and the tight competition between Enterobacteriaceae and lactic acid bacteria regarding spontaneously fermented vegetables colonisation . For the first time This study documents the effects of cutting type on the fermentation rate .

title: Do Not Trust Power Management: A Survey on Internal Energy-based Attacks Circumventing Trusted Execution Environments Security Properties
abstract: Over the past few years , several research groups have introduced innovative hardware designs for Trusted Execution Environments ( TEEs ) , aiming to secure applications against potentially compromised privileged software , including the kernel [ 10 , 63 ] . Since 2015 [ 94 ] , a new class of software-enabled hardware attacks leveraging energy management mechanisms has emerged . software-enabled hardware attacks leveraging energy management mechanisms comprise fault [ 86 ] , side-channel [ 46 ] and covert channel attacks [ 28 ] . software-enabled hardware attacks leveraging energy management mechanisms aim is to bypass TEE security guarantees and expose sensitive information such as cryptographic keys . software-enabled hardware attacks leveraging energy management mechanisms have increased in prevalence in the past few years [ 9 , 24 , 40 ] . Popular TEE implementations , such as ARM TrustZone and Intel SGX , incorporate countermeasures against software-enabled hardware attacks leveraging energy management mechanisms . However , countermeasures against these attacks either hinder the capabilities of the power management mechanisms or have been shown to provide insufficient system protection [ 9 , 55 ] . This article presents the first comprehensive knowledge survey of software-enabled hardware attacks leveraging energy management mechanisms , along with an evaluation of literature countermeasures . We believe that the first comprehensive knowledge survey of these attacks will spur further community efforts towards software-enabled hardware attacks leveraging energy management mechanisms .

title: Enhancing Photocurrent of Bismuth Manganate Photoanodes with Nanoislands of Bismuth Oxide
abstract: Photoelectrochemical ( PEC ) water splitting is a promising method for the energy transition . However , Photoelectrochemical ( PEC ) water splitting is still hampered because the performance of the electrodes is too low . Herein , bismuth manganate ( BMO ) is investigated as a photoanode absorber material for PEC . bismuth manganate ( BMO ) thin films are prepared by a sol – gel method with and without a bismuth oxide ( BO ) overlayer . It is found that a bismuth oxide ( BO ) overlayer forms BO nanoislands after annealing . Under visible light illumination , bismuth manganate ( BMO ) results in a nearly tenfold increase of the current density compared to pristine BMO at the same applied potential . a nearly tenfold increase of the current density is related to a decrease in the charge transfer resistance and in the amount of recombinations based on the formation of a favorable heterojunction between bismuth manganate ( BMO ) and BO . The application of overlayers on electrode materials in combination with suitable band alignment is an effective strategy to improve the performance of PEC electrodes .

title: Climate anomalies and Price dynamics: Insights from Sub-Saharan African Currency Unions
abstract: This paper examines the dynamic impact of climate anomalies on consumer prices within two Sub-Saharan African ( SSA ) currency unions : the West African Monetary Union ( WAMU ) and the Central African Monetary Union ( CAMU ) . Using a local projections method on a monthly panel dataset spanning 2002M1-2019M12 , we find that temperature and precipitation anomalies lead to short-term increases in consumer prices of up to 1 percentage point and 0.1 percentage point , respectively , at the currency union level . Country-level estimations reveal significant heterogeneity , with some economies experiencing inflationary pressures lasting beyond two years . While countries ' reliance on the agricultural sector appears to be the main transmission channel of these inflationary effects , interestingly , economic development , energy consumption , and political stability emerge as effective mitigating factors . Given the limited monetary policy autonomy of two Sub-Saharan African ( SSA ) currency unions : the West African Monetary Union ( WAMU ) and the Central African Monetary Union ( CAMU ) , targeted adaptation strategies-such as investments in climate-resilient agriculture and renewable energy-are essential to prevent these climate-related inflationary risks .

title: Optimization of an exosuit design for elbow and shoulder joints considering comfort and safety
abstract: To ensure comfort and safety in the design of wearable robots , a multi-objective optimization method is defined for shoulder and elbow assistance . a multi-objective optimization method is evaluated with a simulation platform implemented on Matlab integrating biomechanical features from the software OpenSim . Thus , the interaction forces between skin and cuffs and the metabolic cost could be estimated during design phase . Finally a drinking task trajectory is carried out to validate the efficiency of wearing an exosuit reducing the fatigue by 32 % .

title: Additive manufacturing of fully metallic dual polarized leaky wave antenna array for polarimetric radar application
abstract: Polarimetric radar provides additional information by analyzing the polarimetric state of the received backscattered wave with respect to the polarimetric state of the transmitted . One application for a polarimetric radar is to characterize natural environment as foliage for instance . Another specific application is the capability for the radar to separate the echoes from the near-nadir surface . As a well-known example , the SWOT mission for Surface Water and Ocean Topography , is based on a dual-polarized Ka-band interferometer with two reflectarray antennas . In our case , our focus on ocean monitoring applications as well . The polarimetric backscattered wave should provide information about the ocean and wind surface states . Consequently , we need a polarimetric radar antenna . In this communication , our describe a new polarimetric radar antenna design that is compact , efficient , and low-profile . First , a dual mode hollow square waveguide-based K-band leaky wave antenna ( LWA ) is proposed , with a focus on side lobe level reduction by tapering of the radiating apertures . This approach is then applied to a specific polarimetric radar system using the HOMARDS sensor . The antenna of a specific polarimetric radar system using the HOMARDS sensor , which consists of a triangular waveguide based dual polarized Ka-band LWA array , is described . The antenna concept is a monolithic entity formed of 4 LWA connected to an excitation structure made up of power dividers and orthomode transducers ( OMTs ) . Finally , the continuation of a new polarimetric radar antenna design that is compact , efficient , and low-profile through a biggest prototype is depicted . All the exhibited designs are printed by fully metallic additive manufacturing ( AM ) and is manufactured by the Swissto12 company . fully metallic additive manufacturing ( AM ) is a groundbreaking technology for future space microwave passive components . fully metallic additive manufacturing ( AM ) flawlessly balances the tradeoff between high-performance components and small devices by printing complex geometries that are not possible with traditional manufacturing techniques . In our designs , the use of additive manufacturing allows for the monolithic printing of radiators and excitation structures with a very high level of compactness and very lightweight . The impact of fully metallic additive manufacturing ( AM ) on design choices is thoroughly discussed in this communication .

title: Call Rewinding Towards RISC-V Specification
abstract: Memory vulnerabilities are still being exploited today to perform code-reuse attacks by overwriting the return address . Recently , call rewinding has been introduced as a security countermeasure to mitigate this type of abuse , placing call rewinding on the same perimeter as the Zicfiss extension . We propose a thorough comparison of call rewinding with the Zicfiss extension and discuss on call rewinding viability for adoption in industrial systems .

title: New trends in line balancing and model sequencing in assembly, disassembly and machining environments
abstract: The Assembly Line Balancing Problem ( ALBP ) , first formally introduced by Salveson in 1955 , has long been a foundational topic in operations research and production management . Over the past seven decades , The Assembly Line Balancing Problem ( ALBP ) , first formally introduced by Salveson in 1955 , has evolved significantly — from a straightforward task-to-station assignment problem to a complex , multi-objective optimization challenge that reflects the intricacies of contemporary manufacturing systems . evolved has been especially pronounced in the last two decades , driven by the integration of Industry 4.0 technologies , increasing emphasis on sustainability , and the emerging human-centered paradigms associated with Industry 5.0 . In this article , we review recent advancements and integrate contributions selected for this Special Issue , which builds on papers presented at the IFIP APMS 2021 and IFAC MIM 2022 conferences . With 37 papers selected from over 90 submissions , this Special Issue , which builds on papers presented at the IFIP APMS 2021 and IFAC MIM 2022 conferences represents the first dedicated collection on The Assembly Line Balancing Problem ( ALBP ) , first formally introduced by Salveson in 1955 , since the 2006 special issue in the European Journal of Operational Research ( EJOR ) , and this Special Issue , which builds on papers presented at the IFIP APMS 2021 and IFAC MIM 2022 conferences reflects the field ’s remarkable progression during a period of profound transformation in manufacturing .

title: GAIA-FL : Generative AI-Augmented Federated Learning for Intrusion Detection System
abstract: In recent years , federated learning ( FL ) has gained significant attention as a privacy-preserving solution for distributed machine learning , particularly in cybersecurity applications such as intrusion and attack detection . However , traditional federated learning ( FL ) models often face challenges related to limited training data diversity , communication overhead , and the ability to adapt to novel or unforeseen attack patterns . At the same time , generative AI ( GAI ) models have emerged as powerful tools for synthesizing realistic data , enabling enhanced model generalization and robustness . In this work , we propose integrating generative AI ( GAI ) with federated learning ( FL ) to create a more effective and adaptive framework for cybersecurity called GAIA-FL ( GAI-Augmented FL ) . generative AI ( GAI ) can augment federated learning ( FL ) by synthesizing diverse attack scenarios , enriching local datasets , and addressing data heterogeneity across distributed nodes . we analyze the unique capabilities of generative AI ( GAI ) , such as data generation , and highlight generative AI ( GAI ) potential to improve the performance of federated learning ( FL )-based cybersecurity systems . Additionally , we explore the integration of generative models and federated learning ( FL ) , focusing on generative models and FL combined ability to detect complex and evolving threats while maintaining data privacy . Unlike existing studies , this work emphasizes the fusion of generative AI ( GAI ) and federated learning ( FL ) to tackle the challenges of decentralized intrusion detection and attack prevention . To validate we approach , we present a case study where generative AI ( GAI ) is used to enhance FL-based network intrusion detection by generating synthetic attack data , improving detection accuracy and robustness . this work demonstrates how integrating can revolutionize cybersecurity in next-generation networks by providing scalable , privacy-preserving , and adaptive solutions for evolving cyber threats .

title: Side-channel attack hardware detection module added to RISC-V core
abstract: Processor performance optimizations such as Out-of-Order or speculative execution are known to be exploited by attackers for malicious purposes . Numerous side-channel attacks have been developed over decades and more recently transient attacks are considered as serious threats . As a countermeasure , previous works offered detection methods monitoring hardware performance counters ( HPC ) . In this work we propose to take advantage of dynamic instructions insertion to monitor HPCs and detect side-channel attacks . take offers flexibility as take allows to dynamically adapt the events monitored by HPCs to the state of the system . we present our light-weight hardware micro-decoding unit used to insert monitoring instructions in the execution flow of a RISC-V core and detect side-channel attacks .

title: Preprint_Extended / disabled bodies & atmospheres
abstract: As much as a symbolic construction or an object of social representation , the body harbours and expresses changes of register linked to everyday sensory experiences . Thus , ways of moving , of observing or greeting others in public spaces embody variations in urban ambiances . In our day-to-day lives , we are immersed in these diffuse and changing affective tonalities , that we in turn modify by the simple fact of our presence . This aspect , which is much less extensively explored by the social sciences , is the entry point for this chapter . It extend the work on walking in urban spaces , undertaken over more than 40 years in the field of architectural and urban ambiances . From more than 40 years in the field of architectural and urban ambiances , we have seen how ways of walking , whatever ways of walking nature , take form in a plasticity of observation , modes of perceptive attention , postures , rhythms modelled and shaped by the spatial and sensory qualities of the spaces ( Parts II and III ) . The question of accessibility to urban public spaces also arises in more than 40 years in the field of architectural and urban ambiances . Not in terms of physical and material accessibility , as deployed by the fields of design and town planning to take account of people with disabilities through appropriate physical adaptations . Here , rather , accessibility is addressed from the point of view of mutual perceptive accessibility , not predefined by objective or objectified material qualities , but continuously reconfigured depending on the situation . As part of this exposition , we will effectively mention disabilities , but more in terms of situational disability rather than physical stigma-or , more precisely , ordinary social vulnerability and ways of dealing with ordinary social vulnerability ( Part I ) .

title: Towards radiolabeling using metallic astatine-211: evaluation of ligands for complexation of At+
abstract: Introduction : Astatine-211 has been considered as an ideal candidate for targeted alpha therapy for the past decades . However , the radionuclide still faces issues related to the in vivo stability of radiolabeling which is mostly based on the formation of carbon-astatine aryl bonds.[1 ] The chemical behavior of astatine is dual : while recent advances have focused on astatine reactivity as a halogen , approaches considering astatine metallic facet for labeling have been somewhat overlooked.[2 ] We focus herein on interactions between astatine , as a metallic species , with soft Lewis bases as a preliminary work for the rational design of chelating agents for At(I ) . Methods : astatine was obtained from cyclotron ( Arronax Nantes ) and recovered in chloroform . After back-extraction in aqueous solution by NaOH , At(I ) was generated in 0.1 M HClO4 , an oxidizing and acidic solution previously identified as ideal to favor the predominance of the At+ species.[3 ] astatine interactions with a series of simple monodentate ligands ( Figure 1A ) were studied by liquid / liquid extraction experiments in a biphasic system ( toluene/0.1 M HClO4 ) with increasing concentration of ligand ( Figure 1B ) as previously reported.[4 ] After 2 h equilibration , changes in the distribution coefficient of 211At activity ( D ) were indicative of interactions with the ligand . The stoichiometry of astatine and the equilibrium constant were determined by reproducing the experimental D values using a thermodynamic model based on key equilibria at play in the biphasic system . In parallel , DFT calculations were performed to screen a library of potential At(I ) ligands and to characterize both the interactions strength and the structure of the formed complexes . Results : D curves according to ligand concentrations were obtained for dimethylthiourea , tetramethylthiourea , morpholine-4-carbothioamide , 2-picolinic acid and thiocyanate as model ligands . Thiourea-based ligands exhibited the strongest interactions and different behaviors were observed within this ligand family , suggesting the formation of complexes with different At-to-ligand ratios ( examples in Figure 1C ) . On the other hand , anionic ligand ( picolinic acid and thiocyanate ) exhibited weaker interactions . The complexation constants calculated by DFT ( see Table ) corroborate the experimental data , and demonstrate At+ preference for sulfur over oxygen-and nitrogen-based groups . Table 1 : Stability constants variation ( Δ Log Kexc ) of 1:1 complexes relative to tetramethylthiourea . Ligand Δ Log Kexc tetramethylthiourea Reference Morpholine-4-carbothioamide-0.6 Dimethylthiourea-2.6 Thioacetamide-4.8 Urea-19.8 Conclusions : Data collected from extraction experiments and DFT study highlights a superiority of thiourea-based ligands . Variation around these first ligands is now in progress to optimize complexes stability . Overall , the results of this study are of importance for the upcoming investigations consisting in rationally designing chelators for 211At and exploit 211At metallic character in the development of radiopharmaceuticals . Chem . 2022 , 61 , 13462–13470 . [ 4 ] Champion , J. et al . Inorg . Chim . Acta 2009 , 362 , 2654–2661 .

title: 211At-metal N-Heterocyclic Carbene complexes: a promising alternative for targeted alpha therapy
abstract: Introduction : With the high energy of its alpha particle and its intermediate half-life , astatine-211 has emerged as a very promising radionuclide for targeted alpha therapy.1 The traditional vectorization strategy of attaching its to aryl groups often shows suboptimal stability in-vivo.2 We investigate an alternative strategy where its is bonded to various transition metal , coordinated with NHC ligands ( NHC = N-heterocyclic carbene ) . Methods : Metals from groups 9 10 and 11 were investigated for bonding with astatide ( At¯ ) . NHCs were selected for NHCs ease of use,3 NHCs modularity4 and the anti-tumoral properties of NHCs complexes.5 A library of NHC-metal-chloride complexes serving as precursors were prepared . Halogen exchange was performed in reducing conditions and the formation of 211At-complexes was monitored by HPLC . In addition molecular modelling was used the stability of various NHC-metal complexes was evaluated to carefully select metals and NHC ligands . Results : Regarding the strength of the metal-At bond molecular modelling indicated a superiority of group 11 metals when using the IPr ligand ( IPr = N N’-bis(2 6-diisopropylphenyl)imidazolylidene ) . In addition the Gibbs free energy of halogen exchange reactions showed for palladium(II ) platinum(II ) and gold(I ) a preference for its over chloride ( or iodide ) . Calculations also highlighted an improved stability of the metal-At bond with electron withdrawing ligands . Bond dissociation energy ( BDE ) and free energy ( ΔG * ) of radiolabelling reaction of [ MAt(IPr ) ] complexes Metal BDE ( kJ / mol ) ΔG*M – Cl → M – At ( kJ / mol ) Rhodium(I ) 439.0 15.6 Iridium(I ) 471.2 22.1 Palladium(II ) 446.0-3.7 Platinum(II ) 474.8-4.7 Copper(I ) 527.2 2.9 Gold(I ) 562.7-9.2 On the experimental side the possibility to radiolabel [ AuCl(IPr ) ] and [ AuCl(IPrCl ) ] in presence of various reducing agents was confirmed with excellent and reproducible radiochemical yields ( RCYs ) ( Figure 1 ) . [ AuCl(IPr ) ] and [ AuCl(IPrCl ) ] in presence of various reducing agents exhibited a good stability in phosphate buffer and [ AuCl(IPrCl ) ] proved also stable in human blood serum ( HBS ) . In similar conditions attempts at radiolabelling [ PdCl(η3-cinnamyl)(IPr ) ] led to two different radiolabelled species depending on the reducing agent . two different radiolabelled species depending on the reducing agent were prepared in very good to excellent RCYs and two different radiolabelled species depending on the reducing agent proved highly stable after 14 hours in phosphate buffer and HBS . Conclusions : Guided by molecular modelling the first milestones of a large study on transition complexes set proving the concept and opening the door to the vectorization of transition complexes for in-vivo studies . title: Multipodal Au–C grafting of calix[4]arene molecules on gold nanorods
abstract: The interface robustness and spatial arrangement of functional molecules on metallic nanomaterials play a key role in the potential applications of functional nano-objects . The design of mechanically stable and electronically coupled attachments with the underlying metal is essential to bring specific desirable properties to the resulting hybrid materials . In this context , rigid multipodal platforms constitute a unique opportunity for the controllable grafting of functionality [ 1 ] . The characterization of the interface in rigid multipodal platforms is a challenge where modelization greatly helps the comprehension of experimental works . However , the limitations of the cluster size models computed with Density Functional Theory ( DFT ) method to reduce the computational effort are detrimental to the modeling of spectroscopic signatures . In this work , we use Density Functional Tight Binding ( DFTB ) method to circumvent the limitation in size of the system and facilitate the comparison with experimental data . we compute the binding energy of the system for the gold surface indices commonly found in the literature in the case of gold nanorods . Then , we use Placzeck theory to compute the Raman spectra of the system . we observe that the multipodal grafting of calix[4]arene molecules on gold surfaces is very stable , with binding energies of several eV. Subsequently , we compute the Raman spectra of such a large system accounting for different gold surface indices . the Raman spectra of such a large system accounting for different gold surface indices allow the identification of the frequency of the normal modes associated with the grafting , and to distinguish between mono-and multipodal grafting , enhancing comprehension of the experimental spectra . Finally , the location of the plasmon associated with the different wavelengths of the lasers used for the Raman experiment provides insight into the facets present in the system through the displacement of certain normal modes . The combination of experimental and theoretical results [ 2 ] provides , for the first time , an in-depth description of the interface between gold nanorods and a chemically grafted multipodal platform , establishing the foundations for the future design of robust and versatile platforms , later used as catalytic objects . [ 1 ] Q. Lenne et al . Chem . Commun . , 58 , 3334–3337 ( 2022 ) . [ 2 ] A. Tetenoire et al . Chem . Sci . 15 , 14677–14684 ( 2024 ) .

title: Formation Of Gold-Astatine Bonds in N-Heterocyclic Carbene Complexes
abstract: With the purpose of exploring alternatives to the poorly stable astatoaryl bond found in most 211At‐labeled radiopharmaceuticals , the coordination between astatine and metal‐NHC ( NHC = N‐heterocyclic carbene ) complexes was investigated . To orient investigated , relativistic DFT calculations were performed , highlighting a superiority of gold(I ) over rhodium(I ) and iridium(I ) , both regarding the strength of the metal‐astatine bond and gold(I ) preference for astatine over other halogens . relativistic DFT calculations also revealed a more stable metal‐astatine bond with electron withdrawing NHCs . Accordingly , two Au(I ) complexes , [ AuCl(IPr ) ] ( IPr = N , N’‐bis[2,6‐(di‐isopropyl)phenyl]imidazol‐2‐ylidene ) and [ AuCl(IAd ) ] ( IAd = N , N’‐bis[adamantyl]imidazol‐2‐ylidene ) were radiolabelled by halide exchange in excellent radiochemical yields with iodine‐125 and astatine in a water / acetonitrile mixture with a reducing agent . While the adamantyl substituted complex was not investigated further due to the adamantyl substituted complex lack of solubility in aqueous or semi aqueous media , the stability of [ Au211At(IPr ) ] in presence of phosphate buffered saline was evaluated and proved excellent ( 96 % after two half‐lives ) encouraging further studies with relevant cancer targeting vectors .

title: Investigating microstructural features and tensile properties of 3D-printed co-polyester reinforced with carbon fibres
abstract: This study investigates the 3D printing of carbon fibre-reinforced copolyester ( COP-CF ) composites using fused filament fabrication ( FFF ) technology , with a focus on the influence of printing parameters on mechanical performance and microstructure . We explore the effects of different printing angles ( 0 • to 90 • ) on the tensile behaviour , pore connectivity , and microstructural characteristics of 3D-printed COP-CF specimens . Synchrotron X-ray microtomography is employed to analyse the internal structure of printed parts , revealing insights into porosity distribution and fibre alignment . We results indicate that a 45 • printing angle yields the highest mechanical performance , with a tensile strength improvement approaching 70 MPa and a Young 's modulus nearing 1 GPa , attributed to filament alignment in the loading direction and optimal load transfer . Additionally , the elongation at break reaches approximately 10 % , indicating a balance between strength and ductility . This study also highlights the role of process-induced porosity and process-induced porosity impact on mechanical properties . Additionally , the design and testing of a 3D-printed curved hook demonstrate a 3D-printed curved hook potential for functional applications under mixed-mode loading conditions effectively at a 45 • printing angle-outperforming other angles by a factor of 1.71 . The findings underscore the importance of printing angle and microstructure control in optimizing the mechanical performance of 3D-printed COP-CF composites for technical applications .

title: Technical Appendix for Bimodal Depth-First Search for Scalable GAC for AllDifferent
abstract: This document is the technical appendix for the paper entitled " Bimodal Depth-First Search for Scalable GAC for AllDifferent " accepted at IJCAI 2025 . Section 1 presents the complete proof of Theorem 2 . Section 2 details the bimodal algorithm for finding a maximum matching in the variable-value graph . Section 3 details the bimodal algorithm for computing the strongly connected components in the residual graph and finding the variable-value pairs to prune .

title: FPGA design and implementation of fuzzy learning control: Application on DC motor position control
abstract: This paper investigates the implementation of a Fuzzy Model Reference Learning Control ( FMRLC ) on a Zedboard Zynq-7000 FPGA . a Fuzzy Model Reference Learning Control ( FMRLC ) dynamically adjusts a Fuzzy Model Reference Learning Control ( FMRLC ) knowledge base and incorporates a memory-based control mechanism to retain and utilize past results in recurring situations . The design and deployment of a Fuzzy Model Reference Learning Control ( FMRLC ) were carried out using the MATLAB / Simulink environment and applied to the angular position control of a DC motor . Initially , a Fuzzy Model Reference Learning Control ( FMRLC ) was tested using the FPGA-In-the-Loop ( FIL ) approach to assess a Fuzzy Model Reference Learning Control ( FMRLC ) robustness against disturbances in simulation . Subsequently , a Fuzzy Model Reference Learning Control ( FMRLC ) was experimentally validated for real-time motor position control . The results obtained in FIL simulations and experimental tests demonstrate high tracking accuracy and strong disturbance rejection . The results obtained in FIL simulations and experimental tests underscore both the superiority of a Fuzzy Model Reference Learning Control ( FMRLC ) over the conventional PID controller and the effectiveness of the adopted design methodology .
keywords: fuzzy model reference learning control ( fmrlc )

title: Stiffness Modeling of Parallel Robots
abstract: The book focuses on the stiffness modeling of serial and parallel manipulators The book presents fundamentals and enhancements for Virtual Joint Modelling ( VJM ) , Matrix Structural Analysis ( MSA ) and Finite Element Analysis ( FEA ) . Virtual Joint Modelling ( VJM ) , Matrix Structural Analysis ( MSA ) and Finite Element Analysis ( FEA ) consider complex kinematics with numerous passive joints , different types of loadings , including essential loadings leading to critical changes in the manipulator configurations , linear and non-linear stiffness analysis , conventional and non-linear compliance error compensation and stiffness parameters estimation from virtual experiments . Presented enhancement for Virtual Joint Modelling ( VJM ) integrates in the stiffness analysis external force / torque applied to the end-point , internal preloading in the joints , and auxiliary forces / torques applied to intermediate points . Presented enhancement for the VJM includes computing an equilibrium configuration corresponding to the external / internal loading and allows obtaining the full-scale non-linear force-deflection relation for any given workspace point . This enables the designer to evaluate critical forces that may provoke non-linear behaviours of the manipulators , such as sudden failure due to elastic instability ( buckling ) . The presented enhancement to MSA allows users to carry out stiffness analysis for serial underactuated structures and over-constrained ones with multiple closed loops . To increase the model accuracy of Virtual Joint Modelling ( VJM ) , Matrix Structural Analysis ( MSA ) and Finite Element Analysis ( FEA ) a dedicated FEA-based stiffness model parameters identification technique is introduced in The book . a dedicated FEA-based stiffness model parameters identification technique is based on the virtual experiments in the CAD / CAE environment and allows Virtual Joint Modelling ( VJM ) , Matrix Structural Analysis ( MSA ) and Finite Element Analysis ( FEA ) to achieve accuracy comparable with Finite Element Analysis ( FEA ) , but a dedicated FEA-based stiffness model parameters identification technique essentially reduces the computational effort , eliminating repetitive re-meshing through the workspace . All considered stiffness modelling techniques , kinematic particularities and loading conditions are illustrated with practical examples and related analysis .

title: p-Type Al-Doped MoS 2 Nanosheet Films: Electronic and Chemical Interface Properties with Gold for Electronic Device Integration
abstract: High-performance optoelectronic devices based on two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides require precise control of the intrinsic and interfacial properties with metallic contacts . We studied aluminum doping and aluminum doping effect on the chemical and electronic properties of MoS2 nanosheet films prepared by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition ( ALD ) . We combined photoelectron ( XPS / UPS ) and UV-vis absorption spectroscopies , revealing that Al introduction decreases the Fermi level-to-valence band energy difference of MoS2 from 0.61 to 0.04 eV and suppresses Au sputtering damage . Stepwise Au sputtering on MoS2 nanosheet films prepared by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition ( ALD ) reveals chemical modifications in the undoped nanosheets , whereas aluminum doping stabilizes MoS2 , preventing such an alteration . These findings highlight the potential of aluminum doping not only for precise control of electronic properties but also for improving the chemical stability of MoS2 nanosheets , making MoS2 nanosheets more suitable for advanced optoelectronic applications .
keywords: atomic layer deposition transition metal dichalcogenides molybdenum sulfide aluminium doping nanosheet photoelectron spectroscopy interfaces

title: A quantitative assessment of variability in impact polypropylene mechanical recycling
abstract: Plastic recycling has become an environmental and economic necessity . Mechanical recycling by extrusion and injection molding is the preferred method for thermoplastics recycling , owing to Mechanical recycling by extrusion and injection molding energy efficiency and capacity to process large quantities of plastic solid waste at an industrial scale . For a sustainable plastics economy , it is crucial that mechanical recycling produces high-performance products , even from waste of variable quality . In this context we evaluated the performance of a recycled Impact copolymer polypropylene ( PPc ) , considering a wide range of properties such as dimensions , chemical composition , morphology , melt viscosity , and appearance like color , and mass , as well as mechanical properties such as flexural strength and Charpy Impact resistance . This study highlights that reprocessing leads to changes in color , including a gradual shift from white to light yellow with successive injection molding cycles . A reduction in bulk density is also observed during the transition from pellets to reground flakes . Furthermore , significant chain scission in PP becomes evident from the first reprocessing cycle , reflected in increasing melt flow index ( MFI ) values . However , reprocessing does not alter the weight of the specimens molded .

title: Continuous microtomography of the hot press consolidation of high performance CF/PAEK layered composites
abstract: The consolidation of carbon fibre-reinforced thermoplastics is a challenge for the manufacturing of high performance composites , especially for the aeronautics field . Although the effects of pressure and temperature on the quality of consolidation have been widely demonstrated , the understanding of the phenomena occurring during consolidation remains partial . Based on previous developments , this work presents a hot press device specifically designed and fabricated for the in-situ observation of consolidation by X-Ray microtomography . A good correlation is found between the evolution of void content and the measure of the sample through-thickness strain obtained by LVDT sensors .
keywords: thermoplastic composites consolidation hot press microtomography

title: Machine learning in concrete durability: challenges and pathways identified by RILEM TC 315-DCS towards enhanced predictive models
abstract: This review provides an in-depth examination of machine learning applications in assessing concrete durability from 2013 to 2024 , with a particular focus on critical degradation mechanisms , including carbonation , chloride-induced deterioration , sulfate attack , frost damage , shrinkage , and corrosion . This review underscores the field ’s heavy reliance on laboratory-based data and notes the limited use of field data and the scarcity of newly generated datasets . This review reveals that most studies utilize existing literature-based datasets , with few contributing novel data and limited open access to existing literature-based datasets , which hampers broader validation and application . This review classifies the features analyzed in studies into categories such as mixture proportions , engineering properties , exposure conditions , test parameters , and chemical compositions , highlighting a growing emphasis on chemical compositions . Modeling approaches are predominantly standalone , though ensemble and hybrid models are increasingly prevalent , with ensemble models showing particularly strong performance in recent years . High accuracy is observed across studies , with ensemble models , neural networks , and hybrid models leading in performance . Furthermore , This review stresses the growing importance of model explainability , noting that model-agnostic methods like SHAP are frequently used and that the focus on explainability has increased . To propel the field ’s forward , This review advocates for the development of diverse new datasets that include both the chemical and physical properties of various mix ingredients and improved data-sharing practices . This review recommends adopting a multi-task learning approach to simultaneously address multiple deterioration mechanisms , which can yield deeper insights and support the creation of more durable concrete structures .

title: Tailoring Permittivity in Dielectric Resonator Antennas with Ceramic 3D Printing Techniques
abstract: The rapid evolution of wireless communication systems has created an increasing demand for dielectric materials in a wide permittivity range , with minimal dielectric losses . Additive manufacturing has emerged as a highly promising technique for producing complex structures that allow for the adjustment of material permittivity , particularly in applications such as dielectric resonator antennas ( DRAs ) . For microwave applications , dielectric ceramics are used for dielectric ceramics exceptional mechanical strength , chemical stability , and thermal resistance , which surpass those of alternative materials like polymers . dielectric ceramics also demonstrate low dielectric losses across a broad range of permittivity values . Historically , the high costs associated with ceramic molding have limited the ability to manufacture complex dielectric resonators . However , recent innovations in additive manufacturing have revolutionized this area , facilitating the creation of complex and conformal structures with high design flexibility . This study presents a novel approach to the fabrication of ceramic resonators , where the control of permittivity is achieved not through changes in material composition but by the strategic incorporation of air inclusions within the resonator 's structure . Our methodology includes a thorough characterization of dielectric properties , validation against established theoretical models , and the design , fabrication , and characterization of DRA prototypes using two materials : alumina and zirconia . First , cylindrical samples of alumina and zirconia were produced with varying air volume fractions . The results indicated that increasing air inclusions up to 95.5 % led to a reduction in permittivity from 9.4 to 1.3 for alumina and from 32.7 to 6.6 for zirconia , aligning with predictions made by the Maxwell-Garnett approximation . After this , DRAs were fabricated using two materials : alumina and zirconia . The zirconia antenna based on a gyroid structure exhibited performance comparable to that of a bulk alumina antenna while achieving a 50 % reduction in mass , thus , confirming that this innovative approach enables the development of dielectric structures with tailored permittivity suitable for microwave applications .
keywords: ceramics additive manufacturing dielectric materials microwaves antenna application

title: Graph Force Learning from EEG Signals for Mental Workload Classification
abstract: Modeling electroencephalography signals using graphs has recently gained a significant attention for different data analysis tasks in neuroscience . A key challenge is identifying the most effective representation that incorporates both the structural positioning of the electrodes and the signal 's statistical features to distinguish between brain states . Most graph based classification frameworks through the engineering of graph structural features , under-explore the structural positioning of the electrodes . This study introduces a novel EEG classification approach that leverages the spatial arrangement of electrodes and a learned graph structure to define interaction forces between electrodes . interaction forces between them are then used as node features for a brain activity classification using classical classifiers such as Support-Vector Machines . The resulting original method achieves a promising performance level in mental workload classification compared to conventional approaches .

title: Anisotropic expansion and shrinkage behavior of thermosetting prepreg layups with respect to the compaction strategy
abstract: The manufacturing of high-performance thermosetting composites requires precise control over thermo-mechanical and chemical processes , particularly during curing . Cure shrinkage in the thermoset matrix , coupled with thermal expansion and compaction , significantly influences the final part 's dimensional stability and structural integrity . Additionally , improper compaction before curing can lead to defects such as residual porosity . This study characterizes these interrelated phenomena using a combination of advanced experimental tools : a press compaction setup , the PvT-HADDOC apparatus , and the CODEC bench . a press compaction setup optimizes pre-consolidation , while the CODEC bench enables real-time monitoring of vacuum-assisted debulking . the PvT-HADDOC apparatus facilitates precise mutli-axial strain measurements under controlled curing conditions . The results highlight the critical role of pre-compaction and controlled curing parameters in minimizing defects and ensuring high-quality composite manufacturing . This study provides valuable insights for optimizing processing strategies in industrial applications .
keywords: consolidation cure shrinkage porosity thermoset prepreg

title: 3D multi-scale thermal modeling of AFP in-situ consolidation processes for thermoplastic composites using an Eulerian FEM approach
abstract: The Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) process has the potential to significantly reduce manufacturing times of composite materials through in-situ consolidation of thermoplastics ( ISCT ) . Although in-situ consolidation of thermoplastics ( ISCT ) can eliminate the need for post-consolidation in autoclaves , The Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) process demands precise thermal management to rapidly heat the composite above the matrix melting point without causing material degradation . The challenge in numerically modeling The Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) process arises from the high-power density emitted by the near-infrared laser diode , the deformed geometry of the silicon roller used for material consolidation , and the high deposition speeds , which can reach up to 1 m / s. Moreover , The Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) process involves multi-scale features , such as micro-scale absorption of laser energy in the first fiber layers , and macro-scale effects associated with deposition velocity . In this work , we introduce a finite element framework based on a 3D Eulerian approach to simulate The Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) process manufacturing conditions . The numerical model at the macro scale is driven by a highly concentrated volumetric heat source , which is derived from solving radiative heat transfer equations at the microstructure level . Structured meshes , incorporating the silicon roller used for material consolidation , the incoming tape , and the substrate , are used to maintain high mesh quality . The geometry of the silicon roller used for material consolidation is obtained from a semi-analytical model available in literature , while the silicon roller used for material consolidation velocity field is derived from a CFD analysis . a semi-analytical model available in literature accounts for anisotropic properties arising from the difference between the transverse and longitudinal thermal conductivity of fibers , as well as temperature-dependent thermal properties . The results demonstrate that a semi-analytical model available in literature accurately predicts the surface temperature of the composite under various manufacturing conditions . Additionally , a parametric study conducted with varying roller velocities and laser intensities enabled the development of a heating law that can be implemented by the The Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) process machine to strive for proper consolidation while preventing material degradation during The Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) process .

title: Improvement of thermal management of composites forming tools using lattice structures
abstract: The manufacture of composite parts is a complex process , where the final quality of the part depends on several parameters , one of which is crucial : thermal management during the manufacturing process . Whatever the process , thermal management must be carried out with accuracy . Traditional management with circular channels , whether optimized or not , has Traditional management with circular channels limits in terms of efficiency and temperature uniformity , particularly for complex geometries . To overcome these limitations , the use of porous media , and lattice structures in particular , is an alternative for improving uniformity and efficiency . This system , in which the cooling fluid circulates in the lattice structure , is studied in this work in order to analyze heat transfer and fluid dynamics locally , and to demonstrate the feasibility of This system , in which the cooling fluid circulates in the lattice structure .

title: Microwave Scattering from Sea Surfaces: CBFM Hybridized to Kirchhoff and Weak-coupling Approximations and to Identical Block PBFs
abstract: In this paper , the characteristic basis function method ( CBFM ) is accelerated to calculate the monostatic and bistatic normalized radar cross sections from one-dimensional highly-conducting sea surfaces in the microwave bands ( C and Ku ) . In the framework of the two-scale asymptotic model , the subsurface length of the block is judiciously derived to contain all the surface curvature components ( small scale ) and the associated PBFs , assumed to be identical for all blocks , are rapidly calculated from the Kirchhoff approximation . In addition , the reduced matrix calculation is accelerated by neglecting the interactions between far blocks and by introducing a roughness slight approximation ( matrix-matrix products can be done from fast Fourier transforms ) , which also allows us to expedite the resolution of the linear system since the matrix is sparse . Numerical results show the efficiency of CBFM-KA .

title: New Insights on the Origin of the Blue Photoluminescence of Natural Opal Through Raman Spectroscopy
abstract: The blue luminescence commonly observed in natural opal ( amorphous , hydrated silica ) under 3.40 eV light remains poorly understood . Previous studies , lacking evidence of extrinsic activators , have attributed The blue luminescence commonly observed in natural opal ( amorphous , hydrated silica ) under 3.40 eV light to intrinsic defects . Raman spectroscopy has enabled the quantification of Q n units a reliable indicator of silica polymerization degree . Thus , we investigated possible correlation between blue luminescence spectra and opal polymerization degree . we used Raman spectroscopy to measure the proportions of Q n units on eight natural samples . we then decomposed the blue luminescence spectra of eight natural samples and observed 3 components at 2.49 , 2.73 , and 3.00 eV ( respectively 498 , 454 , and 413 nm ) . The intensity of each contribution exhibits a linear relationship with the proportions of Q 3 , Q 4 , and Q 2 centers , respectively . As Q 4 can not induce luminescence , we propose that the 2.73 eV emission band is linked to an oxygen deficiency center .

title: Experimental assessment and 2D-Modelling of the viscous sintering of superimposed filaments based on biopolymer
abstract: Additive Manufacturing by Molten material Extrusion ( AM-ME ) of biocompatible and edible parts based on natural biopolymers , such as zein , a protein extracted from corn , opens prospects for applications in the pharmaceutical field . Cohesion between deposited layers requires filament spreading and diffusion of macromolecules at the interface . Viscous sintering has to be characterized and modelled in the case of zein , a protein extracted from corn , to better control zein , a protein extracted from corn processing in the molten state . Sintering kinetics of polymer melts is generally assessed in an instrumented furnace and modelled using the Frenkel-Eshelby approach . the Frenkel-Eshelby approach is based on the evaluation of the growth rate of the bonding neck between two circular parts , linked to polymer melts surface tension ( Γ ) , the driving force , and viscosity ( η ) . the Frenkel-Eshelby approach was recently completed by the acquisition of 3D scans by dynamic X-ray tomography ( 5.2 μm pixel size , 1 scan / s ) on the ANATOMIX beamline of Synchrotron SOLEIL , to follow the hot-melt sintering of 4 filaments ( LFilament=5 mm , ∅Filament=2 mm ) disposed in two layers . The analysis of the reconstructed volumes leads to assess the decreasing size of the central pore during sintering . 2D modelling is carried out by FEM combined to Level Set with COMSOL Multiphysics ® . 2D modelling requires a simplification of the geometry according to an axial symmetry and an adaptive time-stepping . At 120 ° C , a typical temperature to process zein , a protein extracted from corn , simulated and experimental sintering are similar , with a decrease rate of the central pore at about 1%/s . Increasing sintering rates are obtained as the temperature and surface tension increase .
keywords: additive manufacturing by molten material extrusion ( am-me )

title: Image Despeckling based on the Variance of Diffusion Restoration Models: an Application to SAR and Medical Ultrasound
abstract: Speckle noise poses a major challenge in coherent imaging modalities such as Synthetic Aperture Radar ( SAR ) and Ultrasound ( US ) , degrading image quality and hindering accurate interpretation . This paper proposes a hybrid restoration framework that integrates a physical model with a pretrained diffusion-based generative prior . Beyond addressing additive noise and system degradations , we introduce a novel empirical model-logistic-plus-linear in form-to characterize the stochasticity of diffusion sampling in the presence of multiplicative speckle noise . Leveraging characterize , we use the empirical variance from multiple diffusion samples to estimate noise-free images . a hybrid restoration framework that integrates a physical model with a pretrained diffusion-based generative prior operates directly on uncompressed beamformed data , preserving statistical properties often lost in conventional despeckling techniques . we evaluate a hybrid restoration framework that integrates a physical model with a pretrained diffusion-based generative prior on both numerical data and real-world SAR and US datasets . Results demonstrate a hybrid restoration framework that integrates a physical model with a pretrained diffusion-based generative prior effectiveness and competitiveness compared to state-of-the-art methods , both quantitatively and qualitatively , showcasing a hybrid restoration framework that integrates a physical model with a pretrained diffusion-based generative prior potential as a general-purpose despeckling solution across coherent imaging systems .

title: Singularity-free trajectory tracking for steerable wheeled mobile robots
abstract: Omnidirectional robots can be realized using Mecanum wheels or using a suitable arrangement of conventional steerable wheels . The latter group , known as omnidirectional steerable wheeled mobile robots ( SWMRs ) , are known to have a lower cost with respect to Mecanum wheels , and to be more robust thanks to the presence of conventional wheels . Nevertheless , The latter group , known as omnidirectional steerable wheeled mobile robots ( SWMRs ) modeling and control is complex , due to the presence of singularities in The latter group , known as omnidirectional steerable wheeled mobile robots ( SWMRs ) representation . This paper proposes a framework for trajectory tracking of SWMRs using Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) based on a real-time iteration scheme . Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) based on a real-time iteration scheme generates feasible motions for the robot , avoiding model singularities of the mobile base , together with bounds on driving and steering velocities on the wheels . Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) based on a real-time iteration scheme works alongside a finite state machine , responsible for singularity avoidance during starting and stopping motion , and a state trajectory generation scheme based on dynamic feedback linearization , which makes a framework for trajectory tracking of SWMRs using Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) based on a real-time iteration scheme capable of tracking any trajectory . a framework for trajectory tracking of SWMRs using Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) based on a real-time iteration scheme is validated on a Neobotix MPO-700 on various trajectories .
keywords: omnidirectional steerable wheeled mobile robots ( swmrs )

title: Stratified sampling: fast estimation of quantization effects on DNN
abstract: Deep neural networks complexity has exploded in recent years . exploded brought new challenges in terms of memory , execution time and power requirements . One way of meeting new challenges in terms of memory , execution time and power requirements is to use finite precision . However , finite precision may result in a degradation in output quality . a degradation in output quality needs to be estimated , balancing between time and confidence in the estimation . This paper proposes a parametric method to estimate the degradation caused by finite precision in data processing oriented applications such as deep learning . a parametric method to estimate the degradation caused by finite precision in data processing oriented applications such as deep learning aims to reduce the estimation time and energy requirements while maintaining confidence in the results . a parametric method to estimate the degradation caused by finite precision in data processing oriented applications such as deep learning takes advantage of a priori information about the inputs to select more informative inputs . A method to obtain a priori information about the inputs is also proposed . The results obtained are similar to a simple degradation estimation with a time reduction of one order of magnitude .

title: Contribution of additive manufacturing to the production of ceramic dielectric resonators with adapted permittivity
abstract: The advancement of telecommunications necessitates dielectric materials with optimized permittivity , high quality factor , and nearzero temperature coefficient for integration into dielectric resonator antennas ( DRAs ) . Additive manufacturing ( AM ) offers opportunities to tune permittivity via complex geometries and this study investigates ceramic resonators with controlled permittivity , achieved by introducing air inclusions without altering the material composition . Using gyroids-mathematically defined triply periodic minimal surfaces-we fabricated ceramic / air composite resonators from alumina and zirconia as test materials , integrated into DRAs . Digital light processing ( DLP ) was employed to produce cylindrical gyroid resonators , which were debinded and sintered to achieve high relative density . Dielectric measurements ( 1-16 GHz ) by means of a resonant cavity revealed that effective permittivity of resonators actually decreases with air inclusion volume , from 32.7 to 1.3 using zirconia and then alumina ; results are in accordance with current models . Increased air inclusion also reduces dielectric loss . Prototyped DRAs demonstrate comparable performance , achieving a weight reduction of 50 % for zirconia gyroid resonators relative to solid alumina parts . Future work includes exploring the temperature coefficient of resonance frequency and gradient gyroid resonators .
