title: Advanced Research in Real-Time Scheduling for Energy Autonomous Sensor Nodes
abstract: Energy-aware scheduling policies must be integrated into a sophisticated design process in order to design Energy Harvesting ( EH ) sensor nodes with real-time capabilities . Energy Harvesting ( EH ) sensor nodes with real-time capabilities should achieve energy neutrality by efficiently managing energy resources , ensuring continuous operation even in situations with intermittent energy availability while respecting timeliness constraints . An overview of the ineffectiveness of classical real-time scheduling techniques is given . An overview of the ineffectiveness of classical real-time scheduling techniques motivates more advanced research studies to propose and validate new energy harvesting aware schedulers . The paper presents EED-H , a scheduler which efficiently specifies how processing time and energy should be allocated to the software tasks in order to ensure energy neutrality whenever feasible . The paper finally draws attention to a few technical issues with EED-H , a scheduler which efficiently specifies how processing time and energy should be allocated to the software tasks in order to ensure energy neutrality whenever feasible actual implementation , mainly in relation to measuring energy production , energy consumption and energy prediction .

title: GC-InnOscent: a breakthrough approach to reveal the contribution of individual volatile compounds to pet food aroma
abstract: Odor plays a major role in food choice and preference . Odor results from the simultaneous perception of an often-complex mixture of volatile compounds . Numerous researches aimed at understanding the role of volatile compounds and volatile compounds interactions in the perception of foods . In addition to Numerous researches role in fundamental understanding , Numerous researches help guide formulations and processes to meet consumer satisfaction . In the petfood sector , consumers can not verbalize consumers perception . However , dogs , endowed with superior olfactory acuity , can display marked preferences and prove to be particularly demanding . This study aimed to assess the actual olfactory impact of molecules listed in the bibliography as impacting dog palatability . The approach used is based on the InnOscent chromatographic and olfactometric device , which enables to compose custom-made effluents , by selective omission or addition of molecules making up an aromatic extract . An expert panel , human in The approach used , evaluates molecules listed in the bibliography as impacting dog palatability . Olfactometric analysis of a commercial dry pet food product revealed over 70 compounds , 40 of which have odorant potential . Among the compounds identified were some acids , aldehydes , pyrazines and methional , previously reported to be mathematically correlated with the palatability of petfood products . An expert panel , human in this first approach , assessment of recombinant extracts showed that some molecules or chemical families made a limited contribution to odor when considered individually . However , the joint omission of compounds with the greatest odorant potential led to a significant distortion of the product odor that could affect a commercial dry pet food product palatability . These results must now be faced with the dog 's sense of smell and palatability .
keywords: aroma recombination gc olfactometry palatability petfood volatilecompounds

title: Luneburg Lens Focusing Improvement with the Aid of Graphene Strip Tuned to Plasmon Resonance
abstract: Considered is the plane wave focusing with the aid of concentrically layered cylindrical Luneburg lens decorated with conformal graphene strip , in the TE-polarization case . The angular location and the width of conformal graphene strip are arbitrary . Graphene 's surface impedance is expressed using the quantum Kubo formalism . To build a numerical solution , we apply full-wave analytical regularization technique , based on the analytic inversion of the static part . full-wave analytical regularization technique , based on the analytic inversion of the static part guarantees the convergence of the resulting numerical code . We compute the focusing ability of micron-scale lens in the wide frequency range up to 30 THz . This study shows that a narrow strip of graphene , placed on the lens surface , i. e. in lens focal area , can enhance the focusing ability at the frequency of the strip plasmon mode proportionally to the mode quality factor .

title: MCL-1 expression in breast cancer-associated fibroblasts modulates their ECM properties and influences breast cancer cells behavior
abstract: Introduction : Breast cancer-associated-fibroblasts consist in two major populations of pro-tumoral bCAFs : the inflammatory CAFs that release pro-inflammatory cytokines , and the myofibroblastic CAFs ( myCAFs ) known for their extensive production and organization of extracellular-matrix ( ECM ) proteins , enabling their to influence the behavior of cancer cells . We have previously shown that inhibition of MCL-1 in CAFs leads to a loss of the myofibroblastic characteristics of CAFs , particularly in relation to a role for MCL-1-in actomyosin dynamics . leads defines MCL-1 as a target in stroma-influenced breast cancers , and argues for a comprehensive study of the effects of its targeting in myofibroblastic CAFs . In this study , We investigated whether MCL-1 expression in CAFs alters the characteristics of CAFs extracellular-matrix and the resulting chemoresistance of cancer cells . Methods : We explored the role of MCL-1 in the primary culture of myCAFs obtained from treatment-naive patients with invasive breast carcinoma after surgical resection , by genetically targeting myCAFs obtained from treatment-naive patients with invasive breast carcinoma after surgical resection through MCL-1 knockdown by Crispr-Cas9 . Results : ( 1)A global proteomic analysis of myCAFs + /-KD MCL-1 by mass spectrometry reveals a decrease in the expression of proteins present in the extracellular-matrix such as elastin , metalloproteinase 14 , MXRA8 , COL12A1 and thrombospondins ( THBS3 ) suggesting a modification of ECM proteins production after MCL-1 gene inactivation in myCAFs obtained from treatment-naive patients with invasive breast carcinoma after surgical resection . ( 2)Composition and topology of myCAFs-derived 3D ECMs : After generating myCAF-derived matrices in vitro , We show that inactivation of the MCL1 gene leads to a reorganization of collagen fibers that are more parallel to one another , which , in the literature , is associated with a poor prognosis in breast cancer patients ( Conklin et al , 2011 ) . However , using atomic force microscopy , We show that there is no difference in stiffness between matrices derived from CAFs expressing MCL-1 or not . ( 3)Luminal cancer cells chemoresistance on myCAFs-derived 3D ECMs : Next , We show that ZR-75 luminal breast cancer cells are less sensitive to chemotherapeutic treatment when cells are on myCAFsKD MCL-1-derived ECM compared to myCAFsKD CTRL-derived ECM and are is accompanied by altered expression of anti-apoptotic proteins by ZR-75 luminal breast cancer cells . Conclusion : These results suggest that gene inactivation of MCL-1 in myCAFs alters myCAFs ability to produce and organize matrix proteins , thereby modulating cancer cells chemoresistance . A more detailed study of the myCAFs matrisome by mass spectrometry is currently underway to identify matrix proteins that may be responsible to the induction of signaling pathways conferring a survival advantage for cancer cells . A better understanding of the involvement of MCL-1 in the more or less aggressive phenotype of myCAFs should help to guide the therapeutic choice of patients according to patients response to chemotherapy .
keywords: invasive breast carcinoma after surgical resection

title: Tunable Metasurface Based on Crossed Strip Gratings Consisting of Nonreciprocal Materials
abstract: A non-reciprocal metasurface formed by two crossed strip gratings , the upper of which consists of a magnetically active material ( ferrite ) , and the lower of a dielectric ( silicon ) , is proposed and studied . The possibility of achieving mechanical tuning of the resonance response of the considered metasurface when rotating two crossed strip gratings relative to each other is shown . The phenomenon of extraordinary enhancement of the Faraday effect when using metasurface resonances of this type has been demonstrated . Two factors that allow reconfiguration in the considered metasurface are : firstly , the mechanical rotation of two crossed strip gratings relative to each other and , secondly , the adjustment of the amplitude of the magnetizing field . Thanks to this , we can change the scattering characteristics of the considered metasurface over a wide frequency range , which is necessary for designing the non-reciprocal devices .

title: SLACKVM: Packing Virtual Machines in Oversubscribed Cloud Infrastructures
abstract: Cloud providers generally expose a large catalog of Virtual Machines ( VMs ) offers , some being categorized as premium — guaranteeing dedicated resources — and others being hosted in oversubscribed environments , where virtual resources can exceed the physical capabilities of Physical Machines ( PMs ) . The latter strategy is often employed to increase platform utilization , as hosted VMs are unlikely to fully utilize all hosted VMs allocated resources simultaneously [ 1 ] . However , managing mul-tiple oversubscribed VM levels introduces an additional layer of complexity for Cloud providers , often leading Cloud providers to provision isolated clusters of PMs for each category of offers . In this paper , we introduce SLACKVM , a novel Cloud shared architecture wherein VMs from various oversubscription levels coexist on the same cluster of PMs . In particular , we demonstrate that oversubscription levels can be complementary , meaning oversubscription levels do not saturate the same resource components . By leveraging be , Cloud providers can couple multiple levels to better consolidate VMs offers onto PMs , and reduce the size of Cloud providers clusters by up to 9.6 % . reduce results in both an operational cost reduction and a reduced ecological footprint for Cloud infrastructures , with a limited impact on the Quality of Service ( QoS ) .

title: A compact Vivaldi-shaped array using antipodal Vivaldi antennas for beamforming application
abstract: A compact ultra-wideband Vivaldi antenna with a Chebyshev tapering profile to enhance the impedance bandwidth is proposed for beamforming applications . A compact ultra-wideband Vivaldi antenna with a Chebyshev tapering profile to enhance the impedance bandwidth shows a good VSWR<2.1 between 1.13 and 30 GHz . An array is created and the cross-polarization is cancelled with a mirrored disposition of both antennas . The beam tilt is then controlled by an array arrangement of the radiators along a Vivaldi shape .

title: 40 GHz Beam-Steering Two-Elements Array Antenna Using GaN Varactors for Millimeter-Wave Applications
abstract: A continuously steerable beam patch antenna array employing a classical phase shifter based on GaN HEMTs is presented . Here GaN HEMTs are used as varactor diodes to achieve the tunability purpose . By controlling the DC bias of GaN HEMTs from-2 V to 2 V , A continuously steerable beam patch antenna array employing a classical phase shifter based on GaN HEMTs can provide continuous beam steering from 0 ° to +25 ° in the azimuth plane at 41.20 GHz , while achieving low side lobe level and good impedance matching performances . Using GaN HEMTs as varactors to achieve the beam steering capability has never been tried before from our acknowledgment . Measurement results agree well with the simulation results and validate the effectiveness of the proposed beam steering based on GaN technology . A continuously steerable beam patch antenna array employing a classical phase shifter based on GaN HEMTs will find numerous applications within future wireless communication systems especially for millimeter-wave applications .

title: Towards Digital Sustainability: Involving Cloud Users as Key Players
abstract: Due to the rapid growth of Cloud services , data centers have become major energy consumers , resulting in significant CO2 emissions . Several infrastructure-focused strategies , such as resource consolidation , have been used to reduce the carbon footprint of Cloud infrastructure . However , end-users are often left out of the picture . Since end-users are the primary target of Cloud applications , it would be beneficial to actively involve end-users in reducing the carbon footprint of Cloud applications . In this paper , we offer end-users a way to influence the carbon footprint of cloud applications end-users use . To this end , we ask end-users to select a high-level mode to control the carbon footprint of a cloud application . we then design a dynamic adaptation algorithm that determines an appropriate configuration for a cloud application for each request , based on the end-user mode and on the carbon intensity of the infrastructure energy sources . we implement and evaluate we system on a simple image-resizing application . we run experiments on SeDuCe , a Cloud infrastructure testbed partially powered by solar panels . we results show that we save energy consumption by up to 84 % when all end-users agree to degrade the quality of the application ’s output , and we provide a good quality-energy trade-off when end-users make heterogeneous choices . In addition , we are able to improve quality by leveraging the available green energy budget .

title: Environmental life cycle assessment of drink and yoghurt products using non-nutritive sweeteners and sweetness enhancers in place of added sugar: the SWEET project
abstract: Purpose : There are increasing concerns regarding detrimental health effects of added sugar in food and drink products . Non-nutritive sweeteners ( NNS ) and sweetness enhancers ( SE ) are seen as viable alternatives . Much work has been done on health and safety of NNS&SE when consumed in place of sugar , but very little on Non-nutritive sweeteners ( NNS ) and sweetness enhancers ( SE ) sustainability . This work aims to bridge that gap with an environmental study of replacing added sugar with NNS&SE in the context of drink and yoghurt . Methods : A life cycle assessment ( LCA ) approach was used to compare environmental impact of a drink and yoghurt , sweetened with sucrose , to those sweetened with NNSs or an SE : stevia rebaudioside A , sucralose , aspartame , neotame , and thaumatin . Primary ingredients data were taken from preparation of foodstuffs for clinical trials . Results are reported via the ReCiPe 2016 ( H ) method , with focus on land use , global warming potential ( GWP ) , marine eutrophication , mineral resource scarcity , and water consumption . Impacts are reported in terms of 1 kg product . Scenarios explore sensitivity of the LCA results to change in background processes , functional unit , and sweetener type . This work was conducted as part of the EU Horizon 2020 project SWEET ( sweeteners and sweetness enhancers : impact on health , obesity , safety , and sustainability ) . Results and discussion : Replacing sugar with an NNS or part-replacing with an SE is shown to reduce environmental impact across most impact categories , for example , on a mass basis , GWP for a drink reduces from 0.61 to approx . 0.51 kgCO 2-eq / kg and for a yoghurt from 4.15 to approx . 3.73 kgCO 2-eq / kg . Variability in environmental impact is shown to be relatively small between the NNSs , indicating that choice of NNS is less important than the reformulation changes required to accommodate the loss of sugar . Reporting impact in terms of calorie density , instead of mass , shows greater reduction in environmental impact when using an NNS or an SE and shows how important functional unit is when reporting impact of these products . Conclusion : This work is the first to compare food or drink products sweetened with sugar , NNSs , or SE . Results show that there is great potential to reduce environmental impact of sweetened drinks and yoghurts . Moreover , the choice of NNS does not greatly affect the environmental impact of either product . Therefore , This work shows that choices relating to replacing added sugar may be based more upon health or formulation needs and less on environmental concerns .

title: Polarization Diverse Ku-, K-band Leaky-Wave Antenna Achieved Through Efficient Routing of Meandering Microstrips
abstract: In this work , we propose a novel dual band antenna achieved with the help of meandering microstrips . a novel dual band antenna achieved with the help of meandering microstrips is optimized for operating in Ku-and K band . Circularly polarization is maintained throughout K band , while a novel dual band antenna achieved with the help of meandering microstrips is linearly polarized in Ku-. The open stopband is suppressed at the frequency corresponding to broadside radiation to improve the gain and maintain continuous scanning in Ku-and K band . Theoretical formulations are provided to scale a novel dual band antenna achieved with the help of meandering microstrips to higher or lower bands of operation . The two-band operation is achieved by 2 nd and 1 st spatial harmonic operation . a novel dual band antenna achieved with the help of meandering microstrips demonstrates beam steering capabilities from backward to forward directions , spanning a range of 72 ° , from −42 ° to 30 ° , in the K band frequency range 19.4GHz to 27.5GHz . Additionally , in the Ku-band , which covers frequencies from 11GHz to 15.5GHz , a novel dual band antenna achieved with the help of meandering microstrips offers a beam steering range of 75 ° , from −15 ° to 60 ° .

title: Dynamical Changes Non-Reciprocal Bistability in a Metasurface with a Nonlinear Element on Wood's Anomaly Resonances
abstract: Herein , we introduce a novel nonlinear metasurface architecture featuring a thin metal-dielectric grating incorporated with Kerr-type nonlinear elements . a novel nonlinear metasurface architecture featuring a thin metal-dielectric grating incorporated with Kerr-type nonlinear elements is adept at generating high-Q lattice mode resonances , allowing for the exploration of distinct electromagnetic modes associated with Wood 's anomalies across varying frequency parameters . high-Q lattice mode resonances yield enhancement local field intensities , consequently amplifying nonlinear effects significantly . Notably , the metasurface exhibits bistable characteristics , the dynamics of which can be efficiently changed through alterations in illumination conditions . Through rigorous numerical simulations , we observe a non-reciprocal phenomenon in the transmission of electromagnetic waves through a thin metal-dielectric grating incorporated with Kerr-type nonlinear elements , underscoring the versatility and potential applications of a novel nonlinear metasurface architecture featuring a thin metal-dielectric grating incorporated with Kerr-type nonlinear elements .

title: Disaggregation Patterns for Secure AI Systems
abstract: Disaggregation is a growing trend in large-scale artificial intelligence ( AI ) systems to overcome hardware and software resource limitations and improve performance while preserving security and privacy . This paper takes a closer look at different dimensions of the concept , in AI , security and hardware . We identify two key design patterns that may be combined to build optimized disaggregated AI architectures and discuss benefits and limitations for AI and security . Using a large language model use case , We also highlight some key trade-offs between performance , resource allocation and security for different disaggregation strategies in hardware and in software .

title: Deciphering the Benefits of Coordinated Binders in Si‐Based Anodes by Combined Operando/In Situ and Ex Situ X‐Ray Micro‐ and Nano‐Tomographies
abstract: Abstract The simple addition of a Zn(II ) precursor to a preoptimized poly(carboxylic acid ) binder solution enhances the electrochemical performance and cycle life of silicon‐based electrodes . The binder / cation couple forms a cross‐linked coordinated binder that plays a key role in enhancing the mechanical and chemical stability of the electrode microstructure . The impact of The simple addition of a Zn(II ) precursor to a preoptimized poly(carboxylic acid ) binder solution on the microstructural evolution of the electrode during cycling is investigated at different scales ( from cell / electrode to silicon particle scale ) using complementary operando , in situ , and ex situ X‐ray tomography techniques . Comparative analyses conducted on the reference and with Zn electrode formulations using operando and in situ X‐ray micro‐tomography allow for monitoring of the electrode morphological deformations along with the crack pattern formation and evolution during cycling . The benefits of The simple addition of a Zn(II ) precursor to a preoptimized poly(carboxylic acid ) binder solution include enhancing the mechanical stability of the electrode through a strengthened microstructure more apt to maintaining the electrode integrity , as well as a better anchoring to the current collector leading to decreased electrical disconnections and capacity fade . Moreover , complementary ex situ X‐ray nano‐tomography measurements highlight the benefits of The simple addition of a Zn(II ) precursor to a preoptimized poly(carboxylic acid ) binder solution in terms of chemical stability with mitigated solid electrolyte interface ( SEI ) formation over the electrode cycling .
keywords: binder in situ li ion batteries silicon anode x ray tomography

title: Control analysis of an underactuated bio-inspired robot
abstract: This article is devoted to the control of bio-inspired robots that are underactuated . bio-inspired robots that are underactuated are composed of tensegrity joints remotely actuated with cables , which mimic the musculoskeletal system of the bird neck . A computed torque control ( CTC ) is applied to bio-inspired robots that are underactuated as well as an original control called pseudo computed torque control ( PCTC ) . an original control called pseudo computed torque control ( PCTC ) uses the dynamics and the pseudo-inverse of the Jacobian matrix . The stability of the two proposed controls is then analyzed through linearization of the dynamic model and expression of the closed-loop transfer function in the Laplace domain . We show that , depending on the desired trajectory , A computed torque control ( CTC ) can be unstable when the controlled variables are the end effector position and orientation . For a robot with many joints and a limited number of cables , A computed torque control ( CTC ) is always unstable . Instead , an original control called pseudo computed torque control ( PCTC ) shows a large domain of stability . analyzed is complemented by experimental tests demonstrating that the two proposed controls exhibit similar performance when A computed torque control ( CTC ) is stable . Furthermore , an original control called pseudo computed torque control ( PCTC ) maintains stability on trajectories where A computed torque control ( CTC ) becomes unstable , showing robustness to perturbations as well .

title: POST-FILTERING OF LOSSY COMPRESSED NOISY IMAGES AND ITS EFFICIENCY PREDICTION
abstract: The object of the study is the process of lossy compression of noisy images and noisy images post-filtering . The subject of the study is the approach to efficient two-stage processing ( compression and post-filtering ) for better portable graphics ( BPG ) coder and prediction of the approach to efficient two-stage processing ( compression and post-filtering ) for better portable graphics ( BPG ) coder efficiency . The goal of the study is to analyze performance characteristics of the approach to efficient two-stage processing ( compression and post-filtering ) for better portable graphics ( BPG ) coder and to propose an approach to performance characteristics of the considered two-stage approach prediction . Methods used : numerical simulation , regression , statistical analysis . Results obtained : 1 ) the approach to efficient two-stage processing ( compression and post-filtering ) for better portable graphics ( BPG ) coder advantage is that the approach to efficient two-stage processing ( compression and post-filtering ) for better portable graphics ( BPG ) coder is able to provide improvement of quality of compressed noisy image under condition that an image is compressed with compression ratio smaller than that one corresponding to optimal operation point ; 2 ) the approach efficiency depends on several factors including noise intensity , image complexity , and filter type and parameters ; 3 ) the main characteristics of the approach to efficient two-stage processing ( compression and post-filtering ) for better portable graphics ( BPG ) coder can be quite accurately predicted in advance and predicted allows offering useful information for decision undertaking on what value of the coder parameter to apply ; 4 ) this leads to either improving the compressed and processed image quality compared to its original version or , at least , to avoiding quality degradation . Conclusions : based on the results of the study , it is worth 1 ) predicting performance characteristics for the approach to efficient two-stage processing ( compression and post-filtering ) for better portable graphics ( BPG ) coder ; 2 ) adapting the approach to efficient two-stage processing ( compression and post-filtering ) for better portable graphics ( BPG ) coder to image complexity and noise intensity .
keywords: two-stage processing ( compression and post-filtering ) for better portable graphics ( bpg ) coder efficiency

title: Numerical investigation of a permeability-microstructure relationship in the context of internal erosion
abstract: Internal erosion , characterized by the migration of soil particles within hydraulic earth structures due to seepage , is a significant global concern for risk management and maintenance . Among various mechanisms contributing to Internal erosion , characterized by the migration of soil particles within hydraulic earth structures due to seepage , , suffusion emerges as a prominent process . suffusion involves the simultaneous detachment , transport , and potential self-filtration of fine particles through the pore network , leading potentially to a change in permeability and shear strength . Thus , investigating the link between permeability and microstructure is a key to achieve a better understanding of suffusion and to predict suffusion consequences on the soil 's permeability . The proposed methodology involves generating discrete element method-based samples , characterizing discrete element method-based samples constriction size distribution , and computing permeability using fast Fourier transform . While the Kozeny-Carman model was initially developed for stable microstructures , the Kozeny-Carman model may not apply to suffusion due to microstructural evolution . Thus , a modified approach is introduced , incorporating a characteristic constriction diameter computed from the constriction size distribution . a modified approach is being compared against the Kozeny-Carman model on fourteen gap-graded specimens . Encouraging results are herein being obtained so that a modified approach will be later used on flow modified specimens .

title: Studying the visual behavior of individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in the presence of affinity
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorders ( ASD ) affect between 1 % and 2 % of the global population , causing difficulties in communication and interaction for those affected . Most individuals with ASD develop a deep passion for an object or subject ( which can range from particle physics to cardboard crates ) that takes on a significant role , providing comfort in anxiety-inducing situations . This passion is commonly referred to as a circumscribed interest , or affinity . While the positive role and importance of a circumscribed interest , or affinity in the lives of autistic individuals have been widely described in testimonials from patients and specialists , some psychologists and psychiatrists view a circumscribed interest , or affinity as an obsession that prevents people with ASD from opening up to the world . Currently , there is no objective evidence supporting either theory . The aim of this thesis is to use eye-tracking technology to measure the visual attention of individuals with ASD in the presence of individuals with ASD affinity , as well as in response to neutral stimuli , in order to detect any potential differences . Cross-analyses with those of psychologists have linked the autistic traits of individuals with ASD to individuals with ASD visual behaviors when confronted with their affinity .
keywords: studying the visual behavior of individuals with autism spectrum disorder asd in the presence of affinity

title: Emerging New Roles for Low-Code Software Development Platforms
abstract: Low-and no-code development platforms have introduced two new development roles : the platform engineer and the citizen developer . While the platform engineer are still software developers who implement Low-and no-code development platforms , the latter use Low-and no-code development platforms to develop the latter domain applications . In practice , however , we believe that the citizen developer is shared by two people . For example , in the teaching domain , the citizen developer is shared between a teacher and a teacher assistant . a teacher is the domain practitioner , while the second is the domain engineer . the domain engineer uses the development platform to create a tailored platform for a teacher . To explore the possibility of differentiate two new development roles : the platform engineer and the citizen developer in current low-code development platforms , we used two different low-code platforms-Mendix and OutSystems-to implement two case studies . two case studies reveal the limitations of current platforms for specializing platforms with functionalities close to those of low-code development platforms . To compare two different low-code platforms-Mendix and OutSystems , we consider a list of features that two different low-code platforms-Mendix and OutSystems must satisfy . The results show that current low-code development platforms can not fully support two new development roles : the platform engineer and the citizen developer .
labels: Preparation for New Jobs in the Future Industry

title: Partial Bidirectionalization of Model Transformation Languages
abstract: While most model-transformation languages in Model-Driven Engineering are unidirectional , bidirectionality is valuable when artifacts need two-way synchronization . Although several bidirectional transformation engines have been developed , several bidirectional transformation engines behavior is generally considered more difficult to formulate and predict compared to the unidirectional case . In the bidirectionalization approach , users write the forward direction of users transformations in the same unidirectional language users are used to , and obtain a system that ( besides performing the complete forward transformation ) can automatically propagate in the backward direction the target updates . When possible , full bidirectionalization is desirable , but far from trivial . In this paper we propose a partial bidirectionalization approach , by partial compilation of a unidirectional language into a bidirectional language , and coupled execution of the two language engines . Forward transformation is still complete , whereas the target updates that can be back-propagated are deletions and modifications of a well-defined part of the target model . While the extent of the bidirectionalization depends on the two coupled systems , in this paper we provide a general combination scheme and we briefly discuss a general combination scheme well-behavedness . Then we use we technique to bidirectionalize the ATL model-transformation language on top of the GRoundTram bidirectional graph-transformation system .
keywords: software and its engineering → model driven software engineering abstraction
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: dpDebugger: a Domain-Parametric Debugger for DSLs Using DAP and Language Protocols
abstract: Interactive debuggers are established tools used by developers to understand programs and localize faults . Interactive debuggers are equally valuable in the context of model-driven development , when working on executable behavioral models . However , development costs of interactive debuggers for Domain-Specific Languages ( DSLs ) can be significant . In order to mitigate development costs of interactive debuggers for Domain-Specific Languages ( DSLs ) , several reusable DSLagnostic debugging solutions have been proposed . We argue that the applicability of several reusable DSLagnostic debugging solutions is limited by being tied to a fixed set of debugging services , a specific language engineering approach , or a particular user interface . In this paper , We present dpDebugger , a domain-parametric debugger capable of controlling the execution of a program and providing domain-specific debugging operations ( such as breakpoints and steps ) for heterogeneous DSL runtimes . The debugger relies on a language protocol to communicate with and be configured by heterogeneous DSL runtimes , while also enabling the debugging of DSLs with non-deterministic execution semantics . The debugger can The debugger be controlled using a reinterpretation of the Debug Adapter Protocol ( DAP ) , for an effortless integration in existing Integrated Development Environments ( IDEs ) that support the Debug Adapter Protocol ( DAP ) .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Towards Model-Driven Test Case Concretization for End-to-end Combinatorial Testing
abstract: Combinatorial testing can be used to automatically generate relevant sets of combinations of abstract test data for a System Under Test ( SUT ) . Combinatorial testing requires defining a combinatorial model with possible abstract values for the a System Under Test ( SUT ) input parameters , from which relevant abstract test cases can be generated to reach a chosen coverage criterion . However , concretizing abstract test cases into concrete test cases , and writing corresponding test scripts , is a tedious and error-prone manual process . With a focus on Java unit testing , we present in this paper a first end-to-end approach where combinatorial testing is supplemented with a model-driven concretization step for abstract test cases . To produce concrete test cases out of abstract test cases , the process requires a context-specific data generator provided by the test engineer , which can be implemented using constraint solving techniques . A code generator is used to produce the working JUnit test script for each concrete test case . a first end-to-end approach where combinatorial testing is supplemented with a model-driven concretization step for abstract test cases is implemented and integrated with the PICT combinatorial testing tool , the Choco-Solver Java library for data generation , and the Eclipse Modeling Framework ( EMF ) for model management . While a first end-to-end approach where combinatorial testing is supplemented with a model-driven concretization step for abstract test cases is currently limited to primitive data types , an initial evaluation on five Java methods shows that the testing effort can be greatly reduced when the combinatorial complexity is high .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Compact Implicit Neural Representations for Plane Wave Images
abstract: Ultrafast Plane-Wave ( PW ) imaging often produces artifacts and shadows that vary with insonification angles . We propose a novel approach using Implicit Neural Representations ( INRs ) to compactly encode multi-planar sequences while preserving crucial orientation-dependent information . To We knowledge , this is the first application of INRs for PW angular interpolation . a novel approach using Implicit Neural Representations ( INRs ) to compactly encode multi-planar sequences while preserving crucial orientation-dependent information employs a Multi-Layer Perceptron ( MLP)-based model with a concise physics-enhanced rendering technique . Quantitative evaluations using SSIM , PSNR , and standard ultrasound metrics , along with qualitative visual assessments , confirm the effectiveness of a novel approach using Implicit Neural Representations ( INRs ) to compactly encode multi-planar sequences while preserving crucial orientation-dependent information . Additionally , a novel approach using Implicit Neural Representations ( INRs ) to compactly encode multi-planar sequences while preserving crucial orientation-dependent information demonstrates significant storage efficiency , with model weights requiring 530 KB compared to 8 MB for directly storing the 75 PW images , achieving a notable compression ratio of approximately 15:1
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Categorial Dependency Grammars extended with barriers (CDGb) yield an Abstract Family of Languages (AFL)
abstract: We consider the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) , as computational grammars for language processing . the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) are a class of categorial grammars defining dependency structures . the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) can be viewed as a formal system , where types are attached to words , combining the classical categorial grammars ’ elimination rules with valency pairing rules that are able to define non-projective ( discontinuous ) dependencies . Whereas the problem of closure under iteration is open for the original version of the family of Categorial Dependency Grammars ( CDG ) , we define “ CDG extended with barriers ” , an extended version of the original version of CDG , that solves the problem of closure under iteration . we provide a rule system and we show that an extended version of the original CDG defines an Abstract Family of Languages ( AFL ) , while preserving advantages of the original version of CDG , in terms of expressivity , parsing and efficiency .

title: Reliable Energy Optimization Strategy for Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicles Considering Fuel Cell and Battery Health
abstract: To enhance the fuel efficiency of fuel cell hybrid electric vehicles ( FCHEVs ) , we propose a hierarchical energy management strategy ( HEMS ) to efficiently allocate power to a hybrid system comprising a fuel cell and a battery . Firstly , the upper-layer supervisor employs a fuzzy faulttolerant control and prediction strategy for the battery and fuel cell management system , ensuring vehicle stability and maintaining a healthy state of charge for both the battery and fuel cell , even during faults . Secondly , in the lower layer , dynamic programming and Pontryagin 's minimum principle are utilized to distribute the necessary power between the fuel cell system and a battery . the lower layer also incorporates an optimized proportional-integral controller for precise tracking of vehicle subsystem set-points . Finally , we compare the economic and dynamic performance of a hybrid system comprising a fuel cell and a battery using a hierarchical energy management strategy ( HEMS ) with other strategies , such as the equivalent consumption minimization strategy and fuzzy logic control strategy . Simulation results demonstrate that a hierarchical energy management strategy ( HEMS ) reduces hydrogen consumption and enhances overall vehicle energy efficiency across all operating conditions , indicating superior economic performance . Additionally , the dynamic performance of a hybrid system comprising a fuel cell and a battery shows significant improvement .

title: A Survey on SPARQL Query Relaxation under the Lens of RDF Reification
abstract: Query relaxation has been proposed to cope with the problem of queries that produce none or insufficient answers . The goal is to modify queries that produce none or insufficient answers to be able to produce alternative results close to those expected in the original query . Existing approaches querying RDF datasets generally relax the SPARQL query constraints based on logical relaxations through RDFS entailment and RDFS ontologies . Techniques also exist that use the similarity of instances based on resource descriptions . Techniques have proved Techniques efficiency . Nevertheless , significant challenges arise for query relaxation techniques in the presence of statement-level annotations , i.e. , RDFS reification . In this survey , we overview SPARQL query relaxation works with a particular focus on issues and challenges posed by representative RDFS reification models , namely , standard reification , named graphs , n-ary relations , singleton properties , and RDF-Star .

title: Learning From Interpretation Transitions with Unknowns
abstract: One major challenge when learning dynamical models from actual time series data consists in tackling partial data . Learning from interpretation transition ( LFIT ) automatically constructs a model of the dynamics of a system from the observation of a system state transitions . In this paper , we extend Learning from interpretation transition ( LFIT ) to learn from transitions between partial states where some variable values are unknown . By modeling the unknown , we achieve an overestimation of the real system regarding both the real system dynamics and variables interactions . we show through theoretical results the correctness of we approaches and our approaches effectiveness through an experimental evaluation on benchmarks from biological literature .

title: Weakly-Supervised End-to-End Framework for Pixel-Wise Description of Micro-Calcifications in Full-Resolution Mammograms
abstract: Breast cancer is the most prevalent cancer among women and catching the early signs of Breast cancer is crucial for increasing patient survival rates . Mammography ( MG ) permits the visualization of the smallest abnormalities , such as micro-calcifications ( MCs ) . micro-calcifications ( MCs ) may be an early sign of Breast cancer , micro-calcifications ( MCs ) appear as white blobs on MG and may have various shapes and different distributions . The risk of malignancy is determined according to these parameters . We propose an end-to-end pipeline structured around a deep convolutional neural network backbone inspired by UNet3 + architecture . an end-to-end pipeline structured around a deep convolutional neural network backbone inspired by UNet3 + architecture aims to classify and segment benign and malignant MCs at several scales . a deep convolutional neural network backbone inspired by UNet3 + architecture is trained in a weakly-supervised end-to-end manner by using negative mammograms augmented with artificial calcifications . Images are represented by a stack of patches , preserving the resolution and keeping MC pixel information . A postprocessing stage based on a set of morphological operations is applied to clean the segmentation masks . A postprocessing stage based on a set of morphological operations is designed with clinical knowledge about MCs and is intended to clear false activations without affecting the detection sensitivity . We tested We pipeline on two public datasets INBreast and Breast Micro-calcifications Dataset and achieved a true positive rate of 0.95 and 0.92 at the level of lesions , and 0.95 and 0.94 image-wise .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: A flexible instrument for robotic assisted minimally invasive esophagectomy
abstract: The paper presents a medical flexible instrument for esophagus stapling that can be integrated in robotic assisted esophagectomy . Starting with several considera-tions required for esophagectomy surgery , the forward kinematic model of a medical flexible instrument for esophagus stapling that can be integrated in robotic assisted esophagectomy is presented , followed by a numerical and a graphical simulation to vali-date the mathematical model of a medical flexible instrument for esophagus stapling that can be integrated in robotic assisted esophagectomy . A 3D printed mockup is devel-oped in order to test the design of a medical flexible instrument for esophagus stapling that can be integrated in robotic assisted esophagectomy while simulating the stapling procedure .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: EMVD dataset: a dataset of extreme vocal distortion techniques used in heavy metal
abstract: In this paper , we introduce the Extreme Metal Vocals Dataset , which comprises a collection of recordings of extreme vocal techniques performed within the realm of heavy metal music . the Extreme Metal Vocals Dataset , which comprises a collection of recordings of extreme vocal techniques performed within the realm of heavy metal music consists of 760 audio excerpts of 1 second to 30 seconds long , totaling about 100 min of audio material , roughly composed of 60 minutes of distorted voices and 40 minutes of clear voice recordings . a collection of recordings of extreme vocal techniques performed within the realm of heavy metal music are from 27 different singers and are provided without accompanying musical instruments or post-processing effects . The distortion taxonomy within the Extreme Metal Vocals Dataset , which comprises a collection of recordings of extreme vocal techniques performed within the realm of heavy metal music encompasses four distinct distortion techniques and three vocal effects , all performed in different pitch ranges . Performance of a state-of-the-art deep learning model is evaluated for two different classification tasks related to vocal techniques , demonstrating the potential of the Extreme Metal Vocals Dataset , which comprises a collection of recordings of extreme vocal techniques performed within the realm of heavy metal music for the audio processing community .

title: A Simple Revolute Joint with Coactivation Principle
abstract: Designing joints with adjustable stiffness is of great interest in humanrobot collaboration tasks . In addition , remote cable actuation allows inertia reduction . Actuating a revolute joint with a pulley and two antagonistic cables is a simple solution , but stiffness modulation is possible only with nonlinear springs or other additional devices . This paper proposes a simple solution to overcome this limitation . a simple solution to overcome this limitation consists in using an eccentric pulley . We show that a simple solution to overcome this limitation allows coactivation as in biological joints , i.e. increasing antagonistic forces increases stiffness .
keywords: antagonist actuation stiffness modulation cable actuated joint eccentric pulley
labels: Augmentation of Human Capabilities in Manufacturing

title: The effect of a minor health shock on labor market outcomes: The case of concussions
abstract: The literature on health shocks finds that minor injuries have only short‐term labor market impacts . However , mild traumatic brain injuries ( mTBIs , commonly referred to as concussions ) may be different as the medical literature highlights that mild traumatic brain injuries ( mTBIs , commonly referred to as concussions ) can have longer‐term health and cognitive effects . Moreover , TBIs are one of the most common causes of disability globally , with the vast majority being mild . Thus , it is important to understand the impact of mTBIs on labor market outcomes . We use administrative data on all medically‐diagnosed mild traumatic brain injuries ( mTBIs ) in New Zealand linked to monthly tax records to examine the labor market effects of a mTBI . We use a comparison group of those who suffer a mTBI at a later date to overcome potential endogeneity issues , and employ a doubly‐robust difference‐in‐differences method . We find that suffering a mTBI has negative labor market effects . Rather than dissipating over time , negative labor market effects grow , representing a decrease in employment of 20 percentage points and earning losses of about a third after 48 months . We results highlight the need for timely diagnosis and treatment to mitigate the effect of mTBIs to reduce economic and social costs .

title: Design of a SM-APID Control for Rigid-Body Transportation Under the Effects of Wind
abstract: Aerial transportation in windy conditions is challenging . In this paper , a pose-tracking task for a rigid body suspended by massless rigid bars and quadrotors , in presence of wind , is considered . To tackle a pose-tracking task for a rigid body suspended by massless rigid bars and quadrotors , in presence of wind , a Sliding Mode Adaptive Proportional-Integral-Derivative ( SM-APID ) control is designed . a Sliding Mode Adaptive Proportional-Integral-Derivative ( SM-APID ) control is tested through simulations and the performances are compared with a PID control .
keywords: sliding mode adaptive proportional-integral-derivative ( sm-apid ) control

title: Advanced fine-tuning procedures to enhance DNN robustness in visual coding for machines
abstract: Video Coding for Machines ( VCM ) is gaining momentum in applications like autonomous driving , industry manufacturing , and surveillance , where the robustness of machine learning algorithms against coding artifacts is one of the key success factors . This work complements the MPEG / JVET standardization efforts in improving the resilience of deep neural network ( DNN)-based machine models against such coding artifacts by proposing the following three advanced fine-tuning procedures for deep neural network ( DNN)-based machine models training : ( 1 ) the progressive increase of the distortion strength as the training proceeds ; ( 2 ) the incorporation of a regularization term in the original loss function to minimize the distance between predictions on compressed and original content ; and ( 3 ) a joint training procedure that combines the proposed two approaches . the proposed two approaches were evaluated against a conventional fine-tuning anchor on two different machine tasks and datasets : image classification on ImageNet and semantic segmentation on Cityscapes . a joint training procedure that combines the proposed two approaches is shown to reduce the training time in two different machine tasks and datasets : image classification on ImageNet and semantic segmentation on Cityscapes and still obtain a 2.4 % coding gain in image classification on ImageNet and 7.4 % in semantic segmentation on Cityscapes , whereas a slight increase in training time can bring up to 9.4 % better coding efficiency for semantic segmentation on Cityscapes . a 2.4 % coding gain in image classification and 7.4 % in semantic segmentation are obtained without any additional inference or encoding time . As the proposed two approaches are standard-compliant , the proposed two approaches offer the potential to have a significant impact on visual coding for machine applications .

title: Battery State of Charge estimation with Kalman filter
abstract: This notebook explores the State of Charge ( SoC ) estimation of a battery using a state observer algorithm , the Kalman filter , or more precisely a state observer algorithm , the Kalman filter nonlinear extension : the extended Kalman filter ( EKF ) . This notebook provides three Python implementations of a state observer algorithm , the Kalman filter : 1 . a step-by-step literate programming version of a state observer algorithm , the Kalman filter , using a sequence of notebook cells , to implement one step of a state observer algorithm , the Kalman filter , 2 . a generic implementation ( all the above steps wrapped in a single function ) and 3 . a compact implementation specialized for SoC estimation with baked-in battery model . This notebook is available as supplementary material of this record or as an interactive version at [ URL ]

title: Enabling Delayed-Answer Auctions for RDF Knowledge Graphs Monetisation
abstract: Traditionally , querying knowledge graphs is free of charge . However , ensuring data and service availability incurs costs to knowledge graphs providers . The Delayed-Answer Auction ( DAA ) model has been proposed to fund the maintenance of knowledge graph endpoints by allowing customers to sponsor entities in the Knowledge Graph so query results that include entities are delivered in priority . However , implementing The Delayed-Answer Auction ( DAA ) model with time-to-first results acceptable for data consumers is challenging because The Delayed-Answer Auction ( DAA ) model requires reordering results according to bid values . In this paper , we present the AuctionKG approach to enable The Delayed-Answer Auction ( DAA ) model with a low impact on query execution performance . the AuctionKG approach to enable DAA with a low impact on query execution performance relies on ( i ) reindexing sponsored entities by bid values to ensure sponsored entities are processed first and ( ii ) Web preemption to ensure delayed answering . Experimental results demonstrate that we approach outperforms a baseline approach to enable The Delayed-Answer Auction ( DAA ) model in terms of time for first results .
keywords: knowledge graphs auction model web preemption monetization

title: WazaGaY: An Innovative Aza-BODIPY-Derived Near-Infrared Fluorescent Probe for Enhanced Tumor Imaging
abstract: Aza-BODIPYs represent a class of fluorophores in which the π-conjugated system is rigidified and stabilized by a boron atom . A promising strategy to enhance Aza-BODIPYs fluorescence properties involves replacing a boron atom with a metal ion . Here , we describe the synthesis and characterization of a water-soluble derivative where the metal is a gallium(III ) ion , termed WazaGaY ( water-soluble aza-GaDIPY ) . Water solubility is ensured by two ammonium substituents , inducing a bathochromic shift and a significant increase in quantum yield compared to that of the dimethylamino analog . The cellular behavior of WazaGaY-1 was observed across different tumor cells . In vivo , the distribution and safety profiles were determined , and tumor uptake was assessed in various tumor types . Following intravenous injection , WazaGaY-1 enabled clear discrimination of tumors engrafted subcutaneously in mice with high tumor-to-muscle ratios ( ranging from 7 to 20 ) , even in the absence of specific conjugation . a water-soluble derivative where the metal is a gallium(III ) ion , termed WazaGaY ( water-soluble aza-GaDIPY ) potential as a contrast agent for fluorescence-guided surgery was confirmed .

title: Propagation of insulator-to-metal transition driven by photoinduced strain waves in a Mott material
abstract: Ultrafast photoexcitation can generate internal compressive stress in Mott insulators that lead to strain waves from free surfaces . strain waves from free surfaces can trigger phase transitions in materials . However , a comprehensive physical picture of the phase transformation dynamics that includes acoustic-scale propagation has not yet been developed . Here we demonstrate that such a strain-wave mechanism drives the ultrafast insulator-to-metal phase transition in granular thin films of the Mott material V2O3 . we time-resolved optical reflectivity and X-ray diffraction measurements reveal that an inverse ferroelastic shear occurs before the ultrafast insulator-to-metal phase transition in granular thin films of the Mott material V2O3 , which propagates in the wake of a compressive strain wave . These dynamics are governed by the domain size and film thickness , respectively . we results clarify the morphological conditions for the ultrafast phase transition that is favoured in granular thin films and hindered in single crystals . The resulting physical picture sheds light on the ultrafast phase transitions in quantum materials and future devices based on Mott insulators .

title: Toward frugal calibration protocols for intelligent programmable meta-imagers
abstract: Programmable meta-imagers based on reconfigurable intelligent surfaces or dynamic metasurface antennas constitute a promising low-cost hardware layer for agile intelligent sensing in applications including security screening . However , Programmable meta-imagers based on reconfigurable intelligent surfaces or dynamic metasurface antennas calibration via near-field scans is tedious , time consuming and not easily compatible with large-scale operations . In this talk , we review recent efforts on physical-model based wave control in metasurface-tunable complex media and discuss physical-model based wave control in metasurface-tunable complex media applications to the frugal calibration of intelligent meta-imagers . Frugal here refers to the number of calibration measurements , the number of the parameters to be stored for later use , and the requirement or not for phase-sensitive measurements .

title: Towards a better understanding of kinetic interactions between microalgae and bacteria : from lab to large-scale high rate algal pond
abstract: High rate algal ponds ( HRAP ) are lowenergy consuming wastewater treatment systems where microalgae provide the oxygen to bacteria for aerobic degradation of organic matter . This thesis propose an integrative approach involving different study systems to investigate interactions within the microalgae-bacteria consortium in high rate algal ponds . The assumption that organic carbon is consumed solely by bacteria in HRAP has been discussed in the literature , raising the hypothesis that heterotrophic growth of microalgae could be relevant and potentially impacting the interactions with bacteria . Considering the complexity of trophic interactions inside the microalgae-bacteria consortium , a study in laboratory photobioreactor in controlled conditions using acetate as the organic carbon source and coupled to a modeling approach was conducted . These tools turned out to be oversimplified , however a study in laboratory photobioreactor in controlled conditions using acetate as the organic carbon source and coupled to a modeling approach revealed that interactions between microalgae and bacteria in high-rate algal ponds would be more complex than a simple synergy relying on O2 and CO2 ex-changes . Besides , microalgae played a major rôle not only in trophic interactions with bacteria but also in disinfection mechanisms through Reactive Oxygen Species production .
labels: Reduction and Treatment of Effluents and Waste

title: Exploring colloidal stability and migration dynamics through integrated photonic into aqueous black carbon dispersion
abstract: This study investigates the migration and stability of colloidal suspensions through quasi-surfacic resonant analyses . The stability of colloidal suspensions is crucial in various industries such as food production , pharmaceutical formulations , and petroleum fields , where ensuring product quality and longevity is essential . This study focuses on black carbon nano-powder dispersed in aqueous solutions , both with and without the incorporation of sodium dodecyl sulfate ( SDS ) surfactant . These solutions result in opaque and densely darkened mixtures , presenting challenges for conventional analytical techniques . To address challenges for conventional analytical techniques , sensors based on integrated photonics are developed . sensors based on integrated photonics consist of organic UV210 Micro-Resonators ( MRs ) shaped and fabricated via photolithography onto oxidized silicon substrates . organic UV210 Micro-Resonators ( MRs ) is then integrated into a test platform where detection and signal processing are performed using a spectrometer and dedicated MATLAB codes to monitor optical measurements in real-time , crucial for investigate the dynamics of colloidal stability . Meticulous experimentations enable exploring the influence of black carbon nano-powder size and concentration on colloidal dispersion stability . The findings highlight the impact of the black carbon concentration on black carbon migration and emphasize sodium dodecyl sulfate ( SDS ) surfactant effect on increasing stability by enhancing the repulsive forces between particles . These conclusions are corroborated with rheological plus zeta potential measurements to provide insights into determining colloidal dispersion stability and migration through optical resonant analysis .

title: Beyond Total Locking: Demonstrating and Measuring Mutual Influence on a RO-Based True Random Number Generator on an FPGA
abstract: Ring oscillator-based true random number generators are of interest because of Ring oscillator-based true random number generators well-known and well-characterised conversion of analog noise into random numbers . The main drawback of using ring oscillators as a source of randomness is ring oscillators tendency to be influenced by ring oscillators environment . In particular , oscillators may lock to another signal at a frequency close to the nominal frequency of the ring , or two or more rings may even lock to each other . This is particularly dangerous for generators with multiple rings , which require the rings to be independent of each other . Furthermore , to reduce the risk of manipulable global noise sources , the rings should have the same structure and topology , making the rings even more vulnerable to locking . The metrics commonly used to quantify the degree of locking have limitations that can lead to erroneous conclusions as to whether a ring is locked or not . This is why we prefer to use the term mutual influence . In this paper , we propose a clear definition of the mutual influence between ring oscillators used as sources of randomness . One of the advantages of a clear definition of the mutual influence between ring oscillators used as sources of randomness is that a clear definition of the mutual influence between ring oscillators used as sources of randomness can easily be extended to include the case of the total locking of rings . Based on a clear definition of the mutual influence between ring oscillators used as sources of randomness , we introduce a new metric to quantify the mutual influence between ring oscillators used as sources of randomness , which evaluates a statistical distance between the current distribution of phase differences and uniform distribution . The experimental results of several FPGA implementations of ring oscillators highlighted the suitability of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test as a metric for detecting mutual influence .
keywords: ring oscillator-based true random number generators

title: Assessing Collaboration Using Multimodal Signals in a Triadic Puzzle-Solving Task in Virtual Reality
abstract: In high-stakes collaborative situations , a decline in collaboration quality can lead to significant adverse events . Although human factors ( HF ) specialists are effective in identifying and resolving collaboration issues , human factors ( HF ) specialists analyses are often case-specific and conducted retrospectively . To address these limitations , our research aims to assess collaboration processes in real-time using multimodal signals collected and analyzed during the activity . In this context , our propose a platform that integrates audio , visual , task logs , and spatial metrics computed along the activity , to provide an assessment of various dimensions of the collaboration process . This approach is applied to a triadic collaborative puzzle-solving task in virtual reality .
keywords: collaboration collaboration indexes multimodal signals cve triads

title: Deep Learning‐Based Blood Abnormalities Detection as a Tool for VEXAS Syndrome Screening
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction VEXAS is a syndrome described in 2020 , caused by mutations of the UBA1 gene , and displaying a large pleomorphic array of clinical and hematological features . Nevertheless , these criteria lack significance to discriminate VEXAS from other inflammatory conditions at the screening step . This work hence first focused on singling out dysplastic features indicative of VEXAS among peripheral blood ( PB ) polymorphonuclears ( PMN ) . A deep learning algorithm is then proposed for automatic detection of dysplastic features indicative of the syndrome among peripheral blood ( PB ) polymorphonuclears ( PMN ) . Methods A multicentric dataset , comprising 9514 annotated PMN images was gathered , including UBA1 mutated VEXAS ( n = 25 ) , UBA1 wildtype myelodysplastic ( n = 14 ) , and UBA1 wildtype cytopenic patients ( n = 25 ) . Statistical analysis on a subset of patients was performed to screen for significant abnormalities . Detection of these features on PB was then automated with a convolutional neural network ( CNN ) for multilabel classification . Results Significant differences were observed in the proportions of PMNs with pseudo‐Pelger , nuclear spikes , vacuoles , and hypogranularity between patients with VEXAS and both cytopenic and myelodysplastic controls . Automatic detection of PMNs with pseudo‐Pelger , nuclear spikes , vacuoles , and hypogranularity yielded AUCs in the range [ 0.85–0.97 ] and a F1‐score of 0.70 on the test set . A VEXAS screening score was proposed , leveraging the model outputs and predicting the the UBA1 gene mutational status with 0.82 sensitivity and 0.71 specificity on the test patients . Conclusion This work suggests that computer‐assisted analysis of PB smears , focusing on suspected VEXAS cases , can provide valuable insights for determining which patients should undergo molecular testing . The presented deep learning approach can help hematologists direct hematologists suspicions before initiating further analyses .

title: Deepfake Detection Using Spatiotemporal Transformer
abstract: Recent advances in generative models and the availability of large-scale benchmarks have made deepfake video generation and manipulation easier . Nowadays , the number of new hyper-realistic deepfake videos used for negative purposes is dramatically increasing , thus creating the need for effective deepfake detection methods . Although many existing deepfake detection approaches , particularly CNN-based methods , show promising results , many existing deepfake detection approaches , particularly CNN-based methods suffer from several drawbacks . In general , poor generalization results have been obtained under unseen / new deepfake generation methods . The crucial reason for the above defect is that CNN-based methods focus on the local spatial artifacts , which are unique for every manipulation method . Therefore , it is hard to learn the general forgery traces of different manipulation methods without considering the dependencies that extend beyond the local receptive field . To address this problem , this article proposes a framework that combines Convolutional Neural Network ( CNN ) with Vision Transformer ( ViT ) to improve detection accuracy and enhance generalizability . Our method , named HCiT , exploits the advantages of CNNs to extract meaningful local features , as well as Vision Transformer ( ViT ) self-attention mechanism to learn discriminative global contextual dependencies in a frame-level image explicitly . In a framework that combines Convolutional Neural Network ( CNN ) with Vision Transformer ( ViT ) to improve detection accuracy and enhance generalizability , the high-level feature maps extracted from Convolutional Neural Network ( CNN ) are fed into the Vision Transformer ( ViT ) model that determines whether a specific video is fake or real . Experiments were performed on Faceforensics++ , DeepFake Detection Challenge preview , Celeb datasets , and the results show that Our method , named HCiT significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art methods . In addition , Our method , named HCiT shows a great capacity for generalization on datasets covering various techniques of deepfake generation . The source code is available at : [ URL ]

title: Pectin–Chitosan Hydrogel Beads for Delivery of Functional Food Ingredients
abstract: A common challenge in hydrogel-based delivery systems is the premature release of low molecular weight encapsulates through diffusion or swelling and reduced cell viability caused by the low pH in gastric conditions . A second biopolymer , such as chitosan , can be incorporated to overcome A common challenge in hydrogel-based delivery systems . chitosan is usually associated with colonic drug delivery systems . We intended to formulate chitosan-coated pectin beads for use in delaying premature release of the encapsulate under gastric conditions but allowing release through disintegration under intestinal conditions . release through disintegration under intestinal conditions is of utmost importance in delivering most functional food ingredients . Therefore , this study investigated the impact of formulation and process conditions on the size , sphericity , and dissolution behavior of chitosan-coated hydrogel beads prepared by interfacial coacervation . The size and sphericity of chitosan-coated hydrogel beads prepared by interfacial coacervation depend on the formulation and range from approximately 3 to 5 mm and 0.82 to 0.95 , respectively . Process conditions during electro-dripping may be modulated to tailor bead size . Depending on the voltage , bead size ranged from 1.5 to 4 mm . Confocal laser scanning microscopy and scanning electron microscopy confirmed chitosan shell formation around the pectin bead . chitosan-coated hydrogel beads prepared by interfacial coacervation maintained chitosan-coated hydrogel beads prepared by interfacial coacervation size and shape in simulated gastric fluid but experienced structural damage in simulated intestinal fluid . Therefore , chitosan-coated hydrogel beads prepared by interfacial coacervation represent a novel delivery system for functional food ingredients .

title: Experimental Studies of Advanced/Hybrid Heat Recovery Systems applied to Industrial Appliances
abstract: The study of sustainable energy solutions and effective waste heat management is crucial in the present world , as consumption of energy continues in increasing concerns about environmental consequences . Given the predicted increase in global energy consumption , there is an urgent need for novel methods of energy generation and the recovery of waste heat . This PhD project aimed to tackle this problem by exploring the use of diverse heat recovery technologies , in combination with different energy sources , to enhance industrial sustainability and environmental stewardship . This PhD project investigated the potential of hybrid systems to improve energy efficiency and decrease carbon emissions by conducting experimental tests , thermal modeling , and economic analysis . This PhD project intended to facilitate the adoption of sustainable energy practices in industrial settings by incorporating various heat recovery sources and technologies , such as thermoelectric generators and heat exchangers . This PhD project results and suggestions provided useful insights into optimizing waste heat recovery systems . However , This PhD project serves as a framework for future research in the discipline of energy management and the integration of renewable energy .

title: INVESTIGATION OF MECHANICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF LIGHTWEIGHT CONCRETE USING ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY LIGHTWEIGHT AGGREGATES
abstract: This study aims to investigate the mechanical properties of lightweight concrete using lightweight aggregate and analyze the impact of silica fume on enhancing lightweight concrete using lightweight aggregate compressive strength . The main objective of This study was to improve the value of industrial waste by utilizing GGBFS as a substitute for cement . Four alternative compositions have been used to produce samples of lightweight concrete . The coarse aggregate is substituted with 100 % lightweight expanded clay aggregate , whereas the fine aggregates are replaced with 100 % vermiculite and 100 % polystyrene bead waste . A combination of 20 % GGBFS and 10 % silica fume is employed for cement replacement . The materials used throughout This study consist of aluminum powder and superplasticizer . The workability , compressive strength , tensile strength , and specific gravity of concrete will be determined by testing . The waster curing will be carried out on cylindrical concrete specimens 200 mm in height and 100 mm in diameter . Experimental results showed that the concrete mixture consisting of 80 % cement and 20 % GGBFS as binders , along with lightweight expanded clay aggregate as coarse aggregate and vermiculite as the fine aggregate , exhibits the highest compressive strength compared to other lightweight concrete mixtures .

title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Chronic Lung Allograft Dysfunction
abstract: Background : Chronic respiratory diseases are among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide with 3.3 million deaths each year . For patients with end-stage lung disease , the only viable option is lung transplantation ( LT ) , but graft survival remains limited with only 63 % survival at 5 years post-transplantation . The greatest limitation to long-term survival is the development of chronic lung allograft dysfunction ( CLAD ) which affects arounds 50 % of recipients after 5 years . There is an essential need for better understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in the CLAD phenotype ’s pathophysiology . Methods : We performed the first genome-wide association study GWAS investigating genetic factors associated with CLAD . CLAD is defined by a > = 20 % decline in measured forced expiratory volume from the baseline level ( 3 months after transplant in the absence of infection or another identifiable cause ) . We genotyped a subset of 392 LT donor-recipient pairs from the COLT multicentric cohort ( Cohort in Lung Transplantation ) using the Affymetrix Axiom PRMA microarray ( 900,000 SNPs ) . the COLT multicentric cohort ( Cohort in Lung Transplantation ) represents an accurate snapshot of the COLT multicentric cohort ( Cohort in Lung Transplantation ) as no variable ( e.g. age , sex , initial respiratory disease , survival rate ) significantly diverged from the global cohort ( p>0.05 ) . After quality controls and SNP imputation , We tested 7 million SNPs for association with CLAD using multivariate logistic regression models corrected for age , sex and genetic ancestry . Results : We did not observe any significant association between the donors ’ genotypes and the CLAD development . However , We tested 54 CLAD ( BOS=34 , RAS=9 and mixte=11 ) against 160 stable recipients and We identified four SNPs significantly associated with CLAD in European recipients ( p<5x10-8) . Interestingly , We found a signal in a gene encoding a protein previously associated with the risk for bronchopulmonary dysplasia . Recipients with CLAD exhibited a lower allelic frequency ( 34 % ) for a gene encoding a protein previously associated with the risk for bronchopulmonary dysplasia than recipients without CLAD ( 66 % ) , suggesting a protective role for a gene encoding a protein previously associated with the risk for bronchopulmonary dysplasia against the development of CLAD . Conclusions : Here , We unveiled the first GWAS conducted in lung transplantation , displaying biologically relevant results from the recipient ’s genome . We will next jointly investigate the donor and recipient ’s genomes to assess HLA and non-HLA mismatches that might contribute to CLAD . Further investigations into the functional implications of these genetic variants could provide valuable insights into pathogenesis and potential therapeutic targets for CLAD .
keywords: genome wide association study lung transplantation chronic lung allograft dysfunction immunogenetics

title: Upper-Limb and Low-Back Load Analysis in Workers Performing an Actual Industrial Use-Case with and without a Dual-Arm Collaborative Robot
abstract: In the Industry 4.0 scenario , human – robot collaboration ( HRC ) plays a key role in factories to reduce costs , increase production , and help aged and/or sick workers maintain aged and/or sick workers job . The approaches of the ISO 11228 series commonly used for biomechanical risk assessments can not be applied in Industry 4.0 , as The approaches of the ISO 11228 series commonly used for biomechanical risk assessments do not involve interactions between workers and HRC technologies . The use of wearable sensor networks and software for biomechanical risk assessments could help us develop a more reliable idea about the effectiveness of collaborative robots ( coBots ) in reducing the biomechanical load for workers . The aim of the present study was to investigate some biomechanical parameters with the 3D Static Strength Prediction Program ( 3DSSPP ) software v.7.1.3 , on workers executing a practical manual material-handling task , by comparing a dual-arm coBot-assisted scenario with a no-coBot scenario . In the present study , we calculated the mean and the standard deviation ( SD ) values from eleven participants for some 3DSSPP parameters . we considered the following parameters : the percentage of maximum voluntary contraction ( % MVC ) , the maximum allowed static exertion time ( MaxST ) , the low-back spine compression forces at the L4 / L5 level ( L4Ort ) , and the strength percent capable value ( SPC ) . The advantages of introducing the coBot , according to we statistics , concerned trunk flexion ( SPC from 85.8 % without coBot to 95.2 % ; % MVC from 63.5 % without coBot to 43.4 % ; MaxST from 33.9 s without coBot to 86.2 s ) , left shoulder abdo-adduction ( % MVC from 46.1 % without coBot to 32.6 % ; MaxST from 32.7 s without coBot to 65 s ) , and right shoulder abdo-adduction ( % MVC from 43.9 % without coBot to 30.0 % ; MaxST from 37.2 s without coBot to 70.7 s ) in Phase 1 , and right shoulder humeral rotation ( % MVC from 68.4 % without coBot to 7.4 % ; MaxST from 873.0 s without coBot to 125.2 s ) , right shoulder abdo-adduction ( % MVC from 31.0 % without coBot to 18.3 % ; MaxST from 60.3 s without coBot to 183.6 s ) , and right wrist flexion / extension rotation ( % MVC from 50.2 % without coBot to 3.0 % ; MaxST from 58.8 s without coBot to 1200.0 s ) in Phase 2 . Moreover , Phase 3 , which consisted of another manual handling task , would be removed by using a coBot . In summary , using a coBot in this industrial scenario would reduce the biomechanical risk for workers , particularly for the trunk , both shoulders , and the right wrist . Finally , the 3DSSPP software could be an easy , fast , and costless tool for biomechanical risk assessments in an Industry 4.0 scenario where ISO 11228 series can not be applied ; the 3DSSPP software could be used by occupational medicine physicians and health and safety technicians , and could also help employers to justify a long-term investment .
keywords: mean and standard deviation ( sd ) values
