title: Dual-Band, Dual-Polarized Continuous Transverse Stub Antenna for SatCom Applications
abstract: A dual-band , dual-polarized , and low-profile Continuous Transverse Stub ( CTS ) antenna array is presented at K / Ka-band for for satellite communications ( SatCom ) . A dual-band , dual-polarized , and low-profile Continuous Transverse Stub ( CTS ) antenna array is designed to cover the down-link ( 17.7-20.2 GHz ) and the up-link ( 27.5-30 GHz ) bands of the satellite communications ( SatCom link . The CTS aperture comprises 8 long slots fed in parallel by a corrugated parallel plate waveguide beam forming network which supports the propagation of two orthogonal modes . A dual-band , dual-polarized , and low-profile Continuous Transverse Stub ( CTS ) antenna array radiates a dual-linear polarization by using two orthogonal modes . Full-wave results for A dual-band , dual-polarized , and low-profile Continuous Transverse Stub ( CTS ) antenna array are validated by a prototype and measurements results for the radiation patterns and input reflection coefficient .

title: Full-Metal High Gain Antenna for SatCom Applications at K/Ka Band
abstract: This communication introduces a high-gain antenna designed for satellite communications ( SatCom ) in the K / Ka band , covering the frequency range 17–31 GHz . The antennas based on a long slot array , fed by a corporate feed network ( CFN ) . a corporate feed network ( CFN ) is tapered to reduce sidelobe levels ( SLL ) in the radiating plane orthogonal to the long slots across the frequency range 17–31 GHz ( <-23 dB ) . Additionally , a pillbox coupler serves as a line source generator to illuminate a corporate feed network ( CFN ) , featuring an integrated parabolic reflector illuminated by a displaceable H-plane horn in a pillbox coupler focal plane . a high-gain antenna designed for satellite communications ( SatCom ) in the K / Ka band , covering the frequency range 17–31 GHz is fabricated using computer numerically controlled ( CNC ) milling technology in Aluminum to minimize losses . The total size of a high-gain antenna designed for satellite communications ( SatCom ) in the K / Ka band , covering the frequency range 17–31 GHz is 44.5×33.1×6.2 λ30 with λ0 the free space wavelength at 31 GHz . a high-gain antenna designed for satellite communications ( SatCom ) in the K / Ka band , covering the frequency range 17–31 GHz exhibits a minimum measured realized gain of 34.3 dBi at 17 GHz . a high-gain antenna designed for satellite communications ( SatCom ) in the K / Ka band , covering the frequency range 17–31 GHz can steer a high-gain antenna designed for satellite communications ( SatCom ) in the K / Ka band , covering the frequency range 17–31 GHz main beam along the slot plane to cover a field of view exceeding 50 ° in elevation by displacing a displaceable H-plane horn in the focal plane of a pillbox coupler .

title: GaP WGM microdisks for second order nonlinear optics
abstract: III-V semiconductor whispering gallery mode ( WGM ) microdisks have many assets for second order nonlinear optics . III-V semiconductor whispering gallery mode ( WGM ) microdisks large nonlinear susceptibility combined with III-V semiconductor whispering gallery mode ( WGM ) microdisks high refractive index allows us to consider low power optical function based on nonlinear effects in a broad spectral range . In this paper , we will review we recent results on WGM GaP microdisks . we will present we experimental results on Q-factor characterization and second harmonic generation measurements under modal 4 phase matching . we will also review some phase-matching schemes propositions based on antiphase boundary engineering . Finally , we will discuss other device configurations based on coupled microdisks .

title: Reversible Light‐Triggered Stretching of Small‐Molecule Photochromic Organic Nanoparticles
abstract: Functional organic nanomaterials are nowadays largely spread in the field of nanomedicine . In situ modulation of Functional organic nanomaterials morphology is thus expected to considerably impact Functional organic nanomaterials interactions with the surroundings . In this context , photoswitchable nanoparticles that are manufactured , amenable to extensive disassembling upon illumination in the visible , and reversible reshaping under UV exposure . Such reversibility turns to be strongly impaired for photochromic nanoparticles in close contact with a substrate . In situ atomic force microscopy investigations at the nanoscale actually reveal progressive disintegration of the organic nanoparticles under successive UV – vis cycles of irradiation , in the absence of intrinsic elastic forces . These results point out the dramatic interactions exerted by surfaces on the cohesion of non‐covalently bonded organic nanoparticles . These results invite to harness such systems , often used as biomarkers , to also serve as photoactivatable drug delivery nanocarriers .

title: Robust nonsingular predefined-time terminal sliding mode control for perturbed chains of integrators
abstract: This paper provides a nonsingular predefined-time terminal sliding mode control scheme for perturbed chains of integrators . Based on the linear delayed feedback technique , a class of nonsingular smooth prescribed-time sliding surfaces with artificial time-delays is constructed , and a nonsingular predefined-time terminal sliding mode control scheme for perturbed chains of integrators can achieve predefined-time control for perturbed chains of integrators with matched and mismatched disturbances . Espe-cially , for double integrators , an initial-condition-based sufficient condition is provided to preserve the prescribed-time stability . Finally , several simulation results illustrate the performance of a nonsingular predefined-time terminal sliding mode control scheme for perturbed chains of integrators .

title: Toward integrating reuse approach within scrum process
abstract: Agile Software Development and Reuse-Driven Software Engineering represent established methodologies for enhancing software process efficiency . However , a key challenge in merging Agile Software Development and Reuse-Driven Software Engineering arises from the predominant dependence on tacit knowledge in Agile Software Development . Software development in general and agile development in particular involves successive activities from analysis and design to development and testing . Software development in general and agile development in particular clearly joins the idea of the business process . Regardless of the software development life-cycle model , reusable artifacts can be used in multiple phases of the software development life-cycle model , including analysis , requirements , designs , implementations , testing , etc . In this work , we have integrated reuse into scrum process activities . The idea is to allow the Scrum team to use the reusable artifacts , from the same project or from other projects , classified in a repository and to be guided in the Scrum team choice by the evaluation . To confirm the effectiveness of we proposed method , we conducted experiments within a project aimed at creating an intelligent system to support a COVID-19 crisis unit .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Quality Assessment of Light Field Images
abstract: Light Field Image ( LFI ) has garnered remarkable interest and fascination due to Light Field Image ( LFI ) burgeoning significance in immersive applications . Since LFIs may be distorted at various stages from acquisition to visualization , Light Field Image Quality Assessment ( LFIQA ) is vitally important to monitor the potential impairments of LFIs quality . The first contribution ( Chapter 3 ) of this work focuses on developing two handcrafted feature-based No-Reference ( NR ) LFIQA metrics , in which texture information and wavelet information are exploited for quality evaluation . Then in the second part ( Chapter 4 ) , we explore the potential of combining deep learning technology with the quality assessment of LFIs , and propose four deep learning-based LFIQA metrics according to different LFIs characteristics , including three NR metrics and one Full-Reference ( FR ) metric . In the last part ( Chapter 5 ) , we conduct subjective experiments and propose a novel standard LFIQA database . Moreover , a benchmark of numerous state-of-the-art objective LFIQA metrics on a novel standard LFIQA database is provided .

title: Performance-cost trade-offs in service orchestration for edge computing
abstract: Low latencies connections and decentralized servers are currently showcasing a new potential for distributed computing . By moving away from traditional centralized cloud models and toward edge computing , which allows for more autonomy and decision-making at the network 's edge , almost any physical thing can be turned into an Internet of Things ( IoT ) device that can elaborate on data it senses from it environment . In this context , service management and adaptation routines in a highly dynamic and geographically distributed federation depends on a large number of factors ranging from performance to cost and the fluctuation of the data quality . This paper presents mechanisms for monitoring resources at the edge in real-time , orchestrating service provisioning , performing data-driven decisions on behalf of applications , adapting service locations , and coordinating sensing tasks . This paper focuses on autoscaling of containers , service placement and distributed sensing , while considering utility metrics to help achieve a fluid workload in Kubernetes clusters .

title: Machine-Checked Categorical Diagrammatic Reasoning
abstract: This paper describes a formal proof library , developed using the Coq proof assistant , designed to assist users in writing correct diagrammatic proofs , for 1-categories . a formal proof library , developed using the Coq proof assistant , designed to assist users in writing correct diagrammatic proofs , for 1-categories proposes a deep-embedded , domain-specific formal language , which features dedicated proof commands to automate the synthesis , and the verification , of the technical parts often eluded in the literature .

title: Analysis of the effects of temporary outdoor access during the fattening phase on pig welfare, health and performance
abstract: Currently in the European Union , less than 1 % of pigs are raised with access to outdoor areas . In the PANORAMA project , we analysed the effects of giving pigs temporary access to a pasture during the fattening phase on pigs welfare , health and performance . Indeed , temporary access appears as a valuable option for farmers who can give their animals limited outdoor access , in order to improve their animals welfare , particularly during the fattening phase . In this context , we studied 150 pigs in three batches , reared in a conventional barn without any outdoor access ( O-) ( 75 males and 75 females ) and 150 pigs reared with access to a pasture ( O+ ) twice a week , for 4 hours in mornings ( 75 males and 75 females ) , from D76 to D150 . Pigs were regularly weighed ( D70 , D133 and D150 ) . we observed the behaviour of pigs ( feeding , resting , exploring , social behaviours … ) by scan sampling , for 2h in the morning ( inside vs outside ) , and 2h in the afternoon ( inside for both groups ) , during the first two weeks , week D104 to D107 and the last week . To evaluate the stress experienced by pigs , we scored body lesions and measured the level of salivary cortisol ( D104 and D150 ) . Also , we quantified IgA level in saliva at D150 , since IgA level in saliva was shown to increase with positive emotions . Linear mixed effects models were used to evaluate the effect of outdoor access on these variables . Data obtained on two batches ( 100 O-and 100 O+ ) showed almost no effect of the sex on the variables studied . As expected , pigs with outdoor access ( O+ ) spent less time resting and more time exploring outside than control pigs did inside . Also , during the afternoon , inside , O+ pigs spent significantly more time resting and eating than O-pigs did . Interestingly , both groups exhibited similar growth performance until slaughter . At the end of the fattening phase ( D150 ) , O+ pigs showed significantly less severe body injuries than the O-pigs did . At D104 and D150 , O+ had significantly lower salivary cortisol levels than control pigs did . Finally , at D150 , the level of salivary IgA was significantly lower for O+ pigs . Altogether , studied should provide new knowledge for a better understanding of the consequences of outdoor access on pigs ’ welfare , health and performance .

title: Development of an autonomous system based on piezoresistive sensors for quantitative sports movement
abstract: Human motion analysis plays a vital role in numerous fields , enabling , for instance , the understanding of the nuances of physical performance or biomechanics . The data and information derived from Human motion analysis can enhance performance , prevent injuries , or optimize rehabilitation . Various systems exist , such as video , but Various systems implementation and data processing pose limitations . One solution is to develop integrated wearable systems offering discreet and continuous activity tracking . One challenge lies in the materials and instrumentation domain , where the objective is to develop wearable and autonomous systems that meet the requisite specifications . This thesis work focuses on the design of piezoresistive transducers for the development of energy-autonomous systems , such as an insole for estimating plantar force and a garment for determining joint angles . A viscoelastic model of the piezoresistive transducer has been established , which enables the estimation of plantar force by inversion . Comparative experiments have been conducted with commercial systems , including a force platform .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: $\partial$ is for Dialectica
abstract: Automatic Differentiation is the study of the efficient computation of differentials . While the first automatic differentiation algorithms are concomitant with the birth of computer science , the specific backpropagation algorithm has been brought to a modern light by the specific backpropagation algorithm application to neural networks . This work unveils a surprising connection between the specific backpropagation algorithm and Gödel 's Dialectica interpretation , a logical translation that realizes semi-classical axioms . a surprising connection between backpropagation and Gödel 's Dialectica interpretation , a logical translation that realizes semi-classical axioms is exploited through different logical settings . In particular , we show that the computational interpretation of Gödel 's Dialectica interpretation , a logical translation that realizes semi-classical axioms translates to the differential λ-calculus and that Differential Linear Logic subsumes the logical interpretation of Gödel 's Dialectica interpretation , a logical translation that realizes semi-classical axioms .

title: Automated Proof Tactics for Model Transformation
abstract: When model-driven engineering is applied to critical systems , proving the correctness of model transformations ( MT ) assumes great importance . For instance , users may want a guarantee that the transformation does not produce models that break a critical post-condition , or that the transformation preserves the semantics of the transformed model . Methods for automatic proof of MT correctness have shown Methods for automatic proof of MT correctness effectiveness for simple transformations and/or correctness properties . However , arbitrarily complex transformations and properties may require interactive theorem proving , which is a very costly activity . In this paper , we aim at simplifying the development of interactive proofs for MTs written in the CoqTL transformation language by providing a set of automated proof tactics for MT certification . automated proof tactics for MT certification encode reasoning patterns that depend only on the semantics of the CoqTL engine , hence automated proof tactics for MT certification are generally applicable to proofs on any CoqTL transformation . Each tactic is associated with a direction ( forward if Each tactic derives facts about the target model given facts on the source model , backward if Each tactic derives facts on the source model given facts on the target model ) and a subject ( element or link , respectively if Each tactic derives facts on elements or links ) . automated proof tactics for MT certification are implemented as a set of lemmas and tactics for the CoqTL interactive theorem prover . In we experimentation , we show that automated proof tactics for MT certification allow us to write shorter and easier proofs . The source code for CoqTL and we tactics is provided at [ URL ]
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Rammed Earth Building: Contribution of Moisture Transfer on Indoor Comfort
abstract: To date , only a few scientific articles have quantified by numerical calculation the impact that the hygroscopic character of raw earth , often cited as one of the main advantages of raw earth , can have on the comfort of the building 's occupants . To better quantify this effect , simulations of a building with rammed earth walls subjected to realistic meteorological conditions are performed on the EnergyPlus TM building energy simulation software and the EnergyPlus TM building energy simulation software coupled hygrothermal transfer module : HAMT . The simulations output parameters likely to be impacted by moisture transfer and moisture transfer coupling with heat transfer are studied : temperatures , humidity , and a standardised comfort indicator : the PMV ( Predicted Mean Vote ) . In particular , the evolutions of the previously mentioned outputs are compared through a parametric study . The varying input parameter studied is the type of possible transfer between earthen walls and earthen walls surroundings . We examine two transfer possibilities : hygrothermal coupled transfers , involving thermal and hydric interactions between walls and walls surroundings , and pure heat transfers with disabled hydric interactions . two transfer possibilities : hygrothermal coupled transfers , involving thermal and hydric interactions between walls and their surroundings employ identical models and resolution algorithms . Pure heat transfer represents hygrothermal transfer devoid of water exchange coefficients . a parametric study is conducted by varying the number of earthen walls able to have hygrothermal exchanges with earthen walls surroundings . This paper concludes that consideration of moisture transfer and moisture transfer coupling with heat transfer between earthen walls and earthen walls surroundings has little effect on temperatures and PMV , but contributes significantly to the regulation of indoor relative humidity .

title: Upon This Quote I Will Build My Church Thesis
abstract: The internal Church thesis ( CT ) is a logical principle stating that one can associate to any function f : ℕ → ℕ a concrete code , in some Turing-complete language , that computes f. While the compatibility of The internal Church thesis ( CT ) in simpler systems has been long known , The internal Church thesis ( CT ) compatibility with dependent type theory is still an open question . In this paper , we answer an open question positively . we define “ MLTT ” , a type theory extending MLTT with quote operators in which The internal Church thesis ( CT ) is derivable . we furthermore prove that MLTT is consistent , strongly normalizing and enjoys canonicity using a rather standard logical relation model . All the results in this paper have been mechanized in Coq .

title: Preliminary Results of Interlaboratory Tests on Hygrothermal Properties of CEB
abstract: Determining the hygrothermal properties of earth-based building materials on a material scale is a major challenge in order to highlight and guarantee earth-based building materials performance . This data is also essential to feed models at wall and building scales for prediction and optimization of models at wall and building scales contribution to energy consumption and user ’s comfort . In the context of the activities of the French National Project on earth construction ( PN Terre ) , one round robin campaign has been launched to measure the following hygrothermal properties of compressed earth bricks ( CEB ): dry density , thermal conductivity , specific heat capacity , ad-and desorption isotherms and water vapor permeability . The analysis of the preliminary results from six participating laboratories in France highlighted the main sources of discrepancy and of uncertainties . First recommentions are proposed to improve the accuracy of the measurements .

title: Multi‐objective assessment of the water‐energy‐environment‐food nexus involving a life cycle assessment approach
abstract: This work addresses the multi-objective design of water , energy and food supply systems in isolated rural communities using local resources . The approach used considers objective functions based on life cycle analysis such as water and carbon footprint , as well as economic performance considering the application and integration of normalized metrics to address the water-energy-environment-food nexus . The results show that it is possible to build robust and accessible metrics for the analysis of problems with various design objective functions in decision-making environments . The optimization problem considers decision variables associated with the sizing of units such as photovoltaic panels , wind turbines , thermal and electrical energy storage , wood-fired boilers and the integration of food production systems involving aquaculture and local corn production . Water management is associated with domestic activities and crop irrigation .
keywords: water, energy and food supply systems

title: Off-Grid Time-Delay Estimation for Ground Penetrating Radar: A Nested Sampling Based Block Sparse Representation Method
abstract: In this paper , we propose a nested sampling based off-grid block sparse representation method ( Nested-OGBSR ) for time-delay estimation ( TDE ) of coherent ground penetrating radar ( GPR ) backscattered echoes . Nested sampling strategy is taken to reduce the sampling rate and complexity burden . The off-grid data model is adopted to eliminate the effect of basis mismatch caused by the predefined grids in sparse repre-sentation ( SR ) and thus improve the estimation accuracy . The non-circularity of GPR signals is also utilized to enhance the temporal resolution of BSR . Numerical results are provided to show the superiority of a nested sampling based off-grid block sparse representation method ( Nested-OGBSR ) in terms of estimation accuracy , temporal resolution and computational complexity .
keywords: off grid block sparse representation ogbsr

title: Self-Supervised Joint SAR Image Compression and Despeckling
abstract: SAR image compression is essential for managing the large amounts of data generated by Synthetic Aperture Radar ( SAR ) systems , ensuring efficient storage , transmission and processing without compromising essential information . Various techniques , including wavelet-based methods and predictive coding , are commonly used to achieve an optimal balance between compression ratio and image quality . Autoencoders within a deep learning framework have been successfully applied to SAR image compression ; however , the simultaneous challenge of compression and speckle reduction remains unsolved due to the lack of ground truth . This study addresses this gap by proposing a self-supervised framework for SAR speckle reduction and extending a self-supervised framework for SAR speckle reduction application to the joint problem of SAR image compression . The developed network learns a representation of SAR data that not only facilitates effective speckle reduction , but also enables image compression . We compare We method with state-of-the-art despeckling and compression algorithms and show that we can perform both tasks together with excellent performance .

title: Alpine Snowpack Permittivity Retrieval in Forward-Looking Bistatic Radar (Bizona) Configuration
abstract: This paper presents a method for multi-layered snowpack vertical profile characterization using a low complexity portable MIMO bistatic radar system . An iterative procedure based on calculating the electromagnetic distance which takes into account the refractive index of each layer is proposed . An iterative procedure based on calculating the electromagnetic distance which takes into account the refractive index of each layer estimates the refractive index from the snowpack top to the bottom layers . Furthermore , experimental radar measurements performed at the Col de Porte , in the french Alps , is backed up by in-situ stratigraphic samplings provided by Météo France and which are used as a reference . The obtained results are anaylsed and discussed .

title: Managing Organizational Transformation Within PLM Approach Between Theory And Practice
abstract: Organizational and digital transformation projects are highly challenging and the current practices against these challenges are still limited in terms of efficiency and effectiveness . are is leading to the need of innovative decision supports to help managers conducting such strategies in optimal way . As a first step towards this perspective , this paper summarizes the results of an initial exploratory phase , involving a study of the theoretical foundations and current consulting practices of organizational transformation with PLM approach , in order to identify current limitations .
keywords: organizational transformation co evolution plm approach consulting practices
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Robust DOA Estimation in Co-prime Arrays with Impulsive Noise using EBNC-PFLOM Method
abstract: Recently , direction-of-arrival ( DOA ) estimation in impul-sive noise scenarios has been extensively investigated in the field of co-prime array signal processing . This paper pro-poses a combined enhanced bounded nonlinear covariance and phased fractional low-order moment ( EBNC-PFLOM ) method , which incorporates the advantages of both EBNC and PFLOM and mitigates the impulsive noise by construct-ing the equivalent data covariance matrix of the received signals . Furthermore , when dealing with a limited number of input signals , a combined enhanced bounded nonlinear covariance and phased fractional low-order moment ( EBNC-PFLOM ) method , which incorporates the advantages of both EBNC and PFLOM is capable of directly estimating input signals DOA without spatial smoothing . Sim-ulation results show that a combined enhanced bounded nonlinear covariance and phased fractional low-order moment ( EBNC-PFLOM ) method , which incorporates the advantages of both EBNC and PFLOM outperforms the recently reported methods .
keywords: phased fractional low-order moment ( ebnc-pflom ) method

title: Swot Cal/Val Campaign Based on the Swalis Airborne Sensor. Comparaison of σ0 over the Mont-Saint Michel Bay and over the Gondrexange/Stoke Ponds
abstract: This paper presents the first comparisons of backscattering coefficients σ 0 between acquisitions from the SWALIS ( Still WAter Low Incidence Scattering ) airborne sensor and the space mission SWOT ( Surface Water and Ocean Topography ) over the Mont Saint-Michel ( MSM ) bay and over the Gondrexange and Stoke ponds . The the Mont Saint-Michel ( MSM ) bay area is chosen both as a calibration / validation area for the SWOT mission and as a perfect area for analyzing the backscattering of specific sand areas .

title: Advanced Statistical Modelling of Polarimetric SAR Data for Land Cover Change Detection Analysis
abstract: In this paper , we will present a determinant ratio test ( DRT ) statistic to measure the similarity of two covariance matrices for unsupervised change detection in polarimetric radar images . The multilook complex covariance matrix is assumed to follow a scaled complex Wishart distribution . In doing so , the distribution of a determinant ratio test ( DRT ) statistic to measure the similarity of two covariance matrices for unsupervised change detection in polarimetric radar images is analytically derived which is exactly Wilks ’s lambda of the second kind distribution , with density expressed in terms of Meijer G-functions . Due to the distribution of the DRT statistic , the constant false alarm rate ( CFAR ) algorithm is derived in order to achieve the required performance . More specifically , a threshold is provided by the constant false alarm rate ( CFAR ) algorithm to apply to a determinant ratio test ( DRT ) statistic to measure the similarity of two covariance matrices for unsupervised change detection in polarimetric radar images producing a binary change map . Finally , simulated and real multilook polarimetric radar data are employed to assess the performance of the method and is compared with the Hotelling – Lawley trace ( HLT ) statistic .
keywords: wilks’s lambda of the second kind distribution
constant false alarm rate ( cfar ) algorithm

title: Pavement Inspection and Characterization Using a Constant Offset Sliding Bistatic GB-SAR System and High-Resolution Imaging Techniques
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach in pavement inspection by applying high-resolution imaging techniques onto a Constant Offset Sliding Bistatic Ground-Based Synthetic Aperture Radar system operated in forward-scattering mode . The performance of this configuration , known for its minimal complexity , is significantly improved by incorporating the spectral analysis method . The integration enhances vertical discrimination and proves effective in complex scenarios with fewer actual sources than anticipated . a novel approach in pavement inspection represents a alternative solution in non-destructive road infrastructure analysis , offering a powerful tool for precise pavement condition monitoring .
keywords: sliding bistatic ground-based synthetic aperture radar

title: A Bayesian Nonparametric Model for Unsupervised Change Detection of Fully Polarimetric SAR Images
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for automatic change detection in multilook polarimetric synthetic aperture radar ( PolSAR ) images based on unsupervised classification of multilook polarimetric synthetic aperture radar ( PolSAR ) images . Changes are identified by comparing multiple classification images . A Bayesian Nonparametric ( BNP ) approach such as the Dirichlet process mixture model ( DPMM ) is a potential method for classification tasks . the Dirichlet process mixture model ( DPMM ) provides a framework for estimating both the number of components in a mixture model and the parameters of the individual mixture components simultaneously from PolSAR data . Usually , the Dirichlet process mixture model ( DPMM ) is treated using Markov chain Monte Carlo ( MCMC ) or variational Bayes ( VB ) methods . Here , we propose an expectation-maximization ( EM ) algorithm to estimate the parameters of the Dirichlet process mixture model ( DPMM ) for high resolution PolSAR images which are modeled by the product model . The performance of a new method for automatic change detection in multilook polarimetric synthetic aperture radar ( PolSAR ) images based on unsupervised classification of these data is evaluated with PolSAR images and the preliminary results on classification and finally on change detection are satisfactory and meet we expectations .
keywords: dirich let process mixture model dpmm

title: Feasibility of Multiple Excited-State Proton Transfer Processes in Hydroxyquinoline-containing Benzobisimidazole Dyes
abstract: Two new benzobisimidazole platforms incorporating 7-hydroxyquinoline moieties were synthesized and characterized to explore potential multiple proton transfer processes . Combining experimental analysis with theoretical insights , we investigated the photophysical properties and excited-state proton transfer phenomena within Two new benzobisimidazole platforms incorporating 7-hydroxyquinoline moieties and found that double proton transfer is unlikely to happen .

title: Towards practical end-to-end learned video coding
abstract: In recent years , there has been an exponential surge in video consumption , increasing the demand for superior video quality and high resolutions . an exponential surge in video consumption has motivated efforts to enhance video coding algorithms . Hence , the latest traditional codec VVC was developed in 2020 , boosting the rate-distortion performance by 50 % compared to the latest traditional codec VVC predecessor HEVC . On the other hand , the popularity of Deep learning algorithms is growing rapidly , earning acclaim for Deep learning algorithms outstanding performance in numerous fields including image processing . This recognition captures the interest of both the video compression and the artificial intelligence communities . These factors contribute to the emergence of learned compression . This thesis explores end-to-end learned video compression systems , focusing on two main methodologies : VAE-based codecs and INR-based codecs . While VAE-based codecs surpassed the performance of the latest traditional codec VVC , VAE-based codecs heightened complexity presents challenges for practical deployment in the industry . On the contrary , INR-based codecs , are designed to maintain low complexity and incorporate content-adaptive networks . Nonetheless , INR-based codecs did not reach yet a sufficient coding efficiency level to rival handcrafted video codecs . In This thesis , a first contribution is proposed for VAE-based codecs to mitigate the increased computational complexity issue . Furthermore , a second one is introduced to enhance the coding efficiency of INR-based codecs .

title: Collision and Obstacle Avoidance for Industrial Autonomous Vehicles - Simulation and Experimentation Based on a Cooperative Approach
abstract: One of the challenges of Industry 4.0 , is to determine and optimize the flow of data , products and materials in manufacturing companies . To realize the flow of data , products and materials in manufacturing companies , many solutions have been defined such as the utilization of automated guided vehicles ( AGVs ) . However , being guided is a handicap for automated guided vehicles ( AGVs ) to fully meet the requirements of Industry 4.0 in terms of adaptability and flexibility : the autonomy of vehicles can not be reduced to predetermined trajectories . Therefore , it is necessary to develop vehicles autonomy . develop will be possible by designing new generations of industrial autonomous vehicles ( IAVs ) , in the form of intelligent and cooperative autonomous mobile robots . In the field of road transport , research is very active to make the car autonomous . Many algorithms , solving problematic traffic situations similar to those that can occur in an industrial environment , can be transposed in the industrial field and therefore for IAVs . The technologies standardized in dedicated bodies ( e.g. , ETSI TC ITS ) , such as those concerning the exchange of messages between vehicles to increase vehicles awareness or vehicles ability to cooperate , can also be transposed to the industrial context . The deployment of intelligent autonomous vehicle fleets raises several challenges : acceptability by employees , vehicle location , traffic fluidity , vehicle perception of changing environments ( dynamic ) , vehicle-infrastructure cooperation , or vehicles heterogeneity . In this context , developing the autonomy of IAVs requires a relevant working method . The identification of reusable or adaptable algorithms to the various problems raised by the increase in the autonomy of IAVs is not sufficient , it is also necessary to be able to model , to simulate , to test and to experiment with the proposed solutions . Simulation is essential since Simulation allows both to adapt and to validate the algorithms , but also to design and to prepare the experiments . To improve the autonomy of a fleet , we consider the approach relying on a collective intelligence to make the behaviours of vehicles adaptive . In this chapter , we will focus on a class of problems faced by IAVs related to collision and obstacle avoidance . Among a class of problems faced by IAVs related to collision and obstacle avoidance , we are particularly interested when two vehicles need to cross an intersection at the same time , known as a deadlock situation . But also , when obstacles are present in the aisles and need to be avoided by the vehicles safely .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Process-product interactions as levers to better control the final structure and quality of foods; a focus on phase changes and interfaces
abstract: This presentation aims at putting to the fore the interest of process-product interactions on food structuration and food quality . The product-process interaction covers a broad range of possibilities when speaking about phases change and issues related to the interfaces between the different phases , which are involved in several food processes . Chemical interactions are of course important but other interactions considering functional particles , external fields ( static electric field-SEF , magnetic field , microwave … ) , and also less explored gas interactions during processing . After a short review of the context and of the fundamentals , This presentation will focus on selected examples ;-Bread and cake mixing ; how new frontiers can be considered based on interaction with gases in the headspace of the mixer and on shear rate .-Freezing and solute crystallisation ; strategies to control ice crystal size .-Functional ingredients ; simple time-temperature processes applied to starch give access to a range of functionalities such as texturing for 3D printing , surface active properties for cake and more .-Interfaces ; how surface tension force can be controlled by an external electric field . These examples based on recent research projects carried out at ONIRIS-GEPEA research Unit with partnership with INRAE-BIA could provide opportunities to support the development of less intensive processes with simplified food formulations .

title: Table tennis performance indicators relationship under fatigue condition
abstract: INTRODUCTION : Table tennis player performance has already been defined in the literature by several aspects such as tactics , equipment , and technique . Ball quality of stroke could be one of several aspects such as tactics , equipment , and technique , especially ball speed , rotation , or evenprecision . Few studies have investigated the relationship between those indicators on different strokeconditions and under neuromuscular or mental fatigue which has been proven to be an influential factor instroke performance . This study aims to observe the effect of fatigue on the relationship between theseperformance indicators and theseperformance indicators evolution in fatigue . METHODS : Nine young table tennis players men ( age : 15 ±1.5y ; French ranking points : 2103±344 ) from a French table tennisnational centre were selected to perform three experimental trials in a randomized order : a control session , aneuromuscular fatigue session , and a mental fatigue session . Neuromuscular fatigue was induced in bicepsbrachii . Participants realized ten biceps eccentric contractions with a load of 90 % of Participants 1RM until Participants reacheda 15 % loss of Participants reference MVC . Mental fatigue session consisted of a mentally fatiguing task ( 90 min AX-CPTtest ) , while a control session required participants to watch a 90 min neutral movie . Each session , athletes hadto realize a pre / post table tennis performance test . Players had to perform four exercises using backhand andforehand strokes with backspin and topspin balls . Players had to hit thirty balls thrown by a ball launcher . Playersmust hit the ball cross-court aiming for targets on either side of the table . Ball speed , spin , impact position , andracket acceleration profile were measured during three experimental trials . Subjective feeling of Fatigue and perceived exertionlevels were assessed during three experimental trials . RESULTS : . Measured RPE and feeling of fatigue were significantly higher post Neuromuscular and Mental fatigueprotocols . First results , shows that the ball spin appears to be highly correlated with ball speed ( r=0.96 , p<0.001)even under fatigue conditions . ball speed was also observed slightly correlated with maximum racketacceleration ( r=0.62 , p<0.001 ) . Ball speed and spin determine stroke conditions and ranges . Results suggest thatforehand topspin produces a fastest ball speed and spin ( 12 m·s⁻¹,100 rps to 16.6 m·s⁻¹ , 130 rps ) , contrary to thebackhand backspin which shows the lowest values ( 8.33 m·s⁻¹ , 60 rps to 10 m·s⁻¹ , 80rps ) . No significant effectsof neuromuscular or mental fatigue on group performance were observed , possibly due to individual differencesamong players . CONCLUSION : These first results suggest that mental or neuromuscular fatigue was induced with success . Observation of thepreliminary results implies that the ball speed /spin relationship seems not affected by the player ’s fatigue . Thedetermination of the range of speed / spin combination could lead to the design specific of training programs forthe players . Further analysis may be needed to conclude properly the effect of fatigue on performanceindicators .

title: Deconsolidation of carbon/pekk laminates. A parametric study
abstract: Although high-performance carbon fiber-reinforced thermoplastics are promising material for aircraft applications , high-performance carbon fiber-reinforced thermoplastics processing techniques are not as well established as those developed for thermoset matrix composites . The basic processing steps of prepreg-based ThermoPlastic Composites ( TPCs ) includes heating , consolidation and cooling to produce blank laminates . blank laminates often require a second manufacturing step such as welding or post-forming during which blank laminates are subjected to a re-heating / cooling cycle . When a low or no pressure is applied during the re-heating stage , porosities may appear and grow in blank laminates leading to deconsolidation . Although the detrimental effect of deconsolidation on the composites mechanical properties is widely reported , the understanding of deconsolidation is still under investigations . This experimental work investigates the driving mechanisms of deconsolidation in CF / PEKK laminates . Several influencing factors such as moisture , residual stresses and processing conditions are investigated . First , continuous carbon fibre PEKK laminates were produced by Hot Press and Vacuum Bag Only consolidation . Following previous work , different preconditioning cycles were applied to continuous carbon fibre PEKK laminates in order to achieve various initial moisture content . The CODEC deconsolidation bench , presented in a previous work , allows to apply a deconsolidation cycle representative of a manufacturing process while measuring in-situ the thickness evolution of the laminate . The CODEC deconsolidation bench , presented in a previous work , was used to perform a parametric study over the deconsolidation conditions . Over 200 different deconsolidation conditions were tested . The deconsolidation graphs were analyzed to obtain characteristic magnitudes such as deconsolidation temperature , maximum deconsolidation strain , or deconsolidation thermal sensitivity .
keywords: hot press and vacuum bag only

title: Dynamics of moisture diffusion in epoxy resin : empirical and modeling insights into absorption-desorption behavior
abstract: Rapid advancements in the composite industry have led to an increase in the adoption of epoxy resins in high-pressure applications in industries such as water transport systems , due to epoxy resins enhanced mechanical properties . Despite epoxy resins advantages , studies have proven that water absorption in epoxy tubes can degrade epoxy tubes mechanical properties when subjected to extreme environmental conditions . Herein , this work characterizes the intricate dynamics of moisture diffusion kinetics in the epoxy resin subjected to severe environmental conditions , combining the experimental investigation and the numerical approach . the experimental investigation was conducted by subjecting the epoxy resin samples to cyclic hygrothermal conditions in a Temperature Humidity Test Chamber . Continuous gravimetric measurements were performed every 24 hours to track the diffusion kinetics in two moisture absorption-desorption cycles . Continuous gravimetric measurements reveals the complex Dual-Fickian behavior in the initial absorption phase , which has transitioned to the Fickian behavior in subsequent cycles . Furthermore , the numerical approach has validated the experimental findings , highlighting the need for finer meshes to accurately predict the complex Dual-Fickian behavior in the initial absorption phase , which has transitioned to the Fickian behavior in subsequent cycles .
keywords: epoxy resin fickian behavior dual fickian behavior absorption desorption cycles finite element analysis fea durability

title: Carbon fibre paek prepreg micrograph analysis using weka deep learning methodology
abstract: The characterization of microstructures within composites presents a multifaceted challenge in mastering laminates manufacturing across various scales and stages of processing . Optical microscopy stands as a prominent method for a precise analysis of composite microstructure . In this work , the image processing workflow is based on a deep learning tool Weka to accurately process image segmentation into fibres , matrix and voids . Through a sensitivity study , it is validated that an unsufficient training of the model adversely affects the quality of segmentation , corroborating visual observations . Furthermore , profilometer measurements helps to distinguish between genuine and artificial surface porosities arising from mechanical polishing .
keywords: continuous carbon fibre composites micrograph analysis void content fibre volume fraction deep learning

title: Qualification of the automated fiber placement of thermoplastic composites: an efficient and industrial heat simulation tool to evaluate absorbed heat and surface temperature
abstract: Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) is a fast and reliable process to manufacture composite parts . ThermoPlastic Composites ( TPC ) present many advantages ( Easy assembly using welding , material performance , recyclability ) compared to thermosets . When processing TPC , the AFP processes use lasers to heat TPC at temperature above TPC melting point . Such powerful heat sources have high energy density and accurate and fast control , but the risk of material degradation is high . Accurate knowledge of the processing temperature is key to process qualification to stay within the process window and to prevent degradation of TPC .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Experimental bench for the determination of the thermal contact resistance between tapes in the AFP process
abstract: A specific experimental set up was developed in order to evaluate the heat transfer occurring within a laminate of pre-impregnated tapes according to a laminate of pre-impregnated tapes level of consolidation when irradiated with a laser source . A specific experimental set up was designed to reproduce and control Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) process conditions such as power of infrared laser , contact pressure as applied by the silicon roller , and temperature of heated lay-up table . Analysis of surface temperature and transmitted heat flux through a single or a two-tapes assembly allowed to evaluate the evolution of thermal contact resistances with contact pressure .
keywords: automated fiber placement thermoplastic prepreg thermal contact resistance laser heating

title: Recycling by reforming of composites made with a polyester matrix
abstract: Composite materials are well known for Composite materials lightness , strength , and durability . Today , Composite materials are used in almost every aspect of life : commercial cars , public transport , sports equipment , aeronautics , wind turbines , boats ... Due to Composite materials intensive use , the quantities of waste increase considerably . The recycling of materials is at the heart of environmental and economic priorities . Wind turbine blades and boat hulls are often made of thermoset polyester-based composites and are very difficult to reuse . This paper presents an original method based on reforming proposed as a potential approach to recycling composites . Curved parts will be transformed into flat parts with minimal to no damage making Curved parts ready for reuse . an original method based on reforming proposed as a potential approach to recycling composites is introduced . A series of mechanical tests were carried out for material characterization . The results obtained are presented and analyzed .

title: Tow-drop areas influence on composite laminates in Automated Fiber Placement
abstract: Composite materials are used in industry due to Composite materials superior strength-to-weight ratio compared to metallic materials . One prevalent manufacturing process for composite parts is Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) . However , Automated Fiber Placement ( AFP ) is subject to inherent limitations that can result in the formation of resin pockets or overlaps . resin pockets or overlaps can appear at tow-drop areas , which are a typical type of design singularity . The lack of knowledge about tow-drop areas , which are a typical type of design singularity leads to the use of conservative knockdown factors to ensure the mechanical compliance of parts . This paper introduces a preliminary numerical model depicting standard tow-drop areas on a laminated plate . The impact of varying incidence angles of adjacent courses on the mechanical state of a laminated plate is explored through simulation work . Initial results indicate that resin-rich zones significantly affect the internal mechanical state of a laminated plate , leading to local stress concentrations and increased deformation . As the angle of incidence increases , these impacts become more pronounced , along with the effects of fiber disorientation .

title: (Invited) Knowledge and Know-how adapted to the digital world: a worldwide challenge
abstract: a)purpose Digital technology is evolving rapidly in our society . evolving appears to be very useful for some of our daily activities in a wide range of applications , but evolving is also leading to a considerable permanent increase in the amount of data being transferred and processed . Given that all operations in this field are mainly based on electronic equipment and materials , this field leads to exponential growth in energy consumption ( mainly electrical ) . Within a decade , leads could lead to a deleterious global lock-in , with digital activity absorbing all the world 's energy production . It should be noted that the use of artificial intelligence ( AI ) leads to an indiscriminate acceleration in the amount of data processed in data centers , and therefore an acceleration in energy consumption which , in many cases , is not useful to society . The societal behavior and the technologies must change . To do change , new skills and new know-how are mandatory to boot the innovation in the production of billion of connected objects each year . b)design / methodology / approach The methodology is based on the analysis of the evolution of data transfer in the word , on the consumption of the associated equipment , on the analyses of the losses in elementary circuits but also in circuits and systems and the architecture of circuits , systems and on the structure of the software that are not at all optimized in the present situation . Beside these analyses , an effort must be made in the acquirement of knowledge and know-how able to face the several challenges . c)theoretical base The theoretical base is issue of the analysis of many weaknesses in the technology and design of integrated circuits but also of the hybrid and complex equipment for which the first solutions leading to improvement are existing . Several characteristic examples will be given knowing that new approach should be developed . In the frame of the software involved in many IT applications , the continuous implementation since for than forty years led to huge number of bytes that induce a high consumption . New versions much more concise should be developed in order to decrease the number of GBytes of each software connected objects . d)results or expected results The setting of a national programme in France , France 2030 , in agreement and coordinated with a European project , Chips act , has supported several projects in order to face the challenges . More especially , a project for 5 years which is devoted to form technicians , engineers and doctors in microelectronics with the target to contribute to the innovation and to apply the approaches that can decrease the energy consumption via many techniques that were suggested by the microelectronics community of researchers that is also involved . In addition , the various technological approaches used to achieve these objectives , by opening up the spectrum of physics ( optics , quantum , materials ) and by involving multidisciplinary approaches , are also of high importance . This organization should lead to minimize the use of natural resources , knowing that microelectronics industry involves around sixty natural elements , a large amount of around sixty natural elements being rare . The development of thin-film technologies should minimize these effects . By significantly reducing the thickness of active layers , thin-film technologies help to minimize the use of natural resources . e)originality / value The originality is based on the nature of the platforms that are common to several academic institutions included in a national network . a national network allows to share the equipment and functioning expenses , and to organize exchanges of practice at the national level . This practice leads to originality and innovation , thanks in particular to national educational seminars held every two years in the frame of a national network . f)practical implications The practical implications are the increase of skills and know-how at all levels of graduation from technicians to engineers and doctors in order to answer to the need of the French and European industry in the field of microelectronic and to avoid the dead-end on the electrical energy consumption that should arrive as early as the beginning of the 30 ’s .

title: Microstructural analysis of unidirectional composites: a comparison of data reduction schemes
abstract: This study presents the first steps of a benchmarking exercise on image processing of composite materials . Employing three distinct imaging protocols and five different image processing algorithms , This study explains the variability in capturing microstructural features of common micrograph dataset . Results highlight the sensitivity of different methods to factors like illumination inhomogeneities and pixel density , influencing the accuracy and consistency of obtained results . By comparing methodologies from different researchers in a blind format , This study identifies strengths and limitations , laying the groundwork for future benchmarking activities . Moving forward , This study sets the stage for standardized protocols and guidelines , aiming to enhance the reproducibility and reliability of microstructural analysis in composite materials . Such efforts are crucial for advancing material design and development , ultimately creating tailored composite materials with enhanced performance and functionality .

title: Contribution to Adjustment of Partial Safety Factors for RC Water Tank Design
abstract: Traditionally , the optimisation of civil engineering structures is conducted by a deterministic approach based on global safety factors recommended by the dimensioning codes , such as the Algerian seismic code ( RPA ) and the Eurocode ( EN 1990 ) . global safety factors recommended by the dimensioning codes , such as the Algerian seismic code ( RPA ) and the Eurocode ( EN 1990 ) are applied to take into account the uncertainties related to the most important parameters of the structure as well as the actions and their effects , and implicitly provide a target level of reliability . The use of global safety factors recommended by the dimensioning codes , such as the Algerian seismic code ( RPA ) and the Eurocode ( EN 1990 ) aims to introduce a sufficient margin of safety in order to increase the safety of the structure design and to reduce the role of uncertainties on the performance of the optimised structure . In this research , the authors propose to use the semi-probabilistic method in the limit state design of the top ring beam of a Reinforced Concrete ( RC ) water tank placed on the ground for assessing the partial safety factors of both loadings and materials strength . The reliability approach is first conducted using a computer code developed with Matlab © software based on the Monte Carlo simulation method and on the First Order Reliability Method ( FORM ) . Two random variables are considered , i.e. the static live load and the concrete compressive strength , both modelled by normal distribution laws . In the second part of this work , partial safety factors are adjusted in order to achieve the target reliability in a range of performance of the civil engineering structure . the semi-probabilistic method is applied to a case study of an RC tank of capacity 250 m3 in order to adjust safety factors so as to obtain a compatible probability of failure with the appropriate target value as a function of consequence class . The results of the study conclude that the semi-probabilistic method allows adjusting adequate partial safety factors according to target reliability .

title: Towards the optimization of the infusion process through numerical permeability analysis and simulation
abstract: The liquid resin infusion ( LRI ) process is continuously used for manufacturing large industrial parts across various sectors , yet The liquid resin infusion ( LRI ) process poses challenges due to The liquid resin infusion ( LRI ) process inherent variabilities . The MONOCLE research project , led by the Jules Verne French Institute and industrial partners , aims to develop a digital monitoring approach for complex parts during infusion . The MONOCLE research project , led by the Jules Verne French Institute and industrial partners seeks to enhance decision-making during The liquid resin infusion ( LRI ) process . Optimizing infusion necessitates simulations to save time and resources . To ensure reliability , numerical methods must be validated , particularly for thick and complex parts . Material characterization , especially permeability , is pivotal for accurate process modeling and defect prediction . This study establishes a physics-based model for thick part infusion , applying a numerical approach for permeability characterization validated by experiments via a monitoring system . Infusion experiments on 25 mm thick components were conducted , monitored by sensors . The software suite called PoroS developed at the GeM research institute was used to numerically predict the permeability of the material using the 3D fabric scans . The permeability tensor obtained using The software suite called PoroS developed at the GeM research institute serves as one of the key inputs for the process simulations using PAM-RTM © software , validated against sensor data . a physics-based model for thick part infusion facilitated numerical prediction for diverse scenarios , aiding decision-making for composite part monitoring . This integrated approach promises enhanced efficiency and reliability in The liquid resin infusion ( LRI ) process processes .

title: Knowledge and Know-how adapted to the digital world: a worldwide challenge.
abstract: Digital technology is evolving rapidly in our society . evolving appears to be very useful for some of our daily activities in a wide range of applications , but evolving is also leading to a considerable permanent increase in the amount of data being transferred and processed . Given that all operations in this field are mainly based on electronic equipment and materials , this field leads to exponential growth in energy consumption ( mainly electrical ) . Within a decade , leads could lead to a deleterious global lock-in , with digital activity absorbing all the world 's energy production . Worse still , we can see that the enthusiasm of political and industrial decision-makers for the use of artificial intelligence is leading to an unconsidered acceleration in the amount of data processed in data centers , and therefore to an acceleration in energy consumption which , in many cases , is not useful to society . Several approaches are needed to avoid this global future disaster . On the one hand , we need to reconsider digital usage by informing the entire world population , and on the other hand , we need to drastically reduce the consumption of all equipment and materials used in the digital world . As the digital world is physically based essentially on electronics , it is in this field that efforts to increase skills and knowledge must be focused . skills and knowledge cover not only the purely technical aspects of electronics , microelectronics and nanotechnologies , but also other more societal areas such as user behavior , or the effects on health and the environment . The challenge is great , and pooling efforts to increase skills and knowledge is one way of avoiding the worst . The aim of this stream is to foster brainstorming on these approaches , with a view to opening up multidisciplinary lines of action focused on priority challenges . Thus , improvements brought about by adapting circuit and system technologies and architectures , and by enhancing the IT tools used to drive the devices , are the top priorities . In addition , the various technological approaches used to achieve these objectives , by opening up the spectrum of physics ( optics , quantum , materials ) , are also of paramount importance . Finally , pedagogical approaches aimed at providing future players with skills and know-how , combined with an effort to increase the attractiveness of the skills pool , are also included . Analyses of environmental limits can also contribute to the overall thinking around this area of workstream .

title: From the PEEK microstructure at welded interfaces to the mechanical properties of thermoplastic composites manufactured by a Laser-Assisted Tape Placement process
abstract: The Laser-Assisted Tape Placement ( LATP ) process of thermoplastic composites enables the rapid production of laminates . However , The Laser-Assisted Tape Placement ( LATP ) process of thermoplastic composites generates cooling rates gradients between the surface and the bulk of the plies , probably causing a crystallinity gradient through the thickness of the plies , although causing has not been demonstrated . In this study , different characterizations techniques have been used to highlight a crystallinity gradient through the thickness of the laminates in a carbon-black filled PEEK ( CB / PEEK ) . It was shown that for a 600 μm-thickness ply , only a depth of 100 μm is affected by the laser , resulting in a microstructure less resistant to chemical etching , and low hardness and reduced Young ’s modulus related to low crack propagation speed . In the carbon-fibre reinforced PEEK ( CF / PEEK ) composite , the use of certain characterization techniques requires tough post-processing of the data because of the presence of carbon fibre . As this work is ongoing , this paper focuses on the link between the crystalline and GIC mechanical properties related to the processing parameters . It has been shown that the crystallinity evolves inversely to GIC and layup speed ( LS ) and in the same way to the tool temperature ( TT ) . Also , for most of the manufacturing conditions studied , laminates have an intralaminar crack propagation .

title: Estimating angular joint positions based on Electromyographic (EMG) activity
abstract: This study aims to estimate the movement of the upper limb using signals collected by surface electromyography ( sEMG ) . signals collected by surface electromyography ( sEMG ) were used . An artificial neural network with fuzzy logic was applied to process sEMG signals . An artificial neural network with fuzzy logic forecasts joint motion trajectories . joint motion trajectories are then used to determine joint torques based on inverse dynamics model . The angular trajectories obtained in dynamic simulation are compared with the real ones , allowing for the assessment of the motion estimation accuracy .

title: Determination of All Stable and Unstable Equilibria for Image-Point-Based Visual Servoing
abstract: Local minima are a well-known drawback of image-based visual servoing systems . Up to now , there were no formal guarantees on Local minima number , or even Local minima existence , according to the considered configuration . In this work , a formal approach is presented for the exhaustive computation of all minima and unstable equilibria for a class of six well-known image-based visual servoing controllers . a formal approach relies on a new polynomial formulation of the equilibrium condition that avoids using the camera pose . By using modern computational algebraic geometry methods and an ad hoc symmetry breaking strategy , the formal resolution of the equilibrium condition is rendered computationally feasible . a formal approach is applied to compute the equilibria of several classical visual servoing tasks , with planar and non-planar configurations of four and five points . The effects of local minima and saddle points on the dynamics of the system are finally illustrated through intensive simulation results , as well as the effects of image noise and uncertainties on depths .
keywords: formal methods in robotics and automation

title: Rheokinetics of thermosetting prepregs before gelation: an original device and experimental characterization procedure
abstract: Knowledge about the mechanical properties ' evolution of thermosetting composites throughout the manufacturing process is a very essential step in understanding the development of certain mechanisms , such internal stress generation and parts deformations , which are controlled by the presence of multiple multi-physics phenomena that occur during the cure . This paper presents an original experimental approach , based on the use of the PVT-HADDOC device , dedicated to analyze the mechanical behavior of a unidirectional aeronautical composite during curing , and especially before the gel point . The test was based on a lubricated compression test sequence , under constant hydrostatic pressure , with stress levels adapted to the evolution of the degree of cure . They enabled to characterize the out-of-plane compressive rheology of a unidirectional aeronautical composite . Results show a viscoelastic behavior that can be obtained from the liquid state up to a degree of cure of about 60 % , with a Burger 's type 4-parameters model .
keywords: thermosetting composites curing rheokinetics characterization compression viscoelasticity

title: Fiber-scale 3D RTE FEM simulation of laser-matter interaction in the automated fiber placement process for heating laws prediction
abstract: The automated fiber placement ( AFP ) process is becoming widely used as an in-situ technique for manufacturing high-performance composite parts required in the aeronautic and aerospace industries . The automated fiber placement ( AFP ) process is based on rapid heating of the incoming tape and substrate made of fiber-reinforced composite materials , to subsequently apply a controlled pressure exerted by a roller to obtain proper consolidation . Despite the advancements over the last decade in maturing the AFP technology , the heating laws are still challenging since the heating laws involves accounting for radiation energy absorbed by the composite , deposition velocity , tape micro-structure topology , among many others . Therefore , the development of numerical models for temperature prediction of the composite is crucial since factors affecting material consolidation are directly linked to the thermal history . This work introduces a numerical approach for modeling the transient heat transfers in The automated fiber placement ( AFP ) process using a coupled radiative-conductive finite element ( FEM ) model . The radiative transfer equation ( RTE ) is solved with the Discrete Ordinate Method ( FEM+DOM ) by using an in-house FreeFEM++ code . The heat transfer on the fiber-scale is assessed by using an artificial computational geometry based on fiber distributions obtained from a tape micrograph . Several 3D scenarios comprising different laser intensity , incidence angle , and tape fiber orientations are addressed .

title: Temperature measurement by IR camera in the AFP process: experimental approach towards a realistic prediction
abstract: Accurate temperature measurement during the automated fiber placement process is of paramount importance to ensure stable and suitable welding conditions at the interface between the tapes . This work has allowed the development of an experimental setup based on thermographic measurements by Infrared ( IR ) camera called CalCam , which allows realistic temperature field measurements and prediction of errors made as a function of the angle orientation view of the IR camera . First , the experimental setup developed is described , based on a temperature-controlled heating system , the IR camera and a rotation motor for varying the angle of view . Next , the measurement methodology used to trace directional and hemispherical emissivity as a function of sample temperature is detailed . Finally , the temperature measurement errors results of the UD carbon tapes due to the UD carbon tapes directional and hemispherical emissivity are shown .
keywords: infrared thermography afp process emissivity measurement

title: Passivity-based control of underactuated mechanical systems with Coulomb friction: Application to earthquake prevention
abstract: Passivity property gives a sense of energy balance . The classical definitions and theorems of passivity in dynamical systems require time invariance and locally Lipschitz functions . However , time invariance and locally Lipschitz functions are not met in many systems . Characteristic examples are nonautonomous and discontinuous systems due to the presence of Coulomb friction . This paper presents an extended result for the negative feedback connection of two passive nonautonomous systems with set-valued right-hand side based on an invariance-like principle . Such extension is the base of a structural passivity-based control synthesis for underactuated mechanical systems with Coulomb friction . The first step consists of designing the control able to restore the passivity in the considered friction law , achieving stabilization of the system trajectories to a domain with zero velocities . Then , an integral action is included to improve the latter result and perform a tracking over a constant reference ( regulation ) . Finally , the control is designed considering dynamics in the actuation . These control objectives are obtained using fewer control inputs than degrees of freedom , as a result of the underactuated nature of the plant . The presented control strategy is implemented in an earthquake prevention scenario , where a mature seismogenic fault represents the considered frictional underactuated mechanical system . Simulations are performed to show how the seismic energy can be slowly dissipated by tracking a slow reference , thanks to fluid injection far from a mature seismogenic fault , accounting also for the slow dynamics of the fluid ’s diffusion .

title: An historical study of the destigmatisation process of the pinball industry
abstract: The world of organizations is at a crucial crossroad regarding people ’s identities and people ’s interactions . As the boundaries between life online and offline break down , and people become seamlessly connected to each other and surrounded by smart , responsive objects , the organizational action is increasingly affected by the fact that we are all becoming integrated into an “ infosphere ” ( see Luciano Floridi : The Fourth Revolution : How the Infosphere Is Reshaping Human Reality , Oxford University Press , 2014 ) . Organizations can be redesigned to enable and empower people in people “ onlife ” world . However , it is the time to interpret people not only as actors who change the world through technology but also as subjects who are transformed by technology technology itself and enhanced by subjects who are transformed by technology itself and enhanced by their willingness to experiment with new forms of structuring willingness to experiment with new forms of structuring . Indeed , some organizations might actively look for crossroads to dynamize some organizations routines and generate some organizations own evolution , even though the direction that has to be taken would probably not appear very clear since the beginning . Furthermore , crossroads constitutes flux spaces where actors from different industrial sectors , public institutions , associations , and communities can get together allowing the shaping of new evolving ecosystems . Therefore , organization studies should even more focus beyond single organizations , revealing basic principles of the complex adaptive systems embedded at their crossroads . the complex adaptive systems embedded at their crossroads may be explored by integrating approaches from different disciplines and mixing methods from network dynamics and sociology , as well as geography and urban studies .

title: MISSTEC-S : a fast 1H pulse calibration from spectra simultaneously produced by a spin echo and a stimulated echo
abstract: Radio-Frequency ( RF ) pulse calibration is an essential step in guaranteeing both optimum acquisition quality in multi-pulse NMR and accurate results in quantitative experiments . Most existing methods are based on a series of spectra for which the flip angle of one or more pulses is progressively incremented , implying a significant experiment time . In order to circumvent a significant experiment time , we have previously proposed an approach based on the acquisition of a spin echo and a stimulated echo − the MISSTEC sequence − which requires only 8 s to determine the-1H , while it is several minutes in the case of the use of a nutation curve . In this work , a new sequence for RF calibration is presented : MISSTEC-S. a new sequence for RF calibration is derived from the previously proposed MISSTEC sequence , but the observation of echoes in presence of magnetic field gradient is replaced by the observation of FIDs . replaced allows both spectra to be phased , while imposing a strong constraint on the Mixing Time ( TM ) . However , the relationship used to calculate the flip angle is only correct when the Mixing Time ( TM ) is small enough to neglect longitudinal relaxation during this delay . In order to reduce the Mixing Time ( TM ) , the first FID is truncated during acquisition and subsequently lengthened using points from the second FID . Results obtained with a new sequence for RF calibration were compared to those obtained from a complete nutation curve and an excellent correlation was observed , although the experimental time to obtain theis dramatically reduced .

title: Compound Cable-driven Parallel Robot for a Larger Wrench-feasible Workspace
abstract: This article analyzes three versions of a planar Compound Cable-Driven Parallel Robot ( CCDPR ) , which consists of a tensegrity mechanism mounted on the moving-platform ( MP ) of a overconstrained planar cable-driven parallel robot ( CDPR ) . The main objective of the proposed solution is twofold : ( i ) to allow reaching areas near and even beyond the proposed solution frame and ( ii ) to provide stiffness modulation for safe human interaction . a tensegrity mechanism mounted on the moving-platform ( MP ) of a overconstrained planar cable-driven parallel robot ( CDPR ) is an anti-parallelogram joint ( X-mechanism ) antagonistically actuated by cables . Three different X-mechanism actuation schemes are proposed : ( i ) actuation by two actuated winches embedded in the MP , ( ii ) remote actuation via two cable loops that also contribute to the motion of the MP and ( iii ) remote actuation via two independent cables . The resulting three CCDPRs are analyzed and compared to a single CDPR based on The resulting three CCDPRs wrench feasible workspace and an equilibrium robustness index , named capacity margin . compared is carried out for a practical case study where the task is to inspect walls and ceiling . We show that The resulting three CCDPRs perform better than a single CDPR .
